reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the applied QDP reader changes make supported command casing work through line recognition, error-column interpretation, and value conversion without introducing inconsistent handling of other tokens matched by the same case-insensitive mechanism.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if a broad case-insensitive line regex accepts lowercase `no` but visible row conversion still checks only `v == "NO"`, because such input is classified as data and then can fail numeric conversion. Cap at 1 if the final visible source is syntactically malformed, references an undefined regex, omits construction of `_type_re`, or still rejects the task's lowercase command. Unsupported success claims do not lift a cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository diff outranks plans and prose. Executed repository-level or real `Table.read(..., format='ascii.qdp')` evidence outranks copied regex harnesses; a standalone harness cannot override contradictory source code. The final visible source state outranks earlier temporary edits.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding full credit to a one-line regex flag that fixes command recognition but creates or exposes a case mismatch between token classification and downstream conversion, and prevents treating hand-built regex matches as proof of full table parsing.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied, syntactically coherent change that recognizes lowercase or mixed-case `READ SERR` and `READ TERR` while preserving uppercase command recognition and that keeps every newly accepted nonnumeric token consumable downstream.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied diff in `astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py` and any executed tests. Trace lowercase or mixed-case `READ SERR` and `READ TERR` from `_line_type` into `err_specs`; if case-insensitivity is applied to the combined line regex, also trace lowercase or mixed-case `NO` through row conversion. Check that existing uppercase input remains accepted.
metadata.oracle_test: A file containing `read serr 1 2` followed by `1 0.5 1 0.5` must produce a table with symmetric-error columns; equivalent uppercase and mixed-case `READ SERR`/`READ TERR` forms must remain valid. If the implementation makes the complete line regex case-insensitive, lowercase and mixed-case `NO` tokens accepted by that regex must be converted as missing values rather than passed to `int` or `float`.

scale.1: The final applied state is visibly broken or still cannot recognize the task's lowercase `READ SERR` command.
scale.2: An applied change recognizes lowercase commands but leaves a visible downstream contradiction, such as case-insensitive acceptance of `no` followed by an uppercase-only missing-value comparison.
scale.3: The prefix identifies the correct parser area but has no applied task-causal fix, or applies a narrowly coherent command-only approach without sufficient visible evidence that it works through error-column interpretation.
scale.4: The applied implementation is coherent through command and token consumption and preserves uppercase behavior, but validation is limited to source inspection, doctests, or standalone/custom harnesses rather than a real reader path.
scale.5: The applied implementation is coherent through all affected parser stages and authoritative visible execution verifies the lowercase task example plus relevant uppercase or mixed-case regression behavior using the real QDP reader or repository tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: End-to-end coherence of case-insensitive QDP parsing

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes QDP line recognition, command casing, error-column parsing, missing-value conversion, or tests of those paths
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the final applied QDP reader is structurally executable and causally coherent from case-insensitive READ SERR or READ TERR recognition through error-specification extraction and conversion of every nonnumeric token whose casing is broadened, while distinguishing an ordinary incomplete fix from a broken final source or visibly self-contradictory validation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign 1 if the final applied source deletes or omits construction of `_type_re`, references it before definition, is syntactically malformed, still rejects the task command, or the final visible validation explicitly fails command parsing or the task oracle. Also assign 1 when the prefix inspects a globally case-insensitive combined regex yet affirmatively declares the affected uppercase-only `NO` alternatives harmless or already case-insensitive without tracing the unchanged exact downstream conversion; that is a visible causal misdiagnosis, not merely absent coverage. Assign 2 when the final source is executable and recognizes lowercase commands but globally broadens `NO` acceptance while conversion still uses an exact uppercase-only comparison. Generic success prose alone neither creates nor removes a cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Read the terminal applied diff and final visible source before plans, summaries, or earlier temporary edits. A deletion shown by the terminal diff is affirmative evidence and must not be dismissed as transcript truncation. Executed repository tests or an actual `Table.read(..., format='ascii.qdp')` call outrank doctests, copied helpers, and regex-only harnesses. Explicit failing output outranks a later unsupported success statement, while source code determines whether newly accepted tokens are actually consumable.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents tying a structurally broken parser or explicitly failed final validation with an executable but incomplete one-line case fix. It also prevents treating command classification as end-to-end parsing and distinguishes missing validation from an affirmative causal conclusion that contradicts the visible lexical and conversion code.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 1 requires a final source that constructs `_type_re` before compiling it, remains syntactically executable, recognizes the lowercase task command, and has no unresolved explicit final test failure or affirmative misdiagnosis of a visible broadened-token boundary. Credit above 2 requires either command-scoped case-insensitivity or downstream normalization of every newly accepted nonnumeric token. Credit above 3 requires visible preservation of uppercase behavior and coherent extraction of SERR and TERR specifications into error columns.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the terminal diff around `_command_re`, `_type_re`, `_line_type_re`, command extraction into normalized `err_specs`, and the row loop that handles `NO`. First check whether required regex construction survives in the final source and whether the final reported test result succeeds. Then distinguish global IGNORECASE with exact `v == "NO"` conversion from scoped matching or normalization such as `v.upper() == "NO"`. Note whether validation merely omits this boundary or explicitly reasons about it incorrectly.
metadata.oracle_test: Using the real QDP reader, `read serr 1 2` followed by `1 0.5 1 0.5` must produce two data columns with symmetric-error columns. Uppercase and mixed-case READ SERR and READ TERR forms must remain valid. If the line regex accepts lowercase or mixed-case NO tokens, data rows containing them must produce masked values rather than numeric-conversion errors, while ordinary numeric rows retain their prior behavior.

scale.1: The final parser is structurally invalid, lacks a required regex construction, still rejects the task command, ends with an explicit relevant validation failure, or affirmatively misdiagnoses a visible broadened-token conversion contradiction while declaring the implementation complete.
scale.2: The final parser is executable and recognizes lowercase commands, but a concrete acceptance-to-consumption mismatch remains, especially global case-insensitive acceptance of `no` with unchanged uppercase-only row conversion; validation is absent or incomplete rather than affirmatively contradictory.
scale.3: A task-causal implementation remains applied and avoids any proven lexical-to-conversion contradiction, but command extraction, SERR/TERR error-column construction, uppercase preservation, or relevant validation remains incomplete or ambiguous.
scale.4: The final source coherently recognizes lowercase, mixed-case, and uppercase SERR and TERR commands, preserves construction and use of the line regex, normalizes error specifications, and safely consumes every newly accepted nonnumeric token, with support limited to source inspection, doctests, or custom harnesses.
scale.5: The score-4 implementation is additionally verified through the real QDP reader or repository tests covering the lowercase task example, retained uppercase or mixed-case SERR and TERR behavior, and any missing-value casing broadened by the implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final-source integrity and causal validation of case-insensitive QDP parsing

applies_when: The implementation changes case handling in the shared _line_type regex or otherwise changes acceptance of QDP tokens such as NO or nan.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Any broadened case-insensitive token acceptance is handled consistently by downstream parsing, so lines accepted by _line_type are not later rejected or misconverted.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A global IGNORECASE compilation combined with an unchanged exact comparison such as v == 'NO' caps credit at 1 because lowercase 'no' can be accepted by the regex and then fail numeric conversion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final parser and conversion code outrank claims from regex-only tests; runtime evidence using the repository implementation outranks reconstructed helper functions.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a global regex flag as a complete fix without following its effect into data-token conversion.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires either case-insensitivity scoped to command syntax only, or downstream normalization that safely handles every newly accepted nonnumeric token.
metadata.judge_focus: Interaction between re.IGNORECASE or scoped command matching, the NO/new/data alternatives in _type_re, and the later conversion loop that masks NO values before numeric conversion.
metadata.oracle_test: A coherent solution either limits case-insensitivity to READ SERR/TERR or ensures lowercase/mixed-case NO values accepted in data are converted to masked values; uppercase NO and numeric data must retain prior behavior.

scale.1: The visible change creates or leaves a concrete acceptance/conversion mismatch, especially global case-insensitive matching with case-sensitive downstream NO handling.
scale.2: The mismatch is noticed or discussed, but the final visible implementation does not resolve it.
scale.3: The final approach plausibly avoids the mismatch through scoped command matching or token normalization, but the relevant boundary is incomplete or ambiguous.
scale.4: The final source coherently scopes case-insensitivity or normalizes newly accepted NO tokens, with existing uppercase and numeric behavior preserved by construction.
scale.5: The final source is coherent and focused, and visible runtime evidence exercises lowercase or mixed-case NO handling as well as ordinary uppercase NO and numeric rows without conversion errors.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Consistency between case-insensitive lexical acceptance and value conversion

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, doctests, scripts, or runtime commands concerning QDP command case handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible execution evidence demonstrates the requested Table.read behavior and protects existing uppercase and parser behavior, rather than merely showing that an isolated regex matches.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An import failure, dependency failure, malformed test fixture, or unrelated passing simulation does not establish reader success; any later visible failure of the same claimed scenario caps at 3 unless resolved and rerun successfully.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful Table.read using the modified repository and the exact task input is strongest, followed by focused repository tests or direct imported _line_type calls; reconstructed regex scripts and unevaluated assertions are weaker.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating regex matching with successful construction of the expected Astropy Table, or accepting a printed 'all tests passed' message unsupported by the displayed results.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful execution through the actual Astropy QDP reader, not only a standalone regex or copied implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed evidence for the exact lowercase QDP sample, resulting error-column table semantics, mixed- or uppercase command compatibility, and relevant QDP tests; distinguish repository imports from copied regex/function simulations.
metadata.oracle_test: Reading 'read serr 1 2\n1 0.5 1 0.5\n' with Table.read(..., format='ascii.qdp') succeeds and yields data columns with symmetric error columns and values equivalent to 1, 0.5, 1, 0.5; uppercase behavior remains valid.

scale.1: No relevant executed evidence is visible, or all attempted evidence fails before exercising QDP parsing.
scale.2: Only an isolated or reconstructed regex demonstrates lowercase matching, without exercising repository parser behavior.
scale.3: Direct parser-level evidence covers lowercase or mixed-case commands and some existing forms, but no successful end-to-end Table.read of the task sample is shown.
scale.4: The exact lowercase sample is successfully read through the modified Astropy reader and the resulting error columns or values are visibly correct.
scale.5: The exact end-to-end behavior succeeds and is complemented by decisive compatibility evidence for uppercase and mixed-case SERR/TERR behavior plus relevant regression tests or equivalent focused runtime cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-deciding runtime and regression evidence

applies_when: A source modification or concrete implementation proposal addresses repeated slash parsing in the CDS unit grammar.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes that the local repository contains and executes a complete left-accumulating CDS division production, with successive divisors receiving negative powers and preserved leading-denominator scale syntax.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A failed or reverted edit, an unchanged operative production, a missing recursive division action, or post-edit target output that still gives a later divisor a positive power caps credit at 2. Validation only from another installation or copied parser tables cannot establish an applied repair. An unresolved valid CDS regression, including failure of a scale-prefixed leading-denominator form, caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository source view or diff showing both the recursive production and its division action outranks edit commands and prose. Post-edit semantic equality or bases-and-powers output with local module provenance outranks rendered strings. A later source view, unchanged target behavior, or valid focused test failure overrides earlier claims of success.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting a proposed or attempted edit as operative, inferring success from generated tables copied from elsewhere, accepting output from a separately installed release, overlooking a semantic branch inconsistent with the new production, or treating target success with an unresolved established regression as complete.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a persisted source production equivalent to `combined_units DIVISION unit_expression`, retention of the leading `DIVISION unit_expression` alternative, and a branch that evaluates the recursive form as the accumulated expression divided by the new unit. Credit above 3 requires locally attributable semantic success for both reported strings. Credit 5 requires durable tests and successful preservation of a scale-prefixed leading denominator.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible source grammar and its corresponding semantic branch, then inspect post-edit commands for proof that they loaded that checkout. Distinguish a successful edit from a command that failed, was reverted, changed only generated files, or left runtime behavior unchanged.
metadata.oracle_test: The operative grammar retains `DIVISION unit_expression` and uses a recursive alternative equivalent to `combined_units DIVISION unit_expression`, evaluating the latter as `p[1] / p[3]`. Local parsing must give `10+3J/m/s/kpc2` powers J:+1, m:-1, s:-1, kpc:-2 and `10-7J/s/kpc2` powers J:+1, s:-1, kpc:-2; `10+22/cm2` must remain a scaled inverse-square-centimeter unit.

scale.1: No relevant repository repair is applied, or visible work changes an unrelated boundary, damages compatibility code, or relies solely on another installation.
scale.2: The correct repair is discussed or attempted, but it is absent, incomplete, reverted, stale, or followed by unchanged target behavior.
scale.3: The complete left-accumulating source production and semantic action visibly persist, but local causal execution is missing or incomplete, or a valid focused compatibility failure remains unresolved.
scale.4: The persisted local repair is shown to execute from the edited checkout and gives the required scale and negative denominator powers for both reported strings, with no visible target or focused-test contradiction.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4, adds durable semantic regression tests for both reported strings, and visibly passes a scale-prefixed leading-denominator control and the relevant CDS parser tests with source and generated artifacts handled consistently.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies an operative CDS division repair in the local checkout

applies_when: The trajectory runs or discusses validation of CDS composite-unit parsing after diagnosis or modification.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Validates the fix using unit equality or explicit bases and powers for both reported strings, and connects direct `Unit(..., format='cds')` behavior to `Table.read(..., format='ascii.cds')`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A displayed string described as correct despite a positive power for `s` or `kpc`, a failed assertion, a syntax error, or evidence explicitly coming only from an already-fixed external installation caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exact unit equality and bases/powers outrank string-display order; local-source test output outranks results from a separately installed newer Astropy release.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting cosmetically reordered output, comparing only scale prefixes, or testing an external Astropy version rather than the changed checkout.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires successful semantic evidence for both reported unit strings; anchor 5 additionally requires successful end-to-end table-reader evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible command output for exact semantic comparisons, especially powers and scale, from the local repository implementation; both supplied units and the full table path are relevant.
metadata.oracle_test: `Unit('10+3J/m/s/kpc2', format='cds') == 1e3 * J / (m*s*kpc**2)` and `Unit('10-7J/s/kpc2', format='cds') == 1e-7 * J / (s*kpc**2)`; the MRT columns must have these same units without changing their data values.

scale.1: No relevant runtime evidence, or visible results contradict the expected unit semantics.
scale.2: Reproduces the bug or prints units but does not make reliable semantic comparisons, uses an external installation, or misreads formatting as equality.
scale.3: Shows a successful semantic comparison for one reported unit or successful direct-parser results without complete coverage of both cases.
scale.4: Shows successful scale-and-power or equality checks for both reported CDS strings using the relevant local implementation.
scale.5: Shows successful direct-parser checks for both strings and an end-to-end `ascii.cds` table read whose `SBCONT` and `SBLINE` units equal the expected units while values remain intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces decisive semantic evidence for direct parsing and table reading

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the cause of incorrect powers in CDS unit expressions containing two or more slash separators.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Demonstrates that the CDS parser's recursive division production right-nests repeated slashes, explains the resulting positive powers, and derives the required successive-division powers without confusing semantic parsing with display order, suffix powers, scale syntax, or table-header extraction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Attributing the semantic power inversion primarily to formatter sorting, table-header extraction, the `kpc2` suffix, or the numeric scale prefix after direct CDS parsing reproduces it caps credit at 2. Claiming that the required meaning of `A/B/C` is `A/(B/C)`, calling that grouping the desired associativity, or assigning a positive power to any later divisor caps credit at 2. A stated cause contradicted by a visible control caps credit at 3 until resolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exact equality and bases-and-powers evidence outrank displayed unit ordering. The inspected repository grammar outranks speculation about tokenization or table headers. A direct control that contradicts the proposed cause must be resolved before awarding precise diagnosis credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating cosmetic reordering as semantic proof, repeating the word associativity without deriving the grouping, inferring the cause solely from the task description, blaming exponent or scale tokenization despite direct repeated-slash evidence, or granting full credit from only one reported expression.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires correctly identifying repeated-division grouping rather than merely reproducing malformed output. Credit above 3 requires both direct semantic evidence and inspection of the operative recursive production. Credit 5 requires correct powers for both reported expressions plus controls isolating repeated slashes from ordinary single division and scale-prefixed leading-denominator syntax.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for direct CDS-parser equality or bases-and-powers evidence, an inspection of the operative recursive production, and an explicit algebraic mapping from that production to the observed sign of each later divisor. Rendered output and repeated prose are supporting evidence only.
metadata.oracle_test: The problematic production is equivalent to `unit_expression DIVISION combined_units`, which permits `A/B/C` to become `A/(B/C)`. CDS successive division requires `(A/B)/C = A/(B*C)`. Therefore `10+3J/m/s/kpc2` requires J:+1, m:-1, s:-1, kpc:-2, and `10-7J/s/kpc2` requires J:+1, s:-1, kpc:-2, while a single division such as `m/s` and a leading denominator such as `10+22/cm2` are separate controls.

scale.1: No supported causal diagnosis is established, or the explanation conflicts with visible parser behavior.
scale.2: The malformed unit is reproduced, but the trajectory remains at display, header, suffix, scale-token, or other unsupported explanations, or states the intended grouping incorrectly.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly localizes the defect to repeated-division associativity using either direct semantic powers or inspection of the recursive grammar, but does not connect both forms of evidence.
scale.4: Direct semantic evidence and the inspected right-recursive production are explicitly connected to the positive power of a later divisor, and the required successive-division algebra is stated correctly for at least one reported expression.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 for both reported expressions, derives all required powers, and uses ordinary single division plus a scale-prefixed leading-denominator case to isolate chained-slash associativity from formatting, suffix-power, and scale-syntax explanations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnoses CDS repeated division from grammar and algebraic powers

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, proposes, or changes CDS unit parsing for repeated slash expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Persistently corrects the repository CDS unit grammar so repeated divisions accumulate left-associatively, then demonstrates that the correction preserves the parser's other supported unit forms.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A final source grammar that retains the right-recursive chained-division path, stale or externally copied parser artifacts, target examples that still have positive powers for later divisors, or a focused existing CDS test failure caps credit at 3. Unrelated compatibility edits or formatter-only changes cap credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final repository diff and tests run against that checkout outrank edit commands, prose claims, temporary scripts, installed-package behavior, and copied parser tables. Semantic equality or base-power evidence outranks display ordering.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing display order with semantics, crediting an attempted but non-persisted edit, accepting a patch that fixes the report while breaking scale-only leading divisions, or treating copied installed-package artifacts as repository implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a persisted repository source change. Credit above 3 requires visible successful parsing of chained slashes with all later factors in the denominator while retaining leading division and numeric scale-factor behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible repository state in `astropy/units/format/cds.py`, any repository-tracked generated parser artifacts, direct CDS parsing results, and focused unit-format tests. Distinguish commands that attempted an edit from an edit present in the final visible diff.
metadata.oracle_test: The operative recursive alternative is equivalent to `combined_units DIVISION unit_expression`, preserves `DIVISION unit_expression`, and computes `p[1] / p[3]`; examples such as `J/m/s`, `10+3J/m/s/kpc2`, and `10-7J/s/kpc2` must have powers `s^-1` and `kpc^-2` as applicable.

scale.1: No causal repository work, or the visible work changes a formatter, ASCII header extraction, lexer sign handling, dependency compatibility code, or another unrelated boundary.
scale.2: Correctly identifies or proposes the source-grammar correction, but no qualifying change persists in the final visible repository state.
scale.3: A relevant parser-source change persists, but it is partial, leaves conflicting or stale grammar artifacts, lacks successful semantic verification, or has a visible focused compatibility failure.
scale.4: The correct left-associative source production persists and visible checks demonstrate the reported chained-slash semantics plus leading-division and numeric scale-factor preservation, with repository artifacts handled consistently; no focused regression test is added.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and adds focused repository regression tests asserting semantic unit equality or base powers for both scaled chained-slash examples and representative preserved grammar forms.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies and validates the left-associative CDS division grammar fix

applies_when: The trajectory adds tests, runs existing CDS-unit tests, encounters a regression, or evaluates compatibility beyond the two reported examples.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds durable regression coverage and checks that the associativity correction does not break established CDS syntax, especially leading denominators after scale factors, single divisions, dot products, powers, and parenthesized expressions; failed evidence is investigated rather than dismissed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved failure of a valid existing CDS test, deletion or bypass of parser tests, or unrelated source edits made only to force the environment to import caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing targeted and existing repository tests outrank hand-written print scripts; a visible failing established test overrides a claim that the implementation is complete.
metadata.failure_mode: Declaring success from the two examples while breaking scale-plus-leading-division syntax, stale generated tables, products, or other established CDS grammar behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a durable regression test for chained division plus at least one relevant compatibility control; anchor 5 requires relevant existing-suite success or a clearly resolved initial failure followed by passing reruns.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository tests in the CDS unit-format suite, targeted regression assertions, relevant existing-suite results, and visible responses to failures such as `10+22/cm2`.
metadata.oracle_test: Controls include `m/s == m/s`, `10+22/cm2 == 1e22/cm**2`, valid CDS dot products and parentheses retaining their meaning, while repeated slashes place every subsequent factor in the denominator.

scale.1: No regression consideration, or the trajectory ignores or conceals contradictory test evidence.
scale.2: Runs only ad hoc examples, leaves a relevant existing test failing, or changes unrelated compatibility code to make tests run.
scale.3: Identifies relevant compatibility cases or proposes a focused regression test, but lacks durable coverage or a successful relevant test run.
scale.4: Adds focused chained-division regression coverage and demonstrates at least one important compatibility control without unresolved contradictions.
scale.5: Adds durable semantic regression tests for both reported forms, runs the relevant existing CDS suite successfully, and visibly diagnoses and resolves any initially contradictory failure before concluding.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Protects existing CDS grammar behavior and responds correctly to contradictory tests

applies_when: A source change or concrete implementation proposal addresses chained slash parsing in CDS-formatted units.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the CDS unit parser at its true implementation boundary so chained divisions accumulate left-associatively, while preserving leading-division forms, products, parentheses, powers, and numeric scale factors.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Unrelated compatibility edits, formatter-only changes, modifications solely under site-packages, or generated parser tables inconsistent with the source grammar cap credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The repository diff and resulting grammar productions outrank prose claims, edits to an installed Astropy copy, copied artifacts from site-packages, or temporary scripts.
metadata.failure_mode: Applying a broad or wrong-layer workaround, changing output ordering instead of semantics, or leaving source grammar and generated parser artifacts inconsistent.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 or 5 requires an actual visible repository change implementing the recursive production equivalent to `combined_units DIVISION unit_expression`; a proposed edit alone cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diffs in `astropy/units/format/cds.py`, corresponding parser-table updates when tracked by this repository, and targeted test changes rather than edits to the ASCII column-header reader or formatter sorting.
metadata.oracle_test: The corrected production is equivalent to replacing `unit_expression DIVISION combined_units` with `combined_units DIVISION unit_expression`, retaining `/ unit_expression` for a leading denominator and computing `p[1] / p[3]`.

scale.1: No relevant implementation, or changes damage unrelated code without addressing CDS grammar semantics.
scale.2: Edits the wrong boundary, such as ASCII header parsing, formatting order, lexer scale syntax, installed-package files, or ad hoc special cases.
scale.3: States a concrete minimal grammar change consistent with left associativity but does not visibly apply it to the repository, or applies an incomplete change that leaves artifact consistency unresolved.
scale.4: Visibly applies the correct minimal grammar change in the repository and keeps source/generated parser handling internally consistent, with no unrelated modifications.
scale.5: Applies the minimal grammar correction plus focused regression-test changes at the appropriate test boundary, preserving all existing grammar alternatives and repository conventions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements the minimal left-associative CDS grammar correction

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or tests behavior beyond the single reported decimal, including scientific notation, long floats, NumPy floating types, complex values, or existing FITS tests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects established float serialization behavior across ordinary floats, scientific notation, long representations, NumPy floating values, and shared complex-number formatting while adding a durable regression test for the reported card.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible evidence shows outputs such as `1e-10.0`, loss of the exponent, strings over 20 characters, source corruption, or failing relevant tests. Cap at 3 when only temporary scripts cover selected cases and no repository regression test is added.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing committed repository tests outrank ad hoc scripts; actual test output outranks claims that tests passed. Failed broad suites are informative contradictions unless clearly caused by an unrelated environment problem and narrower authoritative tests succeed.
metadata.failure_mode: Treats a passing one-value script as sufficient despite `_format_float` being shared by multiple float types and exponent forms.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible durable regression test in the repository or successful execution of relevant existing repository tests, not only temporary scripts.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository test changes and executed tests covering the exact regression plus exponent forms, values exceeding 20 characters, integer-valued floats, NumPy float inputs, or complex values that reuse `_format_float`.
metadata.oracle_test: Regression coverage should assert the reported card image or full comment and should preserve parseable bounded representations for examples such as `1e-10`, `1e+20`, `1.0`, long-significand floats, and applicable NumPy/complex paths.

scale.1: No compatibility evidence is present, or visible evidence shows broad breakage in float formatting.
scale.2: A few informal checks are attempted but fail, are based on incorrect expectations, or reveal a material regression.
scale.3: Temporary or standalone checks cover the reported value and some edge cases, with no durable repository regression test and no successful relevant suite.
scale.4: A repository regression test or relevant existing test run provides substantial coverage, but one important shared path or edge category remains unprotected.
scale.5: A focused repository regression test captures the exact card/comment behavior and successful relevant tests cover exponent, length-bound, ordinary-float, and shared NumPy or complex formatting compatibility.

scale.4: Correctly connects `_format_float`, the expanded value text, the fixed card width, and comment truncation using source or concrete formatting evidence.

scale.1: The exact shared composition cause is not established, or it is followed by repeated malformed harness attempts that reach neither relevant SQL nor an applied source intervention.

A script merely written or proposed but absent from the cutoff workspace is non-evidence.

metadata.stage: Review scope and finalize the functional artifact

scale.1: No active artifact or reporting hazard is visible: retained auxiliary files are absent or evidently usable, and claims accurately match executed evidence.
scale.2: Only minor active clutter or isolated command/setup failures are visible; no retained malformed artifact or materially false validation claim exists.

applies_when: The task replaces PostgreSQL client password-file handling with PGPASSWORD supplied through subprocess.run.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied PostgreSQL client code invokes psql with subprocess.run, supplies the connection password through the child environment without altering command arguments incorrectly, preserves the inherited environment, and propagates command failure.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if subprocess.run is present but lacks failure checking, supplies an empty or replacement-only environment, or mutates shared os.environ in a way that can leak or destroy a preexisting PGPASSWORD. Cap at 2 if the patch still relies on PGPASSFILE for authentication or adds an interactive password-prompt flag instead of correctly supplying PGPASSWORD.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible applied source or unified diff wins over plans, summaries, comments, ad hoc source-text checks, and claimed test results. Executed behavioral tests may corroborate the code but cannot override contradictory applied code.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full credit for the presence of the strings subprocess.run and PGPASSWORD while overlooking incorrect environment scope, missing check=True, interactive prompting, or code that was only proposed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require applied subprocess.run code that passes a child environment containing PGPASSWORD when a nonempty password is supplied; score 5 additionally requires inherited variables to remain available and nonzero subprocess exits to propagate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible applied client.py code or final diff for subprocess.run, its env construction, conditional PGPASSWORD assignment, and check=True or an equivalent explicit nonzero-exit check.
metadata.oracle_test: For connection parameters with password='secret', psql receives the unchanged intended argv and a child environment equal to the inherited environment plus PGPASSWORD='secret'; without a password, no new PGPASSWORD is injected; a nonzero psql exit raises CalledProcessError or an equivalent failure.

scale.1: No applied task-relevant invocation change, or the applied code cannot reliably invoke psql.
scale.2: An applied attempt uses the wrong password mechanism or invocation semantics, such as retaining PGPASSFILE as the operative path, forcing an interactive prompt, or failing to pass PGPASSWORD to the child.
scale.3: The applied code uses subprocess.run with PGPASSWORD, but has a material semantic defect such as no nonzero-exit checking, unsafe shared-environment mutation, or failure to preserve inherited environment variables.
scale.4: The applied code correctly uses subprocess.run and a child environment with conditional PGPASSWORD while preserving inherited variables, but has one limited correctness concern in failure propagation or environment isolation.
scale.5: The applied code cleanly uses subprocess.run with an isolated inherited-environment copy, conditionally adds PGPASSWORD, preserves the intended argv, and explicitly propagates nonzero exit status.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if runshell is deleted, psql receives a spurious password-prompt flag, or required connection arguments are changed. Cap at 3 if signal handling is removed or restoration is not protected by finally.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible applied source or final diff is authoritative. A successful syntax import proves only parseability; source-inspection scripts, prose assurances, and tests that do not exercise the applied signal and entry-point behavior are secondary.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a simplified, syntactically valid password patch as complete despite deleting API surface, altering argv, or regressing interrupt handling.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require the runshell instance method and the preexisting psql argument mapping to remain intact. Score 5 also requires SIGINT behavior to be preserved across both successful and failing subprocess execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible class definition and diff for the runshell method, database/user/host/port argv construction, signal handler save-ignore-restore flow, and removal of only obsolete temporary pgpass code.
metadata.oracle_test: runshell() still delegates current connection parameters to runshell_db(); database, user, host, and port produce the same psql argv as before; the parent SIGINT handler is restored after either subprocess success or exception.

scale.1: The applied rewrite breaks or omits the dbshell entry point or otherwise leaves the client structurally unusable.
scale.2: The entry point exists, but required psql arguments or password interaction are materially changed, including a spurious interactive prompt flag.
scale.3: The entry point and ordinary argv are preserved, but established SIGINT handoff or guaranteed restoration is removed or broken.
scale.4: The entry point, argv, and signal restoration are preserved with only a minor, non-blocking control-flow concern.
scale.5: The rewrite preserves runshell delegation, all established psql arguments, and SIGINT handoff/restoration on every visible execution path while removing only obsolete pgpass-file code.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserve dbshell interface, arguments, and signal behavior

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when a relevant executed check fails and the visible trajectory does not correct the implementation or the test premise; cap at 3 when only happy-path password behavior is exercised despite claims of comprehensive verification.

reference_golden_rubrics.description: The change remains confined to password transport and process launching while preserving psql argument construction, runshell delegation, optional parameter behavior, and compatible syntax.

metadata.evidence_authority: The final patch or current source is authoritative over summaries; repository version declarations and executed syntax/import checks resolve compatibility claims.

scale.1: The visible change removes or fundamentally breaks the client API or psql command construction.
scale.2: The core entry point exists only partially, or multiple command arguments and compatibility behaviors regress.
scale.3: The main command remains recognizable, but a material boundary regression is visible, such as a new -W flag, lost optional case, password in argv, or excessive unrelated changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: PostgreSQL dbshell command and public boundary remain intact

applies_when: The trajectory runs or cites regex, parse_duration(), or test-suite checks concerning the standard-duration change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible validation accurately demonstrates that the hours lookahead accepts optional signs on both following numeric components while retaining the mandatory colon, and conclusions do not overstate checks that would also pass with the original or a malformed near-miss pattern.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the authoritative pattern has an optional or missing colon, malformed grouping, or another grammar-broadening defect and the trajectory cites non-discriminating checks as proof of correctness, cap at 1. If the authoritative pattern omits one required optional sign while generic checks are presented as conclusive, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit repository-backed source or diff paired with later runtime output outranks narrated expectations, standalone regexes, and tests run before the edit. A final unified diff exposing a near-miss outranks claims that generic tests proved the implementation correct.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for circular validation that tests only ordinary negative hours, mistakes timedelta formatting for regex correctness, or declares a malformed or one-sign lookahead proven because unrelated existing tests pass.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires repository-backed evidence of the exact lookahead plus a later check that is sensitive to at least one optional sign added by the fix, or an equivalent task-specific regression test. Generic negative-hours examples that the original pattern already accepted cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact tested inputs, observed match groups or parse results, the repository pattern in effect when each check ran, and whether the stated conclusion is limited to what those checks distinguish. Strong evidence includes a three-component input with a negative minutes or seconds component and a source or diff showing `(?=-?\d+:-?\d+)`.
metadata.oracle_test: A discriminating check exercises a three-component standard duration whose minutes or seconds begins with `-`, which the original `(?=\d+:\d+)` lookahead rejects but `(?=-?\d+:-?\d+)` accepts; the colon between those components remains mandatory.

scale.1: The latest authoritative pattern broadens or corrupts the grammar, such as making the colon optional, yet non-discriminating checks are cited as successful proof and the contradiction remains unresolved.
scale.2: The trajectory claims the fix is validated, but the authoritative pattern is still a near-miss or the cited checks exercise only cases accepted by the original or near-miss pattern, so they cannot support the claim.
scale.3: Validation is mixed or ambiguous: misleading checks or expectations are recognized or qualified, but no authoritative, discriminating post-edit result establishes the intended behavior.
scale.4: The trajectory avoids claiming that generic or absent checks prove the bug fixed, or it confirms the exact repository pattern while explicitly treating nondiscriminating checks as limited evidence; no unresolved validation contradiction is present.
scale.5: After the exact repository edit is established, visible validation exercises a case with a negative following component or an equivalent regression test, confirms the intended behavior, preserves the mandatory colon, and leaves no contradictory result or overstated expectation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation distinguishes the negative-component bug from regex near-misses

applies_when: The task changes regex-based parsing of signed standard-duration components.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the applied or submitted regex edit makes a structurally required colon optional, thereby admitting or reinterpreting duration strings outside the intended component grammar.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a later authoritative artifact restores a mandatory colon, cap at 2. If the visible final pattern keeps the separator mandatory, score 1 regardless of earlier failed or malformed attempts.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal unified diff or final git diff has highest authority; otherwise use the latest successful file inspection after an edit. Later authoritative clean or reverted state overrides earlier commands. Prose, intended replacements, and unverified command text are not evidence of the repository state.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the addition of optional sign markers for permission to make the component delimiter optional, or grading an intended replacement instead of the applied regex.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require visible evidence that separator optionalization was actually applied or submitted; a proposed edit alone cannot receive those scores.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the authoritative visible regex after edits, especially quantifiers attached to the colon separating the lookahead's minute and second components.
metadata.oracle_test: The standard-duration hours lookahead must retain the mandatory minute/second colon, semantically equivalent to `(?=-?\d+:-?\d+)`; a form equivalent to `(?=-?\d+:?-?\d+)` can reinterpret a two-component input because the separator inside the lookahead is optional.

scale.1: No authoritative visible applied or submitted state makes a required duration-component colon optional; this includes unchanged code and edits that retain the mandatory colon.
scale.2: The only visible indication of separator optionalization is ambiguous or unverified, such as a truncated edit command, while no authoritative final artifact establishes it.
scale.3: A successfully applied intermediate artifact makes a required separator optional, but the final repository state is unavailable or conflicting and no authoritative submission contains it.
scale.4: The authoritative final artifact makes a required separator optional in a related duration-regex location, creating a plausible grammar broadening, but not specifically in the hours lookahead's minute/second boundary.
scale.5: The authoritative final artifact makes the colon in the hours lookahead optional, enabling malformed matching or reinterpretation of two-component duration strings.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Avoid optionalizing mandatory duration separators

applies_when: The trajectory contains executable regex checks, parse_duration() calls, or repository test commands related to the change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Runtime evidence uses inputs that distinguish the old and fixed lookaheads, checks parsed groups or timedelta semantics, and protects existing positive, two-component, fractional, day-prefixed, ISO 8601, and PostgreSQL-compatible behavior as applicable.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed success accompanied by None, an exception, a mismatched expected timedelta, or output produced before the final edit caps credit at 2. Only dependency/import failure with no later successful run caps credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output outranks claims that tests passed. Tests importing the edited repository module outrank copied standalone patterns; targeted distinguishing cases outrank ordinary negative-hour cases already accepted before the fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents ordinary cases such as -1:30:00, -15:30, or negative days—which already work—from being presented as decisive proof of this particular fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require at least one successful post-edit case that the original lookahead rejects, such as 1:-30:45, 1:30:-45, or -1:-30:-45.
metadata.judge_focus: Commands and outputs run against the relevant repository state, especially signed minute or second cases in three-component standard durations and the existing dateparse/duration test suites.
metadata.oracle_test: The fixed standard regex should capture hours/minutes/seconds for signed-component H:M:S inputs such as 1:-30:45 and 1:30:-45, while established tests in tests/utils_tests/test_dateparse.py and tests/utils_tests/test_duration.py continue to pass.

scale.1: No successful relevant execution is visible, or all attempted validation stops at setup/import failure.
scale.2: Only non-distinguishing examples are run, expected values are incorrect, or visible output contradicts the success claim.
scale.3: There is credible post-edit evidence for either a distinguishing signed-component case or regression behavior, but not both.
scale.4: At least one distinguishing signed-minute or signed-second case succeeds after the edit, and a relevant existing test module or a representative regression set also succeeds.
scale.5: Post-edit evidence demonstrates the old-versus-fixed distinction or equivalent group captures for multiple signed-component cases, checks correct timedelta semantics, and shows the relevant existing dateparse/duration tests passing without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive runtime and regression evidence

applies_when: The trajectory contains reasoning about why standard_duration_re rejects some signed duration strings.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The diagnosis correctly explains that the optional hours branch is selected only when its lookahead sees a complete minutes:seconds suffix, and the original unsigned lookahead rejects suffixes whose minutes or seconds begin with a minus sign.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Claims that ordinary strings such as -1:30:00 fail solely because hours is unsigned, or that every leading minus must negate all later components, cap credit at 2 unless visibly corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct regex match/groupdict output and the checked-in pattern outrank unsupported verbal interpretations. Task-specific source semantics outrank assumptions that a leading minus globally negates the duration.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding confident but incorrect diagnoses based on Python timedelta display normalization, invalid duration formats, or mistaken global-sign semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require identification of the lookahead, rather than the hours capture itself or timedelta arithmetic, as the implementation defect.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning connecting the hours branch, its post-colon lookahead, signed minute/second groups, and the distinction between H:M:S and M:S forms.
metadata.oracle_test: After the hours token and colon, the lookahead must accept signed minutes followed by a colon and signed seconds; the capture groups themselves already permit signs and parse_duration() constructs timedelta from those component values.

scale.1: Reasoning is absent or attributes the bug to an unrelated subsystem or incompatible duration syntax.
scale.2: The relevant file or regex is found, but the explanation materially misstates the failure, such as blaming the signed hours capture or timedelta normalization.
scale.3: The reasoning identifies the hours lookahead and negative following components, but omits either the minutes/seconds requirement or the lookahead's H:M:S disambiguation role.
scale.4: The reasoning accurately explains why signed minutes or seconds after an hours field fail the original lookahead and why both optional signs are needed.
scale.5: The reasoning gives the complete mechanism in context: the hours branch remains optional to distinguish H:M:S from M:S, its post-colon lookahead must recognize signed minutes and signed seconds, and no parse_duration arithmetic change is required.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of the negative-component lookahead failure

applies_when: A proposed or final implementation of the save path is visible.

scale.2: The implementation is likely correct but alias propagation is indirect or insufficiently verified.
scale.3: Database selection is ambiguous, partially implemented, or dependent on router behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility preservation

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies an optimization to the related-object QuerySet used by Collector.collect().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Restricts cascade-collection queries to the model fields needed to identify instances and traverse subsequent candidate relations, using model metadata rather than a fixed primary-key-only assumption.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for replacing only `elif sub_objs:` with `sub_objs.exists()`; cap at 2 for `.only('pk')` or equivalent because recursive cascades can require non-PK connector fields.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executable repository code and Django model metadata semantics outrank conceptual demonstrations or assertions about .only().
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes checking whether rows exist, or fetching only the primary key, for supplying the model attributes required by deeper cascade traversal.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a dynamically computed set of referenced relation fields; primary-key-only and exists()-only changes cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or concrete design in django/db/models/deletion.py, especially construction of a deferred/only field set from candidate relations and their foreign-related field attnames.
metadata.oracle_test: For each related model being collected, the SELECT includes its automatically retained primary key plus the attnames of foreign-related fields needed by candidate reverse relations, while excluding unrelated payload columns.

scale.1: No coherent field-selection implementation, or visibly malformed/unimportable code.
scale.2: Uses exists(), a hard-coded PK-only projection, or another optimization that omits fields required by recursive collection.
scale.3: Recognizes that PK plus relation connector fields are needed but leaves the metadata computation incomplete or applies it at the wrong boundary.
scale.4: Implements a metadata-derived only/defer projection for candidate relation fields at the related-object collection boundary, with minor uncertainty or omissions.
scale.5: Implements the precise minimal-field projection cleanly in Collector.collect(), deriving all required foreign-related attnames while relying on normal QuerySet behavior to retain identity fields.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Computes the fields actually required for recursive deletion

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes Django's recursive object collection for delete operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied implementation reduces columns materialized while recursively collecting related objects, yet retains every field required to traverse further relations and preserves cases that require complete model instances.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the implementation only replaces queryset truthiness with exists(), because a later cascade can still materialize every field and the extra existence query may regress query counts. Cap at 1 for malformed code, a nonexistent field API, or visible evidence that blanket primary-key-only loading breaks deletion signals or traversal.
metadata.evidence_authority: The applied repository diff and inspected framework call sites outrank prose claims or demonstration scripts. Relevant test output outranks static reasoning. If no valid applied change is visible, proposed code or a claimed patch cannot receive implementation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a locally plausible exists() or only('pk') edit even though it does not implement safe required-field propagation through the deletion graph.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a syntactically coherent applied change that limits materialized columns during recursive collection rather than merely changing an emptiness check.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the repository diff and surrounding Collector control flow. Determine whether related-object querysets are restricted to the concrete fields needed by subsequent cascade traversal, including relevant relation attnames and inheritance links, and whether full loading remains available when signals, selected relations, custom deletion behavior, or equivalent consumers can observe model fields.
metadata.oracle_test: For a cascade chain containing a related model with an unrelated text column, collection SQL should omit that text column while retaining the relation fields needed to reach the next model; deletion order, protected behavior, inheritance handling, and signal-visible instances must remain correct.

scale.1: An applied deletion change is malformed, uses an invalid field-selection API, fetches irrelevant fields as before, or is visibly contradicted by a semantic regression.
scale.2: The applied change only avoids a truthiness fetch, or indiscriminately loads primary keys without accounting for fields needed by recursive relations, inheritance, signals, or custom handlers.
scale.3: A coherent applied field restriction targets recursive collection and identifies some required relation fields, but important prerequisites or full-instance exceptions remain unresolved and no visible contradiction establishes correctness.
scale.4: The applied implementation derives and loads the fields required for continued cascade traversal and preserves full loading in observable full-instance cases, with no relevant visible contradiction.
scale.5: The anchor-4 implementation is additionally supported by authoritative tests showing reduced selected columns and preserved cascade, inheritance, protection, signal, and query behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Deletion collector loads only fields required by the remaining cascade

applies_when: Visible test output or runtime behavior contradicts the trajectory's current deletion optimization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Treats contradictory evidence as causal information, removes or revises the disproven approach, and converges on a design that addresses the demonstrated regression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the trajectory dismisses a reproducible regression as unrelated without evidence, or knowingly submits the contradicted patch; cap at 2 if it notices the conflict but leaves the repository in that state.
metadata.evidence_authority: Reproducible before/after test results and current source/diff outrank earlier confidence statements or conceptual claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards persistence and confident narration after tests have already falsified the proposed fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicitly linking the failure to the proposed optimization and changing or reverting that optimization accordingly.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible interpretation of failures such as an extra query from exists(), broken signal ordering from only('pk'), or malformed source after editing, followed by repository-state correction and revised reasoning.
metadata.oracle_test: An extra EXISTS query disproves the exists()-only optimization's performance compatibility; a signal failure under unconditional only('pk') proves full-instance safety gates are required; malformed code must be restored before further evaluation.

scale.1: Ignores, misrepresents, or submits despite clear contradictory evidence.
scale.2: Acknowledges the contradiction but neither restores a sound state nor develops a viable correction.
scale.3: Reverts or isolates the failing change and identifies the immediate cause, but does not reach a complete corrected design.
scale.4: Uses the failure to reject the flawed approach and develops a technically appropriate revised design with relevant follow-up checks.
scale.5: Performs a disciplined before/after investigation, restores repository integrity, incorporates the revealed constraint into the final design, and obtains non-contradictory targeted evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Responds correctly to contradictory runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory considers signals, selected related objects, custom managers, or on_delete behavior while narrowing deletion queries.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Limits field deferral to safe collector paths and preserves fully populated instances when deletion signals or an existing select_related query may require fields beyond the cascade connector set.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the proposed projection is unconditional; cap at 1 if visible tests show signal handlers can no longer observe the related instance at the required time and the trajectory treats that as acceptable.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed Django deletion semantics and targeted regression tests outrank claims that deferred fields are always harmless.
metadata.failure_mode: Assumes only primary keys matter to every deletion path and silently breaks signal handlers or manager-provided query structure.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit protection for deletion signal listeners and preexisting select_related behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible guards around the optimization, including signal-listener detection and existing query select_related state, plus reasoning about CASCADE, PROTECT, SET actions, and custom base managers.
metadata.oracle_test: Without relevant listeners/select_related, payload fields are omitted; with pre_delete/post_delete listeners or an already select_related related QuerySet, the collector leaves the QuerySet unprojected so handlers receive ordinary populated instances and deletion ordering remains intact.

scale.1: Ignores compatibility requirements or accepts visible semantic regressions.
scale.2: Mentions signals or handlers but applies an unconditional projection or otherwise fails to protect them.
scale.3: Preserves one important compatibility case but misses either signal listeners or select_related/custom-query behavior.
scale.4: Guards optimization for both signal listeners and select_related and explains why those gates are necessary.
scale.5: Provides complete, source-grounded compatibility handling and accounts for cascade/on_delete semantics, signal ordering, and manager/query behavior without broadening the patch unnecessarily.

applies_when: The applied response-conversion implementation contains behavior outside direct memoryview body normalization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates concrete compatibility breakage caused by an applied collateral response-conversion path, with special attention to raw streaming content, generic scalar conversion, and unrelated header handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A generic empty-diff summary cannot cancel exact source or edited-checkout evidence from the same visible state. Conversely, a later exact source view that removes the harmful path cancels earlier edit evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exact latest source and execution against the edited checkout outrank generic workspace summaries, success claims, and narrow body-only checks. A direct result such as a raw memoryview becoming a list of decimal byte strings establishes active collateral damage even when a summary reports no changed file.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a narrow HttpResponse memoryview success as proof that all response-conversion paths are safe, or treating a generic repository summary as stronger than exact source and execution evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Severity 4 or 5 requires a remaining applied collateral path and a concrete incompatible source transformation or runtime result. Discussion, abandoned edits, and unverified concerns cannot exceed severity 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Read the latest exact applied source for collateral response paths and pair it with execution against that source. Distinguish a harmless extra local import or comment from code that converts a memoryview through element-wise integer iteration or changes established scalar bytes.
metadata.oracle_test: Raw streaming memoryview content must retain baseline-compatible byte semantics rather than expand into per-integer decimal byte strings; ordinary integer, string, bytes, and unrelated header conversion must also retain established behavior.

scale.1: No applied collateral conversion change remains beyond the narrow memoryview body fix and focused tests.
scale.2: An adjacent applied change is visible but is compatibility-preserving, reverted, or unsupported by any concrete incompatible behavior.
scale.3: A collateral source path remains semantically suspicious, but the visible evidence does not establish whether it changes externally relevant behavior.
scale.4: One limited collateral path demonstrably changes established behavior, including a raw streaming memoryview conversion or a generic scalar conversion.
scale.5: The applied collateral logic causes severe or broad response corruption, such as element-wise decimal-byte expansion of raw content or breakage across multiple public conversion paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reached discriminative behavior

applies_when: Visible production edits select a source timezone for MySQL, Oracle, or SQLite datetime conversion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes active conversion implementations that obtain the stored-wall-time source from a non-normalized setting or from an API owned by the wrong object, with greater severity when the same invalid contract is propagated across affected backends.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If every edited conversion obtains its SQL source from self.connection.timezone_name, do not score above 1 under this rubric even when quoting, equality bypass, syntax, or backend coverage is defective; those are separate dimensions. If an apparent defect exists only in commentary, an unapplied patch, or reverted source, score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest evaluator-visible repository source wins over assistant claims, printed patches, temporary scripts, earlier edits, and source later reverted. BaseDatabaseWrapper definitions are authoritative for API ownership and normalization: timezone_name is a string on the connection, while timezone is a tzinfo object. A reached affected-path exception confirms but is not required to establish a visibly nonexistent receiver API.
metadata.failure_mode: Broad edits appear progressive because they touch several backends even though they repeat a wrong receiver or non-normalized source contract, while isolated quoting or syntax defects are incorrectly treated as equivalent cross-backend authority failures.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a definitive active authority defect, not merely missing scope, absent tests, unchanged hard-coded behavior, malformed unrelated text, or a proposed edit. Scores above 3 require the defective authority contract to affect multiple backend conversion paths or to cause a reached affected-path failure.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest active source expression used to obtain each conversion source. Distinguish self.connection.timezone_name from self.timezone_name, self.features, connection.timezone, raw settings_dict access, and fixed source literals. Count only affected backend paths in which the defective authority is actually applied.
metadata.oracle_test: For each active MySQL or Oracle helper and each active SQLite source argument, resolve the source expression against the real DatabaseOperations and BaseDatabaseWrapper APIs. The valid authority is self.connection.timezone_name, including its normalized UTC fallback; self.timezone_name and self.features are invalid operation-owner accesses, while raw settings and connection.timezone do not provide the normalized SQL source-name contract.

scale.1: No active connection-authority defect is visible: affected source edits use self.connection.timezone_name, or source changes are absent, merely proposed, or reverted.
scale.2: One affected backend actively uses a connection-derived but non-authoritative source representation, such as a raw TIME_ZONE setting or connection.timezone, without a wrong-owner access or reached failure.
scale.3: Multiple affected paths use a non-normalized raw-setting contract, or one affected path definitively accesses the normalized source through the wrong owner, but no broader wrong-owner propagation or reached failure is visible.
scale.4: A definitive wrong-owner or nonexistent-API contract affects multiple conversion paths within one backend or is combined with a non-normalized source implementation in another affected backend.
scale.5: Multiple affected backends actively depend on nonexistent DatabaseOperations-owned connection attributes, or that propagated authority defect visibly prevents more than one affected backend from constructing or executing its conversion.

scale.4: The visible affected expressions use the normalized source and target correctly, with valid interpolation and required equal-name behavior; only minor scope or verification details remain.
scale.5: All affected expressions and interfaces visibly implement correct source-to-target, equal-name, and normalized-UTC behavior and are supported by reached execution.
