applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an automatically created ManyToManyField intermediary inline is editable for a user with view-only permission.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Consistently identifies the auto-created InlineModelAdmin mutation-permission delegation as the cause of view-authorized relationship editing and distinguishes target-object visibility from authority to mutate the relationship.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 when later visible code uses target add/delete permissions despite an earlier target-change diagnosis. Cap at 2 when later work uses parent-model permission, through-model permission, admin registration, or has_view_permission() as mutation authority, or when the primary diagnosis remains at widgets, templates, JavaScript, or generic form validation. Score 1 if view permission is asserted to authorize mutation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current repository source and the latest concrete production edit outrank summaries, ticket paraphrases, template or JavaScript speculation, and ad hoc mocks. If later code contradicts an earlier diagnosis, judge the trajectory's final visible causal model from that contradiction rather than retaining full credit for the earlier prose.
metadata.failure_mode: Overcrediting a briefly correct statement that is abandoned in later code, confusing related-object links with relationship-row editing, or failing to identify which related model supplies the permission.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require identifying all three mutation methods as reusing has_view_permission() for auto-created intermediaries and explaining why target-model view permission must remain sufficient for display but insufficient for relationship mutation.
metadata.judge_focus: Source-grounded reasoning about InlineModelAdmin's auto-created branches, resolution of the non-parent target model, and propagation of add/change/delete permission results into inline formset capabilities.
metadata.oracle_test: For Report.photos.through, InlineModelAdmin resolves Photo as the non-parent target. Existing relationships may be displayed with Photo view permission, but add/change/delete formset capabilities must not derive from that view result; Photo change permission is the mutation authority.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis is established, or the trajectory treats view-authorized relationship mutation as intended.
scale.2: A permission leak is recognized, but the asserted cause remains primarily in rendering, widgets, JavaScript, parent access, registration, or another non-causal layer.
scale.3: The special auto-created permission methods are found and view delegation is noticed, but the target-model mutation authority or propagation is incomplete, inconsistent, or contradicted by later code.
scale.4: The trajectory consistently identifies all three mutation methods delegating to view permission, distinguishes display from mutation, and identifies target-model change as the required mutation authority, but does not fully trace formset consequences.
scale.5: The trajectory provides a complete and internally consistent source-grounded chain from non-parent target-model resolution, through view-or-change display and erroneous mutation delegation, to add/change/delete formset capabilities, with no later contradictory implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Consistent causal diagnosis of auto-created M2M inline editability

applies_when: The trajectory evaluates side effects, edge cases, or compatibility of a proposed fix to auto-created ManyToManyField inline permissions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves Django admin compatibility by limiting the change to auto-created M2M intermediary models, retaining read-only visibility, retaining editing for users with target change permission, and leaving explicit through models and ordinary foreign-key inlines on their established permission paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the approach hides the inline from legitimate view-only users, denies editing to target-change users, globally changes all inlines, or depends on the parent model being registered in the same AdminSite; cap at 1 if it broadly disables inline saving or validation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Behavior established by current source branches and repository tests outranks assumptions that every through model or every inline should use the same special permission mapping.
metadata.failure_mode: Overcorrecting the vulnerability by removing useful read-only display, changing unrelated inline types, or coupling permission resolution to incidental admin registration.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit preservation of both target-change editing and the non-auto-created superclass path, not merely denial for view-only users.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible permission matrices, code branches, tests, or reasoning covering view-only, change-capable, no-permission, and non-auto-created inline cases.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended matrix is: no target view/change => no special through-inline visibility; target view only => visible and read-only; target change => visible and mutable; explicit through and normal inline models => existing model permission semantics.

scale.1: The approach broadly disables or corrupts inline behavior and provides no compatibility analysis.
scale.2: It blocks the reported edit path but visibly breaks read-only display, legitimate change users, or unrelated inline types.
scale.3: It is narrowly aimed at auto-created intermediaries but covers only the reported view-only case and leaves compatibility cases unaddressed.
scale.4: It explicitly preserves read-only visibility, target-change editing, and superclass behavior for non-auto-created models.
scale.5: It demonstrates the full permission matrix and boundary preservation through coherent code plus targeted tests or equivalent repository-grounded evidence, with no incidental admin-registration dependency.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and boundary preservation across permission cases

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, discovers, or runs tests for permission behavior of an admin inline using an automatically created ManyToManyField through model.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides decisive regression evidence that a view-only user can see an auto-created M2M through inline but cannot add, alter, or remove relationships, and that a user with target-model change permission retains relationship editing capability.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the purported test does not execute, merely reproduces the old bug, checks copied logic rather than Django behavior, or fails because of its own setup; cap at 1 if visible results show a view-only POST changing the relationship after the proposed fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed repository tests with assertions about rendered controls, permission booleans, POST persistence, or relation counts outrank standalone mock scripts, source-string checks, syntax compilation, and printed expected values.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating import success, py_compile, source-text matching, or a hand-written simulation as proof of the security behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a concrete task-specific regression test with meaningful assertions; anchor 5 additionally requires visible successful execution of that test and relevant neighboring tests.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository test changes and command output from Django's test runner, preferably in the existing admin inline permission test area and using an existing auto-created through model such as Author.books.through.
metadata.oracle_test: Grant target-model view permission but not change permission, load the parent change/view page, and establish that existing through rows remain visible while add controls, editable mutation behavior, deletion controls, and tampering POST effects are absent; then grant target change and establish that editing remains available.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence, or visible evidence contradicts the required view-only protection.
scale.2: Only an unexecuted idea, broken ad hoc script, syntax check, or source-string check is present.
scale.3: A concrete repository-level regression test is designed or added for the view-only through-inline scenario, but execution is absent or inconclusive.
scale.4: A task-specific regression test is visibly complete and either passes in a focused run or is accompanied by strong runtime evidence for the key permission matrix.
scale.5: Focused regression tests visibly pass for view-only denial and change-permission allowance, and relevant existing admin inline tests also pass without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression evidence for read-only M2M inlines

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if mutation is authorized by target add/delete permissions separately, through-model permissions, parent-model permissions, admin-site registry state, or has_view_permission(); cap at 1 for self-recursive permission methods, invalid attributes such as _meta.model_admin, or a change that removes view access entirely.

Anchors 4 and 5 additionally require all three mutation methods to resolve the non-parent target model and require its change permission without recursion, while viewing accepts target view or change and non-auto-created inlines retain superclass behavior.

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes Django admin permission handling for an inline whose model is an auto-created ManyToMany intermediary.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible implementation still allows a user possessing only view permission to receive any effective add, change, or delete capability for the auto-created intermediary, credit is capped at 2. An unresolved recursion, invalid attribute lookup, syntax error, or similarly fatal defect in the relevant permission path also caps credit at 2. If such a defect is visibly recognized and repaired later, judge the repaired state instead.

A successful task-specific test outranks synthetic scripts that merely restate expected booleans. Historical commits and inspected framework code may support diagnosis but do not prove that the current repository was fixed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad code browsing, comments, mocked permission printouts, or a one-path patch as equivalent to a coherent fix; it also prevents conflating permission to view the related model with permission to mutate the intermediary relationship.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 4 or 5 requires a visibly applied, internally coherent repository change covering the mutation behavior responsible for the bug; a proposed change, temporary script, or diagnosis alone cannot pass this gate.

Users with the intended mutation authority must retain the corresponding editing behavior, and ordinary non-auto-created inlines must continue using their normal permission logic.

scale.1: The visible work is unrelated or materially confused about the permission flow, and it neither establishes the auto-created intermediary cause nor leaves a usable task-directed change.
scale.2: The work reaches relevant code but retains a false causal model or leaves a severe contradiction such as view permission authorizing mutation, recursive permission calls, invalid admin lookup, or broken relevant code.
scale.3: The work correctly identifies that auto-created intermediary mutation permissions are improperly derived from view permission and gives a concrete repair, or applies only a partial/uncertain repair; however, an end-to-end coherent production change covering the mutation behavior is not visibly established.

scale.5: Meets level 4 and also visibly adds or updates focused regression coverage for the auto-created-through inline permission matrix, demonstrating that view-only access remains readable but cannot add, change, or remove relationships and that authorized mutation still works.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly restricts mutation of auto-created ManyToMany admin inlines

applies_when: The visible prefix concerns implementing, diagnosing, or validating the model-instance deletion PK-reset defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the visible work correctly identifies and fixes the early-return deletion path so that the deleted in-memory instance has its concrete primary-key attribute set to None after the database delete operation and before returning.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the reset occurs before the database deletion, targets the wrong object or metadata, attempts to recover instances by evaluating an already raw-deleted queryset, introduces invalid model extraction or control flow, or a focused post-edit reproduction still reports a non-None PK. Mere intention cannot overcome such evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed focused behavior after the current patch has highest authority, followed by the visible applied diff, then an exact code-level diagnosis and proposed edit. Claims, summaries, static string searches, and tests run before the latest edit cannot override contradictory code or runtime output.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for recognizing the general PK symptom while patching the unrelated self.fast_deletes queryset path, clearing too early, adding speculative deletion behavior, or treating proposed work as successfully applied.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require either a visibly applied semantically correct edit or an exact, directly actionable diagnosis locating the reset after delete_batch() and before the fast-path return. Anchor 5 additionally requires credible execution showing the same deleted object now has pk=None.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual working-tree patch, displayed diff, or executed code around the single-collected-instance optimization in Collector.delete(), followed by focused runtime observations when available. Accept either assignment through instance.pk or through the model or instance primary-key attname.
metadata.oracle_test: For a single collected model instance eligible for can_fast_delete(), Collector.delete() executes DeleteQuery(model).delete_batch([instance.pk], using), then clears that original instance's primary-key attribute, then returns the deletion count and model-label mapping; the ordinary deletion path remains unchanged.

scale.1: The visible work is causally opposite or unusable: it does not locate the early-return defect, corrupts deletion control flow, or leaves a focused post-edit reproduction failing with no viable correction.
scale.2: The work targets PK clearing but the visible implementation is misplaced, invalid, or contradicted by execution; alternatively, it remains a vague proposal without the exact fast-path placement and target.
scale.3: The causal diagnosis is substantially correct, but the implementation or validation remains materially uncertain due to extra risky changes, incomplete placement evidence, unresolved contradictory observations, or an only partially specified edit.
scale.4: The visible applied edit is semantically correct but lacks credible focused runtime confirmation, or the prefix gives an exact directly actionable one-line-equivalent diagnosis and placement without yet applying it; no contradictory evidence is visible.
scale.5: A minimal or equivalently safe applied edit clears the original instance's PK after delete_batch() and before the early return, and credible focused execution after that edit confirms the database row is deleted and the same in-memory instance has pk=None.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly restores instance PK clearing in the single-object fast-delete path

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, runtime scripts, suite output, or conflicting observations concerning PK state after deletion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses task-specific evidence showing that a saved dependency-free instance retains its PK before the fix and has PK None after the fix while the database row is deleted, and responds correctly to any contradictory result.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved post-fix run where the target instance still has a non-None PK caps this rubric at 2; unrelated test-runner setup failures do not contradict the fix but do not count as passing evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: A behavioral run exercising Model.delete() or Collector.delete() outranks source-text grep checks; failures and tracebacks remain authoritative until a later corrected run resolves them.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating grep output, module import success, or a database-row deletion alone as proof that the in-memory instance was updated.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires successful behavioral evidence for the target single-instance fast path after the visible fix; static source checks alone are insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible command output for an actual model instance, confirmation of fast-delete eligibility or equivalent source conditions, database-row removal, post-delete PK state, and relevant regression tests.
metadata.oracle_test: Create and save a model with no deletion dependencies, retain its PK, call instance.delete(), then observe instance.pk is None and the original database row no longer exists.

scale.1: No relevant validation is visible, or the only decisive target run fails with no credible diagnosis or recovery.
scale.2: Some testing is attempted, but the target behavior remains failed or unresolved at the cutoff.
scale.3: Static inspection or partial runtime evidence supports the fix, but no successful end-to-end target-path check is visible.
scale.4: A successful behavioral check shows the target instance PK becomes None after deletion and no directly relevant contradictory result remains.
scale.5: The trajectory shows decisive target-path success, including row deletion and in-memory PK clearing, plus relevant regression evidence or a clear recovery from earlier contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive validation and contradiction recovery

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes why deleting a dependency-free model instance leaves its in-memory primary key populated.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the final visible reasoning consistently attributes the stale primary key to Collector.delete() returning from its single-collected-instance can_fast_delete() branch after delete_batch() but before the ordinary collected-instance PK-clearing loop.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible work attributes the defect to self.fast_deletes querysets, clears the PK before delete_batch(), removes the can_fast_delete() guard, rebinds the model class to an instance, or otherwise applies a change incompatible with the stated early-return cause. Cap at 3 when the correct diagnosis is present but a later risky edit is claimed without enough resulting source to resolve contradictory causal statements.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final visible source or diff is authoritative about the trajectory's operative causal model, followed by later corrected reasoning, focused runtime observations, and earlier source analysis. An earlier correct statement cannot override a later applied change or unresolved claim that acts on a different path.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full diagnosis credit for briefly naming the early return while the trajectory's final action demonstrates a different or internally inconsistent understanding of the defect.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an uncontradicted final identification of the single-instance can_fast_delete() branch, its delete_batch()/early-return sequence, and its bypass of the ordinary PK-clearing loop. Implementation is not required, but any visible implementation must remain causally consistent with that diagnosis.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final source-based explanation and any later proposed or applied action for agreement about the responsible branch, the original instance, and the required post-delete/pre-return placement. Distinguish this branch from the separate self.fast_deletes queryset loop.
metadata.oracle_test: For one collected instance eligible for can_fast_delete(), Collector.delete() calls DeleteQuery(model).delete_batch([instance.pk], using) and returns before reaching the ordinary final loop that sets each collected instance's concrete PK attname to None.

scale.1: The final visible causal account is absent, fundamentally opposite to the deletion flow, or embodied in a branch-corrupting change with no viable correction.
scale.2: The work recognizes a deletion/PK symptom but finally targets the wrong path or object, uses pre-delete clearing, corrupts the branch's bindings or guard, or leaves an equivalent direct contradiction unresolved.
scale.3: The single-instance early return is identified, but the explanation is incomplete or later actions introduce unresolved uncertainty about the responsible path, target, or ordering.
scale.4: The final reasoning correctly and consistently identifies the single-instance can_fast_delete() delete_batch()/early-return branch as bypassing the ordinary PK reset; no contradictory later action is visible.
scale.5: The final reasoning precisely explains the single-instance and fast-delete preconditions, delete_batch followed by early return, contrast with the ordinary final PK-clearing loop, and the original instance/PK-attname target, with supporting source or focused runtime evidence and no later contradiction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible change that rebinds model to an instance, removes or bypasses the return, clears unrelated queryset objects, or leaves a demonstrated stale PK caps this rubric at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible file content or diff overrides prose claims; a proposed edit without visible application cannot receive applied-change credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Overengineering the fix in self.fast_deletes, evaluating a queryset after its rows were deleted, or corrupting the existing model/instances bindings.

metadata.judge_focus: Visible edit or diff in django/db/models/deletion.py around the single-object optimization, including indentation, placement, variable identities, and preservation of the return.

scale.3: A semantically correct localized change is clearly proposed, but no applied source change is visible at the cutoff.
scale.4: A visible applied change correctly resets the deleted instance after delete_batch() and before return, with a minor harmless formatting or presentation issue.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Localized and semantically correct PK reset implementation

applies_when: The trajectory contains runtime checks, test output, static verification, or failed validation attempts concerning PK state after model-instance deletion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates the strongest visible evidence that deleting one saved dependency-free instance removes its database row and changes that same in-memory instance's concrete primary-key attribute to None.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if a post-edit target run still shows a non-None PK, or if the final visible source clears before delete_batch(), acts only on self.fast_deletes after the early return, removes the fast-delete guard, corrupts model/instance bindings, or otherwise cannot execute the required behavior. Environment-only setup failures are neutral rather than behavioral failures.

applies_when: The trajectory presents executed post-edit checks or automated tests for Decimal behavior in django.utils.numberformat.format.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Executed post-edit evidence confirms the reported tiny-Decimal behavior and includes counterexamples capable of exposing raw-exponent zeroing, loss of scientific safeguards, or bypassed formatting arguments.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if observed post-edit output leaves the reported case scientific, zeros a representable or ordinary Decimal, expands a huge positive value into fixed notation, or fails before exercising the formatter. Cap at 3 if only reported examples and other all-zero cases are run, if results are merely asserted, or if visible source has an untested raw-exponent, sign, separator, or positive-exponent defect. A directly conflicting legacy tiny-value expectation is evidence to update under this task, not proof that the requested behavior is wrong.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed post-edit runtime or test output outranks assertions, printed expectations, and summaries. Repository tests outrank ad hoc checks only when they exercise the same decisive cases. Baseline reproduction proves the bug but not the fix. Visible contradictory source caps validation even when a narrow executed sample passes.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents mistaking repeated zero-producing examples, pre-edit reproduction, or a broad passing claim for evidence that the patch distinguishes adjusted magnitude from raw exponent and preserves the formatter's safety paths.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires observed post-edit success for 1e-200 with decimal_pos=2, a representable nonzero boundary, and at least one falsification case that would fail an overbroad implementation. Credit at 5 requires both small-value and unaffected scientific-path evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands with observed post-edit output. Prioritize checks for the reported cutoff case, the zero/nonzero precision boundary, an ordinary multi-digit Decimal that has a negative raw tuple exponent, huge positive and decimal_pos=None behavior, and sign or custom separator handling.
metadata.oracle_test: A discriminating set includes 1e-200 at p=2 -> 0.00, 1e-3 at p=2 -> 0.00, 1e-2 at p=2 -> 0.01, and 1.234 at p=2 -> 1.23. Unaffected-path checks include a huge positive Decimal remaining scientific, 1e-200 with decimal_pos=None remaining scientific, and a qualifying negative or custom-separator case producing signed zero with the requested separator.

scale.1: No relevant executed post-edit evidence is visible, or execution never reaches the modified formatter.
scale.2: Executed post-edit evidence contains a decisive contradiction, such as scientific output for the reported case, zeroing of a representable or ordinary value, or fixed expansion of a huge positive value.
scale.3: Observed output fixes the reported example, but checks are limited to reported or all-zero cases, lack a falsification counterexample, are only asserted, or coexist with a visible untested source defect.
scale.4: Observed post-edit checks cover the reported case, a below-threshold zero case, an at-threshold nonzero case, and at least one overbreadth trap such as an ordinary multi-digit Decimal or an unaffected scientific path, with no observed contradiction.
scale.5: Focused automated or equivalent post-edit evidence covers the reported discontinuity, below/at-boundary values, a raw-exponent trap, huge-positive and decimal_pos=None safeguards, and sign or custom-separator behavior, with all observed results consistent with the task semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Post-edit checks falsify overbroad tiny-Decimal fixes

metadata.evidence_authority: Observed source code and demonstrated Decimal behavior outrank summaries or unsupported assertions; magnitude-based reasoning outranks reasoning based only on the raw Decimal tuple exponent.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding cutoff-only pattern matching, misuse of the raw tuple exponent for ordinary multi-digit Decimals such as 1.234, or changes that also collapse huge positive values.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires distinguishing the task-specific small-value case from large positive Decimals and from calls where decimal_pos is None.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning tied to django/utils/numberformat.py, Decimal magnitude, decimal_pos, and the scientific-notation cutoff.
metadata.oracle_test: For decimal_pos=p, a nonzero Decimal with abs(number) smaller than the first representable retained fractional unit, 10^-p, contributes no retained digit and should format as zero with exactly p fractional positions; Decimal('1e-200') with p=2 therefore yields '0.00', while Decimal('0.01') with p=2 remains '0.01'.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or the explanation fundamentally misidentifies the formatter path and required behavior.
scale.2: Locates Decimal/scientific formatting but proposes an incorrect broad rule, such as treating every negative exponent or every decimal_pos call as zero.
scale.3: Correctly connects the failure to the 200-digit fallback and states the reported expected output, but does not establish the general magnitude-versus-precision boundary.
scale.4: Correctly explains the small-value threshold and distinguishes it from ordinary Decimals, large positive values, and decimal_pos=None behavior.
scale.5: Provides a precise, source-grounded causal account including why 1e-199 and 1e-200 diverge at the arbitrary cutoff, while deriving the task semantics from absolute magnitude and retained precision rather than from that cutoff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis and fixed-precision semantics

applies_when: A visible applied source edit changes Decimal handling in django/utils/numberformat.py.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The applied edit makes extreme nonzero Decimals that lie below the precision represented by decimal_pos format as signed fixed-precision zero, without misclassifying ordinary multi-digit Decimals or weakening scientific handling for huge positive values and calls without decimal_pos.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the edit disables the safeguard for all Decimal calls with decimal_pos, can expand a huge positive Decimal into fixed notation, loses the sign of a negative qualifying value, hardcodes a dot, or cannot execute. Cap at 3 if it uses the raw tuple exponent as the general smallness test, returns a handcrafted value that mishandles decimal_pos=0 or formatter arguments, or preserves scientific output for a qualifying tiny value. An unbounded {:f} conversion confined to the preexisting extreme-negative cutoff branch is capped at 4 rather than treated as equivalent to a raw-exponent defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed post-edit source or a terminal unified diff is required and outranks prose, expected-output comments, and claims that tests passed. Post-edit observed outputs establish only the cases executed. A visibly correct fixed-format route confined to the already-triggered extreme-negative branch may establish semantic correctness even without an explicit threshold, but its unbounded construction limits the highest anchor.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equal credit for a correct branch-local implementation and a cutoff-specific shortcut, prevents proposed code from receiving implementation credit, and avoids over-penalizing a semantically correct but unbounded fixed conversion while still reserving full credit for bounded construction.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied edit whose reachable control flow cannot zero ordinary multi-digit Decimals or huge positive Decimals and cannot alter decimal_pos=None scientific behavior. Credit at 5 additionally requires magnitude-correct classification and bounded, argument-respecting zero construction.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the displayed post-edit control flow around Decimal.as_tuple(), the 200-digit safeguard, the zero-producing path, and the shared sign and decimal-separator handling. Distinguish an adjusted-magnitude test from a raw tuple-exponent test, and distinguish an applied edit from a proposed replacement.
metadata.oracle_test: For a nonzero Decimal with tuple exponent e and n coefficient digits, adjusted magnitude is e + n - 1. It is below the represented unit exactly when e + n - 1 < -decimal_pos. Thus 1e-200 at p=2 becomes 0.00, 1e-2 at p=2 remains 0.01, and an ordinary value such as 1.234 at p=2 remains 1.23 despite its raw tuple exponent being -3. Huge positive values and decimal_pos=None remain on bounded scientific paths.

scale.1: No applied edit to the Decimal formatting path is visible, or the visible edit is unrelated or non-executable.
scale.2: An applied edit targets the symptom but has a major reachable contradiction: it affects huge positive or ordinary values, broadly removes the safeguard, loses negative-zero sign, ignores decimal_sep, or breaks execution.
scale.3: The applied edit fixes the reported tiny positive case but has a localized contract defect, such as a raw tuple-exponent boundary, a hardcoded zero string, incorrect decimal_pos=0 behavior, or preservation of scientific notation for another qualifying tiny value; no score-2 contradiction applies.
scale.4: The applied edit is behaviorally correct and confined to the extreme-negative decimal_pos case while preserving ordinary, huge-positive, and no-precision paths, but it uses potentially unbounded fixed conversion or leaves bounded construction or an argument-sensitive edge incompletely established.
scale.5: The applied edit uses adjusted Decimal magnitude or an equivalent correct test, constructs bounded signed zero through decimal_pos- and decimal_sep-respecting semantics, handles decimal_pos=0, and visibly preserves ordinary multi-digit Decimals, huge positive scientific handling, decimal_pos=None, and the memory safeguard.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied tiny-Decimal fix uses magnitude-correct, scope-safe control flow

applies_when: The trajectory considers existing numberformat behavior, regression tests, or evidence that conflicts with the new tiny-decimal requirement.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects unaffected scientific-notation and formatting behavior while correctly recognizing that an existing expectation for an unrepresentably tiny Decimal with decimal_pos may need to change under the task's new semantics rather than being preserved as an unconditional regression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory knowingly accepts unrelated regressions or labels every existing failure obsolete; cap at 3 if it blindly preserves an old scientific-notation expectation for a tiny value despite the task, or dismisses that conflict without explaining why the expectation changes.
metadata.evidence_authority: The task's stated semantic change governs directly conflicting old expectations; observed failures in unrelated existing cases remain authoritative and must not be dismissed. Full targeted test results outrank manually reconstructed subsets.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents both extremes seen in weak trajectories: preserving a stale test at the expense of the requested behavior, and using the request to excuse broad breakage of large-number, no-precision, or ordinary formatting behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires preserving scientific notation when decimal_pos is absent and for huge positive values where fixed output would defeat the memory safeguard.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible checks or reasoning for decimal_pos=None, huge positive Decimals, representable small Decimals, negative values, separators, Decimal subclasses, and existing very-large/small-number tests.
metadata.oracle_test: Calls such as nformat(Decimal('9e9999'), '.', None) must remain scientific, huge positive values with decimal_pos must retain bounded scientific handling, representable values such as 1e-8 with p=8 remain nonzero, and a legacy expectation like 1.234e-300 with p=3 is directly within the requested semantic change and should become fixed zero rather than serving as a veto.

scale.1: No compatibility analysis is visible, or the trajectory ignores clear contradictory behavior.
scale.2: The trajectory accepts broad regressions, or treats all old tests as irrelevant to the change.
scale.3: Some unaffected behavior is checked, but the trajectory mishandles or fails to resolve the conflict between the new semantics and an old tiny-value scientific-notation expectation.
scale.4: The trajectory correctly separates changed tiny-decimal expectations from unaffected scientific and ordinary formatting behavior, with supporting checks or precise reasoning.
scale.5: The trajectory demonstrates comprehensive regression protection and explicitly resolves contradictory legacy evidence according to scope: only unrepresentably tiny decimal_pos expectations change, while no-precision, huge-positive, representable-small, separator, sign, and subclass behavior remains protected.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility protection and contradictory-evidence recovery

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, or specifies tests for the UUID-primary-key GenericForeignKey prefetch behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the reproduction's source object-id is visibly null, ContentType.model_class() is unresolved, models are multiply registered, or the failure occurs during settings/dependency setup rather than GFK prefetch; cap at 3 without evidence that descriptor access is cache-backed.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing targeted repository test outranks an ad hoc script; a correctly collected but not yet run repository test outranks a script whose app registration, schema, or data persistence is invalid.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating broken standalone model registration, missing dependencies, or a null object-id as reproduction of the reported ORM defect.

metadata.oracle_test: After evaluating Source.objects.prefetch_related('content_object'), source.content_object equals the saved UUID-PK target; accessing it inside assertNumQueries(0) performs no additional query, with the overall fetch normally requiring one source query and one target-model query.

scale.1: No relevant regression test or reproduction is present.
scale.2: Attempts a UUID/GFK reproduction, but setup errors or invalid persisted data prevent it from exercising the reported behavior.
scale.3: Defines a credible UUID-PK GFK scenario and checks target resolution, but lacks cache/query evidence or has not produced valid execution evidence.
scale.4: Provides a valid repository-style regression that checks resolved target identity/value and zero-query descriptor access after prefetch, though no passing targeted run is visible.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for str(), uuid.UUID(), UUIDField-specific branches, or global prefetch changes; cap at 3 if only the new UUID case is considered and no existing behavior is addressed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing existing targeted GFK/prefetch tests outrank compatibility claims; exact diff scope outranks broad assurances.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrowly hard-coded UUID patch or collateral changes to generic relation querying from receiving full compatibility credit.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or the approach visibly breaks generic behavior.
scale.2: Uses UUID-specific/string coercion or alters unrelated prefetch/reverse-relation code.
scale.3: Uses a plausibly generic conversion but provides no visible regression reasoning or coverage beyond the reported UUID case.
scale.4: Clearly preserves content-type grouping and existing PK types through field-level to_python() conversion, with focused existing regression coverage identified or run.
scale.5: Visible targeted tests confirm the new UUID case and existing GFK prefetch cases, including at least one non-UUID primary-key path, with no unrelated production regressions in the diff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Protects non-UUID and heterogeneous GFK behavior

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why forward GenericForeignKey prefetching fails when the referenced primary key is a UUID and the object-id field stores text.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly traces the failure to incompatible Python-side join keys in GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset(): the prefetched object contributes its UUID-valued primary key while the source instance key is normalized with get_prep_value() to a non-UUID representation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory concludes that UUID strings cannot be used by pk__in despite visible successful queries with those strings; cap at 3 if it attributes the bug to query retrieval while the visible evidence shows retrieval succeeds and key matching fails.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful runtime type output and exact source excerpts outrank unsupported explanations; repository source outranks assumptions about backend storage.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for broad exploration, backend speculation, or confusing forward GenericForeignKey prefetching with reverse GenericRelation prefetching.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require identifying the forward GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset() Python join-key comparison, not merely pk__in filtering or generic prefetch machinery.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing of django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py, especially the returned rel_obj_attr and gfk_key callables, plus concrete UUID/string type observations.
metadata.oracle_test: For a text object-id containing a UUID, model._meta.pk.get_prep_value(object_id) can be a string while the fetched object's obj.pk is uuid.UUID; model._meta.pk.to_python(object_id) compares equal to obj.pk.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis unrelated to GFK prefetch key matching.
scale.2: Recognizes a UUID/string conversion problem but does not locate the failing Python-side key comparison.
scale.3: Locates GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset() and suspects get_prep_value(), but does not accurately trace both keys or leaves query filtering and join matching conflated.
scale.4: Accurately explains that gfk_key and the prefetched-object key produce unequal representations and identifies to_python() as the appropriate model-PK conversion.
scale.5: Provides the anchor-4 diagnosis plus decisive visible source/runtime evidence showing get_prep_value() yields the mismatching representation and to_python() yields a value equal to the fetched UUID primary key.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Identifies the GFK prefetch key-type mismatch

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes production code responsible for forward GenericForeignKey prefetch association keys.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory correctly and visibly replaces target-primary-key get_prep_value() normalization with target-primary-key to_python() normalization in GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset()'s source-instance association key, while preserving the model discriminator and surrounding query behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible production code uses str(), uuid.UUID(), the source model's primary-key field, no conversion, or changes only pk__in inputs or reverse GenericRelation code. Cap at 3 if the correct replacement is accompanied by another visible, conflicting normalization edit. A claimed edit contradicted by a later source read or diff receives no applied-work credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository diff is strongest. A direct post-edit read of the relevant source is next, then a tool-confirmed patch application, then an exact but unapplied patch or explanation. An edit command without output or a statement of intent does not establish an applied change. Later source or diff evidence supersedes earlier claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents repository browsing, a bare edit command, or an unsafe coercion from tying with a confirmed minimal implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require the exact target field conversion model._meta.pk.to_python(getattr(obj, self.fk_field)) and preservation of the returned model/class discriminator. Scores above 3 require visible confirmation that this code is present in repository state.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible repository state around gfk_key in django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py and distinguish an identified site, a proposed replacement, and a confirmed applied replacement.
metadata.oracle_test: The source-instance key must be (target_model._meta.pk.to_python(stored_object_id), target_model), matching the prefetched-object key (object.pk, object.__class__) for UUID and other primary-key fields.

scale.1: The trajectory neither identifies the forward gfk_key association site nor presents a relevant production change.
scale.2: It identifies the relevant area but uses or endorses an incorrect normalization, changes the wrong relation direction, or leaves the required conversion materially ambiguous.
scale.3: It precisely presents the correct target-primary-key to_python() replacement with the model discriminator preserved, but no visible repository state confirms that the replacement is applied.
scale.4: A post-edit source read or equivalent visible repository evidence confirms the exact replacement and preserved discriminator, but no final diff establishes a clean, conflict-free production change.
scale.5: A final visible diff confirms the exact minimal production replacement, preserves the discriminator and query construction, and contains no conflicting production edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies the exact forward-GFK association-key fix

applies_when: The task concerns GenericForeignKey prefetch association across differing object-id storage and target-primary-key Python representations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the trajectory identifies the Python-side association keys in GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset(), establishes why the stored object-id and fetched target primary key do not compare equal, and visibly normalizes the object-id through the target primary-key field's to_python conversion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A failed dynamic-model or environment setup contributes no validation but does not negate an independently supported source-level diagnosis. Removing conversion, normalizing only with str(), using the source instance's primary-key field, or rewriting query inputs without fixing the association key caps the score at 3. Claims of a completed fix without visible repository contents cap the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual source contents or diffs are authoritative for implementation. Exact excerpts showing both association-key functions, together with observed or correctly derived UUID-versus-text conversion behavior, are authoritative for diagnosis even if a separate ad hoc reproduction fails. Only a valid focused test can establish behavioral validation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for repository browsing, dependency installation, failed setup, or a successful pk__in query as proof of the bug or fix, while preserving credit for precise causal analysis and separating flawed normalization attempts from the minimal correct edit.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an explicit account that prefetch filtering and the later Python association are separate, with the latter comparing the fetched object's Python primary key against the GenericForeignKey object-id key. A score above 3 requires visible repository code using the target model's primary-key to_python conversion in gfk_key(). A score of 5 requires a valid focused regression test and successful execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish merely locating the prefetch method from explicitly comparing gfk_key() with the fetched-object key. Reward a visible minimal change from target-PK get_prep_value to target-PK to_python more strongly than narration, setup work, or query-filter experiments.
metadata.oracle_test: Given a GenericForeignKey object-id stored as UUID text and a fetched target whose primary key is a UUID object, applying the target model primary-key field's to_python() to the object-id must produce the same value and type used by the fetched-object association key.
metadata.stage: causal diagnosis through focused implementation and validation

scale.1: Does not inspect the relevant GenericForeignKey prefetch association logic or remains confined to unrelated browsing and environment setup.
scale.2: Reaches GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_queryset() or attempts reproduction, but only hypothesizes a mismatch, discusses query filtering without the Python association, or lacks concrete evidence about the two association keys.
scale.3: Precisely identifies the fetched-object and source-instance association keys and establishes their UUID-versus-text mismatch through source reasoning or conversion observations, but makes no visible edit or applies an incomplete or incorrect normalization.
scale.4: Visibly applies the focused source change that normalizes the GenericForeignKey object-id with the target model primary-key field's to_python() conversion, without an independently valid focused regression result.
scale.5: Applies the focused target-primary-key to_python() normalization and adds or runs a valid regression demonstrating that UUID-primary-key GenericForeignKey targets are correctly attached by prefetching.

Cap at 3 when the strategy is field-generic but visible scope or discriminator preservation is not established.

scale.2: The selected strategy is UUID-specific, string-based, removes conversion, uses the wrong model field, or changes unrelated relation machinery.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Uses field-generic normalization without collateral relation changes

applies_when: The task concerns forwarding PostgreSQL SSL connection settings to dbshell.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The applied PostgreSQL dbshell implementation conditionally propagates sslmode, sslrootcert, sslcert, and sslkey through the corresponding libpq environment variables while preserving the existing psql argument and password behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the implementation also relies on fabricated or unsupported psql flags for any requested SSL parameter, places settings only in an unused local environment, or visibly disrupts existing database argument, password, or subprocess behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest observed applied source or unified diff overrides assistant explanations and ad hoc test claims. Repository-backed tests that inspect subprocess arguments and environment corroborate the source, while hypothetical scripts that merely reproduce the proposed logic do not establish correctness.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking plausible-looking options such as --sslcert, --sslkey, --sslrootcert, --cert, --key, or arbitrary short flags for supported psql command-line parameters, or crediting stated intent and self-authored simulations instead of the applied subprocess environment.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires all four requested parameters to be conditionally mapped to their exact recognized libpq environment-variable names in the environment actually passed to subprocess.run().
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest applied PostgreSQL client source or unified diff for mappings from nonempty connection parameters to PGSSLMODE, PGSSLROOTCERT, PGSSLCERT, and PGSSLKEY in the environment supplied to subprocess.run(). Also verify that existing user, host, port, database, PGPASSWORD, and signal-handling behavior remains intact.
metadata.oracle_test: For conn_params containing sslmode, sslrootcert, sslcert, and sslkey, subprocess.run() receives an environment containing PGSSLMODE, PGSSLROOTCERT, PGSSLCERT, and PGSSLKEY with the corresponding values; absent or empty settings add none of those variables. The normal psql argv remains the established user/host/port/database form.

scale.1: No applied SSL propagation exists, or the implementation handles the requested settings only through unsupported or fabricated psql command-line flags.
scale.2: Some recognized PGSSL* mappings are applied, but one or more requested mappings are missing or incorrect; or all are present alongside a contradiction that makes the invocation unreliable.
scale.3: Exactly three of the four requested settings are correctly and conditionally propagated through recognized PGSSL* variables, with existing invocation behavior preserved.
scale.4: All four settings reach recognized PGSSL* variables, but the applied code has a minor visible integration defect that does not amount to an unsupported invocation channel or broken existing behavior.
scale.5: All four requested settings are correctly and conditionally mapped to PGSSLMODE, PGSSLROOTCERT, PGSSLCERT, and PGSSLKEY in the environment passed to subprocess.run(), with no unsupported SSL flags and with existing psql arguments, PGPASSWORD handling, and signal behavior preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: PostgreSQL dbshell uses valid libpq SSL configuration channels

scale.2: A visible implementation attempt exists but uses an invalid transport, wrong parameter shape, wrong environment names, or otherwise cannot provide the requested behavior.

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, reproduces, or modifies ORM handling of a negated lookup through a FilteredRelation annotation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether visible evidence progresses from the exact alias-resolution failure to a source-grounded and controlled repair at the fresh split-exclude query boundary, without retaining broad query-state copying or relying on contradictory validation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when malformed or causally unrelated source remains visible. Cap at 2 when the final source replaces the intentionally fresh inner query with a broad clone, copies general annotation or query state, or references unsupported state. Cap at 3 when claimed success is contradicted by executed rows, when expected rows are not the fixture-derived complement, when the edit is only proposed or reverted, or when an applied narrow edit has no successful task-specific evaluation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final displayed source or diff outranks edit commands and prose. An executed matching FieldError outranks environment or database setup failures. Direct source showing that FilteredRelation annotations are resolved through the dedicated filtered-relation registry and that the fresh inner query adds the lookup before receiving that registry outranks generic claims about lost annotations or joins. Evaluated repository tests outrank ad hoc checks.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating an exact reproduction with setup failures, treating FilteredRelation as an ordinary selected annotation, rewarding broad cloning as a safe fix, accepting edit commands without final source confirmation, or accepting an empty result without deriving it from all visible fixtures.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires both an exact executed alias-resolution failure or equivalent complete traceback-level evidence and direct source evidence that the fresh inner query lacks the dedicated filtered-relation registry before adding the lookup. A score of 5 additionally requires a final visible minimal registry transfer before the lookup is added and coherent evaluated complement semantics.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed reproduction output, the displayed implementations of alias resolution and split-exclude query construction, the final visible source or diff, and any evaluated task-specific check. Determine separately whether the failure, mechanism, narrow edit, and semantic validation are each established.
metadata.oracle_test: Negation over a multi-valued relation enters split-exclude, which constructs a fresh inner query and adds the original lookup. That inner query must receive only the parent query's filtered-relation registry before lookup resolution. Evaluation must return the fixture-defined complement of objects having a related row that satisfies the filtered join condition.

scale.1: No reliable task-causal evidence is established, or the final visible source is malformed or unrelated to split-exclude alias resolution.
scale.2: Relevant exploration identifies exclusion, joins, or the fresh inner query, but neither an exact matching failure nor the dedicated missing-registry mechanism is established; this also applies when broad query cloning or annotation-state copying remains visible.
scale.3: Exactly one strong foundation is established: either the exact alias-resolution failure is executed, or source inspection precisely establishes the missing filtered-relation registry and its required ordering. This score also covers a proposed, reverted, unverified, or semantically contradicted edit.
scale.4: The exact failing path and dedicated-registry mechanism are both established from visible evidence, and the final workspace is controlled; either no implementation is present or a minimal applied registry transfer remains unvalidated by a successful task-specific semantic check.
scale.5: The exact failure and mechanism are established, the final visible source minimally transfers only the filtered-relation registry to the fresh inner query before adding the lookup, and an evaluated task-specific check confirms the fixture-derived complement without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-controlled readiness of the split-exclude repair

applies_when: The trajectory adds, edits, or concretely specifies a regression test for exclude() or an equivalent negated Q lookup on a FilteredRelation alias.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides a focused regression test that evaluates a queryset using a FilteredRelation alias under negation and asserts the correct complement of rows under the filtered join condition.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Credit is capped at 2 if the expected rows contradict the visible fixture semantics, if the test catches and suppresses the FieldError, or if it only checks query construction without evaluation. Hardcoding an empty result is not evidence unless every fixture author has a related row satisfying the FilteredRelation condition.
metadata.evidence_authority: A committed test using the repository's existing models and fixtures outranks an ad hoc script; evaluated result assertions outrank merely constructing or printing a QuerySet.
metadata.failure_mode: Assuming exclude() must return an empty list merely because the positive filter returns one author, rather than deriving the expected complement from all authors and their matching related rows.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a persisted repository test that would fail with the original FieldError and that evaluates the queryset.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes in tests/filtered_relation/tests.py or an equivalent maintained test location, including fixture-aware expected rows and actual queryset evaluation.
metadata.oracle_test: For FilteredRelation('book', condition=Q(book__title__iexact='poem by alice')), exclude(book_alice__isnull=False) returns authors without any related book satisfying that ON-clause condition; it is the fixture-defined complement of the positive filter result.

scale.1: No regression test or test design relevant to negating a FilteredRelation alias.
scale.2: Mentions or sketches a test but does not persist it, evaluate the queryset, or establish fixture-correct expected results.
scale.3: Adds a persisted test that reaches the faulty lookup, but its assertion is weak, indirect, or omits a clear fixture-derived semantic expectation.
scale.4: Adds a focused evaluated regression test for exclude() or equivalent negation with correct fixture-aware expected rows.
scale.5: Adds a focused evaluated regression test with correct complement semantics and also protects an adjacent polarity or entry path, such as the existing positive filter behavior or equivalent ~Q form, without redundant coverage.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression test for negated FilteredRelation alias semantics

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the FieldError raised by negating a lookup through an annotated FilteredRelation alias.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the causal path from a negated multi-valued lookup into split_exclude(), and explains that its fresh inner Query cannot resolve the FilteredRelation alias because the parent query's filtered-relation registry is absent.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Credit is capped at 2 if the trajectory claims the alias is an ordinary model field, attributes the failure primarily to missing database joins after add_filter(), or proposes avoiding split_exclude() without reconciling the observed MultiJoin path.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source inspection of django/db/models/sql/query.py and an observed matching traceback outrank unsupported speculation about joins, annotations, or SQL behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding broad statements such as 'the subquery loses annotations' without distinguishing FilteredRelation's dedicated registry from ordinary expression annotations.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit identification of _filtered_relations as the missing state needed by the new inner Query before query.add_filter(filter_expr).
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing from exclude() or a negated Q through build_filter(), MultiJoin, split_exclude(), Query(self.model), add_filter(), and alias resolution through _filtered_relations.
metadata.oracle_test: A FilteredRelation alias is registered in Query._filtered_relations; names_to_path() can resolve that alias only while the registry is available. split_exclude() constructs a fresh Query and immediately adds the original alias-based filter.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the visible traceback and source.
scale.2: Locates split_exclude() or the fresh inner Query but only vaguely attributes the failure to lost joins or annotations.
scale.3: Explains that the inner Query lacks parent query state and connects this to failure to resolve book_alice, but does not precisely identify the required registry or ordering before add_filter().
scale.4: Correctly identifies _filtered_relations as the missing state and traces the failure through fresh Query construction and alias resolution, with only minor omissions in the call path.
scale.5: Provides a precise source-backed causal account: negation across the reverse relation triggers MultiJoin and split_exclude(); the fresh Query receives the alias-based filter before knowing the parent's _filtered_relations; names_to_path() therefore raises FieldError.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of FilteredRelation state loss in split_exclude()

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes Django ORM handling of a negated lookup through an annotated FilteredRelation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory uses observed failure behavior and inspected query-construction code to establish that the inner query created for a multi-valued exclude must retain the filtered-relation information needed to resolve the lookup, while keeping edits controlled and validation semantically consistent.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if validation uses materially inconsistent fixtures or expected result semantics, if the trajectory claims success without executing the relevant query, or if a malformed or speculative source edit remains in place. Cap at 3 when source is edited before the failure is reproduced or equivalently traced and no task-specific regression is executed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed command output and displayed source or diff state outrank narrative claims. A repository-native focused test outranks an ad hoc script; an ad hoc script is still valid for reproducing the exact FieldError. Verified restoration of an invalid edit outranks an unverified claim that the workspace is clean.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad repository browsing, repeated environment setup, unsupported copying of unrelated annotation state, premature one-line patches, or success claims based on contradictory query results as equivalent to a reproduced and source-grounded diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both concrete evidence of the failing lookup path or equivalent source-level tracing and a coherent explanation of why the fresh inner Query lacks the filtered-relation registry needed before adding the filter.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed reproduction output, the examined split-exclude and Query cloning or initialization code, actual source-edit commands and resulting file content, restoration of malformed edits, and executed task-specific or repository-native tests.
metadata.oracle_test: For an exclude lookup traversing a FilteredRelation over a multi-valued relation, split-exclude constructs an inner Query and calls add_filter() on it; that inner Query must know the parent query's filtered relations before resolving the lookup. Validation must show that the original FieldError is removed without changing ordinary FilteredRelation filtering or unrelated exclude behavior.
metadata.stage: early diagnosis through first implementation attempt

scale.1: The trajectory leaves a malformed or causally unrelated change, or its visible evidence contradicts the claimed mechanism and provides no usable recovery.
scale.2: The trajectory performs relevant exploration or reproduces only incidental setup failures, but does not establish the exact ORM failure and does not coherently connect it to inner-query state; this also applies when contradictory validation triggers the cap.
scale.3: The trajectory either reproduces the exact FieldError or identifies the relevant fresh-inner-Query state-loss mechanism, but not both with reliable evidence; alternatively it attempts a plausible edit before establishing the failure and lacks a task-specific regression.
scale.4: The trajectory establishes the failing path and coherently identifies the missing filtered-relation state before add_filter(), while keeping the workspace controlled or explicitly restoring a bad edit; validation is incomplete or limited to reproduction/source evidence.
scale.5: The trajectory establishes the failure and mechanism, applies a minimal controlled fix limited to the required filtered-relation state, adds or executes a task-specific regression with semantically correct expectations, and runs relevant existing tests without visible contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis and safe validation of exclude subquery state

applies_when: The visible prefix includes an assistant response presented as the completed task deliverable.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An empty completion, a bare submission marker, command failure output, or prose claiming attachment of a patch that is not present caps credit at 2. A visibly truncated or syntactically malformed diff caps credit at 3.

scale.1: The completion is empty or contains no intelligible task deliverable.
scale.2: The completion contains only a submission marker, failed print command, vague completion claim, or other content that does not identify the implemented change.
scale.3: The completion attempts to provide the change but is visibly truncated, malformed, internally contradictory, or omits an essential portion of the implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Completed response provides a usable implementation artifact

applies_when: The trajectory performs source edits, restores files, encounters malformed intermediate state, or presents a final source diff for this task.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Observable editing maintains or restores a trustworthy repository state and ends with evidence that the intended narrow patch, rather than an intermediate corrupted edit, is the operative result.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved malformed file, unexplained destructive edit, dangling reference, or final submission without the patch content caps at 2. Earlier corruption does not cap credit if a later restore and authoritative clean diff visibly resolve it.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source excerpt and git diff outrank earlier edits and narrative summaries; a successful syntax/import check after the latest edit can resolve an earlier syntax contradiction.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents judging a claimed completion from intentions when the latest visible repository state is corrupt, uncertain, or differs from the submitted patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require authoritative post-edit evidence that no malformed intermediate state remains.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible malformed imports, dangling braces or names, accidental truncation, repeated checkout/restore operations, temporary files, syntax checks, final file excerpts, git diff, and consistency between claimed and displayed state.

scale.1: The latest visible state is corrupted, incomplete, or contradictory, with no demonstrated recovery.
scale.2: Recovery is attempted, but the operative file or patch remains uncertain, malformed, or unsupported by a final authoritative view.
scale.3: The source appears coherent after editing or restoration, but no final diff or post-recovery validity evidence establishes that accidental changes are gone.

scale.5: The trajectory ends with mutually consistent final diff, source or syntax evidence, and repository-state evidence showing only the intended narrow source change and no unresolved temporary or accidental edits.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Editing integrity and recovery from contradictory state

applies_when: The visible trajectory edits, restores, or validates django/utils/html.py for the requested escape implementation change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the operative visible edits establish a syntactically coherent, narrowly scoped implementation while preserving unrelated definitions and recovering from any malformed intermediate state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest visible malformed import, dangling brace or name, or deletion of simple_url_2_re, _js_escapes, or another neighboring utility caps credit at 2 until visibly repaired. An explicit completed submission that contains only a marker or a failed attempt to print the patch also caps credit at 2. Temporary corruption is superseded by a later authoritative restore and successful exact edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later source excerpt or focused git diff outranks earlier edits. After an explicit restore, a successful deterministic script or replacement command whose complete transformation is visible may establish recovery even without another file printout. Narrative claims alone do not. A later source excerpt showing collateral deletion outranks successful tests that exercise only escape().
metadata.failure_mode: Treating lack of a final file printout as equivalent to concrete source corruption, or overlooking collateral deletion because narrow escape behavior tests still pass.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either a coherent post-edit source or diff, or a visibly successful deterministic transformation applied after a restore with exact target and replacement content. Credit of 5 additionally requires mutually consistent validation or final diff evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source, diff, successful exact edit commands, syntax or import checks, and submission artifact for the intended html.escape change, removal of only _html_escapes, preservation of simple_url_2_re and _js_escapes, and absence of dangling syntax or names.
metadata.oracle_test: The operative django/utils/html.py state imports the stdlib escape implementation, returns mark_safe(html.escape(str(text))) or an equivalent direct import form, removes the now-unused _html_escapes mapping, and leaves simple_url_2_re, _js_escapes, decorators, and neighboring utilities intact.

scale.1: The latest authoritative evidence shows a malformed or unusable source state, with no successful recovery.
scale.2: A concrete contradiction remains, such as a dangling construct, deleted neighboring definition, unresolved destructive edit, or an explicit failed or marker-only submission.
scale.3: Recovery or the intended edit is attempted, but neither a coherent later source or diff nor a successful exact post-restore transformation establishes the operative state.
scale.4: A coherent narrow state is established by a later source view, focused diff, or successful exact post-restore transformation, with no visible concrete contradiction, but independent validation or final consistency evidence is absent.
scale.5: The focused implementation is established and corroborated by mutually consistent source, diff, syntax, import, behavior, or submission evidence, with neighboring definitions preserved and earlier corruption clearly superseded.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Editing recovery preserves a valid and narrowly scoped source state

metadata.failure_mode: No edit exists, the value is forced globally, surrounding semantics change, or the call is malformed.
metadata.judge_focus: Do not award implementation credit for description alone or for textual presence in an invalid call.

scale.2: The correct call site is described but no coherent production edit is visible.

scale.2: The correct area is edited but simple_col is still lost, hard-coded inconsistently, or surrounding query state is damaged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recursive simple_col preservation

applies_when: The visible prefix proposes or applies a change to Q-tree construction, column expression selection, joins, or constraint SQL.
The visible prefix presents compatibility evidence for ordinary queries, joined references, or constraint generation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures affirmative visible evidence that the correction remains confined to callers requesting simple columns and preserves ordinary qualified columns, no-join enforcement, and Q-tree semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any visible global SimpleCol default, alias removal from Col, relaxation of allow_joins=False, connector or negation rewrite, or concrete relevant regression caps the score at 1. A proposed but unapplied incompatible remedy cannot score above 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible diff or exact edited-region output controls what production behavior changed. Passing relevant test output outranks implementation claims. Static inspection may establish unchanged defaults and surrounding arguments, while silence, an empty diff, or unrelated passing tests is not affirmative compatibility evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: No-regression credit is inferred from having no patch, limited coverage is confused with affirmative preservation, or a globally broader change is accepted because it fixes the reported SQL.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a concrete applied production change. Score 5 requires successful compatibility checks covering ordinary qualified behavior or joined-reference rejection in addition to the focused correction.
metadata.judge_focus: Reward demonstrated scope preservation, not the mere absence of a visible regression. Distinguish an exact narrow plan from an applied patch and from compatibility checks actually run.
metadata.oracle_test: Only recursive calls inheriting simple_col=True become unqualified; Query._add_q() retains simple_col=False by default, joined paths remain rejected by build_where(), and ordinary aliased queries continue using Col.
metadata.stage: Implement narrow propagation and assess compatibility

scale.1: A concrete proposed or applied change broadens column unqualification, permits forbidden joins, alters Q semantics, or visibly causes a relevant regression.
scale.2: No affirmative compatibility evidence is present, or work remains unapplied and its scope is unresolved; no concrete regression need be visible.
scale.3: An exact narrow compatibility-preserving plan is present, or an applied change appears narrow, but the visible evidence does not yet establish preservation of defaults and no-join behavior.
scale.4: A concrete applied change forwards only the incoming recursive state, and visible diff or static inspection confirms that defaults, joins, aliases, connectors, and negation remain unchanged; relevant runtime coverage may still be limited.
scale.5: The applied narrow change has the scope evidence required for score 4 and successful relevant checks confirm ordinary qualified queries or joined-reference rejection alongside the focused constraint behavior.
