applies_when: The trajectory includes commands intended to load production Django code or exercise compilation, Collector collection, deletion, SQL generation, row state, or returned counts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards only actually executed commands whose observed output reaches active production loading or the relevant deletion path, with greater credit for isolated and task-discriminative results.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A printed success message does not count when the same run reports an exception, swallowed assertion, or failure before the relevant boundary. A compiler or import failure caused by the active production edit is decisive score-5 evidence. A failure caused before production loading remains score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output is authoritative. A script's source or the assistant's claim cannot prove execution. The result must be attributable to the production state active when the command ran; later edits do not retroactively validate an earlier run.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding execution credit for reading source, applying an edit, writing a test, installing dependencies, constructing Q objects, printing markers, or invoking a harness that fails before production code loads.
metadata.hard_gate: Any trajectory lacking an executed command and observed output that reaches production compilation, production import, Collector collection, or deletion receives score 1. Missing dependencies, missing settings, malformed shell commands, source-marker checks, mock-only helpers, and Q-only demonstrations are score 1.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the deepest production boundary reached by an executed command and its observed output. Separate production compilation or import from setup failures, source inspection, helper-only Q construction, edit-script output, and success text printed after caught failures.
metadata.oracle_test: Strong task evidence includes py_compile or import of the active deletion module, a real Collector reaching collect() or delete(), captured DELETE SQL, an exact two-query assertion, OR predicate shape, affected and surviving rows, and returned deletion counts.

scale.1: No executed observation reaches production compilation, import, Collector collection, or deletion; all attempts are source-only, helper-only, marker-only, or blocked during setup.
scale.2: An executed real Collector or deletion-related path is entered, but the result is materially entangled with an unfaithful harness, model registration, unchanged production, or unrelated database constraints.
scale.3: Active production successfully compiles or imports, or an attributable Collector result is observed, but the probe does not isolate the changed fast-delete behavior.
scale.4: A faithful changed-path probe produces a precise task-relevant SQL, deletion, row-state, count, or exception result, but does not establish the complete focused contract.
scale.5: The active edit causes a confirmed production compilation or import failure, or an isolated focused regression decisively establishes query count, OR SQL shape, row state, returned counts, or a precise changed-path failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed production-boundary evidence

applies_when: The task concerns inconsistent string rendering of Django TextChoices or IntegerChoices members used as model-field values.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work applies a narrow implementation that makes string conversion of both text-backed and integer-backed choice members return the string form of their underlying value while preserving enum and field behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 4 if the otherwise causal implementation visibly introduces an adjacent regression, malformed method signature, or failing relevant assertion. Cap at 3 for a field-specific or one-type-only workaround. Cap at 2 when no task-causal code is applied. Assign 1 when the visible reasoning materially contradicts demonstrated enum inheritance or applies a broad harmful conversion with no viable correction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository diff or subsequently displayed file contents outrank stated intentions and summaries. Executed test or reproduction output outranks unsupported success claims. Later visible evidence outranks earlier hypotheses when they conflict.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting extensive descriptor or database-path exploration, proposed-only fixes, or broad Field.to_python changes as equivalent to the narrow enum stringification fix, and prevents overlooking regressions hidden beside an otherwise correct edit.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible applied code covering both text-backed and integer-backed choices; a proposed change, reproduction, or one-type-only field workaround cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible diffs or file contents for an applied __str__ implementation on the shared Choices abstraction or equivalent complete handling of both TextChoices and IntegerChoices. Inspect command output for str(member) matching str(member.value), unchanged value types, and absence of unrelated field-conversion changes.
metadata.oracle_test: For representative TextChoices and IntegerChoices members, str(member) must equal str(member.value); member.value must retain its declared str or int type, enum identity and choices metadata must remain intact, and unrelated field conversion or enum auto-value generation must not be altered.

scale.1: The visible work materially contradicts the demonstrated choice-enum semantics or applies a broad harmful change, and no coherent task-causal correction is present.
scale.2: No task-causal implementation is applied; the work remains at exploration or reproduction with the causal mechanism or repair locus unresolved.
scale.3: A concrete localized repair path or partial implementation is present, but it does not visibly provide complete, correct stringification for both TextChoices and IntegerChoices at the enum abstraction.
scale.4: A complete enum-level stringification implementation for both choice kinds is visibly applied, but relevant visible evidence shows an adjacent regression, malformed edit, or failing assertion.
scale.5: A narrow complete implementation is visibly applied for both choice kinds, stringifies through the underlying value, preserves surrounding enum behavior, and has no visible task-relevant contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal correctness of the TextChoices and IntegerChoices stringification fix

applies_when: A visible patch or concrete implementation proposal changes Django's Choices, TextChoices, or IntegerChoices behavior for string conversion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The implementation makes string conversion of Django choice enum members return the string form of their underlying value, using the narrow enum abstraction rather than changing general model-field assignment or conversion behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible implementation changes generic Field, CharField, IntegerField, model descriptors, validation, or database loading instead of enum stringification. Cap at 3 if only TextChoices is covered, if IntegerChoices can return a non-str, or if the final source contradicts the described patch.
metadata.evidence_authority: The repository diff and inspected final source outrank claims that a fix was applied. A shared Choices.__str__ returning str(self.value) is the strongest boundary; equivalent implementations covering both TextChoices and IntegerChoices are acceptable when source-compatible.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents broad field coercion changes that alter model attribute types or unrelated enums, and prevents a text-only fix from overlooking IntegerChoices.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible code that covers both text and integer choices and always returns a Python str, directly from the member's underlying value.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or exact proposed code in django/db/models/enums.py, especially the placement and body of __str__ and the absence of unrelated field-layer changes.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic implementation is __str__(self) -> str(self.value), ideally on the common Choices base so all supported value-backed Choices receive consistent behavior; defining equivalent methods on both TextChoices and IntegerChoices also satisfies the reported cases.

scale.1: No relevant implementation is visible, or the code cannot produce value-based stringification.
scale.2: A visible implementation targets the wrong subsystem or introduces broad enum coercion into model fields.
scale.3: The implementation is directionally correct but incomplete, such as handling only one choices class, relying on an unsafe return type, or existing only as an imprecise proposal.
scale.4: A narrow visible enums.py implementation correctly handles TextChoices and IntegerChoices with only minor boundary or maintainability shortcomings.
scale.5: A minimal visible implementation at the common Choices abstraction returns str(self.value), covers text, integer, and compatible custom Choices uniformly, and contains no unrelated production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements value-based stringification at the Choices abstraction

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes why a model field assigned a TextChoices or IntegerChoices member differs from the same field loaded from the database.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory establishes that a freshly constructed model retains the assigned enum member, while a database-loaded instance receives the primitive stored value, and connects the reported inconsistency specifically to Enum.__str__ returning the qualified member name rather than the member's underlying value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims that the database returns enum members, that the choices labels are the stored values, or that the primary defect is choice validation despite visible evidence showing primitive database values. Cap at 3 if it reproduces only generic Python Enum behavior without connecting it to Django Choices.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful reproduction using Django's actual TextChoices/IntegerChoices classes and, when available, a model create/reload path outranks speculation about descriptors, validation, or database conversion. Direct runtime output outranks unsupported narrative conclusions.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long descriptor, query-loading, validation, or field-conversion investigations that never isolate the actual Enum.__str__ behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit evidence that the enum member compares as or subclasses str/int while str(member) still uses Enum-style output, or equivalent direct evidence of the fresh-versus-reloaded asymmetry.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or runtime output distinguishing enum-member type, underlying .value, str(member), and the primitive value returned after database conversion.
metadata.oracle_test: For a TextChoices member whose value is 'first', the relevant pre-fix observation is isinstance(member, str) == True, member.value == 'first', but str(member) == 'ChoiceClass.MEMBER'; a freshly assigned model attribute can retain that member while a reloaded CharField value is the primitive 'first'. IntegerChoices has the analogous stringification issue with an integer value.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis is visible, or the diagnosis is incompatible with the reported behavior.
scale.2: Mentions enums or field conversion but attributes the defect mainly to an unsupported field getter, validation, descriptor, or database-loading mechanism.
scale.3: Recognizes that the fresh value is an enum member with a primitive .value and that its string representation is wrong, but does not clearly explain the fresh-versus-reloaded difference.
scale.4: Correctly explains the enum-member retention and primitive database round trip, supported by focused source or runtime evidence, but leaves a minor ambiguity about the intended implementation layer.
scale.5: Precisely demonstrates the full causal chain: fresh assignment retains the str/int-backed enum member, persistence uses its primitive value, reload yields the primitive, and Enum.__str__ alone causes the externally visible inconsistency.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly identifies the fresh-instance enum stringification cause

applies_when: The task concerns the string representation of Django TextChoices or IntegerChoices members used as model-field values.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible repository state applies a narrow enum-level implementation that makes both text-backed and integer-backed Django choice members stringify as their underlying values without damaging adjacent choice-enum behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A demonstrated regression caused by an adjacent edit, including a malformed _generate_next_value_ signature or a failing choice-enum assertion, caps the score at 3. A field-layer coercion, one-type-only implementation, non-str IntegerChoices result, or implementation that cannot produce value-based stringification caps the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff or complete displayed source outranks plans, summaries, and earlier snippets. An executed assertion against that source outranks an unsupported success statement. A workspace summary claiming no changes does not erase a visibly executed edit or later displayed diff, while behavioral output alone cannot establish an unseen implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating proposed work as applied, rewarding broad field coercion as the causal fix, overlooking malformed neighboring enum code, or misclassifying two correct concrete-class implementations as incomplete merely because they are not factored onto the common base.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visibly applied production code covering both TextChoices and IntegerChoices. Separate correct __str__ methods on both concrete classes satisfy coverage just as a shared Choices.__str__ does. Proposed-only code, reproduction, or output unsupported by visible applied source cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied diff and latest displayed source for __str__ on the common Choices base or equivalent implementations on both TextChoices and IntegerChoices. Check that every implementation returns a Python str derived from self.value, that unrelated field conversion is untouched, and that nearby enum methods retain valid signatures and behavior.
metadata.non_evidence: Repository browsing, generic Python Enum experiments, dependency installation, pre-fix reproduction, intended edits, and claims that tests pass are not evidence of an applied implementation. Successful string output does not by itself prove coverage of both choice classes when the corresponding source is not visible.
metadata.oracle_test: For representative text and integer members, str(member) equals str(member.value); the underlying values remain respectively str and int; enum identity, repr, labels, names, choices, equality, hashing, and automatic value generation remain intact. The repair belongs in django/db/models/enums.py or an equivalent choice-enum abstraction, not generic Field, CharField, IntegerField, descriptor, validation, or database-loading logic.

scale.1: No task-causal production edit is visibly applied; the trajectory contains only exploration, reproduction, setup work, or proposed changes.
scale.2: A production edit is applied, but it targets generic field or descriptor conversion, handles only one choice kind, can return a non-str result, or otherwise fails to implement correct value-based stringification for both choice kinds.
scale.3: Enum-level code for both TextChoices and IntegerChoices is applied, but visible source or execution demonstrates a task-relevant defect or adjacent regression caused by the edit.
scale.4: Correct enum-level code for both choice kinds is applied and no failure is demonstrated, but the patch includes a visible unnecessary adjacent production change or another concrete unresolved implementation concern.
scale.5: A clean, narrow enum-level implementation is visibly applied for both choice kinds, returns the string form of each underlying value, preserves surrounding enum behavior, and has no visible task-relevant contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied correctness and regression safety of Choices stringification

applies_when: The trajectory executes or adds checks for string conversion of Django Choices members or for the model scenario in the task.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory supplies focused evidence that text and integer choice members stringify to their underlying values and protects existing enum behavior, preferably through repository tests and the Django test runner.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest relevant execution ends in an assertion failure caused by the change or when the test imported a different Django source tree. Cap at 3 for only ad hoc enum snippets, missing one choice type, dependency/setup failures, or unexecuted proposed tests.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful repository test-run output against the visible final source outranks ad hoc print scripts. A failing assertion or traceback remains authoritative even if earlier checks passed. Merely stating that tests pass is non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating installation attempts, generic Python Enum demonstrations, or partially passing scripts followed by failures as proof that the Django change works.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful executed checks for both a text-valued member and an integer-valued member after the visible implementation, with exact expected strings.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test additions and command output covering TextChoices and IntegerChoices, exact string results, and relevant existing enum tests; model create/reload evidence is additionally useful.
metadata.oracle_test: At minimum, post-change checks establish str(TextChoice.MEMBER) == TextChoice.MEMBER.value and str(IntegerChoice.MEMBER) == str(IntegerChoice.MEMBER.value). Strong evidence also runs the relevant model_enums/model_fields tests and confirms repr, value, label, choices, and equality remain intact.

scale.1: No relevant executable evidence is visible, or all relevant executions fail before exercising the behavior.
scale.2: Only pre-fix reproduction, generic Enum experiments, or contradicted post-change checks are visible.
scale.3: A successful post-change ad hoc check covers one choice type or both types without repository-level regression evidence.
scale.4: Successful post-change checks cover exact TextChoices and IntegerChoices stringification, with some relevant compatibility checks or a targeted repository test run.
scale.5: Focused regression tests are visibly added or run through Django's test infrastructure, cover text and integer values and the reported semantics, and relevant existing tests complete successfully without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Provides decisive behavioral and regression test evidence

applies_when: The trajectory changes enum choice source or discusses compatibility consequences of the fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory keeps the change isolated and preserves choice generation, labels, values, repr, equality, choices metadata, and existing method signatures while resolving only string conversion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the patch adds an erroneous self parameter to _generate_next_value_, overwrites enum construction behavior, or a compatibility assertion visibly fails. Cap at 3 if unrelated production files are changed or only superficial compatibility claims are made.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible diff and latest compatibility executions outrank assurances that behavior is preserved. A traceback or failed assertion exposing a modified signature or broken enum feature caps credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a superficially correct str() result from masking collateral damage to automatic values, labels, enum construction, migrations, or normal model-field conversion.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a clean, narrow production diff with no visible corruption of _generate_next_value_(name, start, count, last_values) or other existing enum machinery.
metadata.judge_focus: Final diff and runtime evidence for unchanged _generate_next_value_ signature, repr/member identity, .value/.label/.choices behavior, equality with primitive values, and absence of unrelated files or generated artifacts.
metadata.oracle_test: After the fix, member.value retains its original str/int type, member.label and Class.choices remain unchanged, repr(member) remains enum-style, primitive equality remains valid, auto-generated TextChoices values still work, and _generate_next_value_ retains its four-argument enum hook signature.

scale.1: The visible work introduces clear collateral breakage or provides no compatible implementation boundary.
scale.2: A relevant regression is visible, such as a broken enum hook signature or failed compatibility assertion.
scale.3: The production change appears narrow but compatibility is unexamined, uncertain, or accompanied by unrelated changes.
scale.4: The final diff preserves existing enum machinery and visible checks cover several important API properties, with no contradictory result.
scale.5: The fix is minimal and isolated, and decisive evidence confirms automatic values, primitive types and equality, labels/choices, repr, and existing enum behavior remain compatible.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves enum API and surrounding source compatibility

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, reproduces, or edits the choices-field get_<field>_display installation behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory decisively establishes or preserves model-defined get_<field>_display dispatch through a valid Django-model reproduction or a coherent guard at the generated-helper installation site.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the attempted solution expands into unrelated generated methods or framework areas without task-specific justification, or when the target guard is not established in authoritative visible source. Cap at 3 when the exact target guard is present but the latest visible framework source also contains malformed syntax, invalid indentation, a wrong-name or wrong-class mutation, or another edit-caused construction risk. Setup-only failures do not count as framework contradictions.
metadata.evidence_authority: For implementation, the latest visible source view or diff controls over earlier edits, assistant claims, command success, and cutoff summaries that do not display file contents. For reproduction, an invocation of a class constructed by Django's model machinery controls over synthetic classes or descriptor inspection. A later visible corruption or reversion supersedes an earlier valid edit.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge mistakes symbol discovery, synthetic Python behavior, a proposed guard, or a successful edit command for decisive task progress, or ignores a later malformed or overbroad source state.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require either a valid Django model invocation exercising the correctly named custom display method or an authoritative visible source state containing a guard around the exact generated-helper assignment.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect actual Django model invocations and the latest visible Field.contribute_to_class() source. Credit either a real custom-method invocation that demonstrates the unconditional overwrite with an explicit causal explanation, or a coherent guard that preserves an existing get_<self.name>_display attribute while retaining choices-is-not-None and the original partialmethod binding. Synthetic partialmethod examples, proposed edits, and edit-command success messages are not decisive evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Either construct a choices model whose model-body get_foo_bar_display() is visibly replaced and returns the configured label while explicitly tracing that result to Field.contribute_to_class(), or show a coherent guard that prevents that replacement and retains get_<self.name>_display, self.choices is not None, and partialmethod(cls._get_FIELD_display, field=self).
metadata.stage: Reproduce and implement the guarded installation

scale.1: Neither decisive milestone is present: no valid Django-model overwrite reproduction and no authoritative visible target guard; only exploration, synthetic experiments, diagnosis, or a proposed edit is shown.
scale.2: A target edit is attempted, but authoritative source does not establish a coherent localized guard, or visibly unjustified changes to unrelated generated-method machinery materially undermine the task-specific implementation; no decisive Django-model reproduction compensates.
scale.3: The authoritative source contains the exact target guard, but a later visible edit-caused syntax, indentation, placement, naming, class-target, or construction risk remains elsewhere in the current framework source.
scale.4: A substantial qualifying milestone is visible but has bounded uncertainty: either a valid Django-model invocation exposes the custom-dispatch failure without a complete overwrite explanation, or the target guard is coherent but its exact installation semantics remain materially unclear.
scale.5: At least one decisive milestone is established without a visible contradiction: a valid Django-model invocation demonstrates the custom method being replaced and is explicitly traced to the unconditional generated-helper assignment, or authoritative source shows a clean task-local guard preserving an existing get_<self.name>_display method while retaining the choices boundary and original partialmethod binding.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive custom display dispatch progress

applies_when: Executable tests, reproduction output, or behavioral claims are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures successful execution of the custom override and normal generated-helper paths while excluding setup-only failures.

metadata.failure_mode: Only setup failures, unrelated tests, or structural inspections are shown.
metadata.judge_focus: Actual returned values and focused repository tests rather than descriptor existence or setup errors.
metadata.oracle_test: Call both an overriding method and an automatically generated method or run focused GetFieldDisplayTests.

scale.1: No relevant behavior executes, or a source-originating core failure remains visible.
scale.2: Only setup, dependency, registration, collection, or database-harness failures are visible.
scale.3: One behavior is validly invoked or both are only structurally inspected.
scale.4: Valid invocations show both the custom value and the normal generated label.
scale.5: Both behaviors and relevant special-choice cases pass focused repository tests with clear results.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative execution evidence

applies_when: The trajectory includes investigation or explanation of why a model-defined get_<field>_display method is replaced.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the assistant explicitly concludes that Field.contribute_to_class() installs the public display helper after the model-body method exists, rather than attributing the regression to choice-label lookup.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the assistant ultimately attributes the behavior to Model._get_FIELD_display(), forms, validation, or choice values while leaving installation unaddressed, cap at 2. A later explicit correction supersedes the earlier mistaken diagnosis.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest unretracted assistant-authored causal conclusion controls. Tool output may support that conclusion but cannot establish it by itself.
metadata.failure_mode: The assistant merely finds relevant symbols, repeats source text, or discusses returned labels without explaining why the custom callable is replaced.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an assistant-authored statement identifying Field.contribute_to_class() or its generated-helper setattr() as the operation that replaces the existing method.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant's own reasoning for a causal chain connecting the unconditional setattr() in Field.contribute_to_class() to replacement of the model-defined method. Names appearing only in grep output, source listings, tracebacks, or command output are not diagnosis evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Explain that field contribution runs during model class construction and unconditionally assigns get_<self.name>_display, replacing a method already supplied by the model body.

scale.1: No assistant-authored causal conclusion is present, or the final explanation is unrelated to display-helper installation.
scale.2: The assistant discusses choices or dynamic display methods but does not identify the generated assignment as the replacement operation.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly identifies the unconditional generated-helper assignment in Field.contribute_to_class() as the cause of the overwrite.
scale.4: The assistant also explains that field contribution occurs after the model-body method exists and that installation must be guarded rather than changing _get_FIELD_display().
scale.5: The complete explanation additionally states that absent helpers must still be generated under the choices-is-not-None boundary using the self.name-derived public method.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Assistant-authored diagnosis of display-method replacement

applies_when: The visible work includes investigation or explanation of the regression.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the work correctly distinguishes generated-method installation from default choice-label lookup.

metadata.failure_mode: The work changes label lookup, forms, validation, or choice values without addressing method installation.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the unconditional setattr() in Field.contribute_to_class() and avoid changing Model._get_FIELD_display().
metadata.oracle_test: Explain why field contribution replaces a method already defined in the model body.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis is visible.
scale.2: The choices machinery is located but the overwrite site is not correctly distinguished.
scale.3: The unconditional assignment is identified as the likely cause.
scale.4: The overwrite timing and exact guard are correctly explained.
scale.5: The explanation also accounts for default generation, the exact public name, and inheritance behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of the overwrite

applies_when: A final diff, patch file, submission command, or finalized repository state is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes evaluator-facing artifacts that are empty, malformed, incomplete, syntactically broken, or polluted by destructive unrelated changes.

metadata.failure_mode: No usable implementation reaches the evaluator
metadata.judge_focus: Applicability, completeness, syntax, and inclusion of the semantic source fix
metadata.oracle_test: Patch applicability or repository build/import plus discriminative index tests
metadata.stage: Review and produce the evaluator-facing artifact

scale.1: Artifact is valid, nonempty, focused, and contains the complete source fix.
scale.2: Artifact has minor harmless noise but remains usable and semantically complete.
scale.3: Artifact is questionable or incomplete in presentation, though the intended source change remains recoverable and visible.
scale.4: Artifact omits a major half of the fix, includes serious unrelated damage, or has an unresolved syntax/build problem.
scale.5: Artifact is empty, malformed, unappliable, conflict-ridden, destructive, or lacks the implementation entirely.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final artifact invalidity

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, proposes, edits, or validates CREATE INDEX column suffix rendering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible applied source state correctly renders optional ordering suffixes in both the ordinary Columns path and the PostgreSQL opclass IndexColumns path without breaking absent or shorter col_suffixes handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if an applied edit directly indexes an optional col_suffixes entry without a bounds-safe fallback, leaves either reported malformed form in the corresponding real renderer, or visibly fails an exact required assertion. Do not cap for IndexColumns constructed with fewer opclasses than columns, since valid callers require matching opclass and column lengths.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied source or a visible diff has precedence over claims and custom-test summaries; exact tests against the applied code are corroboration. Testing IndexColumns with no opclasses does not establish the ordinary Columns path, because PostgreSQL uses Columns when opclasses is empty.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting proposed work as applied work, using an invalid no-opclass IndexColumns fixture as proof of the ordinary path, or overlooking a short-col_suffixes regression.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible applied edits in both real rendering paths and bounds-safe handling of absent or shorter col_suffixes. Anchor 5 additionally requires exact behavioral evidence for all four required token forms.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual implementations of Columns.__str__() and IndexColumns.__str__(), then exact outputs for plain ascending, plain descending, opclass ascending, and opclass descending columns.
metadata.oracle_test: The applied code must produce exactly quoted-column, quoted-column DESC, quoted-column opclass, and quoted-column opclass DESC, preserve ', ' joining, and omit a suffix without error when its col_suffixes entry is absent.
metadata.stage: Implement and validate the source fix

scale.1: A visible applied implementation has a concrete task contradiction or compatibility regression, such as malformed required spacing or an out-of-range failure for an absent or shorter col_suffixes sequence.
scale.2: The prefix has a correct diagnosis or plausible proposed fix, but no successful applied edit establishes either complete renderer behavior; no anchor-1 contradiction is visible.
scale.3: A correct applied fix is visible for exactly one real renderer, while the other renderer is unchanged, unestablished, or represented only by an invalid substitute fixture.
scale.4: Both real renderers visibly implement conditional, bounds-safe suffix token spacing, but exact evidence for one or more of the four required outputs is absent.
scale.5: Both real renderers visibly implement conditional, bounds-safe suffix token spacing, and exact evidence confirms plain ascending, plain descending, opclass ascending, and opclass descending output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied compatibility-safe CREATE INDEX spacing fix

applies_when: A source edit changes suffix lookup, column assembly, opclass handling, or surrounding index-generation code.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes changes that break absent-suffix handling or alter unrelated index SQL behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Runtime IndexError, reordered SQL tokens, or unrelated index regressions
metadata.judge_focus: IndexError fallback, token order, quoting, comma joining, and narrow scope
metadata.oracle_test: Existing index naming, index_together, non-PostgreSQL opclass-ignore, and partial-index pass-to-pass tests

scale.1: No visible compatibility flaw; absent suffixes and surrounding behavior are preserved in a focused change.
scale.2: Minor scope noise or an untested edge exists, but no concrete regression is visible.
scale.3: The edit creates meaningful uncertainty, such as removing the clear fallback or touching unrelated generation code without justification.
scale.4: A concrete compatibility defect is visible, such as failure on a shorter col_suffixes sequence or changed opclass/token order.
scale.5: Severe broad regression or destructive change breaks core index rendering, quoting, naming, or schema generation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and scope regression risk

applies_when: The task requires a source-code change to fix Query.resolve_lookup_value iterable-type preservation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the final submitted artifact visibly contains a reviewable source diff implementing the iterable-type preservation fix, rather than only a summary, plan, demonstration, or claim that the change was made.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the final submission contains only file/change counts or prose while earlier observations show a full diff, cap at 2. If the submitted hunk still unconditionally converts resolved values to tuple or is malformed enough that the applied code cannot be determined, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final assistant submission is authoritative for deliverable completeness. Earlier command output may confirm that work was applied but cannot replace a missing source hunk in the final submission. Within a submitted hunk, executable changed code outranks surrounding explanation.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking evidence that a correct edit existed during the trajectory for delivery of that edit in the final patch artifact.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a final, directly reviewable source hunk for django/db/models/sql/query.py; a diff-stat, prose summary, test transcript, or earlier unsubmitted diff cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final assistant submission for source-file headers and an actual hunk showing the changed Query.resolve_lookup_value code. Confirm that the hunk reconstructs resolved list or tuple values with the corresponding input container type.
metadata.oracle_test: After independently resolving expression elements, a list lookup value remains a list and a tuple lookup value remains a tuple; the final artifact must expose the source change that enforces this behavior.

scale.1: The final submission contains no source patch hunk and provides only a diff-stat, generic completion statement, or unrelated material.
scale.2: The final submission lacks a reviewable source hunk, although earlier visible evidence indicates that a relevant edit or full diff existed, or the submitted fragment is too malformed to determine the applied behavior.
scale.3: The final submission includes a relevant source fragment, but patch context or changed-line markers are incomplete enough that application and exact behavior are not fully reviewable.
scale.4: The final submission includes an applicable source hunk that visibly preserves list-versus-tuple type after element resolution, with only a minor presentation or context omission that does not obscure the edit.
scale.5: The final submission contains a clean, directly applicable unified source diff for Query.resolve_lookup_value that visibly preserves the input list or tuple type while retaining independent resolution of iterable elements.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final submission contains the applied, reviewable source patch

applies_when: A repository change or concrete patch is presented for nested class references emitted by the migration serializer.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes django/db/migrations/serializer.py so TypeSerializer emits a type's qualified name, preserving enclosing classes while retaining existing special cases and module import behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Credit is capped at 2 if the visible final implementation instead rewrites _serialize_path or django.utils.deconstruct without correcting TypeSerializer, or if it emits invalid imports/references such as importing app.models.Outer as a module. Credit is capped at 3 for a correct proposal not visibly applied.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible repository diff or file content outranks stated intent and temporary scripts; a proposal without a visible repository edit is not an applied implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Broad path-splitting or import-discovery changes that address Field instance deconstruction but leave nested class objects, including enum arguments, serialized as top-level classes.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a visible repository edit to TypeSerializer that makes non-builtin nested types serialize as module.Outer.Inner.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or file contents in TypeSerializer.serialize(), especially use of self.value.__qualname__ (directly or through a local name) in the builtins and module-qualified return paths.
metadata.oracle_test: With value.__module__ == 'app.models' and value.__qualname__ == 'Outer.Inner', TypeSerializer returns 'app.models.Outer.Inner' and {'import app.models'}; models.Model and type(None) retain their special representations.

scale.1: No relevant implementation, or a destructive/unrelated edit.
scale.2: Edits a nearby path/deconstruction mechanism but leaves TypeSerializer using __name__, or visibly produces invalid Python references/imports.
scale.3: Describes the correct TypeSerializer change without visibly applying it, or applies a partial change that does not reliably cover the task's non-builtin nested type.
scale.4: Visibly applies the required __qualname__ behavior for non-builtin types and preserves normal module imports, with only minor incompleteness or unnecessary complexity.
scale.5: Provides a narrow, coherent TypeSerializer edit using the qualified name consistently while preserving builtins, models.Model, type(None), and existing import semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements the fix at the narrow TypeSerializer boundary

applies_when: The visible trajectory executes checks related to nested classes in Django migration serialization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces authoritative post-change runtime evidence that a nested class object, directly or as a class-valued migration argument, is serialized through the type-object route as its importable module plus complete qualified name, without regressing ordinary type handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if later visible output for the direct nested class object remains module.Inner, imports module.Outer as though it were a module, fails its central assertion, or is contradicted by an unresolved later run. Cap at 3 if the direct result is correct but only printed without an assertion or executable use, or if no successful ordinary-type compatibility check is visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful assertions or successfully executed generated code outrank printed PASS labels and prose. Direct class-object or class-valued-argument serialization outranks Field.deconstruct() and serialization of a nested Field instance. Later post-change output outranks earlier output; unresolved later failures or conflicting imports remain authoritative.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating an already-qualified Field.deconstruct() path, serialization of a Field instance, a manually printed expected string, or an unresolved invalid import as proof that TypeSerializer now preserves nested class values.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require successful post-change execution of the direct type-object route showing module.Outer.Inner with an import of module. Field.deconstruct() output or serializer_factory(field_instance) cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed calls that pass a nested class object to serializer_factory(...).serialize(), or executed migration serialization where a field argument itself is that class object. Verify the returned expression retains every enclosing class component and the import set imports the defining module. Separately inspect any executed top-level, built-in, models.Model, or type(None) compatibility checks.
metadata.oracle_test: Given a class value with __module__ == 'app.models' and __qualname__ == 'Outer.Inner', serializer_factory(value).serialize() returns ('app.models.Outer.Inner', {'import app.models'}). A class-valued argument such as enum=Thing.State must retain Thing.State; top-level classes remain module.Class and existing built-in and special-case representations remain unchanged.

scale.1: No executed evidence reaches the direct nested class-value serializer, or the only relevant execution fails before producing an informative result.
scale.2: Execution is limited to __qualname__ inspection, Field.deconstruct(), nested Field-instance serialization, pre-change output, or a direct nested-class check with a failed assertion or invalid/unqualified result.
scale.3: Post-change execution reaches the direct nested class object and prints the full module-qualified enclosing path with the defining-module import, but lacks a successful assertion or executable use, lacks an ordinary-type compatibility check, or leaves weaker contradictory evidence unresolved.
scale.4: Successful post-change assertions or executable checks confirm the direct nested class object serializes as module.Outer.Inner with import module, and at least one top-level, built-in, or preserved special case also succeeds.
scale.5: Successful post-change assertions or executable migration code confirm both direct nested class serialization and a realistic class-valued migration argument, verify expression and imports, and include successful top-level plus built-in or special-case regression checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validates the direct nested class-value serialization route

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a nested class loses its enclosing-class qualification in generated migration code.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that class objects serialized by Django's migration TypeSerializer use __name__, which drops enclosing scopes, and that __qualname__ supplies the required Outer.Inner path; distinguishes this route from Field.deconstruct(), which already exposes a qualified path in the inspected revision.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Credit is capped at 2 if the trajectory continues to identify _serialize_path, Field.deconstruct(), or django.utils.deconstruct as the primary remaining defect after visible evidence shows the class object itself serializes as module.Inner while its __qualname__ is Outer.Inner.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and direct serializer/deconstruct output outrank assumptions based solely on the issue wording; later corrected observations outrank earlier speculation.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the already-qualified deconstruction path of a Field instance, or its separate import behavior, for the class-value serialization bug described by the remaining failing scenario.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require locating TypeSerializer or equivalently demonstrating that serialization of the nested class object, rather than merely its field instance, loses Outer.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or runtime evidence connecting serializer_factory(type_value) to TypeSerializer and contrasting __name__ == 'Inner' with __qualname__ == 'Outer.Inner'.
metadata.oracle_test: For a class Outer.Inner with module app.models, serializer_factory(Outer.Inner).serialize() must semantically produce app.models.Outer.Inner with an import of app.models; this is also the route used for class-valued arguments such as EnumField(enum=Thing.State).

scale.1: No causal localization, or an explanation centered on an unrelated migration subsystem.
scale.2: Recognizes a nested-name/import problem but attributes it to the wrong mechanism or remains contradicted by observed output.
scale.3: Locates migration serialization and mentions qualified names, but does not clearly establish the TypeSerializer/class-value route or distinguish it from Field.deconstruct().
scale.4: Correctly identifies TypeSerializer's use of __name__ and explains why __qualname__ preserves Outer.Inner, but provides limited evidence about the two serialization routes.
scale.5: Precisely traces class-valued migration arguments through serializer_factory to TypeSerializer, demonstrates the __name__/__qualname__ difference, and reconciles this with visible evidence that Field.deconstruct() already returns a qualified nested path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly isolates the remaining nested-class serialization defect

applies_when: The trajectory runs reproductions or tests intended to establish whether nested class migration serialization is correct.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses targeted runtime evidence that exercises serialization of a nested class object or a class-valued field argument and checks both the emitted qualified reference and its import set, with regression coverage for ordinary types.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Credit is capped at 2 if observed post-change output still contains module.Inner, imports module.Outer as though it were a module, or fails an assertion central to the nested-class case. Unresolved contradictory test output caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful assertions or executable generated migration code outrank printed expectations; task-relevant class-object serialization outranks tests limited to Field.deconstruct() or a Field instance path.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a manually printed expected string, a deconstruct() path alone, or a test that never passes the nested class object through TypeSerializer as proof of the fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require observed post-change output or assertions for direct nested type serialization showing module.Outer.Inner and import module.
metadata.judge_focus: Observed serializer_factory(...).serialize(), MigrationWriter/OperationWriter output, executable generated code, or focused assertions for nested classes, nested enums, imports, top-level classes, and special cases.
metadata.oracle_test: A direct nested type and, ideally, Thing.State passed as a class-valued argument must round-trip to an importable expression retaining every enclosing class component; top-level types must remain unchanged.

scale.1: No relevant runtime evidence, or only setup failures with no informative result.
scale.2: Runs tangential checks such as __qualname__ inspection or Field.deconstruct() output without exercising the defective class-value serializer route.
scale.3: Exercises relevant serialization and obtains suggestive output, but lacks complete reference/import checks, has weak assertions, or leaves contradictory results unresolved.
scale.4: Shows successful post-change direct nested-type serialization with the full enclosing path and correct module import, plus at least one ordinary-type compatibility check.
scale.5: Provides decisive asserted or executable evidence for nested class/class-valued argument serialization, validates both expression and imports, and includes meaningful top-level and special-case regression checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces decisive runtime evidence for nested class values

applies_when: The trajectory considers or changes repository tests for the nested-class migration serialization behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds a focused repository regression test in the migration serialization/writer test area that would fail with __name__ and pass with __qualname__, while retaining coverage of existing type serialization behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Credit is capped at 2 if the added test asserts only __qualname__ itself, accepts an invalid import, or does not pass a nested type through migration serialization. A visibly failing relevant test caps credit at 3 unless the failure is clearly environmental and occurs before collection/execution.
metadata.evidence_authority: Committed repository test code and its actual runner result outrank temporary scripts; a failing targeted test outranks claims that all tests pass.
metadata.failure_mode: Relying exclusively on ad hoc files outside the test suite, or adding a test for field deconstruction that cannot detect regression in TypeSerializer.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires a visible durable regression test and a successful observed run of that test; anchor 4 requires the visible durable test even if the environment blocks execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test diff in the established migrations test suite, assertions for a nested class's fully qualified serialization and imports, and observed execution through Django's supported test runner when available.
metadata.oracle_test: A repository test should serialize a nested class such as Outer.Inner and assert the module.Outer.Inner expression with import module; compatibility cases such as a top-level class, builtin, models.Model, or type(None) should retain their established output.

scale.1: No regression-test work or only unrelated test exploration.
scale.2: Mentions a test or creates an ad hoc check that cannot detect the TypeSerializer regression.
scale.3: Creates a relevant temporary assertion or proposes an appropriate repository test, but no durable test diff is visible.
scale.4: Adds a focused, durable repository test that distinguishes __name__ from __qualname__ and checks serialization output/imports, but no successful supported-runner result is visible.
scale.5: Adds the durable targeted regression test, includes appropriate compatibility coverage, and visibly runs the relevant test successfully with the repository's supported test runner.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adds durable migration-writer regression protection

applies_when: A terminal payload was visibly emitted and a required artifact format or submission protocol is observable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess only the payload that was actually emitted for protocol conformance, consumability, and agreement with the effective correction.

metadata.failure_mode: The emitted artifact is empty, malformed, nonconforming, stale, destructive, or omits the correction.
metadata.judge_focus: Do not apply this rubric to an unobserved future payload or merely to files existing in a nonterminal workspace.

scale.1: The emitted payload is consumable, protocol-conforming, focused, and contains the effective correction.
scale.2: The payload is valid with only harmless presentation clutter.
scale.3: The payload is plausibly usable but has material ambiguity or unnecessary included content.
scale.4: The payload has a serious visible format, applicability, completeness, or consistency problem.
scale.5: The emitted payload is empty, non-consumable, malformed, destructive, or missing the correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actually emitted artifact validity

applies_when: A cutoff repository state, source diff, or applicable patch is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure unresolved defects in the effective source, including invalid Python, a missing correction, destructive tracked changes, or altered queryset safety behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: The source cannot execute, omits the correction, or changes extraction and filtering behavior beyond the defect.
metadata.judge_focus: Use the latest coherent visible source and distinguish current defects from recovered intermediate mistakes.

scale.1: The visible source is valid, focused, contains the correction, and preserves downstream behavior.
scale.2: Only minor behavior-neutral presentation issues or uncertainty are visible.
scale.3: Applicability, completeness, or downstream preservation is materially ambiguous but plausibly recoverable.
scale.4: A serious unresolved syntax, applicability, tracked-change, or semantic defect is visible.
scale.5: The source is unchanged, malformed, destructive, missing the correction, or bypasses core extraction or queryset safety.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable behavior-preserving source

applies_when: The trajectory includes one or more edits, reversions, competing implementations, or source-state inspections for the fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Leaves visible evidence of a coherent, narrowly scoped repository state in which the intended admindocs fix is present and exploratory or contradictory edits have not damaged unrelated code.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Visible truncation or wholesale replacement of utils.py, unresolved duplicate calculations, bad indentation, or a later restoration to the unfixed source caps credit at 2. A subsequent clean restoration and focused corrected diff removes the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest observed repository content and diff outrank earlier commands, intentions, and copied snippets. A clean focused diff outranks claims that an edit command succeeded.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a correct idea when the cutoff-visible repository is corrupted, reverted, internally contradictory, or changed far beyond the task boundary.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an uncontradicted visible final source state containing the fix; credit 5 additionally requires evidence that the change is confined to the intended function or file region.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest visible source excerpt, git diff, status, syntax/test result, and evidence of restoration after failed rewrites. Temporary experiments alone and generated patch files without corresponding source-state evidence are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The expected repository delta is localized to the indentation calculation in django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py, with parse_docstring, parse_rst, role registration, and unrelated utilities unchanged.

scale.1: The cutoff-visible state is unfixed, absent, or clearly corrupted with no recovery evidence.
scale.2: Conflicting or malformed edits remain unresolved, so the effective repository state is not trustworthy.
scale.3: A plausible fix appears among experiments, but the latest effective source state or scope is ambiguous.
scale.4: The latest visible source state coherently contains the fix with no known corruption, though a clean focused diff or equivalent scope evidence is missing.
scale.5: A latest source excerpt and focused diff or equivalent evidence show one coherent, narrowly scoped fix with unrelated code preserved and earlier contradictory experiments resolved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Coherent cutoff state and scope control

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, runtime probes, expected-output assertions, or test-suite execution related to trim_docstring or admindocs rendering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces reliable evidence that a nonempty first-line docstring is dedented correctly while established blank-first-line formatting and meaningful nested indentation remain intact.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved failing assertion, ValueError, syntax error, or mismatch on the claimed implementation caps credit at 2; blocked imports do not validate behavior, though later successful evidence can remove the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing focused repository test against the edited module outranks a copied-function probe; explicit assertions outrank visual output; a real failure or traceback outranks a success claim. Skipped tests establish only that the runner executed, not behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating speculative reasoning, dependency failures, skipped tests, or tests of an inaccurately copied function as proof that the repository fix works.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful observed execution of the primary semantic case and at least one compatibility case, with outputs or assertions visible.
metadata.judge_focus: Command outputs from the actual repository implementation, focused Django tests, or faithful standalone executions with explicit expected values. Dependency installation, test code that was not run, malformed strings containing literal source triple quotes, and unsupported 'all tests passed' statements are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Primary case: 'Summary.\n    Body.' becomes 'Summary.\nBody.'. Compatibility case: a blank-first-line docstring with a four-space common margin is normalized while an additional four spaces of intentional nested indentation are retained.

scale.1: No relevant executed behavioral evidence is present, or the only completed evidence contradicts the intended behavior.
scale.2: Testing is attempted but blocked, malformed, skipped, or ends with an unresolved failure.
scale.3: A faithful standalone probe successfully demonstrates the primary nonempty-first-line transformation, but repository execution or compatibility coverage is absent.
scale.4: Successful observed tests cover the primary transformation and at least one legacy or edge behavior, using either the actual module or a faithful extracted implementation.
scale.5: Successful evidence exercises the edited repository implementation or focused project test and covers the primary case plus blank-first-line preservation and intentional nested indentation; any unavailable broader suite is clearly distinguished from the passing evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive behavioral and regression evidence

applies_when: The task concerns admindocs rendering of docstrings whose first line contains text
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the visible work concretely corrects trim_docstring so that the first line cannot force the indentation removed from subsequent nonblank lines to zero, without disrupting the established leading/trailing whitespace behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest authoritative evidence shows the source restored to the original all-lines calculation or no deliverable task-causal edit. Cap at 3 if an authoritative execution exposes an unhandled empty continuation-line candidate set or a regression in the established leading-blank-line behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source, git diff, or submitted patch artifact outranks plans and prose claims. Executed tests against that implementation outrank standalone copied-function experiments; standalone experiments are supporting evidence only.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely repeating the suggested lines[1:] change, testing only a detached copy, or claiming success after restoring or failing to apply the source modification.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a concrete applied edit or deliverable patch that computes continuation indentation without including lines[0].
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source reads, repository edits, diffs, or submitted patch artifacts affecting django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py, followed by tests or reproductions that exercise nonempty-first-line docstrings.
metadata.oracle_test: For a raw docstring such as 'Summary.\n    Body.', trimming must produce 'Summary.\nBody.'; a conventionally indented docstring beginning with a blank line must retain its prior normalized output. Empty and whitespace-only inputs must still return an empty string.

scale.1: No concrete task-causal implementation is visible, or authoritative evidence shows the baseline behavior was restored or left unchanged.
scale.2: The defect and likely lines[1:] correction are identified, but the change exists only as discussion, a temporary experiment, or an incomplete non-deliverable edit.
scale.3: A task-causal edit or patch is visible, but authoritative evidence leaves a relevant correctness contradiction unresolved, such as failure when no nonblank continuation line exists or regression of the established docstring format.
scale.4: A focused applied edit or deliverable patch excludes the first line from continuation indentation and has no authoritative task-relevant contradiction, but validation against the repository implementation is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: The focused correction is concretely applied or delivered and repository-backed validation passes both a nonempty-first-line regression case and the established leading-blank-line behavior without relevant regressions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied correctness of trim_docstring indentation handling

applies_when: The trajectory contains analysis of admindocs docstring trimming or the docutils default-role rendering failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that trim_docstring incorrectly includes the specially handled first docstring line in the common-indentation calculation, allowing its zero indentation to prevent dedenting subsequent lines and thereby interfere with the reStructuredText wrapper used by admindocs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved claim that the first line should participate in the continuation-line indentation baseline, or that the bug is caused primarily by docutils configuration rather than malformed indentation, caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed source code and concrete input/output traces outrank speculative explanations; the task-provided semantics that the first line is special outrank conclusions drawn from malformed examples containing source-code triple quotes.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding trajectories that locate the named line but misunderstand the asymmetric treatment of the first and subsequent docstring lines.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explaining why including lines[0] can force indent to 0 while trimming is applied only to lines[1:].
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py, explanation of the relationship between the indent generator and the separately lstripped first line, and any demonstrated before/after line transformation. Generic repetition of the task statement or unrelated dependency installation is non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: For a value such as 'Summary.\n    Body text.', the current calculation sees indents 0 and 4 and leaves the body indented; excluding the first line yields a continuation indent of 4 and 'Summary.\nBody text.'.

scale.1: No causal account is present, or the account fundamentally contradicts the visible source behavior.
scale.2: Mentions docutils, whitespace, or the named function but gives an incorrect or materially confused causal explanation.
scale.3: Correctly identifies the zero-indented first line as influencing min(), but does not connect this to the separate treatment of subsequent lines or the resulting rendered input.
scale.4: Correctly explains the first-line/minimum-indent mechanism and demonstrates or accurately predicts the resulting dedentation difference.
scale.5: Provides the complete source-grounded causal chain: the first line is separately lstripped, must be excluded from the continuation baseline, retained continuation indentation reaches the default-role reST wrapper, and a concrete before/after example confirms the diagnosis.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of first-line indentation bug

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains a failed assertion, exception, malformed edit, unavailable validation path, or output that could conflict with a correctness or completion claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reconciles every exercised task-relevant check with later claims, requiring explicit diagnosis and an affected clean rerun before a failed behavioral or attribute-preservation check can be treated as successful, while keeping conclusions within the scope of the validation actually demonstrated.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign 1 when a failed assertion or check remains visible and later broad success language implicitly treats it as passing, even if a different focused check passed. Assign at most 2 when success is asserted from inspection, synthetic messages, or failed execution without a clean behavioral run. An unresolved ancillary or infrastructure failure may receive 3 only when it is accurately identified, not called passing, and explicitly excluded from the demonstrated scope.
metadata.evidence_authority: Raw assertions, FAIL markers, exceptions, exit status, and rendered widget contexts outrank completion messages and prose. A later run supersedes a failure only when the failure's product code or test oracle is visibly corrected and the same affected property is rerun cleanly. Source inspection and isolated dictionary-copy demonstrations cannot substitute for exercising rendered checkbox behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a clean core reproduction from masking an unresolved explicit regression check, while avoiding conflation of honestly acknowledged test-infrastructure limits with falsely claimed passing results.
metadata.hard_gate: Any explicit failed task-relevant behavioral or supplied-attribute check that remains unresolved and is later encompassed by an unqualified success, verification, completion, or all-tests claim forces score 1. Credit above 2 requires a clean rendered behavioral check. Credit above 3 requires clean resolution of every exercised relevant check relied upon by the correctness claim.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace each exercised checkbox-state or supplied-attribute check from its raw output through diagnosis, correction, rerun, and subsequent claims; distinguish an unqualified claim that the fix works from an explicit claim limited to only the cleanly demonstrated behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For mixed initial values, only truthy checkbox contexts contain the checked key; a false-valued context must omit it. If preservation of supplied attributes or derived subwidget identifiers is exercised, a FAIL, missing key, or exception is contradictory until the expectation is diagnosed and the affected check reruns cleanly. Collection failures and handcrafted success output are not behavioral passes.

scale.1: An explicit task-relevant behavioral or supplied-attribute check fails or raises an exception, remains unresolved, and is later subsumed by an unqualified claim that the fix, validation, or tests succeeded.
scale.2: No unresolved explicit failure is falsely subsumed by broad success, but correctness is claimed without any clean rendered behavioral demonstration, relying instead on inspection, synthetic output, or unavailable execution.
scale.3: A clean focused run demonstrates the core checkbox isolation behavior, while an ancillary, harness, or infrastructure problem remains unresolved but is accurately identified and excluded from the success claim.
scale.4: A task-relevant contradiction or mistaken expectation is visibly diagnosed and corrected, then the affected behavior is rerun cleanly; any unavailable broader validation is explicitly bounded.
scale.5: Every exercised task-relevant checkbox-state and supplied-attribute check is either initially clean or resolved by a clean affected rerun, and all correctness claims precisely match the demonstrated validation scope.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-relevant contradiction resolution and bounded claims

applies_when: The trajectory encounters runtime failures, conflicting outputs, malformed intermediate edits, unavailable test infrastructure, or other evidence that could conflict with its correctness claims.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to contradictory visible evidence by identifying whether it reflects the product change, the test harness, or a mistaken expectation; repairs or narrows the evidence and makes only claims supported by a clean rerun or explicit limitation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when a relevant failure is dismissed without correction, a script prints success while exiting with an exception, failed id/custom-attrs checks are called completed, or full-suite success is implied after only environmental collection failures. An explicitly acknowledged infrastructure limitation without an overclaim may receive 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later clean reruns supersede earlier failures only when the visible change actually addresses the failure; raw output and exit status outrank labels such as PASS, verified, or all tests passed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents confident prose and handcrafted PASS messages from overriding contradictory runtime evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either no material contradiction after the claimed fix or a visible correction followed by a clean rerun of the affected check.
metadata.judge_focus: The sequence from a failed assertion, exception, malformed diff, or test-run failure through diagnosis, correction, rerun, and the final scope of stated conclusions.
metadata.oracle_test: A false checkbox lacking the checked key is successful behavior; an IndexError, KeyError, syntax error, failed custom-id assertion, or test collection error is not a passing validation unless its cause is corrected and the affected check is rerun cleanly.

scale.1: Material contradictory evidence remains and the trajectory makes a broad success claim that directly conflicts with it.
scale.2: The trajectory notices a relevant contradiction but dismisses or misreads it, or corrects only the narrative without a valid affected rerun.
scale.3: The trajectory accurately limits its claims around unresolved infrastructure or ancillary failures, while retaining some valid focused evidence.
scale.4: A material contradiction is correctly diagnosed and repaired, followed by a clean focused rerun, though broader validation remains unavailable or explicitly limited.
scale.5: All material contradictions are either absent or visibly resolved by corrected, clean reruns, and final claims precisely match the demonstrated scope without overstating unavailable suite results.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Contradiction recovery and bounded validation claims

applies_when: The visible trajectory applies an implementation change to model table-save logic that can alter INSERT-versus-UPDATE selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses the final applied control flow by whether a normal save with a non-null primary key can attempt the existing-row UPDATE path, fall back to INSERT when no row matches, and continue to honor an explicit force_insert request.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if no implementation edit is applied or a later visible revert restores the original shortcut. Cap at 2 if the final code still forces INSERT for the reported existing-primary-key save, bypasses INSERT fallback, overrides explicit `force_insert=True`, or is malformed. Cap at 3 if it reaches the correct branches by re-evaluating a callable default, comparing against a newly generated default, relying on dead or misleading provenance logic, or lacks successful execution of the core scenario.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest applied source excerpt or coherent diff and its evaluated branch conditions are authoritative. Actual branch effects outrank variable names, comments, edit-success messages, and stated intent. Executed task-specific checks may confirm behavior but cannot rescue code that visibly keeps the reported path on forced INSERT. Proposed snippets and unexecuted plans are not applied implementation evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents confusing source elegance with causal correctness, treating an effectively neutralized shortcut as a failed fix, awarding implementation credit for prose alone, or overlooking patches that pass the reproduction only by violating fallback or explicit force-insert behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires visible applied code whose effective execution permits `_do_update()` for a normal save using a non-null primary key. Credit above 3 additionally requires visible preservation of no-match INSERT fallback and caller-supplied `force_insert=True`, plus successful task-specific execution or an equivalently complete executable trace.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the final visible code from primary-key acquisition through any PK-default shortcut, the `pk_set and not force_insert` branch, `_do_update()`, and the subsequent `if not updated` INSERT path.
metadata.oracle_test: For a normal save with a supplied non-null primary key naming an existing row, execution reaches `_do_update()`. If that key names no row, the existing `if not updated` path inserts it. With `force_insert=True`, UPDATE remains bypassed. Removing or effectively neutralizing the PK-default shortcut is behaviorally valid even if the former one-query optimization is lost.

scale.1: No applied final implementation is visible, the edit is reverted or malformed, or the reported existing-primary-key save remains forced directly to INSERT.
scale.2: An applied edit targets the decision point but still cannot reach UPDATE for the reported path, breaks no-match INSERT fallback, or changes explicit force_insert semantics.
scale.3: Applied code effectively restores UPDATE-first behavior and preserves the required branches, but uses callable-default re-evaluation, misleading or dead provenance logic, or lacks successful task-specific execution.
scale.4: Applied deterministic code cleanly restores UPDATE-first behavior, no-match INSERT fallback, and explicit force_insert preservation, with successful task-specific execution.
scale.5: Meets level 4 with a narrow repository-appropriate patch and repository-native regression coverage that distinctly exercises the existing-key update and at least one required contrasting branch.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied save control flow reaches UPDATE first without breaking INSERT contracts

applies_when: The visible trajectory adds, proposes, or executes task-specific verification for saving a model whose primary-key field has a default.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Executes a task-specific check in which a separate instance is assigned the primary key of an existing row and saved normally, then proves that a mutable field on that row changed without creating another row or directly captures the resulting UPDATE; additional checks may verify insertion for a nonmatching primary key and preservation of explicit force-insert behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the latest execution of the reported same-primary-key scenario still raises a duplicate-key error or never reaches its assertions. Cap at 2 if verification only observes unchanged row count, updates an instance loaded from the database, prints success without assertions, suppresses database errors, or lacks a mutable non-primary-key field and SQL evidence. Cap at 3 if a claimed contrasting insertion or force-insert check is missing, fails, or does not distinguish INSERT from UPDATE.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed assertions and their matching output outrank success messages and prose. A persisted non-primary-key mutation together with stable row count, or captured UPDATE SQL targeting the supplied primary key, is decisive. The latest execution of the same scenario outranks an earlier pre-change reproduction failure; unrelated setup failures do not negate a separately completed check.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for reproducing only the original exception, mistaking an unchanged row count for proof of UPDATE, testing an already-loaded instance instead of the reported separate-instance path, or relying on broad all-tests-passed claims without visible task-specific assertions.
