metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a successful executed check using a separate instance with the existing explicit primary key and decisive evidence of an update rather than mere survival of the old row. Credit above 3 requires at least one successfully asserted contrasting insert path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible test setup, executable assertions, captured SQL, persisted non-primary-key values, row counts, and matching command output for the separate-instance explicit-primary-key save.
metadata.oracle_test: Create a row whose primary key field has a default, construct a different instance with that row's primary key and a changed ordinary field, save it normally, and verify one row remains and the stored field changed. For broader coverage, save a separate instance with a nonmatching primary key and verify row count increases, and verify an explicit force-insert request does not update an existing row.

scale.1: No relevant check executes successfully, or the latest execution only reproduces the duplicate-key failure.
scale.2: A relevant successful execution is shown, but it does not decisively prove that the separate explicit-primary-key instance updated the existing row.
scale.3: An executed check decisively proves the reported existing-primary-key save updates a mutable field without creating another row, or captures the corresponding UPDATE SQL.
scale.4: Meets level 3 and successfully asserts either insertion for a nonmatching primary key or preserved explicit force-insert behavior.
scale.5: Applied repository-native regression coverage executes successfully and distinctly asserts the existing-primary-key update, nonmatching-primary-key insertion, and explicit force-insert behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression verification proves explicit-primary-key saves update the existing row

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains an implementation edit to Model saving logic that can affect INSERT-versus-UPDATE selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements a deterministic change at the model table-save boundary so a normal save with a non-null primary key may attempt the existing UPDATE path regardless of whether the primary-key field defines a default, while retaining INSERT fallback when no row matches and honoring an explicit force_insert request.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible logic still forces INSERT for every adding instance whose PK field has a default, calls or compares against a callable default to infer PK provenance, changes caller-supplied force_insert semantics, or visibly produces malformed control flow. Cap at 3 when the effective direction is correct but the final condition or one required branch is not visible enough to verify.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source excerpt or coherent repository diff and its executable control flow outrank comments, stated intent, edit-success messages, and test claims. A later revert outranks an earlier edit. Test output may corroborate code but cannot rescue a visibly ineffective or nondeterministic condition.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents both over-credit for claimed successful tests around an invalid default-provenance comparison and under-credit for a simple removal or effective neutralization of the shortcut that correctly restores the established UPDATE-then-INSERT algorithm.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible applied code whose evaluated branches allow a normal save with a supplied non-null existing PK to call `_do_update()`, preserve INSERT fallback for a nonmatching PK, and leave caller-supplied `force_insert=True` able to bypass UPDATE.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible code around primary-key acquisition, the PK-default force-INSERT shortcut, `if pk_set and not force_insert`, `_do_update()`, and the subsequent `if not updated` INSERT fallback.
metadata.oracle_test: For `force_insert=False`, a non-null PK naming an existing row reaches `_do_update()`; the same path falls back to INSERT when no row matches. For `force_insert=True`, UPDATE remains bypassed. Removing or deterministically neutralizing the PK-default shortcut for non-null PKs is acceptable; preserving its former one-query optimization is not required.

scale.1: No applied implementation is visible, or the final visible code leaves the reported forced-INSERT behavior unchanged.
scale.2: An applied edit targets the decision point but is causally wrong, malformed, nondeterministic, or violates force_insert behavior.
scale.3: An applied edit plausibly restores update-first behavior, but the visible final code is incomplete or leaves one of UPDATE reachability, INSERT fallback, or force_insert preservation unverifiable.
scale.4: The final visible code is deterministic and verifies all three required branches, but it is unnecessarily broad, leaves misleading surrounding logic, or lacks strong repository-level confirmation.
scale.5: The final visible code is a narrow, coherent repository-appropriate change that verifies all required branches without default re-evaluation, provenance guessing, unrelated state, or misleading commentary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied ORM control flow restores update-first saves for supplied non-null primary keys

applies_when: The trajectory considers behavior outside the single duplicate-PK reproduction, including force flags, default-generated primary keys, or deserialization/fixture reloads.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Accounts for adjacent contracts affected by the save decision: caller-requested force_insert remains authoritative, force_update/update_fields retain their errors and update semantics, new rows can still be inserted, and repeated fixture-style saves with explicit PKs update rather than collide.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the proposal disables explicit force_insert, prevents insertion when UPDATE matches no row, or makes callable defaults execute extra times for comparison. Cap at 3 if compatibility is merely asserted or ad hoc test errors are ignored.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual branch analysis and focused tests outrank broad claims that backward compatibility or loaddata is fixed; direct loaddata/raw-save evidence is strongest for fixture claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrowly passing reproduction from masking regressions in QuerySet.create(), explicit save flags, generated defaults, update_fields, or loaddata's repeated explicit-PK saves.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least two independently demonstrated compatibility dimensions beyond the primary existing-row reproduction, one of which must be explicit force_insert preservation or new-row insertion.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, tests, or patch structure addressing force_insert=True, force_update/update_fields, nonexisting explicit PK fallback, fresh callable-default PKs, and raw/deserialization or repeated-load behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Normal save with existing explicit PK updates; normal save with nonexisting explicit PK falls back to INSERT; save(force_insert=True) still inserts or raises on collision; repeated raw/fixture-style saves for an existing explicit PK do not produce a duplicate-key INSERT.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or the proposed behavior visibly breaks core save contracts.
scale.2: Mentions adjacent behavior but contains a demonstrated regression or relies on invalid tests.
scale.3: Correctly reasons about one adjacent contract or provides partial compatibility evidence without sufficient breadth.
scale.4: Correctly protects and demonstrates at least two adjacent contracts, including force_insert or new-row insertion.
scale.5: Provides coherent coverage of explicit force flags, update fallback, fresh default-PK saves, and fixture/raw repeated-load behavior, with no unresolved contradictory evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility coverage for save flags, default-PK optimization, and fixture-style reloads

applies_when: The visible trajectory runs or adds tests for the template-tag argument parsing defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the quality of observed tests for explicitly supplied defaulted keyword-only arguments and duplicate keyword assignments, including preservation of neighboring parser behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if inputs do not use the parser's real keyword token form, the harness fails before exercising parse_bits(), or reported success conflicts with the displayed exception. Cap at 3 if only one core regression is actually observed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed test output from repository or realistic integration tests outranks claimed success. Direct parse_bits() tests with correctly formed bits are secondary. Hand simulations, malformed token arrays, MagicMock-only checks, and dependency failures do not establish behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents counting setup work, mocked filter compilation, or tests that merely fail for some reason as evidence that the task behavior is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require observed passing results for both core regressions: an explicitly supplied defaulted keyword-only argument succeeds, and a duplicate declared keyword produces the multiple-values TemplateSyntaxError.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect exact callable signatures, template/token syntax, expected exception text, command results, and whether tests exercise the real parser path. Relevant cases include explicit optional keyword-only values, omitted defaults, required keyword-only values, duplicates, unknown keywords, and both helper decorators.
metadata.oracle_test: At minimum, verify hello(*, greeting='hello') with greeting='hi' succeeds and hi(*, greeting) with greeting supplied twice raises the exact multiple-values classification rather than unexpected-keyword. Strong coverage also checks omission of the default, an unknown keyword, required-keyword omission, and the shared inclusion_tag path.

scale.1: No relevant test is run, or all visible test activity fails before reaching the target parser behavior.
scale.2: Relevant tests are attempted, but malformed inputs, mocks, configuration failures, or contradictory output make the result non-diagnostic.
scale.3: Exactly one core regression is convincingly observed as correct, or both are tested only through a limited direct-function harness without adequate error assertions.
scale.4: Both core regressions are convincingly observed as correct through realistic parsing, but coverage omits either the second helper type or meaningful adjacent regressions.
scale.5: Both core regressions pass with exact assertions, and visible coverage also protects omission, unknown-keyword, required-argument, and shared simple_tag/inclusion_tag behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Behavioral verification of keyword-only template tags

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates argument parsing for simple_tag or inclusion_tag callables with keyword-only parameters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory correctly explains why a declared keyword-only parameter with a default is misclassified as unexpected and how that same classification causes duplicate keyword arguments to receive the wrong error.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible reasoning proposes changing which keyword-only parameters are required, treating kwonly_defaults as the complete validity set, or claims that optional keyword-only arguments should be rejected when explicitly supplied. Cap at 3 if duplicate handling is explained incorrectly.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed signature inspection and direct readings of the relevant parse_bits() branches outrank unsupported narration. A later explicit correction outranks an earlier mistaken hypothesis; a later return to the mistaken hypothesis supersedes the correction.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a locally plausible edit that confuses required-argument bookkeeping with the callable's accepted keyword namespace.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a causal account that treats every name in kwonly as valid regardless of whether it has a default.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect explanations of parse_bits(), params, kwonly, kwonly_defaults, unhandled_kwargs, and kwargs. Credit recognition that unhandled_kwargs tracks required unsupplied keyword-only parameters, not the complete set of valid keyword names.
metadata.oracle_test: For def hello(*, greeting='hello'), greeting is optional but valid when supplied. unhandled_kwargs may omit greeting because it is not required, but that omission must not make greeting unexpected. For def hi(*, greeting), the first greeting assignment is valid and a second assignment must reach the existing duplicate check and report multiple values.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis, or the final diagnosis is fundamentally unrelated to callable signature validation.
scale.2: Locates the general parser area but retains an incorrect causal model of keyword-only defaults or duplicate detection.
scale.3: Correctly localizes parse_bits() and notices a relationship among kwonly, defaults, and unhandled arguments, but does not state a reliable validity invariant or gives an incomplete account of the second error.
scale.4: Correctly explains that declared keyword-only names remain valid despite defaults and derives a sound fix direction, but does not fully trace why duplicate input reaches the wrong branch.
scale.5: Precisely distinguishes accepted keyword names from required unsupplied names and correctly traces both explicit optional-keyword acceptance and duplicate-keyword error selection.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of keyword-only tag argument validation

applies_when: The visible trajectory reasons about the cause of the keyword-only template-tag errors.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the latest supported reasoning converges on the three distinct roles in parse_bits(): the callable's accepted keyword namespace, the shrinking set of required unsupplied keyword-only arguments, and the set of keyword assignments already parsed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest reasoning treats kwonly_defaults or unhandled_kwargs as the complete accepted-name set, proposes making optional keyword-only names required, or concludes that the original condition is correct. Cap at 3 if both symptoms are observed but the final explanation still relies on moving duplicate detection earlier or adding seen-name state without explaining the underlying validity error.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source flow, FullArgSpec output, and correctly formed parse_bits or end-to-end template observations outrank narration. A later explicit synthesis supported by those observations supersedes earlier confusion; a later incompatible claim or restored mistaken model caps convergence.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding prolonged exploration, passing ad hoc examples, or a locally plausible workaround as if it established the stable causal invariant.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a final invariant that every declared name in kwonly is valid when supplied, while unhandled_kwargs contains only required keyword-only names still missing. Credit of 5 additionally requires tracing the second occurrence of a valid name to kwargs-based duplicate detection.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest supported explanation of kwonly, unhandled_kwargs, kwargs, and the ordering of the unexpected-keyword and duplicate checks. Look for correction of earlier incompatible hypotheses rather than counting exploratory mentions.
metadata.oracle_test: For hello(*, greeting='hello'), greeting is accepted because it is in kwonly even though it is absent from unhandled_kwargs. For hi(*, greeting), the first assignment removes greeting from unhandled_kwargs and records it in kwargs; the second remains a declared valid name and therefore reaches the kwargs duplicate branch.

scale.1: The latest visible account is unrelated to parse_bits signature validation or directly contradicts the displayed source behavior.
scale.2: The parser area is located, but the latest account still uses defaults or the shrinking missing-required set as the accepted keyword namespace.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly explains one reported symptom or intermittently reaches the right distinction, but does not end with a stable account of both validity and duplicate classification.
scale.4: The latest supported account clearly separates all declared kwonly names from missing-required bookkeeping and explains both symptoms, but omits a precise first-assignment versus second-assignment branch trace.
scale.5: The latest supported account precisely traces optional acceptance and repeated required-keyword handling through kwonly, unhandled_kwargs mutation, kwargs recording, and the unexpected-versus-duplicate branches.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Converged causal model of parse_bits keyword handling

applies_when: The task concerns argument validation for Django simple tags or inclusion tags with keyword-only parameters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that parse_bits() incorrectly uses the shrinking required-keyword-only list as the validity set, so defaulted keyword-only parameters are rejected and repeated required keyword-only parameters can be classified as unexpected before duplicate detection.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory asserts that defaulted keyword-only parameters belong in the missing-required set, or that changing token_kwargs or function invocation is the primary fix despite visible parse_bits evidence. Cap at 1 if the causal account contradicts the displayed source flow without later correction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual source excerpts and observed FullArgSpec/parse_bits behavior outrank summaries or unsupported claims; end-to-end template parsing outranks hand-simulated token lists.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing requiredness tracking with the authoritative set of valid keyword names, or treating malformed token simulations as proof about parser behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires distinguishing the complete kwonly parameter set from unhandled_kwargs, which tracks only required keyword-only parameters still awaiting values.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning tied to getfullargspec() outputs, unhandled_kwargs construction, and the unexpected-versus-duplicate branches in django/template/library.py.
metadata.oracle_test: For def hello(*, greeting='hello'), greeting is in kwonly but absent from unhandled_kwargs; it must still be accepted. For def hi(*, greeting), the first occurrence removes greeting from unhandled_kwargs, but the second remains a valid parameter and must reach the param-in-kwargs duplicate branch.

scale.1: No relevant causal account is present, or the final visible account is incompatible with the source and examples.
scale.2: The trajectory locates template-tag argument parsing but gives a materially wrong or unresolved explanation of keyword-only defaults or duplicates.
scale.3: The trajectory identifies parse_bits() and explains the defaulted-keyword rejection, but does not correctly connect the same validity check to duplicate classification or the shared tag-helper path.
scale.4: The trajectory correctly distinguishes kwonly from unhandled_kwargs and explains both reported symptoms, but omits a precise branch trace or the shared simple_tag/inclusion_tag boundary.
scale.5: The trajectory precisely traces both examples through FullArgSpec, unhandled_kwargs mutation, validity checking, and duplicate detection, and recognizes that both tag decorators share parse_bits().

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of keyword-only tag parsing

applies_when: A source edit or exact source-level fix for the template-tag keyword-only argument defect is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest authoritative django/template/library.py state contains an applied, syntactically valid change that validates supplied keyword names against the complete declared keyword-only namespace while preserving required-argument bookkeeping and duplicate detection.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest authoritative source is syntactically invalid, destructively altered, or restored to the original faulty condition. Cap at 2 if the edit recognizes only kwonly_defaults, redefines unhandled_kwargs to include optional names without preserving missing-required semantics, or merely moves duplicate detection ahead of an unchanged validity error. Cap at 3 when the correct change is only proposed or when the applied state cannot be established.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest repository diff or post-edit source excerpt is authoritative. A workspace summary showing no change, a later restoration, or a later malformed replacement supersedes an earlier successful edit. Executed behavior may confirm semantics but cannot establish that an edit remains applied. Narrated plans and unapplied replacement snippets receive proposal-level credit only.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating correct narration, temporary edits, default-only special cases, duplicate-first workarounds, or stale successful experiments as a clean applied solution.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a currently applied, syntactically valid implementation equivalent to rejecting a keyword only when it is absent from both params and kwonly and no varkw exists. Score 5 additionally requires trustworthy observed execution of both reported behaviors against that applied state.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible diff, workspace summary, git status, or post-edit parse_bits() excerpt. Determine whether the operative unexpected-keyword condition accepts every name in kwonly, leaves unhandled_kwargs as the shrinking set of required unsupplied keyword-only names, and allows a repeated valid name to reach the existing kwargs duplicate check.
metadata.oracle_test: The operative boundary is equivalent to: if param not in params and param not in kwonly and varkw is None, raise unexpected; elif param in kwargs, raise multiple values. For hello(*, greeting='hello'), greeting is valid when explicitly supplied although absent from unhandled_kwargs. For hi(*, greeting), the second greeting remains a valid declared name and reaches duplicate detection.

scale.1: No applicable edit is currently present, or the latest authoritative source is restored, syntactically broken, or unrelated.
scale.2: A current edit is present but is semantically wrong: it fixes neither full boundary, handles only defaulted names or duplicate ordering, or corrupts required-keyword bookkeeping.
scale.3: An exact semantically correct replacement is proposed but not shown as applied, or a current partial edit improves one symptom while leaving the other or requiredness semantics unresolved.
scale.4: The latest authoritative source contains a clean, minimal, semantically complete parse_bits() fix, but trustworthy execution against that applied state is absent or non-diagnostic.
scale.5: The latest authoritative source contains the clean, minimal, semantically complete fix, and trustworthy observed execution against that state confirms explicit defaulted keyword-only acceptance and exact duplicate-keyword classification.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and semantically complete parse_bits fix

applies_when: The visible trajectory creates, runs, or precisely specifies evidence for the reported Item and Derived save sequence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses a faithful reproduction to distinguish overwriting the original inherited object from creating a new coherent parent-and-child object after the inherited parent key is reset.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the reproduction asserts that changing the original row to f=False is success, checks only the mutated instance key, omits creation of the child table, or otherwise reverses the ticket's expected behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful database observations from the exact inheritance sequence outrank speculative print statements, comments, or results from a standalone Item, proxy, explicit unrelated OneToOneField, deletion, or malformed schema setup.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a superficially passing script that accidentally tests ordinary updates, has missing tables, checks the wrong primary key, or misunderstands the ticket's intentionally preserved original row.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires preserving the original key before mutation and querying database state after save; merely printing the in-memory instance is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: A runnable model setup or test matching Item(uid primary key, f), concrete Derived(Item), reverse access via item.derived, uid=None, field mutation, save(), and database queries using the pre-reset key.
metadata.oracle_test: After saving the reset child, the Item row at the original key must still have f=True, while the reset instance represents a distinct saved inheritance chain with f=False and a different non-None key.

scale.1: No reproduction or only setup attempts that produce no task-relevant observation.
scale.2: A malformed or semantically different reproduction, or an interpretation that treats overwriting the original row as correct.
scale.3: A substantially faithful reproduction reaches useful state observations but does not decisively distinguish the old row from a new parent/child row.
scale.4: Faithful runtime evidence demonstrates the bug or expected behavior by retaining and querying the original key after the reset save.
scale.5: Decisive evidence checks both sides of the semantic contract: the original row remains unchanged and a distinct, internally consistent Derived inheritance chain stores the reset values; relevant keys and instance state are shown.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-semantic reproduction and database evidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory analyzes why assigning None to the inherited parent primary-key attribute on an existing concrete child instance fails to duplicate it.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the bug as inconsistent parent-primary-key and child parent-link state during multi-table inheritance saving, rather than as a proxy-model, generic-relation, or ordinary standalone-primary-key problem.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory treats Derived as a proxy model or attributes the failure primarily to GenericForeignKey, reverse-descriptor lookup, deletion, dirty-field tracking, or AutoField default generation without reconciling the parent-link state.
metadata.evidence_authority: A source-backed trace of Model._save_parents(), model metadata, or runtime values for the parent PK and parent-link attname outranks unsupported descriptions of generic save behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards broad ORM exploration or mention of pk=None even when it misses the causal distinction between the inherited parent key and the child's concrete parent link.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognizing that Derived is a concrete multi-table child and that assigning uid=None can leave its parent-link value at the old key.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning that distinguishes Item.uid from Derived's auto-created parent-link primary key and traces save() through _save_parents() before per-table saving.
metadata.oracle_test: For an existing Derived loaded through Item.derived, uid may be None while the auto-created child link (for example item_ptr_id) still contains the old key; current _save_parents() can copy that link back into the parent PK and thereby update the old Item row.

scale.1: No task-specific causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis centered on unrelated ORM facilities.
scale.2: Recognizes a save/primary-key issue but materially misclassifies the inheritance type or the relevant relation.
scale.3: Locates model saving or _save_parents() and suspects parent/child key synchronization, but does not clearly explain the two distinct stored attributes and restoration of the old key.
scale.4: Correctly explains that uid=None leaves the child parent-link key populated and that parent-save synchronization can restore the old parent key, causing the original row to be updated.
scale.5: Provides the complete source- or runtime-supported causal chain, including concrete multi-table inheritance, the old parent-link value, _save_parents() restoring the parent PK before table saves, and the resulting overwrite instead of duplication.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct multi-table inheritance diagnosis

applies_when: The visible trajectory performs source inspection, runtime experiments, or test-harness construction to narrow the cause of the inherited-primary-key save behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Makes cumulative, evidence-backed progress toward the relevant multi-table inheritance save path or a faithful database experiment, while resolving rather than preserving task-defining misconceptions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible working theory remains centered on proxy models, GenericForeignKey, reverse-descriptor assignment, deletion, or standalone AutoField behavior. Cap at 3 if relevant evidence is found but is contradicted or semantically misinterpreted without resolution.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed database observations and exact source lines tied to the ticket outrank plans, search volume, comments, or unsupported conclusions. A failed command counts only when its output is used to repair the harness or narrow the mechanism; repeated failures without such narrowing do not accumulate credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long command sequences, dependency installation, unrelated test browsing, or confidently interpreted malformed reproductions as though they were cumulative progress.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one applied task-causal artifact: a successful faithful database observation, a source-backed trace of the relevant parent-save logic, or runtime/model-metadata evidence exposing the parent-link state. Plans and proposed tests alone cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for concrete narrowing artifacts: identification of concrete multi-table inheritance, inspection of _save_parents() or parent-link metadata, a faithful Item/Derived harness, preserved original-key observations, and explicit correction of earlier proxy, generic-relation, or reverse-descriptor hypotheses.
metadata.oracle_test: A convergent investigation should narrow toward the fact that Derived is a concrete child whose inherited uid and auto-created parent link can diverge, and should seek evidence capable of distinguishing update of the original Item row from insertion of a new coherent Item/Derived chain.

scale.1: No task-causal foothold is established; activity consists of generic browsing or setup failures with no reliable narrowing result.
scale.2: Some relevant files or concepts are encountered, but investigation remains organized around a wrong subsystem or repeatedly fails without extracting a corrected hypothesis or usable harness.
scale.3: The trajectory reaches the correct inheritance/save subsystem or constructs a substantially faithful harness, but evidence is incomplete, unexecuted, or leaves a material contradiction unresolved.
scale.4: A source-backed trace, model-state observation, or faithful database result materially narrows the cause, and earlier misconceptions are explicitly corrected rather than retained.
scale.5: Multiple mutually consistent artifacts triangulate the behavior, such as relevant source flow plus faithful database or metadata observations, with the remaining uncertainty precisely isolated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-directed investigative convergence

applies_when: The visible trajectory discusses, adds, or runs regression coverage for the fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes durable tests for cloning a concrete multi-table child by clearing its inherited parent key, including protection for ordinary parent/child saves and relevant primary-key generation variants.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if only one in-memory value is asserted; cap at 2 if the expected assertion is reversed, the model is proxy/abstract rather than concrete multi-table inheritance, or claimed passing tests visibly failed or never ran.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed focused Django tests and their output outrank ad hoc scripts; a visible test diff with exact assertions outranks generic statements that tests should be added.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrow test from passing while stale parent-link restoration, broken child-row linkage, default-generated keys, or fresh multi-table creation remain unprotected.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires assertions that retain the original key and verify both preservation of the old row and creation of a distinct child object, not merely that save() returns without error.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tests in an appropriate model-inheritance suite, assertions on old and new database rows, and successful targeted test execution or clearly reported failures.
metadata.oracle_test: Coverage should reproduce reverse retrieval from the parent, clear the inherited parent PK, mutate f, save, assert the original Item remains f=True, and assert the saved child has a new key with f=False; AutoField and a default-generating key such as UUID are relevant variants, alongside a normal fresh-child save regression.

scale.1: No relevant regression-test work or only unrelated test discovery.
scale.2: A proposed or attempted test uses the wrong model type, wrong expected behavior, or cannot exercise the save path.
scale.3: A faithful core regression test is specified or added, but old/new row identity, child linkage, execution evidence, or compatibility coverage is incomplete.
scale.4: A faithful regression test verifies preservation of the original row and creation of a distinct saved child, with credible targeted execution or strong complementary normal-save coverage.
scale.5: Comprehensive, nonredundant tests cover the exact reverse-access scenario, old and new inheritance rows, child-link coherence, relevant generated-key variants, and ordinary multi-table child saving, with successful targeted runtime evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression tests across inherited-key variants

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates why saving an existing concrete child after assigning None to an inherited primary-key attribute can update the original parent row.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly localizes the behavior to concrete multi-table inheritance and explains how the child's retained parent-link key can repopulate the inherited parent key during the recursive parent-save path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the final visible account still treats Derived as a proxy model, GenericForeignKey case, ordinary standalone model, or reverse-descriptor bug, or attributes the overwrite to AutoField generation without reconciling the populated parent-link value. Cap at 3 when the correct subsystem is reached but the trajectory never establishes how the old key is restored.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source inspection of Model._save_parents(), model metadata showing the parent link, or runtime values of both key attributes outranks terminology, comments, assumptions based on reverse access, or generic descriptions of pk=None save behavior. A later explicit correction supported by source or runtime evidence supersedes an earlier tentative misclassification.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equal credit for a trajectory that merely opens model-saving code or mentions inheritance and one that correctly abandons an initial proxy or relation hypothesis, reaches _save_parents(), and identifies the retained parent-link value.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible evidence that the inherited parent-key attribute and the child's parent-link attribute are distinct and can simultaneously hold None and the old key. Credit of 3 requires at least correct concrete multi-table classification plus inspection of the relevant parent-save path or metadata.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the trajectory distinguishes Item.uid from Derived's auto-created parent-link attname, identifies Derived as a concrete multi-table child, and follows save() into Model._save_parents() before the parent and child table saves.
metadata.oracle_test: For an existing Derived obtained through Item.derived, assigning uid=None can leave the auto-created child link, such as item_ptr_id, equal to the original key. During _save_parents(), that link is copied into Item.uid before the parent table is saved, so the original Item row is updated rather than a distinct inheritance chain being inserted.

scale.1: No task-specific causal localization; exploration does not reach concrete model inheritance or the save path.
scale.2: A save or relationship issue is suspected, but the visible account remains centered on a wrong mechanism such as proxy models, generic relations, reverse descriptors, dirty tracking, or standalone primary-key generation.
scale.3: The trajectory explicitly identifies concrete multi-table inheritance and reaches _save_parents(), parent metadata, or the auto-created parent link, but does not yet establish both stored key values and the restoration sequence.
scale.4: The trajectory establishes that uid can be None while the child parent-link retains the old key and explains that _save_parents() restores the parent key, causing the original parent row to be updated.
scale.5: Source or runtime evidence verifies the complete causal chain across both attributes and table saves, and the explanation correctly predicts overwrite versus insertion for the ticket's exact sequence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal localization of inherited primary-key restoration

applies_when: The rollout concerns changing Django file-widget required-attribute behavior when initial file data exists.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible applied repository state makes FileInput suppress the HTML required attribute when a usable initial value exists while retaining it when no initial value exists, without breaking ClearableFileInput inheritance or surrounding widget behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible source is malformed, leaves FileInput with the original always-required behavior for initial data, or visible checks contradict the claimed behavior. Cap at 3 if the core behavior is applied but the final class ownership or inheritance state remains visibly incomplete or conflicting.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff outranks narration and earlier intermediate edits. Repository-native tests executed against that state outrank ad hoc scripts; focused executable checks outrank unsupported claims. Equivalent implementations receive equal credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for extensive investigation, proposed edits, stale intermediate tests, or successful checks performed before the final source mutation, and prevents confusing the polarity of the required-attribute predicate.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible applied code under FileInput that handles both a present initial value and an absent initial value with the correct polarity.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source or diff for FileInput.use_required_attribute(), the resulting ClearableFileInput behavior, and any tests actually executed after the final edit. Distinguish applied code from plans, patch drafts, or assertions about code that is not visible.
metadata.oracle_test: For a normal non-hidden FileInput, use_required_attribute(initial) must be false for a truthy existing-file value and true for None or another absent/falsy initial value; ClearableFileInput must continue to exhibit the same required-attribute behavior through valid inheritance or an equivalent non-conflicting implementation.

scale.1: No relevant applied implementation is visible, or the applied change clearly preserves or introduces the wrong required-attribute behavior.
scale.2: A relevant edit is visible but is malformed, only proposed, handles the polarity incorrectly, or lacks one of the two task-defining initial-value cases.
scale.3: The core behavior is plausibly applied, but the latest visible state is incomplete, conflicting, ambiguously placed across FileInput and ClearableFileInput, or not verified after the final edit.
scale.4: The latest visible source coherently implements both required-attribute cases in FileInput and preserves ClearableFileInput behavior; verification is limited to source reasoning or focused ad hoc checks.
scale.5: The coherent applied implementation satisfies both cases and is supported by authoritative repository-native regression evidence covering FileInput and inherited ClearableFileInput behavior, with no visible relevant failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied correctness of FileInput required-attribute handling

applies_when: The trajectory encounters failed tests, conflicting observations, repeated edits, or compatibility questions about existing widget behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory preserves established semantics for empty initial values and ClearableFileInput, distinguishes environmental failures from code failures, and leaves the latest visible implementation coherent after correcting any contradictory or destructive intermediate edits.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible source still contains stray returns, duplicate malformed methods, accidental deletion of unrelated widget hooks, or a known failing relevant assertion, cap at 2. Merely calling a failure an environment issue without evidence does not remove the cap when the failure is behavioral.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest verified source and rerun results outrank earlier broken intermediate states; unresolved later failures outrank earlier success claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents over-crediting trajectories that momentarily reach the right idea but leave damaged code, misread a failed test, or silently regress existing ClearableFileInput behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require that all visible edit corruption or behavior contradictions have been resolved in the latest source and that no relevant failure remains unexplained.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible handling of contradictory outputs, restoration after malformed edits, checks of the final diff or source, and reasoning about absent/falsy versus truthy initial values and subclass inheritance.
metadata.oracle_test: Falsy initial values such as None or an empty string continue to permit required on an ordinary FileInput, truthy existing-file values suppress it, and ClearableFileInput retains its former outcomes through inheritance or an equivalent override.

scale.1: Contradictory evidence or edit damage is ignored, and the latest visible state is unreliable or clearly broken.
scale.2: The trajectory notices problems but leaves a relevant contradiction, malformed edit, or compatibility risk unresolved at the cutoff.
scale.3: The latest state appears coherent and major mistakes are corrected, but compatibility reasoning or confirmation after recovery is limited.
scale.4: Visible contradictions and editing mistakes are correctly diagnosed and resolved, with final checks covering existing and absent initial values plus ClearableFileInput behavior.
scale.5: Anchor 4 is satisfied with disciplined recovery: the trajectory uses source/diff inspection and reruns decisive checks after correction, clearly separates environment failures from implementation failures, and leaves no visible unrelated artifacts or regressions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility reasoning and contradiction recovery

applies_when: A visible source edit or concrete patch changes required-attribute handling for FileInput.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible repository state places the initial-file required-attribute predicate coherently on FileInput, preserves ClearableFileInput's adjacent upload and clear-checkbox behavior, and keeps the change structurally complete and locally minimal.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible method is malformed, outside FileInput, reverses the initial-value polarity, or damages adjacent ClearableFileInput behavior. Cap at 3 when the predicate is correct but the visible patch retains the equivalent ClearableFileInput override and also introduces another avoidable precision defect such as a restatement-only docstring, excess blank lines, or comparable local churn.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff outranks editing commands, replacement scripts, prose summaries, and earlier intermediate states. A coherent final source inspection can establish repair of earlier malformed edits. Executable checks may confirm polarity but cannot override contradictory source.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents penalizing the concise task-equivalent `not initial` implementation merely because it omits a redundant parent call, while still distinguishing a clean completed move from a correct but duplicated and unnecessarily noisy patch.
metadata.hard_gate: The two highest anchors require a syntactically coherent method inside FileInput that returns false for truthy initial data and true for absent or falsy initial data. Both `not initial` and the equivalent parent-predicate conjunction are valid for the ordinary FileInput behavior at issue. ClearableFileInput's upload, contradiction-marker, clear-checkbox, and value-omission logic must remain intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible FileInput and ClearableFileInput source or unified diff for method ownership, correct truthy-versus-falsy polarity, preservation of upload and clear-checkbox methods, redundant subclass ownership, unnecessary method commentary, and avoidable local formatting churn.
metadata.oracle_test: For an ordinary FileInput, use_required_attribute(initial) is false for a truthy existing-file value and true for None, an empty string, or another falsy absent value. ClearableFileInput receives the same behavior through inheritance or a non-conflicting equivalent override, without loss of its upload, contradiction, clear-checkbox, or value-omission handling.

scale.1: No coherent FileInput implementation is visibly applied, or the latest implementation clearly has the opposite required-attribute behavior.
scale.2: The latest implementation is malformed, misplaced, behaviorally incomplete, or damages adjacent FileInput or ClearableFileInput behavior.
scale.3: The FileInput predicate is coherent and has the correct polarity, but at least two visible precision defects remain, such as retaining the equivalent subclass override together with unnecessary documentation or formatting churn.
scale.4: The FileInput predicate is coherent, correctly placed, and preserves adjacent behavior, with at most one limited precision compromise such as an unchanged equivalent ClearableFileInput override or minor local explanatory clutter.
scale.5: The latest visible diff cleanly places the predicate on FileInput, removes the redundant ClearableFileInput override, preserves all adjacent file-upload and clear-checkbox behavior, and contains no unnecessary local edits.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise and complete FileInput implementation boundary

applies_when: A visible edit or concrete patch is present for the FileInput required-attribute behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible implementation places the initial-data suppression behavior on FileInput so all file-input variants receive it, while preserving unrelated file upload and clear-checkbox behavior and avoiding unnecessary changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed indentation, a method outside FileInput, reversed initial logic, or collateral removal of ClearableFileInput upload/clear handling caps credit at 2. A later visibly corrected source removes that cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible file content or unified diff outranks earlier attempted edits, prose summaries, and claimed final state; executable source outranks editing-script intent.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a correct explanation when the actual edit is misplaced, malformed, overbroad, or limited to ClearableFileInput.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a syntactically coherent method defined inside FileInput whose result is false for truthy initial data and true for absent initial data for an ordinary visible file input.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest visible source or diff for django/forms/widgets.py, especially FileInput.use_required_attribute(), the not-initial condition, inheritance by ClearableFileInput, and absence of unrelated edits.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended boundary is FileInput.use_required_attribute(initial) with behavior equivalent here to `not initial` or to the inherited visibility decision combined with `not initial`; ClearableFileInput must obtain the same semantics through FileInput.

scale.1: No relevant visible edit exists, or the edit clearly implements the opposite behavior.
scale.2: A relevant edit is attempted but remains malformed, misplaced, incomplete in FileInput, or damages adjacent behavior.
scale.3: A coherent FileInput hook implements the core initial-data behavior, but the diff contains avoidable duplication, suspicious collateral edits, or unresolved structural uncertainty.
scale.4: The latest visible edit cleanly implements the behavior in FileInput with no material unrelated changes; a redundant but semantically identical ClearableFileInput override may remain.
scale.5: The latest visible diff cleanly moves the behavior to FileInput, removes the now-redundant ClearableFileInput override, preserves the prior subclass semantics, and changes only the necessary implementation area.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise FileInput implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory executes or claims validation of choices enum access through Django template variable resolution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates executed proof that a choices enum class supplied under the exact template context root remains uncalled and can be traversed to a member-specific comparison, label, or value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A missing class root, empty interpolation, fallback branch, `VariableDoesNotExist`, or other failed result cannot receive positive traversal credit even if the marker exists. A later successful run may supersede an earlier failed run only when its complete template, context root, and output are visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from an actually executed render using the displayed template and context outranks assistant-authored success claims. A script that was merely written, a proposed command, source inspection, or a run failing before rendering provides no positive traversal evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: The enum class is omitted, only a member is supplied, the render never executes, output is inferred from source, or an unresolved variable's fallback result is called success.
metadata.hard_gate: Before score 3 or higher, an executed render must visibly use a context that contains the enum class under the exact root name traversed by the template.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the executed template text, the actual context mapping, and the observed render output together. The mapping must visibly bind the exact root referenced by the template, such as `'Suit': Suit` for `Suit.DIAMOND`; member-only context and unresolved-variable fallback are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: With `Suit` bound to the enum class, rendering `{{ Suit.DIAMOND.label }}|{{ Suit.DIAMOND.value }}` produces `Diamond|1`, or an equivalent class-root conditional visibly selects the expected member-specific branch.
metadata.stage: Validate template traversal and enum compatibility

scale.1: No applicable render executes, or the visible render omits the exact enum-class context root and therefore does not exercise class-to-member traversal.
scale.2: A render executes with a relevant class root but fails, is blocked before the relevant output, or leaves the member-specific result unresolved.
scale.3: The enum class is visibly bound under the exact root and traversal executes, but the observed output is incomplete or only indirectly member-specific.
scale.4: An executed exact-root render visibly succeeds in a member-specific conditional or produces the expected member label or value.
scale.5: An executed exact-root render visibly produces both the expected member label and value, with assertions or contrasting output showing that unresolved or omitted-class fallback was not mistaken for success.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed enum-class-to-member template traversal

applies_when: A production edit, production-file rewrite, or repository diff is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates observable defects in the surviving production source, including displaced metaclass documentation, unsafe placement, malformed code, whitespace damage, and unrelated rewrites.

metadata.failure_mode: The edit displaces the docstring, uses an unsafe enum-body assignment, corrupts source structure, leaves material formatting churn, or changes unrelated production behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: The production edit remains minimal, syntactically coherent, documentation-safe, and isolated to the required behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: The complete production diff contains only a focused marker-related change, `ChoicesMeta.__doc__` remains the existing description, and the source has no whitespace or syntax defect.
metadata.stage: Review and prepare the evaluator-facing artifact

scale.1: No production-source defect is visible; the surviving edit is minimal, documentation-safe, syntactically coherent, and locally styled.
scale.2: A minor nonsemantic source issue is visible, but the focused production behavior, documentation, and applicability remain clear.
scale.3: There is meaningful avoidable production churn, an unrelated no-op edit, a production backup file, or unresolved cleanliness concern.
scale.4: A strong source-integrity defect is visible, such as substantial formatting churn, an overlong production comment combined with unrelated whitespace changes, or repeated rewriting without a clean surviving diff.
scale.5: The surviving source displaces the metaclass docstring, uses a member-producing enum-body assignment, is malformed, omits the required production behavior, or otherwise creates a direct production regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production-source integrity and documentation preservation

applies_when: A marker implementation for model choices enumeration classes is proposed, applied, or verified.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the active cutoff production implementation guarantees `do_not_call_in_templates is True` for every enum class created through `ChoicesMeta`, including arbitrary user-defined classes, without name gates or false-preserving guards.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if coverage is restricted by built-in class names, per-family assignments, `hasattr()` or another guard that can retain `False`, or inheritance from `Choices` that does not cover every class created directly through `ChoicesMeta`. An absent or reverted marker scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace and production diff override earlier edits, proposed patches, scratch scripts, assistant claims, and tests run against a reverted or different implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: The cutoff source has no marker, marks only selected enum families, conditionally preserves a false value, or relies on evidence from an implementation no longer present.
metadata.hard_gate: A surviving production marker must be visible in `django/db/models/enums.py` before scores above 1 are possible.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff version or diff of `django/db/models/enums.py`. Credit only a surviving metaclass attribute after the docstring or an unconditional assignment to each class returned by `ChoicesMeta.__new__`. Tests may corroborate arbitrary-class coverage but cannot substitute for absent production code.
metadata.oracle_test: An arbitrarily named class created through `ChoicesMeta` resolves `do_not_call_in_templates` to the boolean `True` without appearing in any production allowlist.
metadata.stage: Select and implement a safe centralized marker placement

scale.1: No marker survives in the active production source, or the visible implementation cannot provide a true class-level marker.
scale.2: A surviving marker covers only named built-ins, selected families, or otherwise fails to guarantee `True` for every `ChoicesMeta`-created class.
scale.3: A surviving central implementation plausibly covers all `ChoicesMeta` classes, but its unconditional behavior is ambiguous and no arbitrary-class evidence resolves that ambiguity.
scale.4: The active source visibly applies `True` unconditionally through `ChoicesMeta` for all generated classes; no coverage-limiting condition is present.
scale.5: Level 4 holds, and an actually executed check against the active implementation verifies an arbitrarily named `ChoicesMeta` class receives the boolean `True`.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unconditional ChoicesMeta-wide marker coverage

applies_when: The visible trajectory edits task-relevant source or tests and may later undo those edits before the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible prefix ends after the agent explicitly discarded task-relevant applied changes, with no replacement implementation or test change subsequently applied.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If later visible evidence shows a replacement task-relevant implementation or test change was applied after the rollback, cap the score at 1. Merely discussing a replacement, writing it only in a temporary file, or planning to reapply it does not contradict an unrecovered rollback.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository-state evidence from successful version-control commands, displayed diffs, and post-command file contents outranks plans, explanations, claimed fixes, temporary scripts, and tests of code that is no longer applied. Later visible repository-state evidence outranks earlier state.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting investigation or transient successful experiments as applied progress when the trajectory visibly erases the implementation before the cutoff, while avoiding penalties for rollbacks followed by a concrete replacement.
metadata.hard_gate: Any score above 1 requires direct visible evidence that task-relevant source or test changes were actually applied and then explicitly removed or overwritten. Scores 3 or higher additionally require that some or all removed work remains absent at the cutoff.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect task-relevant edit commands and their outputs, then inspect later restore, checkout, reset, overwrite, diff, or file-view evidence to determine whether the applied work was discarded and replaced before the cutoff.
metadata.oracle_test: For this task, determine whether a retained change still addresses readonly JSONField rendering through display_for_field or an equivalent task-causal path, ideally with retained coverage; an explicit restoration of the target file to baseline with no later task change is a complete rollback.

scale.1: No qualifying unrecovered rollback: no task-relevant applied change was explicitly discarded, or any discarded change was followed by a visibly applied replacement before the cutoff.
scale.2: A task-relevant applied change was explicitly discarded, but visible repository evidence is insufficient to determine whether equivalent task work remained applied at the cutoff.
scale.3: A task-relevant applied change was explicitly discarded and remained absent, but other concrete task-relevant source or test changes were still visibly applied at the cutoff.
scale.4: All visible task-relevant implementation and test changes were explicitly discarded, leaving a clean or baseline repository state with no subsequently applied replacement at the cutoff.
scale.5: Task-relevant changes were discarded without replacement and the visible cutoff also retains repository corruption or unrelated destructive damage caused by the failed editing attempt.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unrecovered rollback of task-relevant changes

applies_when: The trajectory attempts to reproduce, patch, or test the order-sensitive MTI parent-link behavior
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the strength of visible executable evidence that the current repository state accepts both field declaration orders, selects the explicitly marked inheritance link as the primary key, and retains the expected failure when no valid parent link is supplied.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest relevant execution fails, when success is printed without constructing the affected models or asserting the selected primary key, or when a discovered regression remains unverified after a follow-up edit. Environment failures alone do not count as semantic validation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit command output from focused or existing tests is authoritative. Merely writing a test, printing an unconditional success message, narrating an expected result, or showing pre-edit output is not execution evidence. A later relevant failure supersedes an earlier pass until rerun successfully.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing proposed tests, dependency installation, unconditional output, or a single passing field order with evidence that the order-dependent bug and its regression boundary are fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require successful execution against the current edited code for both permutations of the explicit parent link and the ordinary one-to-one relation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect successful model construction, asserted primary-key identity, both declaration-order variants, focused regression tests, existing test-suite output, and whether those results occurred after the latest relevant edit.
metadata.oracle_test: A focused regression should construct equivalent MTI children with the marked parent link before and after the ordinary one-to-one field, verify that the marked link becomes the child primary key in both cases, and preserve the established rejection of a sole unmarked would-be parent link.

scale.1: No successful task-relevant reproduction or semantic test is visible.
scale.2: Some executable investigation occurs, but it is incomplete, fails after the latest edit, or does not verify model construction and primary-key selection.
scale.3: A reliable reproduction or one declaration-order case is executed, or both orders are exercised without verifying the selected parent-link primary key; regression preservation is not established.
scale.4: Both declaration orders execute successfully against the current change and the explicitly marked link is shown or asserted to be the primary key, but the missing-parent-link regression boundary or broader relevant suite is not verified.
scale.5: Post-edit tests verify both declaration orders and primary-key identity, and a focused existing or new regression check confirms that configurations lacking a valid parent link still fail as intended.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable validation of MTI parent-link semantics

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes Django model construction for multiple OneToOneField references from a multi-table-inheritance child to its concrete parent.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory correctly explains and demonstrably addresses why multiple OneToOneField references to the same concrete parent can cause the non-parent relation to be selected instead of the explicitly marked parent link, independent of declaration order.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory attributes the bug only to unordered dictionary iteration, edits only PK promotion without resolving how the wrong same-target field enters the parent mapping, or visible execution disproves the proposed correction. Cap at 3 when the correct change is merely proposed, malformed, not executed, or only demonstrated by bypassing the relevant validation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts and successful command observations outrank unsupported reasoning. Executed focused reproductions and repository tests outrank claimed success. An inspected patch or command-applied edit may establish implementation evidence; a later source inspection, diff, status, test failure, or traceback showing that it was absent or ineffective overrides that claim.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding superficial discovery of the error site, the false claim that ordinary dict ordering is the root cause, fixes at the wrong layer, unexecuted patch plans, or a broad relaxation that silently accepts missing parent_link=True.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a visibly applied task-causal code change and successful execution showing both field declaration orders select the explicit parent_link field. Score 5 additionally requires visible regression evidence that a lone same-parent OneToOneField lacking parent_link=True still raises the established ImproperlyConfigured error, preferably through the repository test suite.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, executed reproductions, concrete edits, and test output concerning ModelBase parent-link collection and Options primary-key promotion. Credit must reflect what was actually inspected, changed, or executed by the cutoff, not intended next steps.
metadata.oracle_test: For each candidate OneToOneField targeting the inherited concrete parent, Django's MTI parent-link discovery must honor remote_field.parent_link=True rather than letting an ordinary same-target OneToOneField overwrite the candidate. Reversing declaration order must not change the selected child PK, while a model whose only candidate lacks parent_link=True must retain the existing configuration error.

scale.1: No task-specific causal progress: remains in generic repository or environment exploration, or advances a mechanism contradicted by visible source or execution.
scale.2: Locates relevant model-construction or PK-promotion code and may reproduce part of the symptom, but explains it only as arbitrary ordering, remains confused about the parent mapping, or attempts an ineffective/wrong-layer change.
scale.3: Correctly connects declaration order to same-target OneToOneField candidate overwrite or otherwise identifies explicit parent_link filtering as the required invariant, but has no successfully executed applied correction covering both orders.
scale.4: Applies a causally appropriate correction and successfully demonstrates that both declaration orders select the explicit parent link, but does not visibly verify preservation of the missing-parent-link error through a focused regression or existing test.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and also visibly verifies the negative regression: a sole same-parent OneToOneField without parent_link=True still raises the established ImproperlyConfigured error, with relevant repository tests passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal and validated resolution of MTI parent-link selection

applies_when: The trajectory investigates multiple one-to-one relations from a multi-table-inheritance child to its concrete parent
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible investigation correctly identifies the mechanism that selects the inheritance parent link and develops or applies a repair that uses the explicit parent_link marker without weakening missing-parent-link validation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory attributes the bug only to unordered dictionary iteration, chooses an arbitrary one-to-one field, or permits a model with no explicit or auto-created valid parent link to bypass the existing configuration error. Cap at 3 if a relevant post-edit failure remains unresolved or untested.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source inspection and observed runtime state take precedence over narrative claims. An applied patch shown in the repository takes precedence over a proposed patch. Relevant test results after the latest edit take precedence over earlier successes.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding edits to primary-key promotion that treat the overwritten parent mapping as authoritative, mask the collection bug, or regress the established missing-parent-link check.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require recognizing that multiple one-to-one fields targeting the same parent compete for one parent-link mapping entry and that explicit parent_link=True must determine the retained inheritance link.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, runtime traces, patches, and test output showing how candidate one-to-one fields are collected by related parent and which field is later promoted to the primary key.
metadata.oracle_test: The repair should make field declaration order irrelevant by retaining the explicitly marked inheritance link during parent-link collection while preserving the error for a user-declared would-be parent link lacking parent_link=True.

scale.1: No task-causal explanation is established, or the explanation is directly contradicted by inspected source or runtime evidence.
scale.2: The trajectory locates relevant primary-key or parent metadata code but gives an incomplete or incorrect mechanism, such as blaming dictionary ordering alone or proposing arbitrary candidate selection.
scale.3: The trajectory demonstrates the order-sensitive behavior and recognizes competition among same-parent one-to-one fields, but does not produce a complete repair that preserves invalid missing-parent-link behavior.
scale.4: The trajectory correctly identifies the parent-link collection/overwrite mechanism and specifies or applies an order-independent repair based on the explicit parent_link marker, with no visible semantic contradiction, but complete validation is absent.
scale.5: A causally correct repair is visibly applied and subsequently validated for both declaration orders and for preservation of the missing-parent-link error or an equivalent regression case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal correctness of the MTI parent-link repair

applies_when: A code change or concrete patch proposal addresses selection among multiple OneToOneField references to the same MTI parent.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the parent-link candidate collection boundary so an explicit parent_link=True OneToOneField is preferred for each related parent while an unmarked OneToOneField remains a fallback candidate when no explicit link exists, preserving the established ImproperlyConfigured path for malformed MTI declarations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for filtering out every parent_link=False field, because that can bypass the existing missing-parent-link error; cap at 3 for an Options._prepare() scan of local_fields that works only for the reproducer but leaves the lossy ModelBase mapping unchanged or alters error semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible repository diff and resulting behavior outrank prose; if no diff is visible, an exact proposed conditional receives proposal credit only.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents accepting the tempting but regressive fixes of filtering solely to parent_link=True or searching arbitrary local fields during PK preparation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both order independence when a marked field exists and preservation of a fallback unmarked candidate when none exists.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or exact proposed logic in django/db/models/base.py around parent_links collection; correct logic retains one candidate per related model, replaces an unmarked candidate with a marked candidate, and never replaces a marked candidate with an unmarked one.
metadata.oracle_test: For each related-parent key: retain the first candidate initially; replace it when a later candidate has remote_field.parent_link=True; do not let a later unmarked candidate replace an already marked candidate.

scale.1: No implementation direction, or a change unrelated to parent-link candidate selection.
scale.2: Suggests or applies an order-sensitive, malformed, or semantically regressive workaround.
scale.3: Selects an explicit parent link for the reported models but does not preserve the unmarked fallback/error behavior, or modifies the wrong layer without adequate compatibility reasoning.
scale.4: Provides exact, coherent ModelBase candidate-preference logic satisfying both explicit-link preference and missing-link fallback, but lacks strong applied evidence or leaves minor integration uncertainty.
scale.5: Shows a clean applied diff at the ModelBase collection boundary implementing the preference invariant with no unrelated changes and with visible evidence that both compatibility conditions hold.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements parent_link preference without removing missing-link validation

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a code change for suppressing the empty choice in this RadioSelect case.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Targets the ModelChoiceField/model-form choice-construction boundary so a required field using RadioSelect has no empty label, while optional fields, ordinary Select widgets, explicit nonempty initial values, and normal RadioSelect selection behavior retain their intended semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for changes that remove empty choices from all RadioSelect or all required choice widgets without preserving optional radios; cap at 3 for a broad ChoiceWidget/template alteration lacking evidence that Select and explicit choices are unaffected.
metadata.evidence_authority: A concrete diff consistent with ModelChoiceField initialization and model-field required propagation outranks broad prose; behaviorally equivalent localized implementations may receive full credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents fixes at the rendering layer that hide legitimate explicit choices, alter every choice widget, or conflate model null=True with form blank=True.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a condition equivalent to required/blank=False plus RadioSelect, rather than globally removing empty choices or changing generic ChoiceWidget matching.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or precise implementation plan using the field's required state and RadioSelect widget type to control empty_label before choices are iterated.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic boundary is: suppress ModelChoiceField.empty_label when RadioSelect represents a required relationship field with no valid blank selection; do not redefine how ChoiceWidget formats empty values or how Select represents an unset required value.

scale.1: No implementation boundary is identified, or the proposed location is unrelated.
scale.2: Proposes a global template/ChoiceWidget workaround or unconditional removal of RadioSelect empty choices.
scale.3: Targets field choice construction but omits either the required-state condition or widget-specific condition, leaving a compatibility risk.
scale.4: Defines or applies the correct required-RadioSelect empty_label condition with a localized change, but provides limited compatibility reasoning.
scale.5: Defines or applies a minimal, behaviorally precise change at field choice construction and explicitly accounts for optional RadioSelect, ordinary Select, and existing selected values.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implementation boundary preserves field and widget semantics

applies_when: The visible trajectory develops or applies a candidate fix for the unwanted empty choice.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the visible candidate fix suppresses ModelChoiceField's generated empty label specifically when the field is required and uses RadioSelect, rather than changing generic choice matching or merely preventing the empty choice from appearing checked.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest candidate changes ChoiceWidget.format_value(), optgroups(), templates, or all RadioSelect instances to hide or deselect empty choices. Cap at 3 if it removes ModelChoiceField empty labels without both the required-state and widget-type restrictions, or if a claimed applied fix is contradicted by the visible diff.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible diff at ModelChoiceField initialization or an equivalent field-construction handoff outranks prose. A source-specific plan naming the existing required flag, the RadioSelect type check, and empty_label assignment outranks a generic statement that the field layer should change. Render-only experiments cannot prove that choice construction was fixed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding implementation-level credit for source browsing, global radio behavior changes, or a rendering workaround that leaves the invalid synthetic choice in the field's choices.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an implementable condition equivalent to required=True and a RadioSelect widget at the point where ModelChoiceField.empty_label is decided. Credit of 5 additionally requires an applied change plus visible task-relevant verification.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest unretracted plan or diff for the exact decision point, available inputs, and effect on generated choices. Distinguish locating ModelChoiceField from specifying an executable required-and-RadioSelect condition, and distinguish a proposed change from an applied change.
metadata.oracle_test: For a model-backed required relationship field rendered with RadioSelect, ModelChoiceField must omit its synthetic empty-label choice so a new form has only valid radios and none selected. Optional RadioSelect retains its empty choice; ordinary Select retains its conventional empty option; a valid initial relationship remains selected.

scale.1: No candidate implementation boundary is identified, or the latest candidate is unrelated to choice construction.
scale.2: The latest candidate operates on generic widget formatting, optgroups, templates, or all RadioSelect choices and would hide, deselect, or remove empty choices without preserving optional radios.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly identifies ModelChoiceField empty_label or field choice construction as the control point, but supplies no executable required-and-RadioSelect condition, or omits one of those restrictions.
scale.4: The trajectory gives an implementable required-and-RadioSelect condition at ModelChoiceField initialization or an equivalent localized handoff; it is only proposed, or it is applied without task-relevant compatibility verification.
scale.5: A localized required-and-RadioSelect empty_label change is visibly applied and verified for the required radio case, with visible evidence that optional radios and ordinary Select behavior remain unchanged.
