reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actionable required-RadioSelect empty-label fix

applies_when: The trajectory encounters failed setup attempts, inconsistent direct-widget results, or observations that conflict with its current hypothesis.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Recognizes invalid experiments, isolates why their evidence is non-authoritative, and revises the diagnosis using the real rendering pipeline rather than continuing from disproven assumptions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory continues to rely on a failed script or a direct optgroups(None) result after discovering that rendering first applies format_value; cap at 3 if contradictions are noticed but not resolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later successful minimal reproduction or repository test supersedes failed scripts and hand-simulated values; unexplained conflicting output limits confidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long exploratory runs that accumulate incompatible claims without determining which experiment matches Django's actual execution path.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both identifying why at least one prior observation was invalid and replacing it with a valid source trace or successful experiment.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible acknowledgment and correction of missing dependencies, invalid field arguments, absent model tables, direct optgroups misuse, stale code, or discrepancies between optgroups and get_context/render.
metadata.oracle_test: ChoiceWidget.get_context() formats an unset scalar into the value representation consumed by optgroups; direct optgroups calls with unformatted None do not model normal rendering, and a static ChoiceField does not establish ModelForm empty_label behavior.

scale.1: Contradictory or failed evidence is ignored and unsupported conclusions continue.
scale.2: Failures are noticed but still used as support, or new experiments repeat the same invalid setup.
scale.3: The trajectory changes direction after contradictions but does not explain their source or establish replacement evidence.
scale.4: Invalid evidence is explicitly diagnosed and replaced by a valid source trace or successful reproduction.
scale.5: Contradictions are systematically reconciled, evidence precedence is stated through the work, and the corrected experiment directly exercises the task's ModelForm rendering path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory or invalid runtime evidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains a failed experiment, an unfaithful reproduction, or outputs that conflict with its working hypothesis.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether invalid or conflicting observations are excluded from the final reasoning and replaced with authoritative evidence from the normal ModelForm-to-ModelChoiceField-to-widget path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when a failed or contradicted observation remains the basis of the latest conclusion. Cap at 2 when the trajectory repeatedly changes setup without obtaining authoritative replacement evidence, or treats direct widget behavior as proof of model blank propagation. Cap at 3 when better evidence appears but an incompatible earlier claim remains unreconciled.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing task-faithful ModelForm reproduction or repository regression test has highest authority. Directly inspected ModelChoiceField initialization and ModelChoiceIterator source is next. Normal get_context/render output may establish selection mechanics. Direct optgroups calls with unformatted values, failed scripts, and static ChoiceField examples cannot establish model-to-form empty-label behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding activity volume, dependency installation, or locally successful but task-unfaithful widget experiments as recovery, and avoids withholding credit solely because a sound replacement was made without a written retrospective.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires that the final visible reasoning no longer depends on invalid evidence and instead uses source or successful execution that reaches the model-backed field-construction path. An explicit verbal postmortem is not required when the replacement and abandonment are clear from subsequent work.
metadata.judge_focus: Track which observations the latest reasoning still relies on. Inspect whether dependency failures, invalid field arguments, missing tables, static ChoiceField substitutes, or direct optgroups calls are abandoned in favor of repository source, a task-faithful ModelForm reproduction, or a relevant repository test.
metadata.oracle_test: Normal rendering formats an unset single-choice value before optgroups, while ModelChoiceIterator contributes the empty choice only when ModelChoiceField.empty_label is not None. Therefore direct optgroups(None), static choices, or a script that never constructs the task's ModelForm cannot decide where model blank=False should suppress the choice.

scale.1: The latest conclusion still relies on failed execution, contradicted output, or an invalid API assumption.
scale.2: The trajectory notices or works around failures but continues with repeated invalid setups or task-unfaithful widget experiments and obtains no authoritative replacement evidence.

metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete latest diffs and syntax/runtime output override narrative assurances; unchanged inspected code is valid evidence of preservation.

metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require no visible corruption or semantic regression in middleware or security-check code.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diffs and file reads for django/middleware/security.py and django/core/checks/security/base.py, plus evidence about response setdefault behavior, explicit None, iterable or comma-separated policies, and E023 validation.

scale.1: Visible changes corrupt or materially break middleware, policy validation, security-check definitions, header preservation, or explicit opt-out behavior.

metadata.evidence_authority: Latest repository contents, unified diffs, syntax checks, and relevant runtime or check output outrank plans and assurances. An explicit SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY=None still suppresses the header and retains the established W022 deployment warning; invalid non-None policies still produce security.E023.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Do not penalize an explicitly acknowledged inconclusive setup failure as though it disproved the hypothesis. Cap at 2 when the trajectory only lacks discriminating evidence but makes no unsupported success claim and leaves no harmful edit. Assign at least 4 when relevant failures are called successful or malformed production source remains unrepaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed exception paths, successful source readbacks, diffs, and discriminating ORM controls outrank stated confidence. Dependency, settings, migration, and missing-table failures establish only that validation was inconclusive. A later explicit correction supersedes an earlier mistaken hypothesis.

metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require observable persistence in a contradicted or unsupported claim, an applied broad workaround, or an unrepaired edit. Merely lacking a direct model-instance control or repository test cannot exceed anchor 2 without evidence that the trajectory misrepresented or ignored what its checks established.

Look for continued broad lazy-wrapper changes after scalar-only checks, claims that setup failures validate ORM behavior, ignored model-instance failures, unrepaired source corruption, and failure to reconsider field identity when relation output-field evidence is available.

scale.1: The trajectory accurately labels the failed or inconclusive evidence, abandons or narrows the unsupported hypothesis, and leaves a coherent source state.
scale.2: The trajectory remains under-evidenced or does not complete a discriminating control, but does not claim confirmation, ignore a relevant contradiction, or leave a harmful production edit.
scale.3: The trajectory continues favoring the original diagnosis after non-discriminating scalar checks or setup failures, or makes an unverified edit, while stopping short of a clear false success claim or visibly broken source.
scale.4: The trajectory persists with a broad lazy-object workaround despite relevant contrary evidence, treats inconclusive checks as support, or leaves a malformed or behaviorally unsupported production change.

Cap at 1 for unrepaired malformed source or a broad change to LazyObject conversion protocols that is supported only by primitive conversion tests and not by ORM semantics. Failed environment setup is not evidence that the regression is fixed.

A command that merely attempts an edit is not proof when later output shows corruption, duplication, or no effective change.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding high credit for a plausible verbal diagnosis, an import-only patch, direct lazy-wrapper conversion tests, or a global proxy modification that does not demonstrate the failing ORM query behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visibly applied, syntactically coherent production change and successful task-relevant test output. Score 5 additionally requires the reported nested Subquery/annotation/filter shape, or an equivalent repository regression test, to pass.

scale.2: Work is task-related but remains fragmentary at cutoff, such as an import-only production edit, an incomplete code path, or experiments that do not establish a coherent fix.

Cap at 3 for a coherent but wrong-layer LazyObject, Field, or lookup-wide experiment, even if primitive tests pass.

scale.1: The last visible production state is malformed, or its only applied change is a behaviorally inert fragment such as an isolated import.
scale.2: Work remains exploratory at cutoff: no effective production change, faithful regression reproduction, or discriminating ORM control is visibly established.
scale.3: A faithful failing reproduction or discriminating control is established, or a coherent applied experiment is confirmed by source readback, but the correct output-field fix and successful regression validation are absent.
scale.4: A coherent narrow correction to single-selection Query/Subquery output-field propagation is visibly applied and inspected, with successful focused semantic checks short of a complete faithful regression run.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Leaves a coherent task-causal artifact at cutoff

applies_when: The trajectory has inspected the composed-index deletion path or attempted a task-specific reproduction, implementation, or validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible evidence is converted into a safe, actionable decision for deleting only the legacy non-unique composed index, including correct rejection of probes that never established the required overlapping database objects.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the assistant accepts an empty constraint inventory, a no-op deletion, setup output, or a descriptive script as proof of the fix. Cap at 3 if the narrow strategy remains only proposed or an edit attempt visibly failed, unless the trajectory explicitly rejects a misleading probe and makes a source-grounded safe decision. Cap at 3 while an executable schema diagnostic, source backup, rewrite utility, malformed file, or other unresolved non-production artifact remains inside the repository. Any visible arbitrary deletion, uniqueness loss, weakened exact-one guard, or name-based targeting forces score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff and source contents determine whether work was applied. Repository-defined _constraint_names() behavior and observed database inventories outrank assistant claims, generated-name reasoning, synthetic printouts, and apparent success from an empty transition. A probe is authoritative only after it shows both same-column object types on the actual table.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards exploration volume, a merely written script, an empty no-op transition, or an intended edit that did not apply as though it were a usable resolution; alternatively, it overlooks a trajectory that correctly invalidates contradictory probe output and avoids redesigning production code around it.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires either an actionable backend-neutral selection strategy using the existing index and uniqueness metadata, or an explicit recognition that an apparently successful operation was non-evidence because the required overlapping pre-state was absent. A score of 5 requires the narrow production change to be visibly present and free of unresolved repository contamination.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant's current decision after its latest relevant source inspection, probe, edit attempt, and workspace observation. Credit an exact proposed remedy separately from a production edit that is visibly present.
metadata.oracle_test: A usable decision identifies the legacy target by same columns with index=True and unique=False, preserves the same-column unique object and the exact-one guard, and treats database success as meaningful only when both objects existed before deletion.
metadata.stage: Establish and implement the narrow fix

scale.1: The current decision is unsafe or causally wrong: it may delete arbitrary or multiple candidates, remove uniqueness, weaken the exact-one guard, rely on names or ordering, or treat contradicted output as success.
scale.2: The trajectory locates the relevant path or two-candidate symptom but ends without an actionable semantic target and without a reliable interpretation of failed or empty validation.
scale.3: The trajectory makes one reliable advance—either it identifies the existing backend-neutral non-unique selection strategy, or it explicitly rejects an apparently successful probe because the overlapping pre-state was absent—but it has not yet produced a clean, usable resolution.
scale.4: The trajectory reaches a safe actionable decision: it specifies index=True with unique=False while preserving uniqueness and one-target safety, or it correctly invalidates a misleading no-op probe and returns to a source-grounded selective-deletion decision; the production change is not yet both visibly applied and meaningfully validated.
scale.5: The narrow selective-deletion change is visibly applied in production code, neighboring unique-deletion and exact-one behavior remain intact, the workspace contains no unresolved non-production artifacts, and visible validation or source checks support the decision without unresolved contradiction.

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or explains why deleting the legacy composed index finds the wrong number of constraints.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credits an assistant-authored causal explanation that the same-column unique object may also satisfy index=True, so legacy index deletion must additionally select unique=False while retaining the exact-one safety check.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the assistant claims index=True excludes unique objects, attributes identity to suffixes or ordering, or treats an empty or broken probe as confirmation. Cap at 3 if unique=False is proposed without connecting it to the exact-one failure and surviving uniqueness.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source defining alter_index_together(), _delete_composed_index(), and _constraint_names(), plus observed output from an actually executed faithful introspection probe, outrank guesses based on generated names or descriptive scripts.
metadata.failure_mode: The trajectory repeats the exception, relies on names or unexecuted examples, or never states the non-unique semantic distinction.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an explicit assistant-authored conclusion that index=True can match both the ordinary non-unique index and the same-column unique object. A score above 3 additionally requires unique=False to be identified as the missing discriminator.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant's own reasoning together with visible source or executed introspection evidence. Names, flags, or exceptions appearing only in tool output do not by themselves establish the diagnosis.
metadata.oracle_test: The supported causal chain is: alter_index_together() supplies index=True; backend introspection may report both objects as indexes; _constraint_names() therefore returns two names; adding unique=False narrows the ordinary-index candidate set to one.

scale.1: No assistant-authored task-causal conclusion is visible, or the conclusion conflicts with visible source or database evidence.
scale.2: Locates the deletion helper or describes the two-result symptom, but does not explicitly distinguish a non-unique index from an indexed unique object.
scale.3: Explicitly explains that both same-column objects can satisfy index=True, using plausible source or executed evidence, but does not clearly establish the unique=False remedy.
scale.4: Connects index=True plus the missing unique=False filter to the exact-one ValueError and states that the unique constraint must survive.
scale.5: Also verifies the relevant _constraint_names() boolean-filter contract and compatibility boundaries such as the unchanged exact-one guard, explicit-object exclusions, or backend forwarding.

applies_when: The trajectory is at a validation stage involving tests, reproductions, introspection, or database integrity behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures actually executed task-relevant validation, from faithful reproduction of the overlapping-object failure through successful deletion and proof that the ordinary index is absent while uniqueness survives.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if no task-relevant validation command ran, or if destructive or invalid output is ignored while success is claimed. Cap at 2 when all real attempts fail during imports, settings, app registration, syntax, runner setup, or before the relevant schema operation; synthetic filtering cannot lift this cap. Cap at 3 when a real operation only reproduces the old failure, or deletion succeeds without any reliable post-deletion preservation evidence. metadata.evidence_authority: Observed database behavior and introspection on the same actual table and connection outrank assistant success claims, synthetic filtering, generated-name guesses, and model declarations. Later contradictory output overrides earlier apparent success. A command failing before table creation or the relevant operation cannot establish task behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge treats a written or descriptive script as executed validation, awards partial-reproduction credit to setup failures or source exploration, counts exception absence as preservation, or overlooks later evidence that uniqueness was removed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires an actually executed validation command with task-relevant output. A score above 2 requires a real database table and a schema-editor or migration operation that reaches the overlapping-constraint behavior. A score above 3 requires either successful index_together deletion or a valid destructive result that is explicitly recognized and followed by a visible revert or correction. A score of 5 requires reliable pre-state and post-state evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Classify only commands that visibly executed and use their observed output. Distinguish source inspection, a script merely written, descriptive printing, model metadata, synthetic dictionaries, skipped tests, and setup failures from a schema-editor or migration operation on an actual table. Apply exactly one scale anchor based on the furthest assertion actually reached.

scale.1: No executed command reaches task-relevant validation output, or the trajectory ignores material invalid or destructive evidence while claiming success.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility boundaries preserved

applies_when: The trajectory discusses why QuerySet.in_bulk() rejects a field whose uniqueness is declared through Meta.constraints.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible reasoning identifies the field.unique-only validation as the cause and correctly limits additional eligibility to an unconditional, single-field UniqueConstraint that guarantees the selected field is unique by itself.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any final claim that every field appearing in a composite or conditional UniqueConstraint is individually eligible caps this rubric at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source observations and concrete model metadata outrank unsupported explanations; later corrected reasoning outranks earlier superseded claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating constraint membership as equivalent to total uniqueness of one field.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly recognizing that membership in a multi-field UniqueConstraint does not make an individual field unique.
metadata.judge_focus: Statements and inspected source showing the current in_bulk() guard, Options.total_unique_constraints, and the distinction between singleton and composite constraints.
metadata.oracle_test: A field covered by UniqueConstraint(fields=['slug'], condition=None) is eligible; a field covered only by UniqueConstraint(fields=['slug', 'locale'], ...) or a conditional constraint is not individually guaranteed unique.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis is visible, or the explanation attributes the failure to an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: Recognizes that UniqueConstraint is relevant but proposes raw constraint membership or otherwise treats composite or conditional constraints as sufficient.
scale.3: Correctly identifies the field.unique-only guard and unconditional constraints, but leaves singleton-versus-composite semantics unstated or ambiguous.
scale.4: Correctly identifies the existing guard, total/unconditional constraints, and the singleton-field requirement, with minor imprecision that does not alter the boundary.
scale.5: Precisely derives the complete boundary from visible source: preserve pk and field.unique behavior, additionally accept exactly single-field total UniqueConstraints, and reject composite and conditional constraints.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct uniqueness diagnosis and semantic boundary

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, or runs tests or reproduction scripts concerning in_bulk() field_name uniqueness.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible tests or runtime evidence demonstrate the new singleton-UniqueConstraint behavior and protect rejection of fields that are not individually unique, while retaining established in_bulk() behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: OperationalError, missing settings, import failures, syntax-only checks, or id_list=[] results cannot establish end-to-end success; any displayed failing relevant assertion caps credit at 3 until a corrected rerun passes.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful repository test-run output is strongest, followed by an executed database-backed reproducer; source inspection and empty-id-list validation probes are weaker because they may avoid query execution.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking passage beyond the validation guard, static string matching, or an empty input fast path for proof that in_bulk() works correctly.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires executed evidence for both acceptance of a singleton unconditional UniqueConstraint and rejection of at least one non-individually-unique field.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed test commands and outputs, test model definitions, assertions, and repository test changes covering positive and negative cases.
metadata.oracle_test: Create rows with distinct constrained values, call in_bulk(..., field_name='slug'), and assert the returned dictionary is keyed by slug; also assert ValueError for an unconstrained field and preferably for one component of a composite or conditional constraint.

scale.1: No relevant test or runtime evidence is visible, or visible evidence directly shows the intended behavior failing without resolution.
scale.2: Only blocked executions, syntax/import checks, source matching, or unexecuted test proposals are visible.
scale.3: A relevant executable check succeeds only for the positive case or only at validation level, without a decisive negative regression case.
scale.4: Executed task-specific evidence passes for singleton-constraint acceptance and non-unique rejection, but does not run the appropriate repository tests or omits broader compatibility coverage.
scale.5: Focused repository tests or equivalent database-backed tests visibly pass and cover singleton UniqueConstraint acceptance, ordinary non-unique rejection, composite or conditional rejection, and preservation of unique=True or pk behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific behavioral and regression evidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains a failed test, traceback, malformed edit, or runtime observation that contradicts an earlier assumption about the proposed fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory uses contradictory evidence to revise the causal model or implementation, removes the defective approach, and produces new visible evidence tied to the corrected behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible state still contains the defect exposed by earlier evidence, or the file is merely reverted with no corrected implementation, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed traceback, test output, latest file content, and latest diff outrank statements that an issue is harmless or fixed; only evidence after the corrective change establishes recovery.
metadata.failure_mode: Continuing after contradictory output, rationalizing a failure as unrelated, or layering edits without restoring a coherent final source state.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both a visible correction addressing the actual cause and a post-correction check relevant to that cause.
metadata.judge_focus: The sequence from contradiction through diagnosis, corrective edit, cleanup, and rerun, especially for composite constraints, pk handling, cached_property use, imports, indentation, and duplicate code.
metadata.oracle_test: Examples include replacing field_name in constraint.fields after a composite case is wrongly accepted, using total_unique_constraints as a property rather than a callable, preserving the pk special case, and rerunning the check that originally exposed the defect.

scale.1: Contradictory evidence is ignored, denied, or followed by further changes that leave the latest state clearly broken.
scale.2: The contradiction is acknowledged or reverted, but no correct replacement is visibly established.
scale.3: The underlying cause is correctly identified and the implementation is visibly corrected, but no relevant post-correction execution is shown.
scale.4: The cause is corrected and the previously failing or equivalent focused check visibly succeeds afterward.
scale.5: The trajectory fully closes the loop: isolates the cause, corrects the semantic or structural defect, removes stale or duplicate artifacts, reruns decisive checks successfully, and shows a coherent latest diff or file state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory implementation evidence

applies_when: The task requires QuerySet.in_bulk() to recognize fields made globally unique by model UniqueConstraint declarations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible implementation makes in_bulk() accept fields covered by unconditional single-field UniqueConstraints while preserving rejection of fields that are only members of composite or conditional constraints.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Accepting a field merely because it appears anywhere in a multi-field constraint, accepting a conditional constraint, mutating Field.unique, using a helper that cannot access the model metadata, leaving the original validation active, or leaving syntax/class structure broken caps the score at 2. A later visible correction removes the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later repository file reads and git diffs override earlier plans or claimed edits. Executed test output against the edited repository outranks standalone predicate simulations, temporary scripts, and narrative claims. A proposed edit receives no applied-work credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for the common but incorrect membership test `field_name in constraint.fields`, for confusing unique-together combinations with individual uniqueness, and for rewarding extensive investigation or temporary tests when no viable repository implementation exists.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a visibly applied, syntactically coherent repository change whose predicate treats a field as constraint-unique only when an entry in model._meta.total_unique_constraints has fields exactly equal to the singleton field tuple, or uses an observably equivalent check.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the cutoff-visible repository code governing in_bulk() field validation and focused execution evidence for singleton constraints, composite constraints, conditional constraints, unique=True fields, and primary-key behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For field_name other than 'pk', validity is established by Field.unique or by an unconditional UniqueConstraint whose fields are exactly (field_name,). A field appearing only in ('field_name', 'other') is not individually unique; conditional constraints are excluded by total_unique_constraints.

scale.1: No viable applied predicate is visible at cutoff: the original behavior remains, the edit is syntactically or structurally unusable, or its design cannot access the required model metadata.
scale.2: A repository change or concrete implementation attempt is visible, but it is incomplete or semantically overbroad, such as accepting any member of a composite or conditional constraint; it does not establish the required behavior correctly.
scale.3: A coherent singleton-only predicate is visibly applied, but focused execution evidence is absent, inconclusive, or leaves a task-relevant semantic case unresolved.
scale.4: A correct singleton-only predicate is visibly applied and executed evidence confirms the target case plus at least one important negative case such as composite or conditional uniqueness, with no remaining task-relevant contradiction.
scale.5: A correct singleton-only predicate is visibly applied, and focused execution evidence confirms the target single-field UniqueConstraint case, rejection of composite and conditional cases, and preservation of unique=True and primary-key behavior, with no unresolved task-relevant contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct and applied in_bulk() uniqueness predicate

applies_when: The task requires QuerySet.in_bulk() to recognize fields made globally unique by model UniqueConstraint declarations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the cutoff-visible in_bulk() validation path for an applied predicate that accepts field-level uniqueness and unconditional singleton UniqueConstraints, rejects composite and conditional uniqueness, and preserves primary-key handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unused helper, retention of the original field.unique-only active path, or unparseable source receives score 1. An actively wired replacement with a localized binding, placement, invocation, primary-key, conditional, mutation, or composite-membership defect is capped at 2. Any unresolved post-edit failure of the active predicate prevents credit above 2; a later visible correction and relevant rerun remove the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest repository file reads and diffs determine the active implementation and override earlier plans or superseded edits. Post-edit execution against that state outranks static inspection and predicate-only simulations. A missing-table error can show that validation was passed but cannot establish successful database behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating an unused proposal with an active but defective implementation, treating ordinary non-unique rejection as proof of singleton-only semantics, or accepting a field merely because it occurs anywhere in a uniqueness declaration.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a callable, active predicate equivalent to Field.unique or an unconditional UniqueConstraint whose fields equal the singleton tuple containing field_name. Credit above 3 requires post-edit execution that demonstrates both singleton-constraint acceptance and rejection of a field appearing only in a composite constraint.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest active path reached by in_bulk(), including helper placement and binding, access to model metadata, exact singleton comparison, preservation of the primary-key exception, and executions performed after the latest relevant edit.
metadata.oracle_test: For field_name other than 'pk', validation may proceed only when the resolved field is unique or model._meta.total_unique_constraints contains an entry whose fields are exactly (field_name,). A field occurring only in a multi-field constraint or a conditional constraint must still raise ValueError.

scale.1: No active replacement exists: in_bulk() still follows the original field.unique-only validation, the proposed helper is unused, or the latest source cannot parse or define a usable call path.
scale.2: A replacement is actively wired into in_bulk(), but a localized defect makes it incorrect or unusable, such as wrong helper binding, membership in a composite constraint, conditional-constraint acceptance, Field.unique mutation, or loss of primary-key handling.
scale.3: A callable active predicate correctly requires field-level uniqueness or an unconditional singleton UniqueConstraint, but post-edit evidence is absent, limited to static or predicate-only checks, uses an empty-input path, or does not demonstrate composite-constraint rejection.
scale.4: The correct active predicate is followed by execution demonstrating singleton UniqueConstraint acceptance and rejection of a field that appears only in a composite constraint, with no unresolved contradiction in the active path.
scale.5: Focused repository or equivalent database-backed tests pass for singleton UniqueConstraint acceptance, composite and conditional rejection, ordinary non-unique rejection, and preservation of unique=True and primary-key behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operative and semantically correct in_bulk uniqueness predicate

applies_when: The task concerns whether a model Meta.ordering path ending in a registered lookup passes Django system checks.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess task-specific executed validation of the model system check, including the valid non-transform lookup case and preservation of errors for invalid ordering paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if setup failures prevent the task-level assertion from running. Cap at 3 if only the positive case is executed or if validation cannot be tied to the applied code. A failed task-level test cannot receive credit merely because its expected result was described.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed test or reproducer output outranks predicted output and assertions in prose. A full model check on representative models outranks isolated get_lookup()/get_transform() introspection. Later failing output supersedes an earlier expectation of success.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents dependency installation, syntax-only checks, isolated class introspection, and unexecuted test scripts from being mistaken for behavioral regression evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require an executed task-level check or focused test with observed results after the relevant implementation state; API introspection alone cannot exceed score 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed model checks or focused tests using a related path ending in isnull, their observed models.E015 results, and negative controls for bogus lookups; also recognize relevant existing-test execution.
metadata.oracle_test: A representative model with Meta.ordering containing supply__product__parent__isnull should produce no models.E015, while a nonexistent terminal lookup should still produce models.E015; registered transforms and ordinary valid ordering fields should remain accepted.

scale.1: No relevant executed validation is visible.
scale.2: A relevant test or reproducer is attempted but does not reach the task assertion because of setup, import, configuration, or collection failure.
scale.3: Executed evidence confirms a prerequisite or reproduces the bug, but does not verify the repaired task-level behavior with adequate controls.
scale.4: An executed task-level check verifies that a representative registered non-transform lookup no longer raises models.E015 after the change.
scale.5: Executed focused validation verifies the corrected lookup case and at least one meaningful regression control, such as an invalid lookup still raising models.E015 or registered transforms remaining valid.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Behavioral validation of ordering lookup checks

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or modifies Django's validation of related paths in model Meta.ordering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes only the related-ordering validation boundary so an unresolved path component is accepted when it is a field-specific registered transform or lookup, while preserving E015 for components that are neither.

metadata.contradiction_rule: No visible applied change caps credit at 3. A malformed file, hard-coded global list of lookup names, unconditional acceptance of unresolved suffixes, or replacement of transform handling with lookup-only handling caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible file content and git diff outrank statements that a fix was applied; syntactically valid source outranks an earlier malformed edit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for broad bypasses, hard-coded built-in lookup lists, lookup-only fixes that regress transforms, and claims of modification unsupported by the visible working tree.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a visible applied source change that preserves both get_transform() and get_lookup() acceptance and remains syntactically valid.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible final source content or diff in django/db/models/base.py, especially the FieldDoesNotExist/AttributeError branch of Model._check_ordering().
metadata.oracle_test: The rejection predicate is semantically equivalent to: reject when no prior field exists, or when the unresolved component is neither a transform nor a lookup registered for that field.

scale.1: The visible change is unrelated, leaves the defect unchanged, or corrupts the source.
scale.2: A change is attempted but is overbroad or semantically wrong, such as accepting all suffixes, hard-coding lookup names, or losing transform support.
scale.3: The correct field-specific transform-or-lookup predicate is clearly proposed, but no valid applied source change is visible, or the applied edit remains incomplete.
scale.4: A syntactically valid applied change implements the correct predicate in _check_ordering(), with only minor style or scope noise.
scale.5: A clean, minimal, idiomatic applied change implements the correct predicate at the existing exception branch without unrelated production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct and minimal validation change

applies_when: The trajectory creates, discusses, or executes evidence intended to demonstrate the ordering-check regression and its fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides a repository regression test using model Meta.ordering with a terminal non-Transform lookup and obtains authoritative focused test evidence, rather than relying only on lookup introspection or an ad hoc script.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Dependency, settings, import, collection, or syntax failures are not passing evidence. If no test reaches Model.check(), credit is capped at 3; if the only evidence tests lookup registration in isolation, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful repository test invoking Model.check() outranks isolated get_lookup() introspection; complete test output outranks assertions that tests passed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating package installation, source compilation, QuerySet construction, or Field.get_lookup() introspection as proof that the model system check is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a tracked regression test for Meta.ordering and a successful focused execution; anchor 5 additionally requires relevant neighboring tests or a broader suite to pass.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible additions under tests/invalid_models_tests, direct Model.check() assertions, test-run commands, and their complete outputs.
metadata.oracle_test: A model whose ordering ends in a valid lookup such as field__isnull or a related path ending in __isnull has no models.E015 result after the fix.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence, or the visible test attempt cannot execute because of syntax or setup failure.
scale.2: Only indirect evidence is shown, such as get_lookup()/get_transform() introspection or an unexecuted ad hoc script.
scale.3: A direct Model.check() reproduction is reached or a suitable repository regression test is added, but the repository test is absent, unexecuted, or lacks a successful result.
scale.4: A focused repository regression test for valid lookup ordering is present and visibly passes, with no broader relevant test result.
scale.5: The focused regression test passes and relevant neighboring ordering/model-check tests also visibly pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression test coverage

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates Django model Meta.ordering validation for lookup-separated field paths.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory correctly explains why a valid terminal lookup in a related ordering path is rejected and identifies the appropriate field lookup API needed to preserve invalid-path detection.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims isnull is a transform, proposes accepting every unresolved suffix, or otherwise removes meaningful invalid-ordering detection. Cap at 3 if it identifies the symptom but never connects it to get_lookup() or equivalent registered-lookup semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly inspected repository code and tool-observed API behavior outrank unsupported assertions. A demonstrated get_transform('isnull') result of None together with a non-None get_lookup('isnull') result is strongest; accurate source-based reasoning is sufficient when execution is unavailable.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding repetitive repository exploration, runtime anecdotes, or generic lookup discussion as equivalent to identifying the exact semantic mismatch in the system check.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require explicit recognition that the terminal component is a valid registered Lookup but not a Transform and that lookup validity must be checked without accepting arbitrary names.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source reads, API inspection, and reasoning about _check_ordering(), Field.get_transform(), Field.get_lookup(), Lookup, Transform, and the terminal isnull path component.
metadata.oracle_test: For a path such as supply__product__parent__isnull, supply, product, and parent resolve as fields; isnull does not resolve as a field or transform but does resolve through the preceding field's registered lookup API. A bogus terminal name must remain invalid.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or the explanation is materially wrong.
scale.2: Locates the ordering check or failing condition but gives only a vague or partly incorrect explanation.
scale.3: Correctly states that isnull is a lookup rather than a transform, but does not establish the governing API or how invalid suffixes remain rejected.
scale.4: Correctly traces the related path and identifies get_lookup() or equivalent registered-lookup resolution as the missing validation alongside existing transform handling.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in score 4 and explicitly accounts for preservation of valid transforms and rejection of nonexistent fields or lookups.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of ordering lookup validation

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes the failure of model Meta.ordering validation for a path ending in a lookup such as isnull.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that Model._check_ordering() resolves relation-path components correctly but rejects the terminal isnull component because it checks get_transform() even though isnull is a registered Lookup rather than a Transform.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the trajectory claims isnull is a Transform, attributes the error to query execution rather than the system check, or proposes treating every unresolved suffix as valid, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and executable method results outrank unsupported narrative; a direct result showing get_transform('isnull') is None and get_lookup('isnull') returns IsNull is decisive.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards precise causal analysis rather than merely repeating the ticket text or assuming that successful QuerySet execution proves how the system-check code validates names.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require locating the related-field loop in Model._check_ordering() and explaining the Lookup-versus-Transform distinction.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing of supply__product__parent__isnull through django/db/models/base.py and concrete evidence distinguishing Field.get_transform('isnull') from Field.get_lookup('isnull').
metadata.oracle_test: For a resolved field path ending in isnull, the terminal name is absent from model fields, get_transform('isnull') is None, and get_lookup('isnull') resolves to the registered IsNull lookup.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the visible source behavior.
scale.2: Recognizes that _check_ordering() raises E015 near get_transform(), but does not correctly distinguish fields, transforms, and lookups.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 for an applied shared-core edit, an empty-alias shortcut, a condition equivalent to update_can_self_select and not single_alias, or removal of the entire delegation guard. Cap at 2 for proposing any of those approaches without applying it. Cap at 3 for a different backend condition whose equivalence is not demonstrated.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible repository diffs and displayed post-edit source outrank prose descriptions. A terminal unified diff is applied evidence. A concrete textual proposal may establish direction but not application; temporary analysis files and scripts are not repository implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating the shared compiler as the correct repair site, confusing an incidental empty alias map with the semantic condition, or rewarding an overbroad backend rewrite merely because it suppresses the example subquery.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require an applied edit in django/db/backends/mysql/compiler.py equivalent to retaining only the single_alias delegation condition. An unapplied proposal cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the proposed or applied file, exact boolean condition, and retained surrounding branches. Check that the change removes only the backend feature alternative rather than changing shared compiler semantics or forcing one path for every delete.
metadata.oracle_test: The narrow boundary is the MySQL SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql() guard: single_alias continues to call the parent implementation, while non-single-alias queries use the existing MySQL DELETE <target> FROM construction regardless of update_can_self_select.

scale.1: An implementation is applied at the wrong layer or with a condition that visibly destroys the required branch split.
scale.2: No implementation is applied and the concrete proposed boundary is wrong or absent.
scale.3: The correct MySQL-specific boundary is concretely proposed but not applied, or a relevant backend edit is applied with unproven equivalence to the narrow condition.

Cap at 3 if it removes the entire single-alias safeguard or introduces a different compound condition without demonstrating equivalent behavior. Unapplied proposals cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible final or intermediate repository diff is authoritative over claims in thoughts or prose. Executed focused tests and captured generated SQL outrank static inspection scripts; source inspection outranks unsupported assertions about compiler behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long but unapplied investigation, superficial text-based verification, broad removal of compiler safeguards, or a change to Django's shared SQLDeleteCompiler as though it were the narrow backend fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a visible task-causal source edit. Score 4 or 5 additionally requires preserving the single-alias base-compiler path while removing the backend-feature gate that sends eligible multi-alias deletes to the self-subquery implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source edits or diffs to the MySQL delete compiler, then inspect any focused SQL-generation or deletion tests. Distinguish an applied source change from a proposed change or explanatory script.
metadata.oracle_test: For this codebase, the task-causal correction is in the MySQL SQLDeleteCompiler: ordinary single-alias deletion continues through the parent implementation, while the backend feature flag no longer diverts multi-alias deletion to DELETE ... WHERE pk IN (SELECT pk FROM the same table). The MySQL-specific DELETE <target-alias> FROM ... path must remain available for the latter case.

scale.1: A visible source edit is applied, but it targets the wrong layer or contradicts the required compiler semantics, such as changing the shared delete compiler or adding an empty-alias shortcut.

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an unfiltered QuerySet.delete() enters the primary-key subquery path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims that super().as_sql() always produces a subquery, that single_alias=True selects the subquery branch, or that DeleteQuery.delete_batch() is the cause of the shown QuerySet.all().delete() SQL without reconciling the actual compiler flow.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly displayed current source and a reproduced compiled query outrank speculation, historical guesses, or comments read without control-flow tracing.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding repeated repository exploration, feature-flag speculation, or inverted branch reasoning as a diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require identifying the core SQLDeleteCompiler fallback as the producer of DELETE ... WHERE pk IN (SELECT pk FROM the same table), not merely locating the MySQL compiler.
metadata.judge_focus: Source-backed tracing through QuerySet deletion and django/db/models/sql/compiler.py, especially SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias, alias initialization or the empty WHERE condition, and the pk__in inner-query fallback.
metadata.oracle_test: For an unfiltered model delete, no predicate or join must be preserved, so the semantic SQL oracle is a direct DELETE FROM the model table; the self-selecting pk__in wrapper is unnecessary.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or the explanation is incompatible with the displayed compiler control flow.
scale.2: Finds delete-related files or mentions aliases/subqueries but leaves the causal branch unresolved or materially confused.

applies_when: The rollout investigates why the reported MySQL or MariaDB delete reaches a self-referential primary-key subquery.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identify from visible source evidence how the MySQL delete compiler's feature-gated delegation allows a non-single-alias delete to enter the parent compiler's primary-key subquery fallback, while correctly recognizing that the parent's single-alias branch is the direct-delete path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the rollout claims that single_alias itself produces the subquery, that super().as_sql() always produces a subquery, or that DeleteQuery.delete_batch() is the demonstrated cause without reconciling the displayed compiler flow. Cap at 1 if it applies or endorses a patch whose rationale remains inverted after contrary source evidence is visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed current source and captured compiled SQL outrank issue paraphrases, historical guesses, comments considered without their control flow, and synthetic scripts that merely restate assumed branch outcomes.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding extensive exploration, empty-alias speculation, or repeated feature-flag discussion when the trajectory has not resolved which concrete branch emits the reported SQL.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require the diagnosis to state that single_alias selects the parent's direct path and that the self-subquery is produced by the parent's non-single-alias fallback reached through the backend feature alternative.

The MySQL override should delegate only for single_alias; allowing update_can_self_select alone to delegate a multi-alias query exposes the parent self-subquery path instead of MySQL's DELETE <target> FROM path.

metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one successful nonconstant resolved-expression check in addition to the constant case.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed comparisons between wrapped and unwrapped resolved expressions, SQL for wrapped field/function expressions, aggregate cases, nested wrappers, or relevant existing Django tests.

metadata.failure_mode: Treats a helper-level empty list, a printed 'PASS', or an invalid SQL substring check as proof that the actual queryset is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful evidence from the full aggregate queryset, not only direct get_group_by_cols() calls.

scale.1: No executed relevant validation, or only setup/import failures occur.
scale.2: An attempted task-shaped test fails or produces contradictory output without recovery.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive regression evidence for generated GROUP BY SQL

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why ExpressionWrapper changes an inner ORM expression's contribution to GROUP BY.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly and stably traces the defect to ExpressionWrapper using generic non-aggregate grouping behavior instead of preserving the wrapped expression's get_group_by_cols() result, then identifies transparent delegation—not constant detection—as the causal repair invariant.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible reasoning still misattributes get_group_by_cols() to the wrong class, treats an excerpt of another class as ExpressionWrapper's implementation, continues toward detecting or filtering constants, or claims all wrapped expressions should contribute no grouping columns. Cap at 3 if delegation is stated but contradicted by an unresolved claim that nonconstant wrapped expressions may be suppressed. Editing failures alone do not reduce a stable causal diagnosis unless they introduce or preserve contradictory semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: Correctly attributed source definitions and direct method-dispatch probes outrank SQL symptom reproduction or broad compiler exploration. A later source read or corrected conclusion supersedes earlier speculation, but later unresolved uncertainty about which class owns an inspected method controls over an earlier plausible statement.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes reproduction of the unwanted SQL for causal diagnosis, infers method ownership from an overbroad source excerpt, rewards an unsettled constant-special-casing direction, or requires a successful patch before crediting an otherwise exact dispatch-level diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a stable, correctly attributed causal trace showing that ExpressionWrapper lacks the needed override and therefore receives generic grouping behavior, or an equally decisive direct comparison showing the wrapper contributes itself while Value contributes no grouping columns. Credit above 3 additionally requires an explicit conclusion that ExpressionWrapper must return its inner expression's own get_group_by_cols() result without classifying constants. Credit 5 requires successful evidence using resolved expressions on both constant and grouping-required sides.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest settled account of which class supplies ExpressionWrapper's grouping behavior, the actual Value grouping override, direct wrapped-versus-unwrapped probes when present, and whether the proposed invariant delegates all grouping decisions to the resolved inner expression.
metadata.oracle_test: The diagnosis should predict that ExpressionWrapper(Value(3), output_field=...).get_group_by_cols() matches Value(3).get_group_by_cols() and is empty, while an ExpressionWrapper around a resolved column or other grouping-required expression returns exactly the inner expression's required grouping columns.

scale.1: No coherent causal account is established, or the latest account attributes the behavior to an unrelated mechanism.
scale.2: The SQL or wrapped-versus-unwrapped symptom is recognized, but source ownership remains unresolved, the explanation is incomplete, or the latest direction seeks to detect constants rather than explain wrapper dispatch.
scale.3: A stable source trace correctly identifies that ExpressionWrapper receives generic grouping behavior because it lacks the needed override, or decisive runtime evidence establishes the wrapper-versus-inner grouping contrast, but transparent delegation is not yet stated unambiguously.
scale.4: Correct source or runtime evidence establishes the dispatch defect, and the trajectory explicitly concludes that ExpressionWrapper must delegate get_group_by_cols() to the inner expression rather than classify constants; two-sided resolved-expression validation is incomplete.
scale.5: The explicit delegation invariant is supported by successful evidence that a wrapped constant contributes no grouping term and a wrapped resolved nonconstant expression retains exactly its required grouping columns.

metadata.evidence_authority: An intact applied diff plus executed task-shaped checks outranks direct runtime probes; direct probes and exact source tracing outrank an unsupported explanation. Later corrected conclusions supersede earlier exploration, but an unrepaired contradictory final implementation supersedes a correct earlier hypothesis.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for symptom recognition alone, speculative constant detection, compiler-level workarounds, or a return-empty implementation that fixes the example by breaking valid wrapped expressions.

applies_when: The visible prefix attempts to execute or compile querysets for the reported self-referential ForeignKey ordering behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the quality of completed empirical evidence showing the erroneous join and ordering direction and comparing it with semantically informative control orderings.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if all reproduction attempts fail before SQL is produced. Cap at 3 if the trajectory reports conclusions inconsistent with its own generated SQL or uses a materially different relationship shape that does not exercise the self-referential terminal-attname case.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual query compiler output or passing assertions outrank predicted SQL and prose. Repository status and command observations determine whether a reproduction completed; installation attempts and scripts that terminate before query compilation are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents dependency installation, model introspection, or copied issue SQL from being mistaken for a successful, causally discriminating reproduction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require visible successful compilation or execution of the problematic queryset. Scores 4 and 5 additionally require at least one completed control that isolates terminal-attname handling from general ordering behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect completed command output for generated SQL, especially the ordered column, direction, and join structure for the terminal-attname form and controls such as explicit primary-key traversal, annotation-based column ordering, or reversed direction.
metadata.oracle_test: The defective form visibly adds traversal to the self-related table and inherits its default ordering direction, while explicit traversal to the primary key or direct local-column ordering avoids that expansion and honors the requested direction.

scale.1: No reproduction attempt or no task-relevant executable setup.
scale.2: Attempts a reproduction but never obtains generated SQL or query results.
scale.3: Successfully produces the defective SQL and verifies at least one of the unexpected join or direction properties, without a completed discriminating control.
scale.4: Successfully reproduces the defect and a control that demonstrates direct FK-column ordering behaves differently, with the relevant SQL differences identified.
scale.5: Provides a repeatable minimal reproduction with multiple complementary controls or assertions that jointly isolate relation expansion, join count, and requested direction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reproduces the SQL defect with discriminating controls

applies_when: The trajectory creates or runs a reproduction for the reported self-referencing ForeignKey ordering behavior or inspects compiled SQL for equivalent models.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces task-specific runtime evidence that contrasts explicit ForeignKey-attname ordering with related-object ordering and confirms both ORDER BY direction and whether the unnecessary self-join is present.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if setup never reaches query compilation, or if the trajectory calls an observed DESC/extra join correct. Cap at 3 if temporary instrumentation changes behavior or the reproduction omits the self-reference or Meta.ordering prerequisite.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful executed output from the repository version outranks predicted SQL or prose. Failed setup attempts are only evidence of environment work, not ORM behavior. Query SQL and result ordering together outrank either alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for dependency installation, speculative tracing, or SQL inspection that does not distinguish the two independent symptoms: direction reversal and redundant join creation.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require successful reproduction output for record__root_id and at least one control variant, with explicit interpretation of ORDER BY direction and join count.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed queryset compilation or tests using a model with Meta.ordering=('-id',), a nullable self-ForeignKey, and an outer model relation; relevant variants are record__root_id, -record__root_id, record__root__id, and record__root.
metadata.oracle_test: Before the fix, record__root_id exhibits recursive '-id' ordering and an extra LEFT OUTER self-join; the correct semantics are ordering directly by the already joined table's root_id column, ASC by default and DESC with a leading '-'. record__root__id is a useful correct control.

scale.1: No successful task-relevant runtime or SQL evidence.
scale.2: Attempts a reproduction but it fails before query compilation, or the setup omits a causal prerequisite.
scale.3: Successfully reproduces the problematic SQL or a control query, but not a decisive contrast covering both direction and join behavior.
scale.4: Shows executed SQL for the failing path and a control, correctly identifying inherited direction and the redundant self-join.
scale.5: Shows a compact executed matrix including positive and negative directions plus explicit-path or relation-name controls, with correct expected SQL semantics and, where applicable, result ordering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive SQL reproduction of direction and join behavior

applies_when: The task concerns ordering through a relation path whose terminal component is a ForeignKey attribute name such as a trailing _id field.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible work correctly explains why an explicit ordering path ending in a ForeignKey attname is expanded through the related model's default ordering instead of being treated as the local foreign-key column.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims explicit order_by() normally combines with model default ordering, attributes the behavior primarily to self-join alias reuse, or proposes changing sort polarity without preventing erroneous relation expansion. Cap at 3 if its claimed condition values contradict visible source or runtime output.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful runtime traces and inspected repository source take precedence over summaries; source-grounded reasoning takes precedence over unsupported speculation. The relevant semantic fact is that the terminal path component denotes the resolved relation field's attname even though the full lookup string does not equal that attname.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad ORM exploration or plausible-sounding join theories that do not identify the full-path-versus-terminal-attname comparison responsible for the behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require identifying both the erroneous related-model ordering expansion and why the explicit terminal attname fails the existing shortcut check; merely naming the compiler method or Meta.ordering is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, traced values, and explanations involving ordering-name resolution, the final relation field, its attname, related-model default ordering, and the resulting extra join and direction change.
metadata.oracle_test: For a multi-hop path ending in the attname of a nullable self-referential ForeignKey, ordering should target the already joined table's local FK column with the requested direction; it should not recurse into the related model's Meta.ordering or require a further self-join.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis, or only repository navigation and restatement of the reported SQL.
scale.2: Connects the behavior to related-model default ordering or ordering compilation, but gives no correct field-resolution mechanism.
scale.3: Locates the relation/default-ordering branch or recognizes that a trailing _id name resolves to a ForeignKey field, but does not correctly connect the terminal attname to the failed shortcut check.
scale.4: Correctly traces how the terminal attname resolves to the relation field and how comparison against the full ordering path triggers related-model ordering, accounting for both the extra join and inherited direction.
scale.5: Provides the level-4 diagnosis with direct source or runtime-value evidence and states the robust semantic correction: test the terminal path component against the resolved field's attname so direct FK-column ordering bypasses related-model ordering expansion.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly localizes the ForeignKey-attname ordering bug

applies_when: The trajectory designs, adds, or runs regression tests for the compiler behavior around nested ForeignKey attnames and related model ordering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Covers the reported nested self-ForeignKey attname case while protecting established behavior for ordering by a relation name, explicit related primary-key paths, and reversed direction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if tests encode the wrong expectation that ordering by record__root should ignore related-model Meta.ordering, or if they only test record__root__id. Cap at 3 when tests are proposed but not added/run, or when full SQL assertions are backend-fragile.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing focused repository tests with committed regression assertions outrank ad hoc scripts; semantic result assertions outrank brittle full-SQL string equality, while targeted join-count or alias-independent SQL assertions are valid for the optimization symptom.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrowly passing patch from silently disabling Django's documented related-model ordering behavior or only fixing one ordering direction.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a regression test for record__root_id with the self-reference and descending Meta.ordering prerequisites, plus at least one compatibility control.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test model definitions, assertions on queryset order or compiled ORDER BY expressions, join-count assertions, and focused test commands in the existing Django test suite.
metadata.oracle_test: Required semantics include: record__root_id orders the local root_id storage column with the requested direction and no extra traversal; -record__root_id reverses that direction; record__root continues related-object ordering expansion; record__root__id remains an explicit primary-key path.

scale.1: No relevant regression-test reasoning or tests.
scale.2: Mentions testing generally, or tests only a workaround/control without the failing attname path.
scale.3: Specifies a valid primary regression test but lacks a compatibility control, robust assertions, or executed evidence.
scale.4: Adds or precisely designs the primary regression plus at least one relation-ordering or direction control in an appropriate existing test module.
scale.5: Shows focused tests covering the failing path, reverse direction, and preserved relation/explicit-pk behavior, with successful execution and no relevant regression failures.

metadata.oracle_test: cache.tests.DBCacheTests.test_cull_delete_when_store_empty and cache.tests.DBCacheWithTimeZoneTests.test_cull_delete_when_store_empty

scale.1: The unsafe unconditional fetchone()[0] remains, or the proposed change still crashes on no row.
scale.2: The issue is recognized but the visible implementation is absent, incomplete, or uses an unsafe fabricated boundary.

applies_when: The assistant analyzes the traceback, DatabaseCache._cull(), or cache_key_culling_sql().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the assistant's explicit causal explanation that the threshold query can return no row, fetchone() then returns None, indexing that result causes the exception, and the absent-row transition should skip only the boundary deletion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the assistant attributes the failure to cached Python None values, middleware, serialization, or the COUNT query. Cap at 3 if it proposes broad exception suppression, a fabricated boundary, or repeated fetchone() calls.
metadata.evidence_authority: Assistant-authored analysis or explanation is authoritative for this reasoning rubric; tool output and source text may support but cannot independently establish a diagnosis.
metadata.failure_mode: The assistant misidentifies the cursor operation, never states the causal chain, or recommends semantics that can delete valid cache entries.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an explicit assistant-authored connection from the threshold query's absent result to fetchone() returning None and the unsafe subscript.
metadata.judge_focus: Credit only causal conclusions stated by the assistant. Look for a distinction between the earlier COUNT fetch and the later offset-boundary fetch, plus an explanation of why no row is legitimate and why normal row-present deletion must remain. Names or facts appearing only in source listings, grep output, tracebacks, or generated script output are not reasoning evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Consistency with the empty-store or concurrently depleted threshold-query state exercised by test_cull_delete_when_store_empty.
metadata.stage: Inspect the culling path and choose absent-row semantics

scale.1: No assistant-authored task-specific diagnosis is present, or the explanation targets an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: The relevant method is mentioned, but the assistant does not correctly identify the absent threshold row and unsafe subscript.
scale.3: The assistant identifies fetchone() returning None and the subscript failure but does not explain the non-destructive absent-row transition or preservation of normal deletion.
scale.4: The assistant correctly explains the threshold no-row result, the resulting TypeError, one-fetch handling, and skipping only the boundary DELETE.
scale.5: The explanation additionally distinguishes the threshold fetch from the count fetch and connects the empty or concurrently depleted offset state to completion of the triggering cache write.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Submission validity and focus

applies_when: The trajectory creates, runs, locates, or specifies evidence intended to reproduce or validate the reported failure
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The evidence exercises a related field in an application whose actual label contains uppercase characters and demonstrates the expected preserved-label/lowercase-model relation identifier, preferably through both focused deconstruction assertions and migration-state or makemigrations behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A script that fails before reaching relation construction because of missing dependencies, settings, imports, or test-runner setup cannot score above 2; fabricated success messages without assertions or observable behavior cap at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing or failing repository tests and self-contained reproductions outrank printed expectations; a reproduction with an actually importable and registered mixed-case app outranks direct manipulation of `_pending_operations`.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a standalone demonstration that lowercase app lookup fails as proof of the root cause or of a successful fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require evidence that uses an installed or isolated app with a genuinely mixed-case label and checks the serialized relation or migration behavior, not merely `get_app_config()` lookup.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed output and test code involving a real mixed-case AppConfig label, a related model, ForeignKey deconstruction, state rendering, lazy-reference checks, or makemigrations.
metadata.oracle_test: The regression case must distinguish `DJ_RegLogin.category` from `dj_reglogin.category` and establish that the former resolves without `fields.E307` or migration-state `ValueError`.

scale.1: No relevant executable evidence or test design is visible, or the purported evidence never exercises the behavior.
scale.2: An attempted reproduction is relevant but fails during environment setup, or only demonstrates case-sensitive registry lookup.
scale.3: A concrete focused test or reproduction is specified or partially executed and checks a mixed-case relation, but it does not establish successful deconstruction or migration resolution.
scale.4: A focused test is visibly executed or added and verifies preservation of the mixed-case app label in the deconstructed ForeignKey target or successful state rendering.
scale.5: Visible tests cover both the focused serialization contract and an end-to-end migration/lazy-resolution path, with relevant existing tests also passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces decisive mixed-case ForeignKey reproduction and regression evidence

applies_when: The trajectory endorses, applies, or directly evaluates a specific code-level correction for the mixed-case related-model failure
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the selected intervention repairs relation-target construction by preserving the registered app-label spelling and normalizing only the model-name component, without redefining app-label identity, weakening exact-case lookup, or masking malformed references in downstream diagnostics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign 1 when the endorsed or applied correction adds lowercase or case-insensitive app lookup, globally folds app labels, changes only error checking or diagnostics, or removes model-name normalization. If prose proposes a safe fix but the visible diff implements an incompatible one, the diff controls. Do not penalize a discarded exploratory idea as the selected fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: The cutoff-visible diff is authoritative for applied behavior and outranks prose. An exact expression or patch at the relation-deconstruction boundary outranks a generic casing promise. Executed deconstruction, migration-state, and app-registry assertions outrank printed expectations or self-authored success messages.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring mere investigation as a safe correction, treating an unapplied suggestion as a repository change, accepting a downstream fallback because it suppresses the exception, or overlooking that a patch changes app-label semantics globally.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires an exact component-wise replacement at relation deconstruction or equivalent serialization. Score 4 requires that replacement in the visible diff. Score 5 requires execution that verifies both the mixed-case relation result and preserved case-sensitive lookup or equivalent adjacent compatibility behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: First identify the concrete intervention the trajectory endorses; exploratory possibilities that remain unresolved do not count as selected corrections. Then inspect the visible repository diff and executed checks to distinguish a verbal direction, an exact proposal, an applied edit, and a validated edit.
metadata.oracle_test: The selected correction constructs the migration-facing target from the unchanged registered app label and a lowercase model name. Exact-case app lookup remains required, conventional lowercase-label relations remain unchanged, and truly missing applications retain their existing lazy-reference diagnostics.

scale.1: The selected intervention is incompatible: it changes app-label identity or lookup semantics, globally lowercases app labels, patches only downstream diagnostics, or stops required model-name normalization.
scale.2: A correction is endorsed, but it is generic, targets an uncertain location, or does not specify how the app-label and model-name components are handled separately.
scale.3: An exact source-level correction is selected at the relation-serialization boundary that preserves the app label and normalizes only the model name, but it is not present in the visible repository diff.
scale.4: The correctly scoped component-wise correction is present in the visible diff, but executed compatibility evidence is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: The safe correction is visibly applied, and executed focused evidence verifies preserved mixed-case app labels, lowercase model names, and unchanged exact-case app lookup or missing-app behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantic safety of the endorsed casing correction

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the mixed-case application label and unresolved ForeignKey lazy reference
