scale.1: Contradictory evidence is ignored, denied, or followed by further unrelated work.
scale.2: The contradiction is noticed but misunderstood, or attempted fixes leave the same semantic failure visible.
scale.3: The contradiction is correctly diagnosed and a plausible correction is made, but the decisive case is not rerun successfully.
scale.4: The contradiction is correctly diagnosed, the implementation or test is repaired, and the intended semantic case passes on rerun.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and additionally simplifies or restores the implementation after false starts, reruns affected edge cases, and reconciles all previously contradictory evidence without weakening assertions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory implementation or test evidence

applies_when: The visible investigation traces or tests Django's ASGI middleware response path, including middleware construction, sync/async adaptation, exception wrapping, or MiddlewareMixin response dispatch.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Localizes the boundary at which an awaitable could reach response middleware while distinguishing exact source evidence, faithful handler-chain execution, local toy behavior, and setup failures. Rewards investigations that keep unvalidated mechanisms provisional, use contrary output to narrow the hypothesis, and make concrete progress toward testing the real middleware chain.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the trajectory's architecture is directly ruled out by inspected source, such as assigning process_response dispatch to the handler core after source shows it belongs to middleware invocation. Cap at 2 if a proper response, unrelated exception, failed import, or generic unawaited call is presented as confirmation of the reported leak, or if a contradicted mechanism remains asserted without qualification. Contrary output may support 3 only when it is explicitly treated as falsifying the tested mechanism and leads to a narrower boundary or a more faithful next experiment.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed arguments at process_response in a configured checkout-based handler chain outrank all other evidence. Exact source at the nested invocation boundary ranks next. A focused local wrapper can establish only that wrapper's behavior, while generic coroutine facts, incomplete imports, and unrelated exceptions establish neither the full defect nor middleware-order sensitivity.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding repeated source enumeration, confident declarations that merely name MiddlewareMixin or adaptation helpers, claims that response middleware is absent, and toy calls that manufacture a coroutine by omitting an await. It also avoids treating productive repair of a faithful reproduction harness as equivalent to circular or unrelated setup attempts.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires either an architecture-correct trace through middleware construction into MiddlewareMixin response dispatch that identifies the precise unresolved invocation or awaiting boundary and keeps it provisional, or material progress toward a faithful real-handler reproduction in which successive blockers are correctly classified and repaired. Credit above 3 requires target-boundary evidence showing what process_response receives and an explicit comparison or causal account addressing middleware position.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the investigation correctly connects the ASGI entry point, the nested middleware callable, mode adaptation, exception conversion, and MiddlewareMixin.__call__/__acall__; whether runtime failures are classified by where execution stopped; whether proper-response observations revise the hypothesis; and whether setup work advances a real handler-chain test rather than another toy.
metadata.oracle_test: A sound partial investigation can state who invokes process_response, what callable supplies its response, which awaitability boundary remains unverified, and why current output does not yet prove the defect. A sound completed investigation observes that boundary in the configured chain and explains the placement-dependent behavior with a focused comparison.

scale.1: Uses a source-inconsistent middleware architecture, mistakes unrelated dispatch for response middleware, or treats visibly unrelated output as direct proof of the proposed mechanism.
scale.2: Finds relevant async components but remains speculative, repeatedly uses unfaithful toys or blocked scripts, overstates a generic coroutine observation, or fails to revise a mechanism after process_response visibly receives a proper response.
scale.3: Correctly reaches MiddlewareMixin response dispatch and identifies a specific unresolved invocation or awaiting boundary while keeping it provisional, or materially advances a faithful real-handler harness through correctly diagnosed blockers; no target-boundary validation or order explanation is yet complete.
scale.4: Obtains focused source or runtime evidence at process_response, uses any contrary result to narrow the mechanism, and coherently connects the remaining or confirmed boundary to middleware placement.
scale.5: Demonstrates the awaitability boundary in the configured Django handler chain and independently confirms the causal, placement-sensitive account with a controlled comparison or regression-style test.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Calibrated localization of the ASGI middleware response boundary

applies_when: A code change is present or concretely proposed to stop an unresolved coroutine from reaching response middleware.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the narrow Django middleware callable/adaptation boundary responsible for the leak so ASGI response middleware receives a resolved HttpResponse, without masking the problem in response sending or third-party middleware.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the change merely awaits arbitrary values inside process_response(), alters send_response() to accept coroutines, or patches the example/third-party middleware. Cap at 3 if it fixes the symptom by broad double-awaiting without preserving exception and mode semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository diff implementing the diagnosed invariant outranks prose proposals. Changes to generic ASGI response serialization, uvicorn, or django-cors-headers are non-authoritative unless source evidence establishes them as the actual boundary.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents symptom masking, broad ASGI rewrites, and fixes at the consumer rather than at the callable-classification or adaptation defect.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied diff in the responsible Django core boundary. Credit of 5 additionally requires that the edit is minimal and consistent with the repository's existing sync/async adaptation conventions.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or precise edit affecting the responsible BaseHandler, exception-wrapper, or MiddlewareMixin mode boundary; preservation of exception conversion and request/response ordering.
metadata.oracle_test: The middleware stack must resolve get_response before invoking process_response, while each callable remains in the mode declared or selected by BaseHandler and exceptions continue to become responses at each layer.

scale.1: No relevant implementation or only vague statements about adding await.
scale.2: A concrete proposal or diff targets the wrong layer, broadly masks awaitables, or is incompatible with the observed call path.
scale.3: A plausible narrow edit is described precisely but not applied, or an applied edit addresses the right boundary with unresolved semantic concerns.
scale.4: An applied, focused implementation fixes the responsible adaptation boundary and visibly preserves surrounding middleware behavior.
scale.5: An applied minimal implementation exactly enforces resolved-response delivery, follows existing Django async adaptation patterns, and is directly supported by the diagnosed call chain.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Minimal implementation at the middleware adaptation boundary

applies_when: The investigation or change affects middleware callable classification, adaptation, or MiddlewareMixin execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects existing synchronous and asynchronous middleware semantics while fixing the ASGI path, including response ordering, short-circuit responses, exception conversion, and thread-sensitive execution of legacy hooks.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the proposed change forces all middleware into one mode, bypasses capability flags, reverses response order, or removes thread_sensitive execution. Cap at 3 if compatibility is asserted without visible evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Targeted repository tests and existing test-suite results outrank general compatibility claims. Existing Django capability flags and adaptation contracts outrank assumptions based solely on callable syntax.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrow symptom fix from breaking WSGI, mixed middleware stacks, exception handling, or Django's thread-affinity guarantees.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires applied tests or successful existing suites covering at least one unaffected sync path and one mixed/async path in addition to the primary regression.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, tests, or diffs covering WSGI/synchronous handling, mixed sync/async middleware, process_request short-circuiting, process_response order, exception-to-response conversion, and thread_sensitive behavior where relevant.
metadata.oracle_test: The fix must preserve inward request and outward response ordering, support legacy synchronous MiddlewareMixin hooks under ASGI, leave synchronous handling functional, and avoid extra unawaited or double-awaited responses.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration or evidence.
scale.2: Mentions compatibility generically while proposing or retaining a change that risks established middleware semantics.
scale.3: Reasoning addresses the principal sync/async risks, but no applied cross-mode regression evidence is present.
scale.4: Applied tests or visible suite results protect both the primary ASGI path and at least one relevant synchronous or mixed-mode behavior.
scale.5: Comprehensive visible evidence covers ASGI and synchronous paths plus ordering, short-circuit or exception behavior, and thread-sensitive legacy middleware execution as applicable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Sync/async compatibility and middleware semantics protection

applies_when: Visible experiments fail for environment reasons, produce behavior contrary to the current hypothesis, or use simplified wrappers that differ from Django's real middleware chain.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Distinguishes setup failures and non-faithful simulations from task evidence, reconciles contradictory observations, and updates the working hypothesis toward a faithful reproduction instead of repeating the same unsupported conclusion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims a reproduction succeeded when output shows an unrelated exception or a proper HttpResponse. Repeated dependency installation or near-identical failed scripts without isolating the setup issue cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A controlled reproduction using the checkout and real handler chain outranks toy scripts; contradictory runtime output must supersede the hypothesis it falsifies until a concrete setup difference is shown.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long but circular debugging that treats import errors, settings errors, or contrary results as confirmation of the proposed root cause.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an explicit correction or narrowed hypothesis after contradictory evidence, followed by a materially more faithful source trace or experiment.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible handling of missing dependencies/settings, wrong import paths, installed-versus-checkout source confusion, toy simulations, and experiments where process_response receives a valid HttpResponse.
metadata.oracle_test: A valid investigation must separate 'the program did not reach process_response', 'a toy wrapper behaved differently', and 'the real ASGI middleware chain reproduced the coroutine argument'.

scale.1: Ignores or misstates contradictory output and repeatedly pursues the same unsupported hypothesis.
scale.2: Acknowledges setup failures or contrary results but does not revise the hypothesis or improve experimental fidelity.
scale.3: Correctly classifies non-evidence and narrows the hypothesis, though no decisive follow-up is completed.
scale.4: Revises the diagnosis in response to contradiction and performs a substantially more faithful source trace or experiment.
scale.5: Uses contradiction productively to isolate the decisive boundary and produces controlled evidence that resolves the discrepancy.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-driven recovery from misleading reproductions

applies_when: The visible investigation encounters a setup failure, a simplified middleware experiment, an unawaited-call artifact, or runtime output inconsistent with its current ASGI middleware diagnosis.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly classifies failed or contradictory observations, revises the working hypothesis accordingly, and redirects the investigation toward a more faithful ASGI middleware call path rather than treating non-evidence as confirmation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if an unrelated exception, a valid HttpResponse result, or a deliberately unawaited toy call is presented as reproducing the reported coroutine argument. Cap at 2 if failures are acknowledged but the trajectory repeats equivalent scripts or resumes the same unsupported diagnosis. A trajectory may reach 3 when contrary output causes a genuine shift to the real handler or middleware-dispatch path, even if cutoff prevents completion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Runtime output from the configured checkout and real handler chain has highest authority. Exact source tracing through middleware construction and dispatch is next. Simplified wrappers and generic coroutine demonstrations are diagnostic aids only, while import, dependency, settings, syntax, and command-format failures establish no middleware response behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents both rewarding confident claims unsupported by output and underrating a meaningful, evidence-driven course correction merely because the corrected investigation has not yet reached a decisive reproduction.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires an observable investigative correction: the trajectory must identify why an earlier observation is non-decisive or contrary and then materially improve fidelity or trace a newly narrowed source boundary. The improved follow-up may be incomplete for score 3. Credit above 3 requires completed evidence connecting the narrowed boundary to the object supplied to process_response.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the trajectory distinguishes failure before middleware execution, behavior of a simplified wrapper, an awaitable created by an intentionally unawaited call, and behavior of Django's configured middleware chain; then whether that distinction visibly changes the subsequent source trace or experiment.
metadata.oracle_test: Ask what the latest successful observation actually establishes and whether the next visible work changes because of it. Productive recovery separates environment failure, toy-wrapper behavior, and real-chain behavior, then narrows the unresolved discrepancy without overstating the evidence.

scale.1: Ignores or misstates blocking or contrary output and treats non-evidence as confirmation of the diagnosis.
scale.2: Acknowledges the failure or contradiction, but continues with equivalent low-fidelity work or unsupported claims without materially redirecting the investigation.
scale.3: Correctly limits what the observation proves and visibly redirects to a more faithful experiment or a newly narrowed middleware source boundary, though the corrected investigation remains incomplete.
scale.4: Completes the corrected trace or experiment and connects a concrete middleware boundary to whether process_response receives a resolved response or an awaitable.
scale.5: Resolves the discrepancy with a faithful handler-chain observation and independently checks the causal explanation with a focused comparison.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-driven correction after misleading ASGI observations

applies_when: The task concerns an __in lookup applied after a JSONField key transform on one or more non-PostgreSQL database backends.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible trajectory converges on a coherent implementation that makes JSON key-transform membership compare each right-hand-side value using the backend's JSON scalar representation, rather than merely adding a generic lookup, coercing all values to text, or changing a different lookup.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible work substitutes an unrelated lookup, treats membership as key existence, unconditionally converts JSON values to text, or leaves the edited source malformed. Cap at 3 if the work only registers or subclasses the generic In lookup without addressing backend-specific RHS representation, or if the implementation remains only proposed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed targeted tests or compiled-query evidence outrank an applied diff; an applied diff outranks a concrete code-level plan; a concrete plan outranks unsupported narration. Repository observations and displayed source outrank assumptions about framework internals.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding lookup-name discovery, repeated source browsing, synthetic class-instantiation checks, or unrelated text/contains changes as though they fixed typed JSON membership.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible applied repository changes that preserve __in membership semantics and handle each direct RHS parameter as a JSON-comparable value where the backend lacks native JSON comparison behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source reads, diagnosis, edits, diffs, and targeted query or test evidence concerning KeyTransform, the In lookup's per-item RHS processing, and MySQL, Oracle, and SQLite JSON value expressions.
metadata.oracle_test: For a JSON key containing numeric 0, filtering with value__key__in=[0] must select the same rows as value__key=0 on MySQL, Oracle, and SQLite; the design should process every direct RHS member with the appropriate JSON_VALUE, JSON_QUERY, or JSON_EXTRACT-style representation while preserving expressions, subqueries, null behavior, and native-backend behavior.

scale.1: The visible trajectory has no coherent task-causal direction, or its applied edits corrupt the relevant source and do not visibly recover to a valid implementation.
scale.2: The trajectory identifies the general JSON/key-transform area but pursues a contradictory mechanism such as another lookup, key existence, blanket text coercion, or transformed-LHS-only handling.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly identifies the need for a dedicated key-transform membership path and provides either a concrete backend-aware plan or a coherent partial edit, but no applied evidence yet covers both per-item RHS JSON representation and regression behavior.
scale.4: The visible repository contains a coherent applied implementation that registers the membership lookup and performs backend-appropriate processing of direct RHS members, with a relevant regression test or compiled-query check present but not successfully completed across the affected behavior.
scale.5: The applied implementation satisfies the oracle semantics and visible targeted tests or equivalent query evidence successfully verify typed key-transform membership, including the numeric-scalar case, without contradictory regressions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Convergence on correct JSON key-transform __in semantics

applies_when: The repository contains JSONField querying tests and the proposed behavior can be exercised through ORM filters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds or identifies executable ORM regression tests showing that key-transform `__in` membership has the same typed JSON semantics as exact lookup, especially on the affected database backends.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Failed setup, missing dependencies, invalid settings, or a test that only confirms class inheritance cannot establish behavioral success and caps credit at 3; a failing relevant queryset test caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A focused Django test result from the repository test runner outranks ad hoc class construction, successful import, SQL speculation, or an unexecuted test script.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing module importability or lookup registration with proof that backend SQL compares typed JSON values correctly.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a queryset-level regression assertion containing at least the reported one-element numeric case and evidence that the focused test was run or a complete runnable test is visibly present.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tests and command output using a real model, persisted JSON values, `value__key__in`, and asserted queryset contents; import checks and lookup-registration introspection are only preliminary evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Given a row whose JSON object contains the selected key with numeric value `0`, filtering with `value__key__in=[0]` returns that row just as `value__key=0` does, while rows with different values or missing keys are excluded.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence or only unrelated existing tests are mentioned.
scale.2: Performs import, syntax, inheritance, or registration checks without an ORM query asserting results.
scale.3: Shows a plausible queryset regression test or attempted focused run, but it is incomplete, blocked, or covers only a weak string case.
scale.4: Shows a complete queryset regression test and a successful focused run for the numeric reproducer, with at least one additional typed value or multi-element membership case.
scale.5: Shows successful focused repository tests covering one- and multi-element `__in` membership across representative JSON scalar types and relevant backend paths, followed by an appropriate surrounding JSONField test module or suite run.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Provides decisive queryset regression coverage

applies_when: A visible patch or concrete implementation proposal changes JSONField key-transform lookup handling for `in`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds and registers a `KeyTransformIn` lookup in `django/db/models/fields/json.py` that retains `lookups.In` behavior while adapting each direct RHS JSON value using the checkout's established backend-specific conventions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A malformed file, duplicate class or registration, incomplete SQL string construction, arbitrary LHS override, or use of `KeyTransformTextLookupMixin` for general JSON membership caps credit at 2 until visibly repaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later clean source excerpt or `git diff` outranks earlier edit commands and narrative claims; the checkout's existing `KeyTransformExact` and JSON parameter APIs determine the appropriate conversion form.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full credit for `class KeyTransformIn(lookups.In): pass`, which exposes the lookup name but leaves the original incompatible RHS preparation unchanged.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both `KeyTransform.register_lookup(KeyTransformIn)` and concrete per-element RHS handling for all three affected backend families.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible class inheritance, registration, iterable-RHS hook, parameter preservation, and vendor branches in the actual source or diff.
metadata.oracle_test: The lookup must preserve an `IN (...)` predicate and make every direct RHS placeholder or literal represent the same JSON type as the extracted key value: numeric remains numeric, boolean remains boolean, string remains string, and structured JSON uses the backend's appropriate JSON function.

scale.1: No relevant implementation, an unrelated lookup is added, or the visible source is syntactically or structurally broken.
scale.2: Adds only a pass-through class and registration, uses a text lookup mixin, or handles only one affected backend.
scale.3: Adds the correct class and registration plus meaningful RHS conversion, but backend coverage or parameter handling is materially incomplete.
scale.4: Implements coherent per-value conversion for MySQL, Oracle, and SQLite using the checkout's iterable-RHS hook, with at most one limited edge-case or formatting defect.
scale.5: Shows a clean, minimal implementation that subclasses `lookups.In`, uses the version-appropriate per-element hook such as `process_rhs()` or `resolve_expression_parameter()`, follows existing JSON extraction conventions for MySQL and SQLite, selects Oracle `JSON_VALUE` versus `JSON_QUERY` as appropriate, preserves parameters and expressions, and registers the lookup exactly once.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements the specialized `KeyTransformIn` boundary correctly

applies_when: A specialized JSON key-transform `in` lookup could affect PostgreSQL, expression RHS values, subqueries, null handling, or generic `In` list behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Keeps generic `lookups.In` semantics intact and limits JSON-specific adaptation to direct RHS values and the backends that require it, without regressing PostgreSQL or expression-based membership.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Hand-built `IN` SQL, interpolation of user values into SQL, unconditional conversion on PostgreSQL, or loss of expression/subquery handling caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Existing `lookups.In` contracts and backend feature/vendor checks outrank custom reimplementations of `IN` SQL generation.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing the reported literal list by replacing Django's mature `In` implementation and thereby introducing SQL-injection, parameter, subquery, or large-list regressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires retaining `lookups.In` rather than replacing its SQL assembly and avoiding JSON wrapping of compiled RHS expressions or subqueries.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inheritance and control flow preserving subqueries, expression compilation, empty-list behavior, parameter-list splitting, and native-JSON backend behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: The specialized lookup changes only the representation of direct JSON RHS elements; membership cardinality, empty RHS handling, maximum-list splitting, expression parameters, and PostgreSQL native JSON behavior remain those of Django's standard `In` lookup.

scale.1: No compatibility reasoning, or the approach replaces generic `In` with unsafe or unrelated custom SQL.
scale.2: Preserves basic syntax but unconditionally rewrites all backends or all RHS forms, including expressions or subqueries.
scale.3: Inherits from `lookups.In` and limits some backend behavior, but leaves material uncertainty about expressions, PostgreSQL, nulls, or list splitting.
scale.4: Clearly preserves generic membership behavior and scopes conversion to affected direct RHS values, with only one minor compatibility omission.
scale.5: Demonstrates a minimal specialization that preserves all standard `In` mechanics, bypasses conversion for compiled expressions and subqueries, leaves native PostgreSQL behavior unchanged, and follows version-specific MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle, and SQLite JSON conventions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves generic `In` and cross-backend compatibility

applies_when: A reproduction, assertion, test, traceback, source check, or validation claim is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether validation executes the latest inspected repository implementation with a task-correct oracle and covers meaningful comparison paths.

metadata.exclusion: A validation score does not erase a source-visible semantic defect
metadata.judge_focus: Evidence provenance
metadata.oracle_test: Latest inspected-source focused checks plus lifecycle, ordering, syntax, and relevant regression validation

scale.1: The oracle is inverted, or the correctness claim relies on stale output, an unexecuted edit, or a code-triggered failure represented as success.
scale.2: Evidence is pre-fix, environment-only, syntax-only, or produced by a separate comparator.
scale.3: A focused check reaches the repository implementation and establishes part of the behavior, but a relevant path fails, is omitted, or is not rerun after correction.
scale.4: Latest-source checks establish the principal outcome and meaningful lifecycle or ordering behavior, with environment failures correctly separated.
scale.5: The complete focused matrix, relevant regressions, syntax validation, diff review, and artifact consistency checks succeed against the same source.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation and oracle fidelity

applies_when: The active implementation includes equality or hashing behavior for tied-counter fields attached to concrete models.
Abstract-model field copies or equivalent attached tied-counter fields are present.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether active Field equality and hashing distinguish copies with the same creation counter after they are attached to different model objects, yielding distinct sibling set members.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Current execution showing attached concrete siblings compare equal or collapse to one set member forces score 1. An oracle requiring sibling concrete copies to remain equal also forces score 1. A source-only model-sensitive implementation cannot exceed score 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff source and execution against that same source outrank earlier runs, comments, edit-script messages, source-string searches, mock comparators, and separately reimplemented comparison functions. Output preceding a later equality or hashing edit is stale unless the relevant active bodies are visibly unchanged.
metadata.failure_mode: Do not use different-counter fields, generic object inequality, mock-only output, ordering behavior, or pre-edit execution as proof. Unbound-field safety and Field.__lt__ defects belong to the ordering and lifecycle rubric and do not negate an attached-model identity result unless they prevent the identity execution itself.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require successful current execution of the repository Field methods on tied-counter fields attached to distinct concrete model objects. Score 5 additionally requires pairwise coverage of the original abstract field and both concrete inherited copies.
metadata.judge_focus: Examine the active Field.__eq__ and Field.__hash__ bodies and current executions of those repository methods on attached tied-counter fields. Determine whether equality uses both creation_counter and the actual attached model object, whether equal fields remain hash-compatible, and whether concrete sibling copies compare unequal and remain distinct in a set.
metadata.oracle_test: For abstract A and concrete descendants B and C inheriting myfield, the B and C field copies share a creation counter but compare unequal, ordinarily have distinct hashes, and form a set of size two; pairwise A/B/C distinction supports score 5.

scale.1: The active implementation or current execution preserves attached sibling equality or set collapse, contains a blocker that prevents the defining equality check, or relies on an inverted sibling-equality oracle.
scale.2: The active equality and hashing remain creation-counter-only, are incoherent with one another, or otherwise lack the attached-model distinction; no current successful sibling identity result exists.
scale.3: The active source coherently combines creation_counter with actual attached-model identity in equality and hashing, but repository-backed tied-counter execution is absent, stale, or incomplete.
scale.4: Current repository-backed execution shows two concrete inherited copies with a shared counter compare unequal, have distinct ordinary hashes, and form a set of size two.
scale.5: Current repository-backed execution pairwise distinguishes the original abstract field and both concrete copies, with coherent equality, hashes, and set behavior based on their actual attached model objects.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Attached inherited-field identity

applies_when: Comparison source, restored original source, a task-relevant traceback, or a focused comparison result is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Records the worst established defect in the latest operative comparison state. This is a negative rubric: score 1 means no material defect and score 5 means a severe blocker.

metadata.anti_overcredit_rule: Score 1 requires complete visible source and affirmative full-contract evidence; passing equality, set, or generic orderability output is insufficient
metadata.judge_focus: Worst operative causal defect
metadata.oracle_test: Latest inspected source plus task-relevant execution
metadata.scale_direction: Ascending scores mean increasing harm and must reduce reward

scale.1: Complete current method bodies and focused execution affirmatively establish the safe comparison contract with no material operative defect.
scale.2: Only a minor validation or presentation gap remains; no unsafe or semantically incorrect operative branch is visible, and the principal contract is established.
scale.3: A plausible complete correction is visible but incompletely validated, or source visibility is insufficient to exclude a meaningful contract gap; score 3 is the best possible score when full bodies or critical lifecycle branches are not visible.
scale.4: The source is original/restored or visibly incomplete, or it contains an unexecuted major defect such as unconditional model access, missing required semantics, creation-counter-only tied ordering, or model-first ordering.
scale.5: The operative source or execution establishes a severe blocker: a tied __lt__ branch returns model identity or equality and therefore makes a field less than itself, raw-model TypeError, absent-model AttributeError, recursive hashing, equality attribute typo, malformed production code, inverted defining oracle, or an unresolved directly demonstrated comparison failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operative defect severity

applies_when: The trajectory is in a reproduction or validation state with an executed command, observed test output, traceback, syntax result, or diff-check result.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the quality and breadth of commands actually executed against the active repository revision with task-correct assertions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An inverted defining oracle, stale or mock output represented as current repository success, or an unresolved task-relevant failure represented as passing forces score 1. A failure followed by a source edit remains unresolved for validation purposes until the relevant command is rerun. Environment or collection failures provide no semantic credit but do not themselves contradict source correctness.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed terminal output from an executed command is authoritative for that source revision. A proposed command, script contents, source-string check, edit-script message, mock comparator, or assistant summary is not execution evidence. After a relevant source edit, earlier output is stale unless the active body is visibly equivalent. Repository Field execution outranks separate simulations.
metadata.failure_mode: Do not infer success from command intent, a script merely being created, partial output before an exception, generic sorting, a pre-fix reproduction, a separately implemented comparator, or an environment failure. Trajectories with no applicable successful post-edit semantic execution remain at the same low anchor.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires at least one successful post-edit semantic execution reaching the active repository Field implementation. Score 4 additionally requires the defining attached sibling outcome and at least one applicable ordering or lifecycle path. Score 5 requires the full focused matrix, relevant regression execution, final syntax or compilation, diff checking, and artifact consistency.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify commands that actually ran and their observed outputs, then map each result to the repository source revision it exercised. Record successful coverage of sibling equality, hashes, set cardinality, creation-counter priority, tied ordering, unbound and mixed states, self-comparison, non-Field delegation, relevant regressions, syntax, and diff checks.
metadata.oracle_test: Applicable executed checks include B/C inequality with a shared counter, distinct ordinary hashes, set size two, pairwise A/B/C identity, different-counter priority, tied bound ordering, unbound and mixed-state safety, field < field being false, both operand directions, non-Field delegation, relevant Django regressions, syntax parsing, and git diff --check.

scale.1: Validation relies on an inverted oracle, represents stale or simulated output as current repository behavior, or claims success despite an unresolved task-relevant failure in the same active revision.
scale.2: No successful post-edit semantic command reaches the active repository implementation; evidence is only pre-fix, environment-only, syntax-only, source-string, proposed, or simulated.
scale.3: At least one post-edit semantic command reaches the active repository implementation and validates part of the task, but important paths fail, are omitted, contradict one another, or become stale after a later edit.
scale.4: Successful execution against the active source establishes the defining sibling equality/hash/set outcome and at least one meaningful ordering or lifecycle path, with failures and environment issues accurately separated.
scale.5: Successful executions against one active source cover the complete identity and lifecycle-ordering matrix, relevant Django regressions, final syntax or compilation, git diff --check, and consistency with the cutoff artifact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed validation provenance and coverage

applies_when: The visible trajectory considers how an assigned Query should select a result iterable.
The visible trajectory compares values(), values_list(), annotations, or ordinary model queries as possible result-shape signals.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the rollout identifies nonempty Query.values_select as the sole recoverable values-mode signal and respects the limits of Query-only restoration without broadening the trigger to annotations or ordinary queries.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Using annotation_select, extra_select, selected columns generally, or unconditional assignment as an alternative trigger caps the score at 2. Claiming that Query alone preserves flat or named values_list presentation caps the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Local Query and QuerySet source plus real-object observations outrank assumptions about what pickle preserves. Explicit behavior checks outrank naming-based guesses about values_list presentation.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating every annotated or selected query as dictionary-producing, attempting to reconstruct unavailable values_list presentation metadata, or overwriting existing non-values iterable behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require explicit evidence that annotation_select alone is not a values-mode signal and that Query-only restoration cannot recover tuple, flat, or named values_list presentation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source checks, experiments, or proposed conditions involving values_select, values_list variants, annotation_select, ordinary queries, and receiver iterable preservation.
metadata.oracle_test: A nonempty values_select selects ValuesIterable; values_list(), flat, and named Query-only restorations yield dictionaries; annotate()-only and ordinary assigned Queries remain model-producing; no non-values reset branch is introduced.

scale.1: No task-specific trigger is identified, or the rollout proposes an unconditional or unrelated result-shape rule.
scale.2: The rollout notices values-related Query state but leaves the trigger ambiguous, includes unsafe alternative signals, or does not distinguish values selection from annotations.
scale.3: The rollout identifies nonempty values_select as the trigger and visibly checks at least one values_list form or a non-values control, but does not establish the full Query-only presentation boundary.
scale.4: The rollout establishes that all values_list forms share the recoverable values_select signal and must restore as dictionaries, while annotate()-only and ordinary Queries remain model-producing.
scale.5: In addition to anchor 4, the rollout preserves existing non-values iterable behavior by avoiding a reset branch, verifies the condition through real Query assignment, and excludes eager evaluation or serialization-format expansion.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Scope-safe recoverable result-shape signal

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains task-relevant work at the Result-shape data-flow localization stage.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the rollout visibly establishes the causal failure in the query-only pickle path: Query.values_select survives serialization, a fresh QuerySet retains ModelIterable, and assigning the Query through QuerySet.query therefore interprets values-style rows as model data. The strongest evidence identifies the query setter as the narrow implementation point rather than changing SQL compilation or whole-QuerySet pickling.

metadata.failure_mode: Conflating whole-QuerySet pickling with Query-only restoration, blaming SQL/GROUP BY, or failing to identify the QuerySet.query setter as the state-transition boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Causal distinction between Query-side selected-field state and QuerySet-side result-conversion state.
metadata.oracle_test: A values().annotate() Query round-trip assigned to a fresh QuerySet, with values_select and the receiver's iterable class inspected.

scale.1: No task-specific causal localization; the rollout remains at generic repository exploration or unrelated setup failures.
scale.2: Recognizes that values() should produce dictionaries or observes a crash, but does not distinguish Query-only serialization from whole-QuerySet pickling or identify the retained Query state.
scale.3: Identifies either the fresh receiver's ModelIterable or the restored Query's values_select, but the causal chain or implementation boundary remains incomplete.
scale.4: Correctly explains that values_select survives while the fresh QuerySet retains ModelIterable, and points to QuerySet.query assignment as the likely fix location.
scale.5: Faithfully reproduces the Query-only assignment path, confirms both sides of the mismatch and the malformed model result, and precisely derives the lazy setter change without proposing unrelated SQL, compiler, or serialization changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Query-only pickle failure localization

applies_when: The prefix proposes, prepares, or applies a fix for the diagnosed result-shape mismatch.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether an actionable production operation follows from the observed cause and targets the correct source location.

metadata.failure_mode: No actionable operation, comment-only plans, fake implementations, edits to the wrong layer, or omission of the production fix.
metadata.judge_focus: Require an exact or applied QuerySet.query setter intervention rather than general intent.
metadata.oracle_test: Applicable edit around the QuerySet.query setter in django/db/models/query.py.

scale.1: No actionable production intervention is visible, or the proposed intervention targets the wrong layer.
scale.2: The correct area is mentioned, but only vague comments, scratch logic, or non-applicable pseudocode is provided.
scale.3: An exact setter operation is specified or prepared but not applied to the production implementation.
scale.4: A production setter edit is applied at the correct change point but contains visible repairable coding or condition defects.
scale.5: A valid, minimal production setter edit is applied and retains the existing Query assignment without unrelated production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable causal intervention

applies_when: The prefix attempts to reproduce, inspect, or validate the reported behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether evidence comes from the exact Query-only pickle workflow using real Django Query and QuerySet objects.

metadata.failure_mode: Whole-QuerySet pickling, setup-only failures, fake classes, or scripts that never evaluate the restored QuerySet.
metadata.judge_focus: Assign an unpickled Query to a fresh QuerySet and separate semantic evidence from environment failures.
metadata.oracle_test: Assign pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(source.query)) to a fresh QuerySet and inspect evaluated row type and contents.

scale.1: No relevant real-object execution succeeds.
scale.2: The exact workflow is attempted, but setup fails before producing semantic evidence.
scale.3: A real query-only round trip observes the malformed-model failure or restored result shape, but evidence is incomplete or print-only.
scale.4: The workflow reliably compares source and restored row types and verifies selected or annotated contents.
scale.5: Evidence covers annotated values, values_list variants, a normal-query control, and laziness or nested-query behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Faithful query-only reproduction and evidence

applies_when: The prefix contains an implementation, an exact proposed intervention, or a claim that the defect is fixed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures post-change validation of public result semantics and neighboring behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: No rerun after editing, crash-only checks, fake setters, unrelated suites, or unresolved relevant failures.
metadata.judge_focus: Require post-change evidence from real ORM objects rather than original-failure reproduction alone.
metadata.oracle_test: Focused queryset_pickle tests for annotated values, values_list fallback, callable defaults, ordinary model queries, and nested __in laziness.

scale.1: No post-change semantic validation is visible.
scale.2: Only a fake check, import check, or crash-only rerun provides post-change evidence.
scale.3: A real restored values query is checked after the change, but exact contents or neighboring cases are missing.
scale.4: Exact annotated dictionaries and values_list dictionary fallback pass with at least one normal-query or laziness control.
scale.5: Focused evaluator-like tests and relevant neighboring suites pass with exact assertions and no unresolved relevant failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative post-change validation

applies_when: The visible work investigates or changes QuerySet.ordered behavior for a query whose aggregation or selected values can produce GROUP BY.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess cutoff-visible progress toward making QuerySet.ordered preserve empty-queryset and explicit-order precedence while preventing model Meta.ordering from implying an ORDER BY for any truthy GROUP BY representation. Distinguish failed exploration, reliable causal reproduction, defective implementation, robust implementation, and successful behavioral validation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible implementation limited to `group_by is True`, or otherwise known to miss a nonempty expression tuple, cannot exceed 2 even if the primary annotate case passes. An implementation that lets grouping override explicit order_by/extra_order_by, loses EmptyQuerySet behavior, changes SQL generation instead of introspection, is malformed, or reverses the required result scores 1. An opaque claimed edit followed only by failed setup cannot exceed 2. Successful checks cannot prove unexercised tuple handling, but they may establish applied behavioral progress when the exact edited condition is truncated.
metadata.evidence_authority: Use the strongest mutually consistent cutoff-visible evidence. A complete post-edit source view or repository diff establishes implementation semantics directly. Successful before/after QuerySet.ordered observations and generated SQL establish the exercised behavior and outrank summaries; repository-native focused tests outrank conflicting ad hoc checks. A successful edit command plus later behavioral change establishes that relevant code was applied even if the exact condition is truncated. A claimed or opaque edit with only failed execution is weaker than a reliable reproduction with a correct causal diagnosis.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equating all partially inspectable edits, rewarding a narrow sentinel check merely because it was applied, undervaluing successful before/after behavior when source output is truncated, or treating dependency failures as equivalent to a reliable reproduction and correct boundary diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either a fully inspectable robust QuerySet.ordered implementation or a visibly applied relevant edit supported by successful behavior for both ordinary model ordering and grouped aggregation. Credit of 5 requires a fully inspectable robust implementation plus successful focused evidence for ordinary default ordering, grouped aggregation without explicit ordering, and explicit ordering on a grouped queryset. A proposal without an applied repository change cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: First determine whether the issue was reliably reproduced rather than merely asserted. Then inspect whether a repository edit was applied and whether its complete condition is visible. For visible logic, check EmptyQuerySet first, explicit extra_order_by/order_by before grouping, and a falsey-group_by requirement on the Meta.ordering fallback that covers both True and nonempty tuples. Separately count successful observations of ordinary, grouped-unordered, and grouped-explicit behavior; do not infer an unobserved tuple case from a True-sentinel test.
metadata.oracle_test: Equivalent correct behavior is: EmptyQuerySet is ordered; explicit extra_order_by or order_by is ordered even with grouping; otherwise model Meta.ordering implies ordered only when default_ordering is enabled and query.group_by is falsey. Aggregate grouping without explicit ordering is unordered for both the True sentinel and a nonempty expression tuple.
metadata.stage: diagnosis through early implementation and focused validation

scale.1: Only failed setup, unsupported claims, or exploratory inspection without a reliable task-specific reproduction is visible; alternatively, the visible change is malformed, targets SQL generation, suppresses explicit ordering, loses EmptyQuerySet behavior, or reverses the required semantics.
scale.2: A relevant edit is applied or concretely exposed, but it has a known material defect such as checking only `group_by is True`; or an edit is reported but its decisive condition is hidden and no successful task-specific behavior follows.
scale.3: The failure is reliably reproduced and its causal boundary is correctly identified, with a concrete robust proposal preserving explicit ordering and excluding truthy grouping, but no repository change is visibly applied.
scale.4: A robust applied boundary is fully inspectable but focused validation is absent or incomplete; alternatively, a relevant applied edit whose exact condition is partly truncated is supported by successful observations showing ordinary model ordering remains ordered and grouped aggregation without explicit ordering becomes unordered, with no visible contradictory behavior.
scale.5: A fully inspectable applied implementation preserves EmptyQuerySet and explicit-order precedence, excludes every truthy group_by form from the model-default fallback, and successful focused evidence confirms ordinary default ordering, grouped aggregation without explicit ordering, and explicit ordering on a grouped queryset.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-grounded progress on the QuerySet.ordered grouping boundary

applies_when: The task concerns QuerySet.ordered behavior when aggregation introduces GROUP BY on a model with default ordering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work correctly changes QuerySet.ordered so explicit ordering still reports ordered, while model default ordering does not report ordered for a grouped query whose generated SQL lacks ORDER BY.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the applied condition handles only group_by is True and therefore misses tuple-based grouping, or otherwise suppresses explicit order_by(). Cap at 2 if no relevant repository change is visibly applied. Score 1 if failed setup attempts or unsupported assertions are the only evidence, or if the applied change contradicts the required ordering semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: An applied repository diff supported by successful task-specific execution is strongest. An applied diff without execution outranks a proposed edit. Generated SQL and actual QuerySet.ordered observations outrank verbal claims. Repository-native focused tests outrank ad hoc scripts when they conflict.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a correct-sounding diagnosis as completed work, treating ad hoc plans as applied fixes, or accepting a narrow group_by is True check that misses values()/annotate() grouping represented by a tuple.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visibly applied change in the relevant QuerySet ordering logic. Credit of 5 requires evidence that the implementation preserves explicit ordering and ordinary model default ordering while rejecting implicit default ordering for all truthy GROUP BY representations.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible repository patch, successful reproductions, and focused checks for ordinary default ordering, aggregate-created grouping without explicit ordering, and grouping with explicit order_by(). Also inspect whether the condition covers every supported truthy Query.group_by form, including True and an expression tuple.
metadata.oracle_test: For a model with Meta.ordering: an ordinary queryset is ordered; annotate(aggregate) with no explicit order_by is not ordered when GROUP BY suppresses the default ORDER BY; the same grouped queryset with explicit order_by is ordered. The grouped case must work whether Query.group_by is True or a nonempty tuple.

scale.1: No reliable task-specific reproduction or relevant applied change is visible, or the applied behavior contradicts the required semantics.
scale.2: The issue is successfully reproduced and the exact relevant logic is identified, but the fix remains proposed rather than applied.
scale.3: A relevant fix is applied but is semantically incomplete, such as handling only one truthy GROUP BY representation, or validation leaves a material ordering case unresolved.
scale.4: A robust fix covering truthy GROUP BY forms is visibly applied and preserves explicit-order precedence, but validation is absent or does not meaningfully exercise the key grouped and nongrouped cases.
scale.5: A robust applied fix is supported by successful focused evidence showing ordinary Meta.ordering remains ordered, grouped aggregation without explicit ordering is not ordered, and explicit ordering on the grouped queryset remains ordered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly implements QuerySet.ordered semantics for grouped queries

applies_when: The trajectory considers behavior outside the single annotate example, including existing QuerySet.ordered contracts or alternate group_by representations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects established ordered semantics and demonstrates that the fix is keyed to truthy grouping rather than annotate() broadly, including tuple-based group_by and ordinary non-grouped querysets.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the approach equates all annotate() or values() calls with grouping, rejects explicit ordering on grouped queries, or fails for a visible nonempty group_by tuple. Cap at 3 when contradictory test evidence remains unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual query state, generated SQL, repository tests, and diffs take precedence over guessed behavior; contradictory runtime evidence must be resolved rather than ignored.
metadata.failure_mode: Passing only the common group_by=True reproduction while regressing tuple grouping, non-grouped values queries, explicit ordering, or legacy EmptyQuerySet behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Higher anchors require preserving ordinary default ordering and explicit ordering in addition to fixing the grouped implicit-ordering case.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, tests, or runtime checks for ordinary Meta.ordering, cleared/no default ordering, explicit and extra ordering, empty querysets, non-grouping values(), and values().annotate() or another tuple-group_by query.
metadata.oracle_test: Expected matrix: ordinary queryset with Meta.ordering=True; order_by() clearing defaults=False; model without ordering=False; EmptyQuerySet=True; grouped query without explicit ordering=False for True or tuple group_by; grouped query with explicit or extra ordering=True; values() alone remains governed by its actual group_by state.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or visible evidence shows broad regressions with no recovery.
scale.2: Mentions edge cases but applies an overbroad rule or leaves decisive contradictory behavior unexplained.
scale.3: Checks or reasons correctly about ordinary default and explicit ordering, but omits alternate group_by forms or another established ordered contract.
scale.4: Provides coherent protection across the main state matrix, including explicit ordering and at least one non-grouped control, with no unresolved contradiction.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and visibly covers both group_by=True and tuple-based grouping plus the principal legacy cases, resolving any initially mistaken expectation using source or runtime evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility across ordering and group_by states

applies_when: A visible code change or concrete patch proposal modifies the behavior of QuerySet.ordered for grouped queries.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes only the QuerySet.ordered decision so empty querysets and explicit ordering remain True, model default ordering counts only without a truthy group_by, and grouped queries without explicit ordering return False.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if grouping is checked before explicit order_by/extra_order_by, if EmptyQuerySet behavior is lost, or if the condition handles only group_by is True while allowing a nonempty group_by tuple to use Meta.ordering. Cap at 1 for edits to SQL generation that reintroduce implicit ORDER BY instead of correcting introspection.
metadata.evidence_authority: The actual visible diff takes precedence over summaries or claimed edits; a minimal equivalent boolean condition is authoritative regardless of formatting.
metadata.failure_mode: Overbroad changes that mark explicitly ordered grouped queries unordered, narrowly checking only the True sentinel and missing tuple-based grouping, or changing SQL behavior instead of the property.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 or 5 requires an applied, syntactically coherent change in QuerySet.ordered rather than an unexecuted proposal.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff in django/db/models/query.py, especially condition ordering and treatment of EmptyQuerySet, extra_order_by, order_by, default_ordering, Meta.ordering, and Query.group_by.
metadata.oracle_test: Equivalent correct logic is: EmptyQuerySet => True; explicit extra_order_by or order_by => True; otherwise default_ordering plus model Meta.ordering => True only when query.group_by is falsey; else False.

scale.1: No visible implementation, or the visible edit targets the wrong subsystem or reverses required behavior.
scale.2: A partially relevant edit is visible but has a major boundary error, malformed code, or handles only one group_by representation.
scale.3: A coherent implementation is visible and fixes the primary annotate case, but its precedence or compatibility boundary is insufficiently clear or contains avoidable unrelated changes.
scale.4: A minimal applied implementation correctly preserves empty and explicit-ordering cases and excludes all truthy group_by forms from the Meta.ordering fallback.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 with an especially precise, idiomatic change whose visible diff is narrowly confined to QuerySet.ordered and clearly matches surrounding Django style.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise QuerySet.ordered implementation boundary

applies_when: The prefix states, attempts, or implements a repair.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the observable semantics of the repair, independent of whether it is merely proposed or already edited into the repository.

metadata.failure_mode: cast omission, retained inner cast, FloatField substitution, mutation, or rendered-SQL rewriting
metadata.judge_focus: cast placement, output typing, isolation, and structural compilation
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect whether the repair yields one outer CAST around the completed Decimal Window while preserving its DecimalField output.

scale.1: The repair is absent from the visible claims or is structurally incapable of fixing the defect, such as retaining the malformed cast or producing invalid code.
scale.2: The repair can avoid the syntax error but violates a required invariant by dropping the cast, forcing FloatField, special-casing a function, mutating shared state, or rewriting rendered SQL.
scale.3: The repair targets the Window boundary and complete-window casting, but inner-cast suppression, output preservation, isolation, or exact scope remains incomplete or ambiguous.
scale.4: The repair clearly suppresses the inner cast and applies an outer NUMERIC cast at the SQLite Window boundary while preserving Decimal output semantics.
scale.5: The repair additionally uses an isolated expression tree, preserves normal vendor dispatch, remains general across Decimal-valued Window expressions, and avoids rendered-SQL manipulation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Expressed repair invariant fidelity

applies_when: The trajectory contains a task-specific diagnosis or causal claim about the malformed SQLite Decimal window SQL.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the assistant explicitly explains that a resolved Decimal-valued Lag source is cast by SQLiteNumericMixin during source Func compilation and that Window subsequently appends OVER, causing the invalid pre-OVER cast.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the assistant treats unresolved F output_field/as_sql errors as the defect, attributes the malformed ordering solely to SQLite version support, or claims the cast is added after OVER.
metadata.evidence_authority: Assistant-authored conclusions supported by inspected source or resolved-query SQL outrank speculative remarks. Observed resolved SQL outranks assumptions from an unresolved standalone expression.
metadata.failure_mode: Partial source discovery is mistaken for a causal explanation, or unresolved-expression errors are misidentified as the product failure.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an explicit authored connection among Decimal output, SQLiteNumericMixin source compilation, and Window's later OVER assembly.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant's own causal conclusions. Names appearing only in grep output, source listings, tracebacks, or command output are not diagnosis. Credit a resolved QuerySet explanation or an explicit correct account of query resolution; do not treat direct failures on unresolved F('amount') as evidence about the reported compilation path.
metadata.oracle_test: Resolve Lag('amount') through a model QuerySet; Func's SQLiteNumericMixin emits CAST(LAG(...) AS NUMERIC), then Window.as_sql() interpolates that source SQL before OVER.
metadata.stage: Establish the compilation path and failure mechanism

scale.1: No task-causal conclusion is authored, or the stated cause is materially contradicted by the visible SQL and source path.
scale.2: The assistant identifies Decimal casting or Window assembly, but omits or misstates the connection between them; unresolved F errors may dominate the diagnosis.
scale.3: The assistant correctly identifies the malformed pre-OVER cast and at least one responsible compilation step, but the resolved Decimal source, mixin dispatch, or later Window assembly remains unstated.
scale.4: The assistant explicitly connects resolved Decimal output, SQLiteNumericMixin casting of the source Func, and Window appending OVER after source compilation.
scale.5: The complete chain is explicit and the assistant correctly concludes that repair requires suppressing the premature source cast before casting the fully assembled Window expression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Assistant-authored diagnosis of the Decimal Window compilation chain

applies_when: The prefix contains task-specific diagnosis, source inspection, SQL interpretation, or a causal claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible reasoning correctly connects resolved Decimal output, SQLiteNumericMixin on the source Func, and Window's later assembly of the OVER clause.

metadata.failure_mode: missing or incorrect explanation of where the cast is introduced and why it precedes OVER
metadata.judge_focus: observable causal claims rather than exploration volume
metadata.oracle_test: Resolve Lag('amount') through a model QuerySet and trace compiler vendor dispatch through Func and Window.
metadata.stage: Establish the compilation path and failure mechanism

scale.1: The visible claims are unrelated, materially incorrect, or attribute the failure to a cause contradicted by the generated SQL.
scale.2: The prefix locates relevant classes or SQLite window support but does not correctly connect Decimal source casting to Window's later OVER assembly.
scale.3: The prefix correctly recognizes the malformed pre-OVER cast or reproduces it, but only part of the responsible compilation chain is established.
scale.4: The prefix correctly identifies resolved Decimal output, source Func casting through SQLiteNumericMixin, and Window appending OVER after source compilation.
scale.5: The complete chain is explicit and includes the consequence that a valid repair must suppress the premature source cast before casting the fully assembled Window expression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Resolved causal-chain accuracy

applies_when: The cutoff workspace contains source edits, tests, scratch artifacts, or an evaluator-facing patch for the task.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the active cutoff artifact is an applicable, narrowly scoped framework change that preserves compiler dispatch, expression state, non-Decimal behavior, and repository cleanliness.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for global output-field changes, Lag-only behavior, broad vendor-dispatch bypass, mutation of reusable expressions, rendered-SQL reconstruction, duplicate replacement source files, or an artifact consisting only of scratch scripts. Cap at 1 for malformed or inapplicable framework source.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff diff and observed test or syntax output are authoritative. A clean claim cannot override scratch artifacts, broad active edits, malformed code, or failed applicable checks.
metadata.failure_mode: Exploratory or unsafe workspace contents are treated as a clean compatible patch merely because they are task-related.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires a coherent active framework diff with visibly narrow SQLite Decimal Window handling, preserved original expression state, and no material scratch or duplicate source artifacts.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active git diff and status rather than claimed intentions. Distinguish framework source edits from scratch scripts, duplicate .fixed files, generated files, proposed patches, and reverted edits. Check SQLite-only scope, non-Decimal fallback, expression-copy isolation, valid syntax, and absence of unrelated changes.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the final diff for a localized Window compilation change, ordinary non-Decimal fallback, isolated temporary typing, valid syntax, and no unrelated tracked artifacts.
metadata.stage: Run compatibility checks and finalize the patch

scale.1: There is no applicable framework artifact, or the active framework source is malformed, inapplicable, or structurally unsafe.
scale.2: An active task-directed edit exists but is broad, function-specific, mutating, dispatch-bypassing, SQL-rewriting, or accompanied by material duplicate or scratch artifacts.
scale.3: The active framework edit is plausibly localized and syntactically coherent, but backend scope, expression isolation, non-Decimal preservation, or artifact cleanliness remains unestablished.
scale.4: The active diff is clean and localized, preserves normal non-Decimal and non-SQLite paths, isolates temporary expression changes, and contains no material unintended artifacts.
scale.5: Level 4 is met and actually executed compatibility checks cover ordinary windows, representative frames or validation, syntax, and diff integrity.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff workspace scope and compatibility safety

applies_when: The prefix contains analysis or edits concerning JSONField serialization for admin or forms.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures visible evidence that both JSONField.prepare_value() and admin display_for_field() emit literal non-ASCII characters using ensure_ascii=False.

metadata.failure_mode: One-sided fix, escaped Unicode, or storage-only change.
metadata.judge_focus: Coverage of both evaluator-facing paths with correct JSON serialization.
metadata.oracle_test: forms_tests.field_tests.test_jsonfield.JSONFieldTest.test_prepare_value and admin_utils.tests.UtilsTests.test_json_display_for_field

scale.1: No relevant fix, or changes only unrelated/storage serialization.
scale.2: Correct cause is mentioned but neither required path is reliably implemented.
scale.3: Exactly one of form prepare_value or admin display_for_field is correctly fixed.
scale.4: Both paths are edited toward ensure_ascii=False, with minor uncertainty or incomplete direct evidence.
scale.5: Both paths clearly serialize with ensure_ascii=False and produce the exact literal-Unicode outputs expected by evaluator-like tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Both JSONField presentation paths preserve Unicode

applies_when: The active cutoff workspace changes JSONField.prepare_value() or the JSONField branch of admin display_for_field().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether active presentation-path edits retain the configured encoder and the existing invalid-input, TypeError-fallback, and empty-value control flow applicable to those edited paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Dropping self.encoder or field.encoder, removing the InvalidJSONInput return, removing the admin TypeError fallback, or changing the existing empty-value branch caps the score at 2. A visible failed compatibility assertion caps the score at 3 unless a later run after correction passes.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active target-method source is primary. Executed compatibility tests with observed results may strengthen it; source listings from before the edit, plans, scratch assertions that were not run, and unrelated model-field behavior do not.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting untouched baseline code, preserving only unrelated storage behavior, losing a custom encoder, overquoting malformed input, or allowing admin rendering to raise instead of falling back.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires a valid active edit to at least one exact presentation path. A score of 5 requires compatible active edits to both paths and successful executed checks covering their distinctive guards.
metadata.judge_focus: For a form edit, inspect retention of the InvalidJSONInput early return and cls=self.encoder. For an admin edit, inspect cls=field.encoder, the existing TypeError fallback to display_for_value(), and the surrounding falsey/empty handling. Untouched baseline mechanisms and compatibility in model storage methods are not evidence of preserving an edited presentation path.
metadata.oracle_test: test_custom_encoder_decoder, test_redisplay_wrong_input, test_null_display_for_field, and the tuple-key fallback case in test_json_display_for_field

scale.1: No valid active target-path edit exists, so preservation under a changed presentation path is not demonstrated.
scale.2: A target path is edited but at least one applicable encoder, guard, fallback, or empty-value contract is visibly removed or broken.
scale.3: At least one target path is edited and its obvious compatibility structure remains, but preservation is incomplete, uncertain, or contradicted by an unresolved failed check.
scale.4: All compatibility mechanisms applicable to the active target edits are visibly retained, with no contradictory result, but discriminative checks are incomplete.
scale.5: Both target paths retain their correct encoders and all applicable guards and fallbacks, and executed compatibility checks visibly pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Target-path edits preserve JSONField compatibility behavior

applies_when: The prefix has reached validation or makes claims that the fix works.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether validation exercises the modified Django paths and exact Unicode/fallback behavior rather than only demonstrating json.dumps in isolation.

metadata.failure_mode: Source counting, standalone-only demonstrations, false pass claims, or ignored failures.
metadata.judge_focus: Direct, honest, task-specific test evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Targeted form JSONField and admin_utils test labels with Chinese, emoji, accented text, and invalid JSON fallback.

scale.1: No meaningful validation or visible failing tests are falsely reported as passing.
scale.2: Only standalone json.dumps demonstrations or textual grep checks are shown.
scale.3: A modified Django path is exercised, but one required path or key compatibility case is missing.
scale.4: Both target paths are tested with Unicode and results are credible, with limited neighboring coverage.
scale.5: Supplied evaluator-like tests and relevant compatibility tests pass with exact expected outputs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-like validation quality

applies_when: The active cutoff workspace contains source edits, tracked artifacts, or generated patch content.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures cutoff-visible risk from malformed active source, unapplied-only implementation artifacts, destructive changes, and unnecessary edits outside the two JSONField presentation paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible syntax error, conflict marker, destructive deletion, or implementation existing only in an unapplied patch forces score 5. A later visible restoration or correction removes that defect from consideration.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace and resulting parseability override terminal-status labels, earlier malformed edits that were visibly reverted, proposed commands, and patch text not applied to repository source.
metadata.failure_mode: Ignoring active defects because no terminal submission exists, penalizing reverted experiments, conflating harmless scratch scripts with production changes, or overlooking broad cross-subsystem serialization edits.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a material active production-source or evaluator-artifact defect; mere nonterminal status, absence of a final response, or a harmless scratch file cannot produce those scores.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff diff and resulting files regardless of whether the trajectory is terminal. Identify syntax or indentation defects, conflict markers, deletions, implementation present only in a patch file, and unrelated changes to storage, validation, query SQL, signing, serializers, json_script, admin logs, widgets, or other serialization protocols. Harmless untracked demonstrations are lower risk than modified production subsystems.
metadata.oracle_test: cutoff git diff and status, resulting source around edited hunks, git diff --check, Python compilation, import startup, or targeted test startup

scale.1: No material active risk: there is no source edit, or the active production diff is valid and narrowly limited to the two presentation paths and focused tests.
scale.2: Only minor harmless noise or scratch artifacts are present; active production source remains focused and valid.
scale.3: The active workspace contains several unnecessary files or limited unrelated production edits, but source remains parseable and the evaluator-facing implementation is still usable.
scale.4: Broad active changes alter unrelated storage, validation, query, serializer, HTML, or admin protocols, or a recoverable import or structural defect materially threatens the task.
scale.5: Active source is syntactically malformed, conflicted, destructive, non-importable, or the intended implementation exists only as an unapplied artifact rather than in repository source.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active workspace scope and source-integrity risk

applies_when: The checked-out implementation may already contain the behavior requested by the task
A rollout must determine whether a source modification is warranted before submission
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly determine from repository evidence whether PEP 415 suppression behavior is already implemented, and leave a deliverable whose actual diff state is proportional to that determination.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Prose, comments, or historical diff text presented as the current patch caps the score at 1. A source rewrite made after repository evidence establishes that the requested semantics are already implemented cannot receive 5, even if behavior remains equivalent.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual file contents and repository diff/status outrank assistant claims, commit-message interpretation, ad hoc copied snippets, and prose labeled as a patch. Executed verification may support but cannot override contradictory source or diff evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding full credit for recognizing an already-fixed baseline without producing a valid deliverable, for manufacturing patch-like prose, or for changing correct code solely to create a nonempty diff.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a cutoff-visible, syntactically valid deliverable consistent with the repository state. Anchor 5 additionally requires either a necessary focused implementation or, when the baseline already satisfies the task, an unchanged source tree with a valid empty-diff/no-op submission artifact.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual implementation of exception-cause selection, working-tree diff/status, any applied source edit, and the cutoff-visible patch or no-op deliverable.
