metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an assertion that the squashed migration key is absent after backward migration; credit of 5 additionally requires a demonstrated relevant test pass.
metadata.judge_focus: A repository test under tests/migrations, preferably extending executor coverage, that queries MigrationRecorder or an equivalent fresh persistent-state view rather than only checking schema tables or a stale loader cache.
metadata.oracle_test: Using test_migrations_squashed, apply 0001_squashed_0002, establish that its applied state is recorded, migrate migrations to None/zero, then assert 0001_squashed_0002, 0001_initial, and 0002_second are all absent from fresh MigrationRecorder.applied_migrations().

scale.1: No relevant regression scenario is present, or the scenario cannot exercise replacement migration bookkeeping.
scale.2: Mentions or tests squash unapplication but checks only table removal, the plan, or replaced keys and therefore misses the reported stale squash key.
scale.3: Defines the essential apply-then-unapply scenario and squash-key assertion, but it is incomplete, not integrated, or not successfully executed.
scale.4: Provides a repository-integrated test that checks the squash key and replaced keys through persistent recorder state, with no contradictory completed result.
scale.5: Provides the complete focused regression test and visible successful execution with the replaced migration files still present.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression test for recorder state with replacement files present

applies_when: The visible trajectory proposes or performs a code change for unapplication bookkeeping of a migration with a nonempty replaces list.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Specifies or implements a change in MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration() that retains deletion of every key in migration.replaces and also deletes the replacement migration's own app/name recorder key, while preserving ordinary-migration and schema-reversal behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the adopted change removes only replaced keys, changes only the ordinary else branch, targets loader or graph state instead of the recorder boundary, or says the replacement's own key should not be removed. Cap at 3 if the own-key deletion is only general intent, branch placement is ambiguous, replaced-key deletion is lost, or the proposal remains mixed with unresolved incompatible implementations. An unnecessary application-side change prevents a 5 but does not erase an otherwise coherent backward fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final visible source change or diff is strongest. An exact executable patch, edit command, or unambiguous code-level specification is sufficient to establish the implementation design even if the final file is not displayed. Such evidence receives credit only when the trajectory's adopted explanation has the same polarity; a later reversion or endorsed contrary explanation controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Separates a complete code-level solution from mere method discovery, while avoiding false credit for an exact-looking patch whose surrounding reasoning gives it the opposite purpose or later rejects it.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an exact call or equally precise executable specification that record_unapplied(migration.app_label, migration.name) executes for a replacement migration in addition to the retained loop over migration.replaces. A contradictory claim that the replacement key should remain recorded prevents credit above 2.
metadata.judge_focus: The proposed or visible form of the migration.replaces branch in django/db/migrations/executor.py::unapply_migration(), including the complete set of record_unapplied calls, their branch placement, and the trajectory's stated purpose for them.
metadata.oracle_test: For replacement S of R1 and R2, the specified replacement path must request record_unapplied for R1, R2, and S; for ordinary migration N, the ordinary path must continue to request it once for N.

scale.1: Provides no actionable change at the persistent unapplication recording boundary.
scale.2: Locates relevant code but proposes an incorrect, reversed, contradictory, or out-of-scope change that does not reliably delete the replacement's own recorder key.
scale.3: States the correct remedy in general terms or gives a partially specified call, but does not establish complete branch placement and preservation of all replaced-key deletions.
scale.4: Gives a coherent exact implementation, whether proposed or performed, that deletes all replaced keys and the replacement's own key while preserving the ordinary branch and reversal flow.
scale.5: Shows the minimal correctly placed final source change with no unnecessary application-side, loader, graph, schema, planning, fake-mode, or callback modifications.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct replacement-unapply recorder change

applies_when: The cutoff contains reasoning about how a squashed migration and its replaced migrations are represented in django_migrations during backward migration.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that unapplying a replacement migration deletes the records named in migration.replaces but leaves the squashed migration's own recorder row behind, even though check_replacements may previously have created that row.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims the existing replacement branch already removes the squashed key, that check_replacements removes stale rows, or that only the replaced migrations should become unapplied; cap at 3 if it never distinguishes persistent recorder state from loader-local state.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly quoted repository control flow and observed MigrationRecorder contents outrank assumptions based on method names, local in-memory applied_migrations sets, or migration-file presence alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad discussion of graph planning or file discovery that misses the persistent stale row responsible for the bug.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires identifying both the surviving squashed key and why deleting only the replaced keys does not delete it.
metadata.judge_focus: A code-grounded trace through MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration(), record_migration(), check_replacements(), and MigrationLoader's replacement-state synthesis, distinguishing actual recorder rows from loader-derived applied state.
metadata.oracle_test: After a squash replacing 0001_initial and 0002_second has been applied, django_migrations can contain all three keys; migrating the app to zero must leave none of those three keys applied.

scale.1: No relevant causal account, or an account centered on an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: Recognizes that replacement migrations are special but gives an incorrect or internally inconsistent explanation of which records remain applied.
scale.3: Correctly states that the replacement branch removes the replaced migration records but not the squashed migration's own record.
scale.4: Also explains how check_replacements or loader replacement handling caused the squashed key to be considered and recorded as applied, and why the current unapply path leaves it stale.
scale.5: Provides a complete, code-grounded state transition from application through backward migration, explicitly separating database recorder rows, loader-synthesized applied state, and the presence of replacement files.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of the stale squashed-migration record

applies_when: The cutoff contains commands or observations presented as runtime evidence about squashed migration application or unapplication.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses Django's repository-native test environment or a correctly configured equivalent, treats setup failures as non-evidence, and updates conclusions when runtime results conflict with the proposed causal model.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if import errors, missing settings, missing migration nodes, empty recorder output from a misconfigured app, or a script that never reaches migration execution is claimed as proof. Cap at 3 if repeated invalid attempts are not replaced by valid evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successfully discovered Django test run using tests/runtests.py and fresh database state outranks standalone scripts; setup exceptions and empty results from misconfigured applications have no semantic authority.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding conclusions drawn from ModuleNotFoundError, NodeNotFoundError caused by bad setup, stale executor loaders, or no-op migration configurations.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one successfully executed repository-native migration test or an equivalently valid configured reproduction that reaches migration operations and assertions.
metadata.judge_focus: Command provenance, successful test discovery, actual assertions reached, freshness of recorder/loader state, and whether failed imports or misconfigured apps are interpreted cautiously.
metadata.oracle_test: The reliable command is a focused migration executor test through Django's own test runner; evidence is meaningful only after the intended migrations app and test database are loaded and recorder assertions execute.

scale.1: Runtime claims rely on invalid setup, or contradictory output is ignored.
scale.2: Attempts execution but repeatedly treats setup or discovery failures as behavioral evidence.
scale.3: Correctly recognizes invalid or inconclusive runs as non-evidence and refines the setup or reasoning, but no valid task-specific execution is reached.
scale.4: Successfully runs repository-native migration coverage and interprets its scope accurately, without claiming that an existing broad test proves the new recorder assertion.
scale.5: Successfully runs a focused reproduction or regression assertion for the stale squash record and reconciles all earlier contradictory or invalid observations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliable runtime evidence and recovery from invalid reproductions

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes applied-state bookkeeping for unapplying replacement migrations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the trajectory establishes the recorder-level cause of the stale squashed-migration status and converges on the minimal backward-bookkeeping correction without unnecessarily changing forward migration semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the trajectory finishes by denying that the squashed row must be removed, reverses the requested behavior, or proposes changing forward application or loader graph semantics without a demonstrated need. Resolved and reverted experiments do not trigger the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Cutoff working-tree contents and git diff outrank earlier attempted edits; executed test output outranks claimed verification; direct observations of executor and loader code outrank speculative explanations. A final clean tree means temporary edits are evidence of reasoning only, not an applied fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely finding replacement-related code, confusing graph membership with persisted recorder state, treating a proposed edit as completed work, or adding a symmetric forward-recording change that the bug does not require.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require correctly identifying that the replacement branch removes the replaced migration records but can leave the squashed migration's own recorder row present. Score 5 additionally requires a source-grounded account of how that own row can be recorded or maintained.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, reasoning, cutoff-visible file contents, and tests concerning MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration(), record_migration(), check_replacements(), and the recorder rows for a replacement migration and its replaced migrations.
metadata.non_evidence: Repository browsing volume, repeated restatement of the issue, failed environment setup, unexecuted test scripts, and assertions about behavior unsupported by source or command output are not independently creditworthy.
metadata.oracle_test: With the squash file and the files it replaces all still available, after the replacement has been represented as applied and is migrated backward, the recorder must contain neither the replacement migration key nor any of its replaced migration keys. Forward recording behavior should remain otherwise unchanged.
metadata.stage: early trajectory diagnosis and patch planning

scale.1: No coherent task-causal diagnosis is reached, or the final position confidently asserts the opposite bookkeeping behavior.
scale.2: Finds migration replacement code but remains materially confused about which records persist, primarily pursues unrelated graph or environment theories, and gives no viable focused remedy.
scale.3: Identifies a likely asymmetry in replacement-migration recording or proposes deleting an additional record, but leaves the persisted-state mechanism unresolved, retains significant contradictions, or proposes unnecessary production-code scope.
scale.4: Correctly explains that backward handling removes replaced records while failing to remove the squashed migration's own record and identifies the focused unapply-side remedy, but lacks either the full source chain, a clear scope boundary, or reliable validation.
scale.5: Correctly and consistently traces the full invariant: replacement application records the replaced statuses, replacement maintenance can record the squash key, and the replacement unapply branch currently deletes only the replaced keys; it therefore targets deletion of the squash key as well, avoids unrelated forward-semantic changes, and any claimed implementation or validation is supported by cutoff-visible evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly diagnoses squashed-migration unapply bookkeeping

applies_when: A source change for the subwidget label ID defect is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements the fix at BoundWidget.id_for_label in django/forms/boundfield.py by using the option ID stored in self.data['attrs']['id'], without changing BoundField.id_for_label or unrelated rendering behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest source contains duplicate decorators or returns, invalid indexing, broad accidental replacements, or edits BoundField.id_for_label instead. Cap at 3 if the normal path still reconstructs the ID from name and index.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest valid source or unified diff overrides earlier proposed edits and narrative claims; a clean diff is strongest.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for modifying the similarly named BoundField method, retaining the defective reconstruction, or leaving a malformed automated edit.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require syntactically valid visible code in BoundWidget.id_for_label that obtains the result from self.data['attrs']['id'].
metadata.judge_focus: The latest visible source excerpt or diff for BoundWidget.id_for_label and the absence of unrelated edits.
metadata.oracle_test: The task-specific patch changes the BoundWidget property body from hardcoded name/index formatting to return self.data['attrs']['id']; BoundField.id_for_label remains unchanged.

scale.1: No concrete relevant implementation is visible, or the change targets the wrong method.
scale.2: A relevant edit is attempted, but the latest visible source is malformed, duplicated, or unusable.
scale.3: A valid BoundWidget edit consults attrs but retains independent name/index reconstruction as ordinary behavior or includes unnecessary behavioral changes.
scale.4: The latest valid source directly uses data['attrs']['id'] in the correct BoundWidget property, but final diff-level scope evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: A clean minimal diff changes only BoundWidget.id_for_label to return self.data['attrs']['id'], with unrelated behavior untouched.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise BoundWidget implementation

applies_when: A reproduction, test, or runtime check for iterable choice-widget label IDs is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Exercises CheckboxSelectMultiple with a genuinely nondefault form auto_id and demonstrates that every BoundWidget.id_for_label equals its corresponding data['attrs']['id'] and the expected formatted indexed input ID.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if only default id_%s behavior is exercised. Cap at 3 if the custom-ID check fails, cannot run, or only inspects rendered HTML without directly exercising BoundWidget.id_for_label.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed assertions or explicit runtime comparisons override predicted behavior; repository regression tests outrank disposable scripts; failed or unexecuted commands do not prove success.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating default IDs or widget-template rendering that bypasses the property as decisive proof of the fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require successful post-change runtime evidence using a custom auto_id and a concrete equality between id_for_label and data['attrs']['id'].
metadata.judge_focus: Visible custom auto_id setup, concrete pre-fix or post-fix values, assertions comparing id_for_label with option attrs IDs, and command results.
metadata.oracle_test: With auto_id such as custom_%s and field name choices, option zero's actual ID is custom_choices_0 and BoundWidget.id_for_label must return that exact value rather than id_choices_0.

scale.1: No relevant test or runtime evidence.
scale.2: Only setup failures, default-ID checks, or unrelated rendering checks are visible.
scale.3: A custom-ID reproduction exposes the original mismatch, or a suitable test is written but no successful post-fix execution is shown.
scale.4: An executed focused check shows the corrected custom ID for CheckboxSelectMultiple options, but no durable repository regression test is added and passed.
scale.5: A task-specific repository regression test asserts the formatted indexed IDs or equality with option attrs, and visible focused execution passes after the implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive custom-auto-id runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory visibly inspects, changes, or executes a check involving BoundWidget.id_for_label or iterable choice-option ID attributes.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how decisively the visible trajectory establishes the current provenance of an iterable choice option's label ID: from default-ID coincidence or incomplete setup, through an inspectable correction or successful post-change equality, to coherent runtime proof that an unresolved implementation still synthesizes a label ID instead of using the concrete option attrs ID.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when only default IDs or rendered HTML are observed and no relevant source change is visible. Cap at 2 when a custom check does not execute. Cap at 3 when the latest source uses the option attrs ID or an executed post-change comparison shows equality. Cap at 4 when an otherwise direct mismatch diagnosis claims that built-in rendered option HTML consumes BoundWidget.id_for_label despite visible output or templates showing that rendering path bypasses the property.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest executed direct comparisons and latest visible source override earlier predictions or reproductions. A comparison of BoundWidget.id_for_label with the same option's data['attrs']['id'] outranks rendered HTML, because built-in option templates may render attrs directly. Successful execution outranks unexecuted assertions, while a final visible patch outranks an earlier transient edit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents default id_%s coincidence from proving provenance, distinguishes a persisted source-confirmed mismatch from a completed correction, and avoids treating correct rendered labels as proof that BoundWidget.id_for_label itself is correct.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires an executed genuinely nondefault direct comparison that diverges, latest visible source that still constructs the label ID independently of the option attrs ID, and no visible contradiction about which rendering path uses the property. Score 4 requires an executed nondefault divergence but permits causal ambiguity or contradictory rendering claims.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest BoundWidget.id_for_label source, the concrete option data['attrs']['id'], the directly returned property value, whether the ID is genuinely nondefault, whether execution succeeded, and whether claims about rendered HTML agree with the visible template or rendering path.
metadata.oracle_test: Create an iterable choice field with a nondefault ID format, inspect one BoundWidget, and compare id_for_label directly with data['attrs']['id']. A returned id_<name>_<index> that differs from the option's concrete ID proves the unresolved provenance defect; equality after an attrs-based implementation proves correction but is weaker evidence of a persisting defect.

scale.1: No decisive provenance evidence: only default-ID coincidence, unrelated rendered HTML, or exploration without a relevant inspectable source change is visible.
scale.2: Relevant source reasoning or an attrs-based correction is visible, but the nondefault direct comparison fails to run, remains incomplete, or is only predicted.
scale.3: The trajectory provides meaningful but non-persistent-defect evidence, such as successful post-change equality with a nondefault option ID, visible source-level correction, source-only synthesis evidence, or an exercised fallback that fabricates an ID when the option has none.
scale.4: An executed nondefault direct comparison shows id_for_label diverging from the corresponding option attrs ID, but the latest implementation is ambiguous or the causal account is contradicted by visible evidence about a rendering path that bypasses the property.
scale.5: An executed nondefault direct comparison shows a concrete divergence, the latest visible implementation still independently synthesizes the label ID, and the trajectory coherently attributes the mismatch without contradictory rendering claims.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Strength of option-label ID provenance evidence

applies_when: Evidence concerns how IDs flow through BoundField subwidgets, ChoiceWidget options, or BoundWidget.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that ChoiceWidget places each option's actual indexed ID in BoundWidget.data['attrs']['id'], while BoundWidget.id_for_label independently reconstructs a default-style ID and therefore ignores custom auto_id formatting or widget IDs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final diagnosis targets BoundField.id_for_label, claims attrs never reach BoundWidget despite contrary visible data, or attributes the defect solely to templates.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete source excerpts and runtime values showing both data['attrs']['id'] and id_for_label override unsupported claims; later explicitly corrected analysis overrides earlier speculation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a generic ID complaint or confusion between BoundField.id_for_label and BoundWidget.id_for_label.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require identification of both the authoritative option attrs ID and the hardcoded reconstruction in BoundWidget.id_for_label.
metadata.judge_focus: Source inspection or runtime output tracing the ID from BoundField.subwidgets through ChoiceWidget.create_option into BoundWidget.data['attrs']['id'].
metadata.oracle_test: For CheckboxSelectMultiple with a nondefault form auto_id, each option has a formatted indexed ID in data['attrs']['id'], while the original BoundWidget.id_for_label returns id_<name>_<index>.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis or a final diagnosis aimed at an unrelated component.
scale.2: Recognizes an ID mismatch but gives a materially incorrect account of where the authoritative ID is produced or ignored.
scale.3: Correctly identifies the hardcoded BoundWidget.id_for_label implementation but does not establish that the desired ID is already present in option attrs.
scale.4: Correctly traces the option ID into data['attrs']['id'] and explains why custom auto_id values diverge from the hardcoded result.
scale.5: Provides a complete evidence-backed chain from BoundField's base ID through ChoiceWidget's indexed option attrs to BoundWidget, while explicitly distinguishing BoundWidget from BoundField.id_for_label.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of the subwidget ID mismatch

applies_when: Visible execution contradicts a proposed fix, claimed interpretation, expected string, or edge-case assumption during the trajectory.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to contradictory evidence by correcting the interpretation or implementation and re-establishing the exact task semantics rather than declaring partial output successful or continuing from a corrupted premise.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Declaring success while the visible output differs from the task oracle, dismissing the oracle as a typo, or repeatedly substituting '<lt!', '<!', or '&ltlt!' caps credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest correctly formed real-implementation execution outranks earlier reasoning; the task's exact literal input and expected output outrank speculative reinterpretations of the report.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents long exploratory traces and claimed fixes from receiving credit when their own runtime evidence disproves the required semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit resolution of the contradiction; merely noticing it without correcting the premise or rerunning the relevant case cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether failed outputs, malformed test inputs, syntax errors, unexpected entity decoding, or regression failures lead to a precise correction followed by coherent source and exact-output evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Resolution returns to the literal '<!' input and confirms that '<' remains the anchor text, '%3C' appears in the href, and only '!' follows .

scale.1: The contradiction is ignored, rationalized away, or followed by a success claim incompatible with visible output.
scale.2: The trajectory notices conflicting evidence but continues with materially confused inputs, expectations, or source state.
scale.3: The contradiction is correctly identified and the premise or approach is revised, but no decisive exact rerun resolves it.
scale.4: The contradiction is resolved with a corrected interpretation or implementation and a later exact task run is coherent, though broader confirmation is limited.
scale.5: The trajectory cleanly isolates the contradiction, restores or corrects any faulty edit/test premise, reruns the exact oracle, and reconciles additional regression evidence without unresolved conflicts.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory runtime evidence

applies_when: A source change or concrete implementation proposal targets urlize() punctuation trimming.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the core django.utils.html.urlize() punctuation boundary so trailing punctuation is separated without replacing or corrupting the original escaped link text, while URL construction can still use the unescaped value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the implementation assigns the retained middle from middle_unescaped, produces literal '<' or '<' instead of preserving the task's '&lt' display spelling, duplicates 'lt', or drops punctuation, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The visible diff and task-specific runtime output outrank comments or claimed intent. If they conflict, an exact failing output caps credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents superficially passing fixes that decode the displayed text, use an unescaped index directly on escaped text, modify the wrapper filter, or special-case '&lt!'.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied source change in the core django/utils/html.py implementation; a proposed snippet or edits only to defaultfilters/tests cannot reach them.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes in django/utils/html.py, especially trim_punctuation(), that preserve the original middle prefix and transfer exactly the trailing punctuation suffix to trail.
metadata.oracle_test: The split for 'google.com/?q=1&lt!' is retained middle 'google.com/?q=1&lt' and trail '!'; the href is built from the decoded URL and contains q=1%3C. A sound boundary may use the decoded removed-character count to slice the end of the original middle or an equivalent mapping.

scale.1: No relevant implementation is visible, or the change targets an unrelated layer.
scale.2: A visible or proposed change addresses the block but violates entity preservation, punctuation placement, or the exact task output.
scale.3: A semantically plausible implementation is proposed or partially applied, but its boundary behavior is incomplete, special-cased, or not coherent enough to establish the exact retained prefix and suffix.
scale.4: An applied core change correctly preserves the original encoded prefix and moves exactly the decoded trailing-punctuation count for the task case, with no visible contradictory result.
scale.5: An applied core change implements the boundary generically for escaped and unescaped URL words, preserves display spelling and existing urlize flow, and is supported by coherent visible runtime or test evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Entity-preserving punctuation split in the core implementation

applies_when: A source edit or concrete implementation proposal concerns punctuation trimming inside the core urlize() implementation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements or precisely specifies a generic core boundary that determines trailing punctuation in the decoded representation while retaining the corresponding prefix from the original escaped source for displayed link text.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assigning the retained middle from middle_unescaped, indexing the escaped source directly with an absolute decoded index, special-casing '&lt!', duplicating entity letters, dropping punctuation, or producing a literal '<' or '<' instead of the required '&lt' caps credit at 2. A reverted edit cannot receive applied-work credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: A post-edit exact execution of the real urlize() implementation outranks source comments and hand calculations. The latest visible core source or diff determines whether work is applied; an explicit later restoration overrides an earlier temporary edit. A proposal is credited only when its complete boundary operation is visible.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents vague mismatch diagnoses, unescaped-coordinate slicing, and temporary or proposed edits from being treated as an applied representation-preserving repair.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires an explicit generic boundary operation equivalent to removing from the original middle exactly the number of trailing characters removed from its decoded form. Score 4 or 5 requires that operation to be visibly applied in django/utils/html.py and followed by an exact passing real-implementation run.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect django/utils/html.py changes or concrete proposals for trim_punctuation(), especially how the count or boundary of decoded trailing punctuation is mapped to a suffix of the original middle string.
metadata.oracle_test: For original middle 'google.com/?q=1&lt!', decoding yields a value ending '<!'; removing decoded trailing '!' must remove exactly the final original character, leaving original middle 'google.com/?q=1&lt' and trail '!', while href construction from the decoded middle yields q=1%3C.

scale.1: No task-causal core boundary change or complete proposal is visible; work remains at reproduction, unrelated layers, or materially altered literals.
scale.2: A core edit or proposal targets punctuation trimming but its boundary is incomplete, special-cased, or demonstrably corrupts the escaped display prefix, href, or trailing punctuation.
scale.3: A complete generic representation-safe boundary is visible and would remove the decoded trailing-suffix count from the end of the original middle, but it is not both applied in the core source and confirmed by an exact post-edit run.
scale.4: The representation-safe boundary is visibly applied in the core implementation and the literal task oracle passes, but focused controls for ordinary punctuation or other entity boundaries are absent or unresolved.
scale.5: The applied core boundary passes the exact oracle and focused controls demonstrate preserved behavior for ordinary trailing or wrapping punctuation and relevant complete or incomplete HTML-entity text without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Representation-safe punctuation boundary in core urlize()

applies_when: Visible execution, source evidence, or literal-string analysis conflicts with an earlier interpretation, proposed repair, or success claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Converges from contradictory evidence to a stable account of the escaped-source versus decoded-URL boundary, correcting the work when necessary and confirming the literal reported behavior when execution is available.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved latest claim that the oracle is wrong, a success claim paired with output containing 'lt!', a literal '<' or '<' in place of the required '<', or continued reliance on an altered input caps the score at 1. Earlier contradictions do not impose a permanent cap after a later authoritative exact pass.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest correctly formed execution of the real implementation outranks earlier simulations and reasoning. A later exact passing run may supersede earlier malformed experiments or failed edits unless still newer source or runtime evidence contradicts it. The task's literal input and expected output outrank speculative reinterpretations.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents both false recovery claims and the opposite error of ignoring a decisive later correction because the trajectory previously explored malformed literals.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires a stable final account that preserves the original '&lt' display lexeme, decodes it for the href, and moves only the final '!'. Score 4 or 5 additionally requires a post-correction execution of the real urlize() implementation on the literal reported input.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest coherent treatment of the literal '&lt!' input, any correction to the punctuation-boundary calculation, and subsequent execution of the real urlize() implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: For urlize('Search for google.com/?q=1<! and see.'), the href contains http://google.com/?q=1%3C, the linked display text ends exactly in google.com/?q=1<, and exactly ! follows .

scale.1: The latest usable evidence remains incompatible with the literal oracle, or the trajectory declares success while retaining an altered input, duplicated entity letters, decoded display text, or another unresolved contradiction.
scale.2: The exact defect is acknowledged or localized, but the latest reasoning still lacks a stable representation-preserving boundary or continues to conflict with visible source or runtime evidence.
scale.3: The trajectory finishes with a coherent correction that explicitly preserves the original escaped prefix while moving only decoded trailing punctuation, but no post-correction execution of the real implementation proves the exact oracle.
scale.4: After correcting the premise or implementation, a later real-implementation run on the literal input matches the exact href, display lexeme, and punctuation placement; broader reconciliation is limited.
scale.5: A later exact real-implementation run resolves the contradiction, and additional relevant source or regression evidence is reconciled without any newer conflicting result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Convergence after contradictory urlize evidence

applies_when: The task concerns urlize() processing of HTML entity text adjacent to trailing punctuation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work implements and validates a representation-aware punctuation boundary: URL recognition may use the unescaped value, while the displayed middle retains the corresponding original escaped lexeme and only genuine trailing punctuation is moved to the trail.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the visible post-edit reproducer still duplicates entity letters, places the exclamation mark inside the link, changes the displayed &lt lexeme into a literal less-than sign for the reported call, produces the wrong href, or if the production edit is visibly reverted. Cap at 4 if the exact reproducer passes but there is no relevant control or regression check for ordinary punctuation or entity preservation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed post-edit behavior and the visible production source take precedence over stated intent, hand calculations, or claims that a fix works. scale.2: No real FormSet class-sensitive assertion completes; evidence is limited to source inspection, list equality, isolated ErrorList construction, an empty or wrong-path fixture followed by a success claim, or a command that fails before the assertion.
scale.3: One real FormSet path completes and verifies the enclosing ErrorList classification, without a contradictory result, but only an empty result or a single lifecycle is covered.
scale.4: A real FormSet produces a nonempty nonform-classified result with exact rendering or equivalent metadata, and either a second lifecycle or a focused repository test also passes.
scale.5: Both initialized/management and caught-ValidationError replacement paths are class-sensitively verified, with nonempty exact rendering plus unchanged Form nonfield behavior and custom error_class compatibility.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed and contradiction-free nonform verification

applies_when: Production code has been edited.
The proposal changes FormSet error construction, validation state, getters, rendering methods, or ErrorList behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures collateral semantic damage independently of whether the nonform marker itself is present.

metadata.failure_mode: Deleted validation state, getter reconstruction, automatic FormSet error insertion, global mutation, or bypassed customization.
metadata.judge_focus: Preservation of self._errors, cached lifecycle, self.error_class, validation behavior, and rendering composition.
metadata.oracle_test: self._errors remains initialized; non_form_errors() and FormSet as_* methods remain unchanged; no global ErrorList or Form non-field behavior changes.

scale.1: No collateral state, API, rendering, or customization regression is visible.
scale.2: A localized unnecessary edit or concrete compatibility risk is visible without a demonstrated core behavior change.
scale.3: A substantive getter, cache, rendering, or customization deviation changes some established behavior.
scale.4: A core validation-state statement is removed, FormSet rendering composition is changed, or the customization boundary is clearly bypassed.
scale.5: The current implementation causes destructive validation behavior or broad framework-wide classification regressions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation-state and public-API preservation

applies_when: A production edit, patch, or implementation claim concerning BaseFormSet non-form errors is visible at the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the active production implementation validly applies the exact nonform marker through self.error_class at both BaseFormSet.full_clean() ErrorList construction sites.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Invalid Python argument ordering, a wrong token, direct ErrorList construction, getter reconstruction, post-construction mutation, or an actively unmarked required constructor caps the score at 2 for that attempted two-site implementation. A later visible repair removes the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct production-file excerpt or authoritative diff wins over edit commands, assistant summaries, source-string scripts, earlier excerpts, and runtime output from an uncertain source state. A successful edit command is applied-work evidence only when its resulting production text is subsequently visible.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding an issued edit, a malformed second call, or two approximate mechanisms more highly than one confirmed exact constructor.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require both syntactically valid exact calls to be visible in active production source. Score 5 additionally requires visible control-flow context establishing initialization before the unbound return and replacement in except ValidationError.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible django/forms/formsets.py content or authoritative cutoff diff for the initialization before the unbound return and the replacement inside except ValidationError. Distinguish source that was merely proposed or used in a stand-in script from source visibly applied to the production file.
metadata.oracle_test: The active method contains self._non_form_errors = self.error_class(error_class='nonform') before the unbound return and self._non_form_errors = self.error_class(e.error_list, error_class='nonform') inside except ValidationError as e.

scale.1: No production constructor is visibly changed, or the active change affects only an unrelated layer.
scale.2: A production change is proposed but not confirmed, or an active attempt is malformed or non-equivalent, such as invalid syntax, a wrong token, direct ErrorList construction, mutation, getter wrapping, or template-only classification.
scale.3: Exactly one required BaseFormSet.full_clean() constructor is visibly and validly changed to the exact self.error_class nonform call while the other remains absent or unconfirmed.
scale.4: Both syntactically valid exact self.error_class nonform calls are visible in active production source, but their required control-flow positions are not both visible.
scale.5: Both exact calls are visible in context: initialization precedes the unbound return and replacement occurs inside the caught-ValidationError path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and valid two-site nonform construction

applies_when: The trajectory contains source investigation, implementation reasoning, a failed edit, or a failed validation attempt relevant to FormSet non-form errors.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether visible reasoning correctly maps both non-form ErrorList state transitions and accurately diagnoses whether observed failures came from production code, fixtures, rendering observation, or the execution environment.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A retained getter reconstruction, invalid constructor syntax, wrong token, or unsupported declaration of success after the intended path visibly failed caps the score at 2. A visibly repaired mistake with a corrected rerun does not retain the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete source excerpts and executed diagnostic output outrank assistant assertions. A visible error traceback or empty result determines whether the intended path ran; later corrected and rerun evidence supersedes an earlier mistake.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating workflow activity with understanding, requiring an edit before crediting a complete safe diagnosis, or accepting success prose that conflicts with the visible assertion path.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require both construction sites to be identified or an equivalent precise account of the initialization/append and caught-ValidationError replacement lifecycles. Score 5 requires accurate handling of all visible failures without an unresolved conflicting edit or success claim.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for concrete recognition that management errors append to the initially classified list while min/max and custom-clean ValidationErrors replace it, that the class belongs to the enclosing ErrorList, and that custom-clean fixtures must be bound with valid prefixed management and form data.
metadata.oracle_test: The trajectory explains that full_clean() first creates self.error_class(error_class='nonform'), management errors append to it, and caught ValidationErrors replace it with self.error_class(e.error_list, error_class='nonform'), while distinguishing fixture and environment failures from product failures.

scale.1: The reasoning remains directed at the wrong API or layer, or retains destructive source damage without recognizing it.
scale.2: A material lifecycle misunderstanding, malformed implementation, or unsupported success conclusion remains unresolved despite visible contradictory evidence.
scale.3: One lifecycle is understood correctly, or both sites are noticed but append-versus-replace behavior, enclosing-list evidence, or a visible failure cause remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: Both lifecycle sites and the relevant failure causes are correctly identified, with any fixture or environment mistake isolated or repaired and no conflicting production proposal retained.
scale.5: The trajectory precisely explains initialization/append versus ValidationError replacement, preserves self.error_class and cached validation behavior, and consistently validates or diagnoses every visible assertion without overclaiming.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actionable lifecycle understanding and calibrated diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory is implementing disabled-field value selection in BaseForm._clean_fields().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether active production source cleans disabled fields from the form-cached, widget-normalized BoundField.initial rather than independently evaluating or preparing an initial value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Calling get_initial_for_field() for the disabled value, using bf.value(), constructing uncached BoundField objects, reading an empty cache directly, using a nonexistent iterator/helper, returning bf.initial without field.clean(), or damaging BoundField.initial caps the score at 2. A definite syntax or runtime failure on the cleaning path also caps it at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active workspace or final source diff controls implementation credit. A plan, assistant-authored claim, inspected baseline source, temporary method, scratch script, or reverted edit is not an implementation. Executed tests may corroborate the source but cannot rescue a contradictory active path.
metadata.failure_mode: The former rubric gave scores of 3 or 4 for recognition, plans, malformed integrations, and no-edit workspaces even though the active disabled branch still bypassed the cached BoundField initial.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a reachable active disabled branch that obtains a cached BoundField and passes bf.initial to field.clean(). A score above 3 requires valid all-field iteration and no independent get_initial_for_field() or bf.value() path for disabled cleaning.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff _clean_fields() path and the bound-field acquisition it uses. Each disabled field must be obtained through self[name] or a valid ordered helper that calls self[name], select value = bf.initial, and pass that value to field.clean(). Confirm BoundField.initial remains cached and retains the widget supports_microseconds normalization.
metadata.oracle_test: Source must make a disabled DateTimeField's cleaned value derive from the same cached form['dt'].initial whose callable is evaluated once and whose unsupported microseconds are removed.

scale.1: No active production edit repairs disabled cleaning, or the active source still plainly uses the independent initial lookup with no reachable replacement.
scale.2: An active attempt references BoundField but uses bf.value(), an uncached or invalid accessor, broken iteration, or bypasses field.clean(), so the required path cannot operate.
scale.3: A reachable active branch selects bf.initial and calls field.clean(), but caching provenance, all-field iteration, or preservation of BoundField.initial normalization remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: Active source validly obtains cached bound fields through self[name], cleans disabled fields from bf.initial, and leaves cached callable evaluation and widget microsecond normalization intact.
scale.5: Meets score 4 with a complete, internally consistent active source path whose helper definitions, iteration, imports, and surrounding cleaning flow are all visibly valid and free of contradictory disabled-value access.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active cached BoundField initial for disabled cleaning

applies_when: The prefix edits or reasons about BaseForm.changed_data or a new BoundField change method.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether per-field changed-data logic is correctly encapsulated on BoundField while preserving ordinary initial/data comparison and hidden-initial conversion behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Logic remains duplicated in BaseForm, ignores prefixes, omits to_python(), or mishandles ValidationError.
metadata.judge_focus: Delegation architecture and compatibility of show_hidden_initial.
metadata.oracle_test: Equal ordinary or hidden initial data is unchanged; unequal data is changed; malformed hidden initial conversion returns changed rather than raising.

scale.1: Change detection is absent, broken, or materially loses established semantics.
scale.2: A BoundField method exists but omits major behavior such as show_hidden_initial or ValidationError handling.
scale.3: Most logic is moved correctly but evidence or one compatibility detail is incomplete.
scale.4: The method and BaseForm delegation preserve all visible branches with internally consistent naming.
scale.5: Complete implementation plus focused evidence for equal, unequal, hidden, and malformed-hidden cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: BoundField change-detection preservation

applies_when: The trajectory is performing focused semantic validation of the disabled callable-initial behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures executed, observed evidence for the ticket-specific disabled DateTimeField invariant, distinguishing a useful baseline reproduction from a successful check of the active edited implementation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Import, dependency, settings, syntax, or setup failure before form validation remains score 1. A post-edit run that fails before the relevant assertion cannot exceed 2. A reached assertion showing multiple callable evaluations, retained unsupported microseconds, cleaned_data unequal to bf.initial, or a validation exception caps the score at 3 even if other assertions pass.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from an actually executed command is authoritative. A written but unexecuted script, proposed command, source inspection, assistant-authored prediction, generic test, or command that failed during import, dependency loading, settings setup, or before the relevant assertion is not successful behavioral evidence. Post-edit output outranks pre-edit or baseline output.
metadata.failure_mode: The previous anchors credited source reasoning and generic examples as focused evidence and did not require the judge to establish execution timing, assertion reachability, or whether setup failures occurred before the behavior under test.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires an executed command that reaches some relevant form behavior. A score above 2 requires a disabled callable datetime-style case that reaches validation or a baseline reproduction that directly observes the ticket mismatch. A score above 3 requires execution against the active edited production source and observation of at least one successful ticket invariant.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify commands that were actually executed and their observed output. Determine whether the run used a bound form, reached full_clean(), is_valid(), or equivalent field validation, used a disabled datetime-style field with a callable initial containing unsupported microseconds, and asserted callable count, normalized bf.initial, cleaned_data equality, and absence of validation errors. Record whether the run occurred before or after the active production edit.
metadata.oracle_test: Execute a bound form with a disabled DateTimeField whose stateful callable returns a value with microseconds unsupported by its widget; validation should finish without errors, invoke the callable once, produce microsecond zero, and satisfy form.cleaned_data['dt'] == form['dt'].initial.

scale.1: No task-relevant command was executed, only source or a script was displayed, or every attempted run failed before reaching relevant form behavior.
scale.2: An executed generic form, changed_data, constant-initial, or rendering check reaches Django behavior but does not exercise the disabled callable datetime mismatch; a focused post-edit attempt that fails before its decisive assertion also belongs here.
scale.3: An executed disabled callable datetime-style baseline directly demonstrates the old normalized-BoundField versus cleaned-data mismatch, or a focused active-source run reaches validation but proves only diagnosis or one partial invariant while leaving the fix unconfirmed.
scale.4: An executed post-edit bound-form check reaches validation and observes normalized cleaned_data equal to bf.initial or a single callable invocation, with no visible contradictory result, but does not establish every oracle condition.
scale.5: An executed post-edit regression reaches all relevant assertions and visibly proves one callable invocation, removal of unsupported microseconds, cleaned_data equal to the cached BoundField initial, and no validation error.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed disabled callable-initial regression evidence

applies_when: The trajectory has an active source modification, cutoff diff, tracked auxiliary file, or submitted patch artifact.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the implementation and task-related files actually present at the cutoff form a syntactically coherent, internally consistent, localized, and usable patch. This criterion concerns integrity of the current source or submitted artifact, not whether the chosen behavior solves the task.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible syntax error, undefined attribute on an ordinary execution path, malformed or duplicated function body, or terminal artifact omitting the functional source caps the score at 1. Retained tracked backup modules or task-unrelated scratch settings and reproductions cap the score at 3 even when functional source is coherent.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest inspectable cutoff source and git diff take precedence over editing-script messages and earlier file views. For a terminal submission, the submitted patch is authoritative; a script that was merely written, an edit that was reverted, and an untracked temporary file absent from the submitted artifact are not current-source evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring intended or reverted edits instead of current source, treating mere incompleteness as corruption, overlooking present malformed code, or rewarding a clean-looking artifact that omits the functional implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an inspectable active implementation or submitted patch whose changed Python ranges are structurally coherent; an empty or unavailable active diff cannot receive credit for patch integrity merely because intended edits were discussed.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff workspace diff or submitted patch for malformed indentation, duplicate parameters or dictionary entries, undefined attributes, duplicated code, conflict markers, missing functional hunks, and retained backup or scratch files. Do not infer defects from nonterminal status, an earlier failed script, or source that was subsequently restored.
metadata.oracle_test: The active changes compile, pass diff-format checks, contain each new parameter and forwarding key once, include the intended django/forms/models.py implementation, and exclude backup modules and ad hoc repository-root artifacts.

scale.1: The authoritative current source or submitted artifact is unusable: it is syntactically malformed, contains execution-blocking undefined or duplicated code, is unappliable, or omits the functional source after claiming submission.
scale.2: An active implementation is inspectable but has a concrete serious integrity defect or uncertain partially applied rewrite that prevents reliable execution or interpretation.
scale.3: The active functional source is structurally coherent, but tracked backup or scratch artifacts, duplicated non-executing material, or unresolved artifact completeness issues remain.
scale.4: The active patch is coherent, localized, and free of material repository pollution, with no visible syntax or structural defect.
scale.5: The complete task-focused patch is coherent and localized, static checks or equivalent compile evidence succeed, the artifact is applicable, and repository status contains only intentional deliverables.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active cutoff source and artifact integrity

applies_when: The prefix changes validation, management-form handling, queryset resolution, deletion, default creation, or commit behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates preservation of valid crafted submissions, queryset isolation, default creation, deletions, and commit=False/save_m2m behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Extra forms are rejected solely by policy, management hints are trusted, excluded objects are changed, or legacy save behavior regresses.
metadata.judge_focus: Edit-only is a persistence policy, not client-trusted access control or a new validation rejection.
metadata.oracle_test: Crafted extra data remains valid, excluded primary keys remain untouched, default creation works, and commit=False bookkeeping remains available.

scale.1: The visible approach conflicts with required behavior or provides no compatible handling beyond a generic count, rendering, or management-form restriction.
scale.2: Some compatibility behavior is visibly preserved or correctly reasoned about, but important validation, isolation, or regression behavior remains unaddressed.
scale.3: The implementation appears compatible with validation and existing-object handling, with incomplete isolation or regression evidence.
scale.4: Required compatibility and isolation behavior is clearly implemented or directly established by focused checks.
scale.5: Database-backed tests visibly confirm valid crafted submissions, queryset isolation, inline behavior, default creation, deletion, and commit=False/save_m2m compatibility.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Behavioral compatibility and isolation

applies_when: The prefix runs or prepares tests, reproductions, imports, rendering checks, or database assertions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether visible evidence actually exercises a freshly bound model formset and persistence rather than only construction, counts, rendering, environment setup, or mutated cached state.

metadata.failure_mode: Only form counts are checked, data is assigned after construction, no table exists, imports fail, or save is never called.
metadata.judge_focus: Evidence must match request binding and database save behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Construct with data=..., assert validity, call save(), and compare database state using the modified checkout.

scale.1: No valid behavioral evidence is visible, or the evidence relies on a broken environment, post-construction data mutation, rendering, or counts alone.
scale.2: A relevant reproduction partly executes or establishes a limited observable fact, but it does not establish database persistence behavior.
scale.3: A valid freshly bound reproduction exercises save behavior but omits one or more discriminative scenarios.
scale.4: Focused database-backed checks cover creation suppression and preservation of an existing update using the modified checkout.
scale.5: Focused checks additionally cover inline behavior, queryset isolation, default creation, deletion, and commit=False/save_m2m.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validity of behavioral evidence

applies_when: AutocompleteJsonView source, a focused diff, or direct inspection of the response path is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether AutocompleteJsonView defines serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name) and whether get() dynamically dispatches every emitted object through that method using self.

metadata.failure_mode: The hook is absent, incompatible, outside the class, or bypassed by get().
metadata.judge_focus: Both the compatible method definition and its active per-object call site.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect get() and serialize_result() together; use a subclass response only if dispatch remains uncertain.

scale.1: Neither a usable hook nor active dispatch is visible.
scale.2: Only one required half is effective, or the signature or call is incompatible.
scale.3: Both pieces are suggested, but active class placement or response dispatch remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: The compatible instance method and active per-object dispatch are both visible.
scale.5: The complete extension point is cleanly visible and ordinary subclass overriding with super() is directly supported.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete per-object serializer dispatch

applies_when: A current AutocompleteJsonView implementation, focused production diff, or evaluator-facing representation of that implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether AutocompleteJsonView provides a usable class-level serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name) extension point and reaches dynamic dispatch through it once for every emitted result on the ordinary valid response path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when authoritative source is syntactically or structurally unusable, or when an active surrounding edit necessarily raises before result emission, bypasses the hook, or corrupts required lifecycle methods. Cap at 2 when exactly one half of the hook-and-dispatch contract is usable or their signatures disagree. Unrelated behavior-preserving formatting does not cap credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest coherent current production source or current evaluator-facing diff wins over plans, edit commands, scratch files, synthetic demonstrations, earlier malformed versions, and isolated direct serializer calls. A later visible restoration removes earlier defects.
metadata.failure_mode: Judging textual presence as a completed feature even though the hook is inert, incompatible, outside the class, or unreachable because the active response path is broken.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires both a compatible class-level serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name) and active self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) dispatch for every emitted object. A score of 5 additionally requires no visible active contradiction that necessarily prevents the ordinary valid response path from reaching or emitting those calls.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the authoritative get() and serialize_result() together, including only surrounding active code needed to determine whether a valid request can reach the per-object calls. Confirm class scope, compatible arguments, dispatch through self, and iteration over context['object_list'].
metadata.oracle_test: For a valid autocomplete request, get() must retain the resolved local to_field_name and emit each object from context['object_list'] through self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name); the default method must remain ordinarily overridable at class scope.
metadata.stage: Implement and verify the per-result extension point

scale.1: No operational extension seam exists: both required pieces are absent, the authoritative class is structurally invalid, or an active contradiction necessarily prevents a valid request from reaching and emitting serializer results.
scale.2: Only one required piece is usable, or the method placement, signature, call arguments, dispatch mechanism, or per-object target is incompatible.
scale.3: Both pieces are visible, but the authoritative current state or reachability of the response dispatch remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: The compatible hook and per-object dispatch are active and reachable, but a specific minor ambiguity remains about coverage of every emitted object.
scale.5: The authoritative implementation unambiguously defines the compatible class-level hook and reaches self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) for every emitted object on the unchanged valid response path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operational serializer hook and per-object dispatch

applies_when: The trajectory has reached final review, patch preparation, or an explicit submission state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the cutoff exposes a current, coherent evaluator-facing unified diff for the intended production change, distinct from merely having correct workspace source.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later raw-source, empty, missing-file, stale, malformed, or non-patch submission overrides an earlier valid preview. A previously defective attempt ceases to cap the score only when a newer current unified diff is visibly emitted.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final terminal payload or latest visibly displayed current unified diff wins over earlier previews. When no terminal payload exists, the latest displayed diff generated after the last source edit may establish partial readiness but not terminal delivery. Workspace source alone cannot establish patch form.
metadata.failure_mode: No patch is displayed at final review, the attempted payload is empty or raw source, the diff is stale or malformed, or it disagrees with the latest production state.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 5 requires a visibly emitted current unified diff in the evaluator-facing submission state. A score above 3 requires an actual displayed unified diff generated from the current source, not merely a claim that patch.txt exists.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest actual patch-generation or submission output. Confirm unified-diff headers, the intended file path, applicable hunks, and agreement with the latest tracked source. A command that was only proposed, a patch file that was only written but never displayed, raw module text, or an earlier patch superseded by later edits is not a ready artifact.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the latest displayed or submitted patch with the current django/contrib/admin/views/autocomplete.py diff and confirm standard diff headers and current hunks.

scale.1: An explicit final submission emits no usable patch, emits raw source, references a missing file, or presents a malformed or stale artifact.
scale.2: Only workspace source or an undisplayed claim that a patch exists is available after patch preparation; evaluator-facing patch form is not established.
scale.3: A patch-like representation is visible, but its headers, completeness, freshness, or agreement with the latest source remains materially ambiguous.
scale.4: A coherent current unified diff is visibly displayed and matches the source, but terminal delivery is absent or only minor presentation uncertainty remains.
scale.5: The final evaluator-facing payload visibly contains a coherent, current, applicable unified diff matching the latest intended production change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing patch readiness

applies_when: The effective production source or its focused diff exposes surrounding lifecycle code.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes active changes to authorization, request validation, queryset behavior, filtering, ordering, distinct handling, exceptions, context construction, or pagination.

metadata.judge_focus: Defects remaining in the effective production state.

scale.2: A minor unnecessary active edit remains but is visibly behavior-preserving.
scale.3: Broader restructuring creates concrete unresolved compatibility risk.
scale.4: A visible regression affects request handling, queryset behavior, exceptions, context, or pagination.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Visible source-to-submission inconsistency
