reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate completed post-edit checks of established timesince() and timeuntil() behavior outside the exact reported regression case.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A relevant failure from the supported repository runner caps the score at 2 unless the same invocation visibly fails on the unmodified baseline. A completed focused manual assertion failure caps at 3 unless it is visibly an incorrect expectation or setup artifact. Pre-assertion failures do not establish a regression.
metadata.evidence_authority: A correctly labeled tests/runtests.py execution with normal setup outranks focused manual checks. Completed focused direct calls are valid limited evidence. Direct TestCase invocation without normal setUp is provisional, and a same-command unmodified-baseline comparison overrides an unsupported isolated failure.
metadata.failure_mode: No non-target compatibility behavior executes, an applicable completed check fails, or setup and lifecycle failures are treated as semantic compatibility results.
metadata.hard_gate: At least one compatibility behavior distinct from the exact reported aware 31-day case must execute to a returned value or assertion before scores 4 or 5 are possible.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands that actually reach assertions or observable returned values for naive inputs, timeuntil or reversed behavior, differing aware timezones, date inputs, calendar boundaries, depth, formatting, ignored microseconds, or custom tzinfo objects. Merely writing a script, inspecting tests, testing only the exact 31-day case, or failing during imports, settings, discovery, database setup, or fixture setup is non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The existing timesince suite and focused checks preserve naive and date inputs, timeuntil/reversed behavior, differing zones, month and leap boundaries, depth, formatting, custom naive-like tzinfo objects, and ignored microseconds.
metadata.stage: Validate the discriminative behavior and compatibility

scale.1: A supported execution demonstrates a severe patch-attributable regression in a core established compatibility path.
scale.2: A supported execution reaches and fails a relevant compatibility assertion without an equivalent baseline failure.
scale.3: No applicable compatibility check completes, or only provisional unsupported failures, setup failures, test inspection, or conflicting limited checks are visible.
scale.4: One or more focused non-target compatibility checks complete successfully with no authoritative relevant failure, but supported suite coverage is absent or limited.
scale.5: The supported repository runner completes the relevant timesince compatibility suite successfully across multiple established paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed non-target compatibility coverage

applies_when: The production implementation changes pivot construction or timezone handling.
Concrete source semantics or supported compatibility executions are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate preservation of naive datetimes, tzinfo objects whose utcoffset() returns None, differing aware timezones, timeuntil(), date inputs, month and leap-year boundaries, depth, formatting, and ignored microseconds.

metadata.failure_mode: The change visibly breaks an established path or introduces broader timezone normalization or changed pivot fields.
metadata.judge_focus: Use effective source and correctly configured executions; do not convert setup artifacts into regressions.
metadata.oracle_test: Supported timesince tests and focused checks preserve established outputs across naive, aware, reversed, calendar-boundary, date, depth, and custom-tzinfo cases.
metadata.stage: Implement the focused production correction / Validate the discriminative behavior and compatibility

scale.1: The implementation fundamentally breaks an established path, or a correctly configured compatibility test shows a severe regression.
scale.2: A concrete source defect or supported execution shows an important compatibility regression such as broken reversed or differing-timezone behavior.
scale.3: Compatibility remains materially uncertain because the implementation broadens semantics or only provisional conflicting evidence exists.
scale.4: The source is focused and representative visible evidence shows no regression, though supported coverage is limited.
scale.5: The source semantics are exact and supported tests cover the important established compatibility paths without failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Established compatibility preservation

applies_when: Repository-wide status, a cutoff repository diff, or task-local files inside the checkout are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the observable cutoff repository contains only the intended production change and an optional focused repository regression test.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any task-local helper or generated file visibly remaining at cutoff prevents scores 4 and 5; numerous such files cap at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest repository-wide cutoff status and diff win. A path-limited production diff, terminal patch payload, workspace summary, cleanup intention, or prose claim cannot prove that repository-root files are absent.
metadata.failure_mode: Scratch scripts, custom settings, summaries, patch.txt, dependency artifacts, or unrelated changes remain, or cleanliness is inferred solely from a focused diff.
metadata.hard_gate: Repository-wide evidence after the last repository-local file creation or cleanup is required for score 5.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect repository-wide git status and cutoff diff for tracked and untracked helpers, settings files, summaries, generated patches, installation artifacts, and unrelated edits. Files under /tmp are outside this criterion.
metadata.oracle_test: After cleanup, repository-wide status and diff contain only django/utils/timesince.py and, if intentionally added, a focused test in the repository's existing test suite.
metadata.stage: Review and submit a clean artifact

scale.1: Numerous task-local, generated, or unrelated files visibly remain in the cutoff repository.
scale.2: One or a small number of definite scratch or generated files remain alongside the intended change.
scale.3: Repository cleanliness is unproven because only path-limited or stale evidence is visible and no remaining noise is definitively established.
scale.4: Current repository-wide evidence shows only intended source or focused test changes, but either status or complete diff coverage is incomplete.
scale.5: Post-cleanup repository-wide status and diff, captured after the last file operation, visibly contain only the intended production change and any focused in-suite regression test.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff repository artifact set

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates Django CommandParser subparser construction or missing-argument error behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory uses direct evidence to identify that argparse already constructs subparsers with the configured parser class but does not automatically pass the parent CommandParser's task-relevant error-handling context into each subparser constructor.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory continues to attribute the bug solely to formatter_class or solely to subparsers being plain ArgumentParser instances after visible evidence disproves that account. Cap at 3 if its proposed propagation route visibly sends unsupported keywords to _SubParsersAction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed parser types, attribute values, tracebacks, and inspected argparse call paths outrank narrative claims. A focused reproduction of the reported missing-subparser-argument path outranks unrelated parser experiments.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding lengthy argparse exploration that notices the symptom but confuses parser-class inheritance, help formatting, and propagation of CommandParser initialization state.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible evidence that the subparser is already a CommandParser and that the failure is missing constructor context at subparser creation, not merely use of the wrong parser class.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect reproductions, constructor-argument traces, subparser attribute inspection, and argparse source inspection that distinguish parser-class inheritance from propagation of called_from_command_line and other relevant CommandParser constructor state.
metadata.non_evidence: Restating the issue, observing only that a CommandError occurred, inspecting formatter output alone, or asserting that a patch should work without tracing the child parser's construction does not establish the causal boundary.
metadata.oracle_test: For a command-line-created parent CommandParser, a child made through add_subparsers().add_parser() must preserve the error-mode context needed for a missing child positional to produce argparse usage and an error without a CommandError traceback; programmatic parsing must retain Django's non-SystemExit behavior.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis is established, or the visible account is contradicted by the trajectory's own observations.
scale.2: The symptom is understood, but the trajectory pursues an incorrect or materially incomplete cause such as formatter-only inheritance or the child being a plain ArgumentParser.
scale.3: The trajectory observes missing child-parser state or the relevant argparse creation path, but does not yet connect both facts reliably or still proposes a visibly invalid propagation route.
scale.4: Focused evidence correctly establishes that the child is a CommandParser whose relevant constructor context was not propagated through subparser creation, but the exact safe injection mechanism or semantic boundary remains incomplete.
scale.5: Controlled evidence establishes the full causal chain and a locally viable propagation boundary while preserving explicit parser-class behavior and the distinction between command-line and programmatic parsing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of CommandParser subparser context loss

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a required argument on a management-command subparser raises CommandError or produces a traceback instead of argparse CLI output.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that argparse already constructs the child as the parent parser type, but constructs it without Django's command-line context, leaving the child CommandParser.called_from_command_line unset and causing CommandParser.error() to raise CommandError.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory continues to identify formatter_class or the child parser's class alone as the root cause after visible evidence shows the child is a CommandParser with called_from_command_line unset. Cap at 1 if it denies or ignores a directly observed reproduction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed child attributes and an error-path traceback or runtime result outweigh speculation about argparse behavior; Django and argparse source shown in the trajectory outrank unsupported assumptions.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding plausible but false diagnoses that argparse selects the wrong parser class or that help-format ordering controls the traceback.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognizing that the child is already normally a CommandParser because argparse defaults parser_class to type(self), rather than merely asserting that it is a plain ArgumentParser.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or runtime evidence showing the parent and child parser types, constructor kwargs or child attributes, and the resulting branch in CommandParser.error().
metadata.oracle_test: For a parent CommandParser created with called_from_command_line=True, add_subparsers().add_parser('create') currently yields a CommandParser whose called_from_command_line is None; a missing required child argument therefore reaches the CommandError branch.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by visible source/runtime evidence.
scale.2: Recognizes that subparser creation is involved but attributes the failure mainly to the wrong parser class, formatter_class, or unrelated management-dispatch behavior.
scale.3: Connects missing child configuration to CommandParser.error(), but does not clearly establish that called_from_command_line is the decisive lost value or that the child is already a CommandParser.
scale.4: Correctly establishes that the child is a CommandParser constructed without the parent's called_from_command_line value and links this to CommandError versus argparse CLI handling.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain with decisive source/runtime evidence, distinguishes relevant constructor context from unrelated formatting settings, and reconciles any earlier contrary hypothesis.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of lost subparser CLI context

applies_when: The visible trajectory attempts or validates a code change for Django management-command subparser error handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether a repository-applied, locally scoped change propagates the relevant CommandParser error context into constructed subparsers and is validated against the reported CLI behavior without breaking programmatic parsing or argparse extension points.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest applied code has a syntax/import error, passes unsupported keywords to _SubParsersAction, recursively rebinds add_parser incorrectly, or globally mutates argparse behavior without isolation. Cap at 3 when tests still show missing child context or a CommandError traceback on the CLI path.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible repository readback and test output outrank plans, claimed success, scratch-only prototypes, and earlier passing experiments against code that was later replaced. End-to-end command execution outranks direct manual calls to error().
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents proposed work, scratch monkey patches, attribute-only assertions, and false success declarations from receiving the same credit as an applied and behaviorally verified fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires an applied syntactically valid repository change plus direct evidence that a child parser receives the intended context. Score 5 additionally requires behavioral validation of the reported missing child argument and no visible unresolved contradiction.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual repository code or readback after editing, syntax or import checks, child-parser state, the missing-child-argument path, emitted usage and error text, absence of a traceback, and any programmatic CommandError check.
metadata.non_evidence: Installing dependencies, compiling unrelated code, testing only the missing top-level subcommand, checking only that the child class is CommandParser, or printing an expected message without exercising parsing does not verify the fix.
metadata.oracle_test: Running a management command with a selected subcommand but an omitted required child argument must print that child's usage and a human-facing argparse error, then exit normally for a CLI parse rather than exposing a CommandError traceback. A programmatic parse must continue to raise CommandError rather than unconditionally exiting.

scale.1: No relevant repository implementation exists at the cutoff, or the latest implementation is corrupt, unrelated, or based on a contradicted formatter-only mechanism.
scale.2: A relevant change is applied or prototyped, but it visibly fails construction, syntax, import, or the reported parsing path and no working replacement is demonstrated.
scale.3: The implementation is plausible and syntactically usable, but child context remains unverified, a focused test still fails, or only scratch-level evidence supports it.
scale.4: A locally scoped applied implementation visibly propagates the intended child-parser context and passes focused structural or parsing checks, but end-to-end CLI behavior or programmatic compatibility is not both established.
scale.5: The applied implementation is directly validated on the reported missing-child-argument CLI path with usage and no traceback, preserves programmatic CommandError semantics, and has no visible unresolved regression or integrity failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implemented subparser error-context propagation and behavioral verification

applies_when: The trajectory executes or attempts to execute parsing after selecting a management-command subparser whose own required argument is omitted.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures cutoff-visible runtime evidence that the selected child parser, under the latest relevant implementation, emits its usage and required-argument error through argparse termination instead of exposing CommandError or a traceback.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest target execution reaches the selected child but raises CommandError or prints a traceback. Assign 1 when execution never reaches parsing because of setup, import, syntax, or construction failure. A failure against a visibly replaced implementation does not cap newer code, but indirect checks of the newer code cannot by themselves establish corrected runtime behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: A management-command CLI or run_from_argv execution against the latest code is strongest, followed by a direct parse_args execution using an equivalent CommandParser tree. Actual stderr, exception type, and exit status outrank PASS labels, expected-output prints, child attributes, and manual calls to error().
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents invalid setup, baseline reproduction, wrong argv, attribute inspection, manual error invocation, and stale executions from tying with direct behavioral proof against the current implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a parse against the latest relevant implementation with the child selected and its required argument omitted, visibly ending through argparse rather than CommandError. Credit at 5 additionally requires a management-command CLI-equivalent execution with child-specific output and status 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Check the exact argv, confirmation that the named child was selected, whether execution used the latest relevant code, the usage prefix, required-child-argument text, observed exception or exit status, and presence or absence of CommandError and traceback output.
metadata.oracle_test: For input equivalent to manage.py cheeses create when create requires name, stderr contains the create child usage and 'the following arguments are required: name', termination has argparse status 2, and no uncaught CommandError traceback appears.

scale.1: No selected-child missing-argument parse is executed, or the attempt fails before parsing because of invalid setup, import, syntax, or parser construction.
scale.2: A valid target-path baseline or latest-code execution selects the child but still raises CommandError, prints a traceback, or otherwise demonstrates the regression.
scale.3: A newer implementation has only indirect runtime support such as verified child context or error-branch state, or target parsing output is incomplete or ambiguous; corrected argparse termination is not directly observed.
scale.4: A direct parse against the latest code selects the child, emits child-specific usage and the missing required argument message, and visibly terminates with argparse-style SystemExit rather than CommandError.
scale.5: A management-command CLI or run_from_argv execution against the latest code proves child-specific usage and error text, exit status 2, and absence of an uncaught CommandError traceback, with any additional parent-path evidence consistent.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Runtime proof of corrected missing-child-argument handling

applies_when: The trajectory considers caller-supplied parser_class values, CommandParser subclasses, nested subparsers, or programmatic management-command parsing in addition to the primary CLI case.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves argparse customization and Django's non-CLI semantics while propagating command-line context only to compatible CommandParser children.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the implementation unconditionally replaces an explicit parser_class, assumes every parser class is a CommandParser, or converts programmatic parse errors into SystemExit. Cap at 3 if primary behavior works but compatibility is only asserted.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed construction and exception behavior outweigh generalized compatibility claims; explicit parser_class behavior takes precedence over assumptions about defaults.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrow CLI fix that breaks documented argparse extension points or Django's deliberate distinction between command-line and programmatic calls.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence that a caller-supplied non-CommandParser parser_class is not forced to accept Django-only constructor keywords, or an implementation whose guarded logic makes this unambiguous.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible implementation branches or tests for an explicit non-CommandParser parser_class, a CommandParser subclass, caller-provided child kwargs, nested subparsers, and called_from_command_line=False or None.
metadata.oracle_test: Default and CommandParser-subclass children inherit called_from_command_line; an explicitly supplied unrelated ArgumentParser-compatible class remains usable; with called_from_command_line false, Django's programmatic CommandError behavior remains intact.

scale.1: Compatibility is ignored and the visible design plainly breaks parser customization or programmatic behavior.
scale.2: The primary case is addressed by forcibly replacing parser classes or globally changing error behavior, with a concrete compatibility hazard.
scale.3: The implementation appears compatible but provides no guarded handling or evidence for explicit parser classes and non-CLI calls.
scale.4: Visible guarded logic or focused checks preserve explicit parser-class and programmatic behavior while fixing the default child path.
scale.5: Comprehensive evidence covers unrelated parser classes, CommandParser subclasses or nesting, caller overrides, and both CLI and programmatic error semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility with parser-class overrides and programmatic invocation

applies_when: A source change or concrete source-change proposal for floatformat() is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the floatformat() implementation at the narrow precision or whole-number boundary so zero-decimal formatting cannot construct an invalid Decimal context while preserving established formatting behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible implementation that returns every integral value without honoring p>0, produces invalid precision for another Decimal shape, or has syntax/indentation damage is capped at 2; a focused test failure caused by the current implementation caps at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible current diff and runtime behavior outrank prose describing an intended fix; later corrected code outranks abandoned earlier candidates.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating any suppression of the reported exception as correct, especially broad early returns such as `if not m:` that discard requested trailing decimal places.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a coherent implementation that makes both reported calls return '0' and does not route all integral values away from positive requested decimal places.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible final/current diff or exact proposed edit in django/template/defaultfilters.py, including its behavior for p=0, positive p, negative p, fractional values, and large-exponent Decimals.
metadata.oracle_test: floatformat('0.00', 0) and floatformat(Decimal('0.00'), 0) return '0'; floatformat(6.0, 3) remains '6.000'; floatformat(7.7, 0) remains '8'; default/negative precision behavior and large scientific-notation inputs remain valid.

scale.1: No concrete implementation, or the visible implementation is malformed or unrelated.
scale.2: A change targets the relevant code but is overbroad, internally inconsistent, or visibly breaks established floatformat behavior.
scale.3: A plausible narrow fix is visible and handles the reported case, but compatibility across positive precision, fractional rounding, or unusual Decimal exponents is not established.
scale.4: A coherent minimal fix is visible at the appropriate precision/whole-number boundary and available evidence supports both the reported behavior and ordinary positive/negative precision semantics.
scale.5: The visible implementation is minimal and causally aligned, handles the reported string and Decimal cases, and is supported against high-risk compatibility cases including positive trailing-zero formatting and large or unusual Decimal exponents.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically bounded floatformat implementation

applies_when: The trajectory discusses or changes tests for floatformat().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds or precisely specifies repository regression assertions covering both reported input representations and their expected output.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Tests that merely assert no exception, expect the wrong representation, or replace/relax existing compatibility assertions are capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible test diff takes precedence over statements that tests were added; exact assertions take precedence over vague plans for edge-case coverage.
metadata.failure_mode: Giving full credit to ad hoc shell scripts while the repository receives no durable regression test for one or both reported forms.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit assertions for both floatformat('0.00', 0) and floatformat(Decimal('0.00'), 0), expecting '0' without exception.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes or exact proposed assertions in tests/template_tests/filter_tests/test_floatformat.py, including string and Decimal inputs, argument 0, and expected value '0'.
metadata.oracle_test: The permanent regression test must fail on the original implementation because Context receives prec=0 and pass when each reported call returns the string '0'.

scale.1: No repository regression test or concrete test assertion is visible.
scale.2: A test location or general zero-value case is proposed, but the reported precision-zero behavior is not asserted exactly.
scale.3: An exact assertion is visible for only one of the string or Decimal forms, or both are described without a visible test change.
scale.4: A visible repository test change asserts both reported calls return '0' without weakening existing tests.
scale.5: The visible test change covers both reported forms in the established floatformat test module and is cleanly integrated with nearby zero/precision behavior so the original defect is specifically guarded.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Permanent regression coverage for zero-valued inputs at precision zero

applies_when: The rollout addresses the floatformat failure for zero-valued Decimal representations at zero output precision.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible applied implementation prevents invalid Decimal context precision for the reported zero case while preserving floatformat rounding, requested decimal places, and handling of Decimal exponents.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest applied change visibly causes a supported regression, including dropping requested positive decimal places, forcing context precision to one for arbitrary zero-place rounding, or under-allocating precision for positive-exponent or multi-digit values. Cap at 3 if the applied state is unresolved, internally inconsistent, or contradicted by a relevant execution. Dependency, settings, or test-runner setup failures alone are not semantic contradictions.
metadata.evidence_authority: The most recent visible file inspection or unified diff is authoritative for the applied implementation; later edits supersede earlier ones. Successful executions of the exact reproductions and relevant existing tests corroborate the code. Applied code and observed test results override plans, explanations, expected-output comments, and claims that testing passed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting a trigger-only workaround or a passing ad hoc reproduction when the applied precision calculation or early return breaks other documented floatformat behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a stable applied code change visible before the cutoff and evidence that the reported string and Decimal forms are handled, either by direct execution or by an exact, mechanically checkable equivalent through the changed calculation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source state or emitted patch, then relevant executions. Verify that floatformat('0.00', 0) and floatformat(Decimal('0.00'), 0) return '0' without an exception, while positive precision still retains requested trailing places and values with fractional or positive-exponent Decimal representations retain enough quantization precision.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic reference is Django floatformat behavior: zero-valued inputs such as '0.00' and Decimal('0.00') with argument 0 produce '0'; argument n > 0 preserves n output decimal places; nonzero values continue ROUND_HALF_UP quantization; and Decimal context precision remains at least one and sufficiently large for all coefficient/exponent shapes.

scale.1: The latest applied state is nonfunctional, unrelated, or still demonstrably raises the reported precision error.
scale.2: The reported trigger may be avoided, but the latest applied code has a clear semantic regression or an invalid precision path for another supported floatformat input.
scale.3: The diagnosis and candidate correction are technically specific, but no stable applied fix is visible or relevant contradictory evidence remains unresolved.
scale.4: A stable applied fix resolves the reported string and Decimal cases with no visible contradiction, but preservation across requested precisions and Decimal exponent shapes remains materially unverified.
scale.5: The stable applied fix resolves both reported forms, and visible code semantics or relevant executions establish that rounding, positive precision formatting, and Decimal exponent handling remain intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied floatformat fix preserves Decimal precision semantics

applies_when: The trajectory contains a reproduction, test change, or test execution concerning FileField storage deconstruction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides decisive evidence that deconstruction retains the original callable when it returns `default_storage`, together with coverage of established storage behavior and preferably a permanent Django regression test.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the only execution ends in dependency, settings, collection, import, or assertion failure; cap at 3 when tests exercise reimplemented mock logic rather than the modified FileField.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful targeted Django test run against the modified tree outranks ad hoc scripts; actual failures and tracebacks override claims that tests passed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents custom scripts that merely print expected text, unsuccessful test-runner attempts, or tests of duplicated logic from being treated as decisive validation.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires an executed test against the real FileField implementation asserting identity with the original callable; anchor 5 additionally requires a permanent focused regression test and successful relevant suite execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test source, assertions, command lines, exit status, and output for the actual repository implementation rather than a copied or mocked version of the logic.
metadata.oracle_test: Construct FileField(storage=get_storage) with get_storage returning default_storage, deconstruct it, and assert `kwargs['storage'] is get_storage`; complementary cases assert direct default is omitted and direct/callable custom storage remains represented correctly.

scale.1: No relevant test or runtime evidence is visible.
scale.2: A relevant test is proposed or attempted, but execution fails or assertions do not establish the required callable identity.
scale.3: A successful ad hoc reproduction exercises the real FileField and proves the reported case, but lacks permanent regression coverage or meaningful compatibility cases.
scale.4: Successful real-implementation tests prove callable identity for the bug case and cover the important direct-default and custom-storage cases.
scale.5: A focused permanent regression test is visibly added in the appropriate Django test area and the targeted test plus relevant existing tests run successfully.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression evidence

applies_when: The trajectory edits FileField.deconstruct(), encounters contradictory results, or evaluates behavior beyond the single reported case.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves existing FileField and inherited ImageField deconstruction semantics and responds correctly to failed experiments, malformed edits, or newly exposed regressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest visible code still removes `kwargs['upload_to']`, loses direct custom storage, or contains malformed syntax; cap at 2 if a discovered regression remains unresolved or the trajectory declares success despite contrary output.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest verified repository state and real execution results take precedence over earlier claims; a demonstrated restoration can supersede an earlier broken edit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents confident but destructive edits, stale success claims after failures, and fixes that solve only the reported branch while regressing ordinary fields.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a clean final visible implementation with no known unresolved contradiction and explicit protection of at least direct default and direct custom storage behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible before/after diffs, restored files, corrected edits, compatibility checks, and the final visible state of upload_to, max_length, direct storage, callable storage, and ImageField inheritance.
metadata.oracle_test: Unspecified or direct `default_storage` remains omitted; direct custom storage remains serialized; callable storage is serialized as the original callable regardless of its return value; ImageField inherits the corrected FileField behavior.

scale.1: The latest visible state contains a known severe regression or malformed edit, with no demonstrated recovery.
scale.2: Some recovery or compatibility reasoning is present, but a contradiction remains unresolved or the final state is not established.
scale.3: The final visible code appears clean and the trajectory notices at least one compatibility concern, but checks are incomplete or mostly asserted.
scale.4: The trajectory detects and repairs mistakes or explicitly validates direct default and direct custom storage while preserving surrounding deconstruct behavior.
scale.5: Shows disciplined recovery from any contradictory evidence and establishes a clean minimal final state across callable/default/custom behavior, surrounding kwargs, and inherited ImageField semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility preservation and evidence-driven recovery

applies_when: The trajectory contains reasoning or runtime evidence about FileField storage initialization and deconstruction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that FileField preserves an explicitly supplied callable in `_storage_callable`, evaluates it into `self.storage`, and then incorrectly decides whether to serialize `storage` by comparing that evaluated result with `default_storage`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims the callable itself is repeatedly evaluated during deconstruct(), or attributes the omission to migration randomness without identifying the evaluated-result comparison.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current repository source and successful runtime observations take precedence over unsupported narrative; later corrected reasoning takes precedence over an earlier mistake.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards superficial repetition of the issue description without understanding why the callable reference is lost.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require recognition that the original callable and its evaluated storage are distinct values with different deconstruction roles.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source excerpts, runtime identity checks, or explanations connecting FileField.__init__() with FileField.deconstruct().
metadata.oracle_test: For FileField(storage=get_storage) where get_storage() returns default_storage, `_storage_callable` is get_storage, `self.storage is default_storage`, and deconstruct() must nevertheless emit `kwargs['storage'] is get_storage`.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis incompatible with the visible FileField implementation.
scale.2: Locates FileField.deconstruct() or the default_storage comparison but gives an incomplete or materially confused causal account.
scale.3: Correctly states that comparing evaluated `self.storage` with `default_storage` causes omission when a callable returns the default, but does not fully connect this to `_storage_callable` preservation.
scale.4: Accurately traces callable capture, evaluation, and the faulty deconstruction condition, with supporting source or runtime evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal trace and explicitly derives all required semantics: preserve the original callable, omit an implicit/direct default, and retain direct or callable non-default storage.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of callable-storage deconstruction

applies_when: The rollout addresses callable storage deconstruction for FileField and inspects or edits the relevant implementation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible prefix contains a coherently applied and validated change that preserves the original storage callable when it evaluates to default_storage without regressing existing FileField deconstruction semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible implementation removes upload_to, omits direct non-default storage, serializes the evaluated storage instead of the original callable, leaves malformed source, or has unresolved contradictory test evidence. Score 1 when no task-causal source fix is visibly applied.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest directly displayed source or unified diff outranks earlier plans and assistant claims. Successful repository-native tests outrank ad hoc scripts; executed ad hoc checks outrank unexecuted test code. A later verified restoration supersedes transient source corruption for current correctness.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding correct diagnosis, proposed work, self-reported success, or mock-only validation as equivalent to a stable applied patch, and catches narrow fixes that regress adjacent deconstruction paths.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a visible applied source change, a coherent final implementation inspection, preservation of both callable and non-callable storage paths, and no visible loss of existing deconstruction behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible FileField.deconstruct() source or diff and executed checks for a callable returning default_storage, direct default storage, direct non-default storage, callable non-default storage, and retention of unrelated kwargs such as upload_to.
metadata.oracle_test: For FileField(storage=get_storage) where get_storage returns default_storage, deconstruct() must include kwargs['storage'] as the original get_storage callable. Direct default_storage must remain omitted; direct and callable non-default storage must remain represented; upload_to and other existing kwargs must remain intact.

scale.1: No task-causal source fix is visibly applied, or the latest visible implementation is malformed or unusable.
scale.2: A task-causal edit is visible, but it has an unresolved adjacent regression, contradictory evidence, or no coherent final implementation inspection.
scale.3: A coherent applied implementation visibly preserves the callable, direct-default, direct-custom, and upload_to paths, but validation is absent or limited to weak ad hoc evidence.
scale.4: Meets 3 and executed targeted checks credibly cover the callable-returning-default defect and principal default and custom-storage preservation cases without unresolved contradiction.
scale.5: Meets 4 and adds an appropriate repository regression test with a successful relevant repository-native test run.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: FileField deconstruction fix application and integrity

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, proposes, applies, or tests a mechanism for suppressing runserver response bytes on HEAD requests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the latest visible concrete direction can preserve the normal WSGI application, status, header, and cleanup lifecycle while preventing only HEAD representation bytes from reaching the socket.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 when the latest concrete direction replaces the core WSGI run lifecycle without necessity, calls header transmission before the application has necessarily established status and headers, suppresses the write operation that must emit headers, or returns without closing/finalizing the response result. Score at most 2 for a narrower unresolved defect such as reading the method from an unavailable object, consuming a streaming iterator merely to discard it, forcing representation length to zero, or claiming success from a failed or unparsable exchange. A later visibly applied correction removes an earlier cap only when its control flow resolves that defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: A valid raw socket exchange or focused executed server test outranks the latest repository implementation; the latest repository implementation outranks earlier abandoned edits and narrative claims; a fully specified proposed control flow outranks vague intent. Missing dependencies, connection refusal, an empty status line, a setup-induced 500, source-text checks, and client APIs that automatically hide HEAD bodies are not evidence that the mechanism works.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating activity, an applied patch, an empty response caused by server failure, or a body-skipping snippet as progress when the mechanism also suppresses headers, relies on unavailable request state, leaks the iterable, executes discarded streaming content, or rewrites the server lifecycle.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require an applied focused change and a functioning server exchange that separately proves a normal status/header block, zero HEAD body bytes, and a preserved body for a comparable non-HEAD request. Score 5 additionally requires repository regression coverage and explicit iterable finalization evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest concrete repository code or fully specified proposed control flow: where REQUEST_METHOD comes from, when start_response establishes status and headers, whether write or result iteration is bypassed, whether result.close and handler cleanup still execute, and whether non-HEAD responses retain the inherited path.
metadata.oracle_test: For HEAD, runserver invokes the WSGI application sufficiently to establish the same status and applicable representation headers as GET, transmits no representation-body bytes, closes the application iterable and handler normally, and leaves GET and other methods on the established response path.

scale.1: A latest concrete mechanism is structurally non-viable: it bypasses or replaces the normal WSGI run lifecycle, can attempt headers before status exists, suppresses header-producing writes, or omits required result finalization.
scale.2: The direction is focused but has a definite unresolved causal blocker, such as invalid request-method access, discarded-body iteration, incorrect metadata rewriting, or runtime evidence that the chosen path fails.
scale.3: No structurally fatal current direction is established, but the work remains inconclusive: it is exploratory, only proposed, corrected but unverified, or lacks trustworthy evidence for both HEAD and non-HEAD behavior.
scale.4: A focused mechanism is applied and valid execution shows normal HEAD status and headers with zero body bytes plus preserved non-HEAD body delivery, without a visible cleanup contradiction.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and adds maintainable repository tests covering representation headers, ordinary and streaming or lazy results, result closure or finalization, and unchanged non-HEAD behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current mechanism viability at the WSGI transmission boundary

applies_when: The trajectory creates, runs, discusses, or locates tests or runtime checks for runserver HEAD behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces trustworthy test or runtime evidence that a nonempty application response yields status and headers but zero transmitted body bytes for HEAD, while an equivalent GET still transmits its body.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when a claimed passing HEAD result follows a server traceback, empty status line, connection failure, 500 caused by test setup, or an assertion that mistakes header text for body data. Cap at 3 when no test is successfully executed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Raw process output, assertions, exit status, traceback, and parsed bytes outrank printed PASS messages or narrative conclusions; a server exception, empty response, connection refusal, or malformed setup invalidates an apparent empty-body success.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents false confidence from urllib clients that automatically hide HEAD bodies, curl formatting ambiguity, checks that search the whole response for body-like words, or tests that pass only because the server failed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a successful HEAD check against a valid 2xx response with a deliberately nonempty application body and explicit header/body separation. Anchor 5 additionally requires a successful GET or equivalent non-HEAD control and repository-appropriate regression coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed focused Django server tests or a real socket/runserver exchange that separates the HTTP header block from body bytes, plus a non-HEAD control; relevant repository test additions also count when coherent.
metadata.oracle_test: A valid HEAD exchange contains a normal HTTP status line and headers followed by an empty byte sequence after the header terminator; the same application under GET returns its known body.

scale.1: No relevant validation, or the only visible evidence directly demonstrates body transmission or a broken server.
scale.2: Attempts a test but its setup, parsing, or execution is invalid, inconclusive, or contradicted by raw output.
scale.3: Provides a sound test design or coherent unexecuted regression test, or executes only a partial check without a valid control.
scale.4: Successfully demonstrates a valid HEAD response with headers and an empty transmitted body using trustworthy parsing or assertions.
scale.5: Successfully demonstrates HEAD suppression and preserved GET body behavior, with a focused maintainable regression test or equivalent server-level evidence and no contradictory failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive HTTP and regression test evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, changes, or tests runserver's transmission of responses to HTTP HEAD requests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory has established and validated a focused server-layer mechanism that executes the WSGI response normally but suppresses only transmitted body bytes for HEAD requests, while preserving headers, non-HEAD bodies, iterable cleanup, and connection behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An observed body on HEAD, an exception in the chosen response path, use of an unavailable request-method attribute, or a test that never reached a functioning server caps the score at 3 until corrected and rerun. A concrete design that skips application or result iteration before status and headers can be established, replaces the core WSGI run lifecycle without necessity, or omits required result cleanup caps the score at 2; if that remains the trajectory's only concrete direction, score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful executed integration or focused repository tests outrank inspected source changes; inspected source changes outrank command-confirmed failures that localize a mechanism; those outrank reasoning or proposed snippets. Existing repository code and history establish semantics but do not prove the trajectory's implementation works. A test is authoritative only if the server actually started, returned a parseable response, and the body was checked separately from headers.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a plausible-sounding HEAD check that is only proposed, suppresses headers as well as the body, changes Content-Length merely to hide a body, accesses request state from the wrong object, leaks the response iterable, or appears to pass because the server or application failed before producing a response.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a focused change applied to the relevant repository source and valid executed evidence that a HEAD response transmits no body while a comparable non-HEAD response still transmits its body.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible repository source changes, the active request-method source, the WSGI application/start_response/result-iteration/close flow, and executed tests that separately examine HEAD bytes, GET bytes, headers, and iterable cleanup. Credit applied work or a decisive executed falsification more than an unexecuted proposal.
metadata.oracle_test: A conforming runserver invokes the WSGI application and preserves the response headers a corresponding GET would produce, including a legitimate representation Content-Length, but sends zero representation-body bytes for HEAD. GET continues to send its body, and regular, streaming, or lazy response iterables are finalized or closed according to the normal WSGI lifecycle.

scale.1: The only concrete direction is visibly non-viable or unnecessarily replaces the WSGI run/response lifecycle, and there is no later applied correction or valid causal evidence.
scale.2: The server boundary and HEAD requirement are identified, but the work is only proposed or unverified and leaves header establishment, result iteration, cleanup, or non-HEAD behavior unresolved; no executed result has yet localized the issue enough to support a focused correction.
scale.3: A focused repository change is visibly applied or an executed result decisively falsifies and localizes the current mechanism, but valid evidence for both bodyless HEAD and body-preserving non-HEAD behavior is still absent or a visible contradiction remains.
scale.4: A focused server-layer implementation is applied, and valid executed evidence shows no transmitted HEAD body, preserved response headers, and an unchanged body for a comparable non-HEAD request, with no visible lifecycle contradiction.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and adds repository-level coverage for ordinary and streaming or lazy responses, verifies normal iterable finalization or closure, and checks that HEAD retains representation headers without forcing an incorrect zero length.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validated HEAD response suppression at the server lifecycle boundary

applies_when: The trajectory encounters a failed edit, failed test, syntax error, dependency error, formatter rejection, or other visible contradiction to its completion claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to visible contradictory evidence by diagnosing it, correcting what is controllable, and presenting a coherent final state without overstating failed checks.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An explicit submission-format rejection followed by a completion marker without the required patch, or a failed relevant test followed by an unqualified success claim, caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later successful evidence for the same operation may resolve an earlier failure; explicit tool or formatter errors remain authoritative until a compliant retry is visibly completed.
metadata.failure_mode: Ignoring tool feedback, treating missing dependencies as passing tests, or losing an otherwise correct patch during an unsuccessful final handoff.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require every task-relevant, controllable contradiction to be visibly resolved or accurately bounded before completion is asserted.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether each visible failure is acknowledged, whether corrective evidence follows, and whether the eventual handoff remains consistent with the latest verified diff and test status.
metadata.oracle_test: After a failed edit or check, the next reliable evidence should show the corrected source or rerun result; after a rejected handoff, a compliant handoff containing the intended patch should be visible.

scale.1: The trajectory leaves a task-relevant contradiction unresolved and provides no coherent recoverable implementation or handoff evidence.
scale.2: A correct implementation may be visible elsewhere, but a later explicit failure or rejection remains unresolved while completion is still asserted.
scale.3: The trajectory acknowledges contradictions and preserves recoverable source evidence, but recovery is incomplete or the final status overstates what was validated.
scale.4: All controllable contradictions are visibly corrected, while uncontrollable environment limitations are accurately reported and the final implementation evidence remains coherent.
scale.5: Recovery is prompt and complete: failed edits or checks are corrected and rerun as appropriate, limitations are precisely bounded, and the final handoff is fully consistent with the latest visible diff and validation evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory execution or submission evidence

applies_when: The prefix reasons about, edits, or tests reduction between consecutive AlterField operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible causal model correctly makes target identity sufficient for the later AlterField to supersede the earlier one, including when their field definitions differ.

metadata.failure_mode: The reported differing-definition sequence remains unreduced because equality or selected attributes are treated as prerequisites.
metadata.judge_focus: Reject field-definition equality as an applicability condition.
metadata.oracle_test: Use independently constructed same-target fields with differing max_length, help_text, default, field class, validators, or other options.
metadata.stage: Inspect and implement the operation-local reduction semantics

scale.1: Explicitly requires equal fields, equal deconstructions, or matching selected field attributes before supersession.
scale.2: Recognizes related AlterField operations but retains an equality-based or otherwise contradictory applicability rule.
scale.3: States that differing same-target definitions should collapse, but the causal rule remains incomplete, inconsistent, or weakly evidenced.
scale.4: Clearly uses operation type and same-target identity without a field-definition comparison, with only minor ambiguity.
scale.5: Consistently establishes that every later same-target AlterField supersedes the earlier one regardless of definition changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unconditional same-target AlterField supersession

applies_when: The prefix contains an execution intended to validate consecutive AlterField reduction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest successful post-edit execution evidence that an AlterField-only sequence with differing definitions reduces to the required final operation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest focused run that leaves multiple differing-definition AlterFields or retains stale state caps the score at 1. Count-only success cannot exceed 2, and a direct AlterField.reduce() call without optimizer execution cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest successful task-relevant execution after the latest relevant edit wins. A later focused failure overrides earlier success until a causal correction and rerun are visible. Import, dependency, settings, discovery, and runner failures are non-evidence about optimizer semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: An already-working AddField case, an identical-field example, a count-only assertion, or a setup failure is mistaken for proof that the reported bug and stale-operation risks are fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a successful MigrationOptimizer.optimize() execution over at least two same-target AlterField operations whose field definitions visibly differ. Score 4 additionally requires proof that the survivor carries the final definition or complete operation state; score 5 requires exact-later preservation plus successful repository optimizer coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executions after the latest relevant production edit; distinguish direct reduce() checks, optimizer count checks, final field-state checks, exact operation preservation, and suite coverage.
metadata.oracle_test: Optimize independently constructed same-target AlterField operations that differ in max_length, help_text, default, field class, validators, or preserve_default; verify one result and that it is the final supplied operation or preserves its complete deconstruction and operation-level state.
metadata.stage: Run discriminative validation and recover from environment issues

scale.1: No successful post-edit AlterField-only optimizer evidence is visible, or the latest focused execution still shows multiple differing-definition operations or stale final state.
scale.2: A successful direct reduce() check or optimizer count-only check is visible, but differing definitions and the surviving final state are not both established.
scale.3: A successful AlterField-only optimizer run uses visibly differing definitions and leaves one AlterField, but exact final field or operation state is not verified.
scale.4: A successful post-edit optimizer run uses differing definitions and verifies the survivor's final field definition or complete operation state, without successful repository optimizer-suite evidence.
scale.5: Post-edit validation proves the survivor is the exact final input operation or preserves its complete state, and the repository optimizer suite succeeds with relevant legacy reductions covered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Post-edit proof of final AlterField preservation

applies_when: The prefix encounters source or execution evidence that contradicts its claimed implementation behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the prefix claims resolution while a causally relevant contradiction remains unresolved.

metadata.failure_mode: A stale, count-only, or unrelated success is treated as proof despite contradictory source or focused execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Current source and post-edit focused evidence must support any success claim.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the final operative branch and rerun a differing-definition AlterField-only case after the last relevant edit.
metadata.stage: Validate and reconcile the operative behavior

scale.1: No unresolved contradiction is visible, or the prefix explicitly continues diagnosing it.
scale.2: A minor discrepancy remains, but current source and focused evidence support the claimed causal correction.
scale.3: Material uncertainty remains between the latest source and validation, without a strong unsupported success claim.
scale.4: The prefix treats the issue as resolved while a relevant source or validation contradiction remains insufficiently reconciled.

applies_when: A production edit, patch, or concrete implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the operative implementation is reachable in AlterField.reduce() and retains the supplied later operation.

metadata.failure_mode: The rule is missing, misplaced, unreachable, malformed, or implemented by retaining or reconstructing the wrong operation.
metadata.judge_focus: Use is_same_field_operation() and return the supplied operation.
metadata.oracle_test: Call the earlier operation's reduce() with the later operation and assert the sole result is that later object.

scale.1: No operative or concretely applicable AlterField.reduce() realization is visible.
scale.2: A relevant attempt exists but is misplaced, unreachable, malformed, or reconstructs incomplete operation state.
scale.3: The local implementation is substantially correct, but reachability or exact object preservation is ambiguous.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reachable exact-later-operation realization

applies_when: The trajectory discusses the cause of the APPEND_SLASH redirect defect in AdminSite.catch_all_view().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly explains that URL resolution uses the path component, while the redirect target must append the slash to the path before retaining the request query string.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory asserts that normal Django request.path contains the query string, recommends appending '/' to request.get_full_path() without force_append_slash, or otherwise derives /path?query/ as correct. Later explicit correction removes the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed Django source and real RequestFactory/client behavior outrank unsupported assertions and hand-built mock request fields.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking path and full-path semantics or preserving the query in the wrong syntactic position.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognizing that the slash belongs before the question mark, not after the complete path-and-query string.
metadata.judge_focus: Cutoff-visible reasoning or runtime evidence distinguishing request.path, request.path_info, request.META['QUERY_STRING'], and request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True), including the required /?query ordering.
metadata.oracle_test: For a request to /admin/auth/foo?id=123 whose slash-appended route resolves, the redirect Location is /admin/auth/foo/?id=123; without a query it is /admin/auth/foo/.

scale.1: The visible diagnosis is absent or fundamentally attributes the failure to an unrelated component.
scale.2: It locates catch_all_view() but gives materially incorrect path/query semantics or an incorrect /path?query/ target.
scale.3: It correctly identifies that the redirect drops QUERY_STRING, but does not establish the slash-before-query requirement or a robust construction.
scale.4: It correctly explains the loss and the /path/?query ordering, with a semantically valid construction identified.
scale.5: It additionally grounds the diagnosis in Django request source or realistic runtime evidence and clearly separates resolver-path handling from redirect full-path construction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of query-string loss

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects, changes, or verifies the APPEND_SLASH redirect target in AdminSite.catch_all_view().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visibly persisted redirect expression appends the slash to the request path before preserving a nonempty raw query string, while retaining a usable slash-appended Location when the query string is empty.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the persisted expression drops the query, omits the slash or '?' delimiter, places the slash after the query, or is syntactically unusable. Cap at 3 if the reported nonempty-query case is correct but the empty-query branch returns an empty or otherwise structurally unusable Location. Cap at 4 if the only visible defect is a usable path-plus-slash Location with an unnecessary empty-query delimiter.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or git diff at the cutoff overrides earlier edits, proposed snippets, summaries, and demonstrations of different expressions. Faithful execution of the persisted expression outranks toy reconstruction; a reverted edit receives no implementation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equal credit for a harmless-looking trailing '?' and a precedence bug that collapses the entire no-query Location, while still rejecting get_full_path() followed by '/', missing delimiters, query-dropping code, and reverted edits.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a visibly persisted source edit whose nonempty-query Location is path-plus-slash followed by '?' and the unchanged query string. Score 5 additionally requires the empty-query Location to remain path-plus-slash.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible repository source or unified diff for the successful redirect branch and evaluate the resulting Location separately for a nonempty QUERY_STRING and an empty QUERY_STRING.
metadata.non_evidence: Narrated intent, future edits, terminal formatting, dependency installation, test-runner setup, claims that tests passed, and scripts that do not execute or faithfully reproduce the latest persisted expression.
metadata.oracle_test: For request.path '/admin/auth/foo' and raw QUERY_STRING 'id=123', Location is '/admin/auth/foo/?id=123'. For an empty QUERY_STRING, Location is '/admin/auth/foo/'. A framework helper is equivalent only if it inserts the slash into the path before adding the query.

scale.1: No effective task-relevant source edit is visibly persisted, the original query-dropping redirect remains, a prior edit was reverted, or the edited branch is not executable.
scale.2: A source edit is persisted, but the nonempty-query Location is observably wrong because it drops a required component, omits '?', omits the appended slash, or places the slash after the query string.
scale.3: The persisted edit is directed at the correct behavior but the reported query case remains unresolved, or that case is correct while the empty-query branch visibly yields an empty or otherwise unusable Location.
scale.4: The persisted edit produces the required slash-before-query Location for a nonempty query, but the empty-query result has only a concrete secondary defect such as an unnecessary trailing '?'.
scale.5: The persisted edit unambiguously produces path-plus-slash followed by the unchanged nonempty query string and produces path-plus-slash with no query delimiter when the query is empty.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Persisted catch-all redirect preserves path, slash, and query order

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects, modifies, or verifies AdminSite.catch_all_view() behavior for APPEND_SLASH redirects.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visibly persisted implementation constructs the permanent redirect by appending the slash to the path before preserving any nonempty query string, without changing the no-query behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible code drops the query, omits the required slash, appends the slash after the query, or otherwise contradicts the required Location. Cap at 4 if the reported nonempty-query case is correct but the no-query branch visibly emits an unnecessary delimiter or has another concrete secondary defect. If the final visible source has reverted to the original buggy redirect, score 1 regardless of earlier successful-looking snippets or tests.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or git diff at the cutoff overrides earlier patches, proposed code, summaries, explanations, and standalone simulations. A faithful execution of the actual branch overrides a toy string-construction claim.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for get_full_path() followed by '/', '?query/' constructions, missing '?' delimiters, unconditional empty-query delimiters, reverted edits, and tests that validate a different expression from the persisted source.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visibly persisted source edit in the task-relevant redirect branch. The redirect must place the appended slash before the query delimiter to receive score 5.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source content or diff for the redirect branch in AdminSite.catch_all_view(), including the relative positions of the path, appended slash, query delimiter, and query string.
metadata.non_evidence: Terminal formatting, claims that tests passed, package installation, test-runner setup effort, proposed future edits, and toy scripts that do not execute or faithfully reproduce the persisted redirect expression.
metadata.oracle_test: For path /admin/auth/foo and raw QUERY_STRING id=123, the Location must be /admin/auth/foo/?id=123. With an empty query string it must be /admin/auth/foo/. Equivalent framework helpers are valid only when they force the slash into the path before adding the query string.

scale.1: No effective task-relevant source edit is visibly persisted at the cutoff, the original query-dropping redirect remains, or the edited branch is structurally unusable.
scale.2: A task-relevant edit is persisted, but its visible URL construction is demonstrably wrong, such as dropping the query, omitting '?', omitting the slash, or placing the slash after the query string.
scale.3: A persisted edit is causally directed at preserving the query and is not demonstrably equivalent to the failures in score 2, but visible evidence is insufficient to establish correct behavior for the reported query case and the no-query case.
scale.4: The persisted edit produces the required slash-before-query redirect for the reported nonempty-query case, but a concrete secondary defect or unresolved branch remains, such as emitting an unnecessary delimiter when the query is empty.
scale.5: The persisted edit unambiguously produces path-plus-slash followed by the unchanged nonempty query string, preserves the original path-plus-slash behavior when the query is empty, and has no visible contradictory source or execution evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied catch-all redirect preserves URL component order

applies_when: A cutoff-visible source edit or concrete patch changes AdminSite.catch_all_view() redirect construction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes only the successful slash-append redirect path so the permanent redirect preserves the original query string after the added slash and retains the no-query behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible final expression yields /path?query/, /path?query/, /path?query/, /path?query/ with the slash after the query, omits the '?', emits a trailing '?' for an empty query, returns an empty Location due to conditional-expression precedence, or is syntactically/structurally invalid.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest cutoff-visible file content or unified diff outranks earlier proposed snippets, narration, and synthetic demonstrations of different code.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting code that mentions QUERY_STRING but composes the URL in the wrong order or mishandles the empty-query branch.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible source change that yields /path/?query for a query-bearing request and /path/ when the query is empty.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible final diff or source state in django/contrib/admin/sites.py, especially the Location produced for nonempty and empty QUERY_STRING values.
metadata.oracle_test: A canonical implementation is request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True); an equivalent implementation must first form request.path + '/' and then conditionally append '?' plus the query string.

scale.1: No applicable source change is visible, or the edit clearly cannot produce a valid redirect.
scale.2: The correct branch is edited but the final URL composition is observably wrong, malformed, or query-dropping.
scale.3: A correct implementation is only proposed, or the visible edit is plausibly correct but has unresolved precedence, empty-query, or structural ambiguity.
scale.4: The visible edit correctly preserves query and no-query behavior with a focused, valid manual construction.
scale.5: The visible edit is concise and robust, preferably using get_full_path(force_append_slash=True), while leaving the resolver and redirect gates intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct and focused redirect implementation

applies_when: The trajectory changes or evaluates behavior within AdminSite.catch_all_view().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves the existing conditions under which the catch-all view redirects versus raises Http404, including APPEND_SLASH, route resolution, custom should_append_slash, URL configuration, and already-slashed handling.

metadata.evidence_authority: Actual final source control flow and relevant Django tests outrank statements that compatibility is maintained.

scale.2: One or more established redirect gates are removed, bypassed, or contradicted.
scale.3: The edit is localized but compatibility with one or more guards is unclear or unexamined.
scale.4: The final source visibly preserves all original guards and limits production changes to redirect-target construction.
scale.5: The final source preserves all guards with minimal scope, and cutoff-visible tests or runtime evidence exercise at least one nonredirect or no-query compatibility case in addition to the reported case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of catch-all redirect guards and compatibility

applies_when: Select this rubric only when the visible trajectory changes or evaluates AdminSite.catch_all_view() redirect construction or the conditions controlling redirect versus Http404.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest persisted change preserves every existing catch-all redirect guard while retaining the externally visible request path, appending exactly one slash before any query string, and preserving the original no-query redirect behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final source removes or bypasses a redirect guard, changes resolver eligibility incompatibly, redirects a branch that should raise Http404, drops a deployment path prefix by constructing the Location from path_info, omits the appended slash, omits the query delimiter, drops the query, or places the slash after the query. Cap at 3 if the reported query-bearing Location is correct but the empty-query branch emits an unnecessary delimiter, an extra slash, an empty Location, or another concrete compatibility defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff is authoritative for control flow and redirect construction. Faithful execution of that persisted branch may confirm behavior, but earlier edits, narration, helper simulations, and tests of a different expression cannot override contradictory final source.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a localized-looking edit from receiving full regression-safety credit when it preserves the guard syntax but changes externally visible behavior through malformed component order, loss of a script or mount prefix, broken empty-query handling, broadened redirect eligibility, or altered Http404 behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a visibly persisted edit inside the original successful slash-append branch, all original redirect-versus-Http404 guards to remain intact, and source that yields an externally mounted path plus one slash followed by the unchanged query only when nonempty. Score 5 additionally requires faithful cutoff-visible execution of the persisted branch covering compatibility behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final source around settings.APPEND_SLASH, the unslashed-URL check, resolution of request.path_info plus a slash with the request URL configuration, Resolver404 handling, should_append_slash, and the final Http404. With an empty query it redirects to the same path plus one slash and no question mark. If APPEND_SLASH is disabled, the URL is already slashed, slash-appended resolution fails, or the matched view disallows slash appending, the preexisting Http404 behavior remains.
