reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal localization and state model

applies_when: The trajectory claims correctness, passing tests, successful validation, or completion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes claims that exceed or contradict visible source and output, while keeping concrete implementation and execution progress dominant.

metadata.failure_mode: Wrong-source execution, simulation, a known failing sequence, or non-executed tests are presented as proof.
metadata.judge_focus: Consistency of claims with cutoff evidence
metadata.oracle_test: Reconcile each claim with the loaded source, executed command, output, and final visible artifact.

scale.1: Claims accurately match the visible evidence, or no success claim is made.
scale.2: The evidence is limited but appropriately qualified.
scale.3: A meaningful claim exceeds available validation or overlooks a visible warning sign.
scale.4: A central claim conflicts with source provenance, a failed check, or an obvious implementation defect.
scale.5: The trajectory repeatedly presents unrelated execution, a simulation, non-executed tests, or self-invalidating output as definitive proof.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unsupported or contradicted success claims

applies_when: A production edit, proposed patch, repository diff, or absence of such an edit is visible by the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores how far the trajectory advances from diagnosis to a concrete, runnable, evaluator-applicable production artifact, separately from whether every semantic detail is correct.

metadata.failure_mode: No-edit or test-only work is treated as equal to a completed implementation, or an immediately unusable edit is treated as finished.
metadata.judge_focus: Concrete implementation progress
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect whether production code changed and whether ordinary relevant paths can execute.

scale.1: No production implementation is visible; the trajectory stops at diagnosis, reproduction, or test scaffolding.
scale.2: An implementation is proposed or partially edited, but the final production state is missing, indeterminate, or plainly unfinished.
scale.3: A concrete production edit exists, but malformed structure, missing dependencies, branch-local state misuse, or another major defect prevents an ordinary relevant path from being reliably usable.
scale.4: The production edit is focused and substantially runnable, but remains incomplete, stale, polluted, or uncertain on a material path.
scale.5: A focused, syntactically coherent, evaluator-applicable production artifact is visible; behavioral mistakes, if any, are scored separately.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production artifact progress and applicability

applies_when: Editing, building, runtime validation, recovery, or finalization activity is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalize unresolved combinations of source-integrity, worktree, provenance, and validation hazards that make the visible result unreliable.

metadata.failure_mode: The trajectory reaches cutoff with compounded source, artifact, provenance, or failure-signaling hazards that were not followed by a clean causally matched final check.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for observable combinations of malformed editing, in-place build pollution, tracked backups, wrong-provenance success, defective simulations, unresolved imports, and missing final reinspection.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect final git diff and status, compile or import the edited source, confirm no tracked backup or generated artifact, and rerun an assertion-based reproduction from that exact worktree.
metadata.stage: Implement and inspect the focused source change; Finalize an evaluator-consumable worktree

scale.1: No material hazard remains, or every visible intermediate failure was removed and followed by clean checkout-backed revalidation.
scale.2: A minor temporary probe or scratch artifact remains, but source integrity and validation provenance are clear.
scale.3: Notable validation ambiguity or tracked scratch noise remains, though an applicable source fix is still inspectable.
scale.4: A tracked backup, wrong-provenance verification claim, unresolved generated artifact, or similarly serious evaluator risk remains.
scale.5: Multiple hazards remain compounded at cutoff, such as malformed editing or in-place builds combined with unresolved imports, defective simulations, contradictory provenance, or no clean final reinspection.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unresolved compounded worktree or evidence hazard

applies_when: Runtime results, helper inspection, simulations, tests, or verification claims are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward evidence whose module provenance and process failure behavior make it causally relevant to the visible source edit.

metadata.failure_mode: Installed or patched site-package execution is presented as checkout validation, or scripts print failures while exiting successfully.
metadata.judge_focus: Check imported paths, runtime source identity, assertions, and resolution of contradictory installed and checkout observations.
metadata.oracle_test: Print matplotlib.__file__, cbook.__file__, and runtime helper source in the asserting process, and ensure an incorrect result exits nonzero.
metadata.stage: Trace and reproduce the x-conversion failure; Validate artist, color-cycle, and compatibility semantics

scale.1: Verification claims rely on unresolved mixed provenance, defective probes, or swallowed failures and are presented as conclusive.
scale.2: The trajectory recognizes provenance or probe limitations but does not obtain checkout-backed assertion evidence.
scale.3: Some relevant execution is assertion-based, but module paths or runtime source identity remain incompletely established.
scale.4: Assertions execute through modules visibly loaded from the edited checkout and fail normally on incorrect results.
scale.5: Checkout paths, inspected runtime source, nonzero failure signaling, and identity between the tested and submitted source are all explicitly confirmed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Checkout provenance and failure signaling

applies_when: A candidate source fix is visible or Axes.bar behavior is exercised.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward direct evidence that the edited checkout creates the expected NaN-geometry Rectangle and consumes the normal patch color.

metadata.failure_mode: Only helper behavior is simulated, exceptions are swallowed, the container is empty, geometry is fabricated or missing, or normal color selection is bypassed.
metadata.judge_focus: Separate no-exception evidence from Rectangle geometry and color-state evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Assert one Rectangle from ax.bar([nan], [nan]), NaN x and height, NaN x from ax.bar([nan], [0]), and next-color equivalence against a finite bar created and removed.
metadata.stage: Validate artist, color-cycle, and compatibility semantics

scale.1: No relevant integrated behavior is observed, or visible evidence shows missing artists, fabricated geometry, or bypassed color selection.
scale.2: Only installed-release behavior, a standalone simulation, or print-only no-exception output is visible.
scale.3: Checkout-backed execution or strong source structure shows normal bar creation, but Rectangle geometry or color state is not fully asserted.
scale.4: Checkout-backed assertions verify one Rectangle and the required NaN geometry for both reported x-NaN cases.
scale.5: The geometry assertions pass and an explicit subsequent-bar color comparison or focused figure-equivalence test confirms phantom-bar color consumption.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Integrated Rectangle and color-cycle semantics

applies_when: Visible work edits or proposes handling of all-nonfinite input in _safe_first_finite or Axes._convert_dx.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward an applied source change that preserves the actual all-nonfinite conversion reference after finite search is exhausted, retains later-finite selection, covers both _convert_dx reference searches, and avoids widening the shared helper's exception contract.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied None or fabricated-value fallback is capped at 1. One-sided local handling is capped at 2. A helper-wide new exception on nonempty all-nonfinite input, even if selected _convert_dx callers catch it, is capped at 3 unless visible evidence establishes compatibility for the helper's broader callers.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest clean visible repository source or diff supersedes earlier experiments and prose. Source inspection outranks standalone simulations and installed-package behavior; checkout-backed assertions may raise a valid implementation from anchor 4 to 5.
metadata.failure_mode: Judging all exception-suppressing patches alike, despite visible differences between preserving the real NaN reference, returning None, handling only one conversion reference, or introducing a new shared-helper exception contract.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applicable source edit that handles both x0 and xconv exhaustion directly or through one shared fallback, preserves an actual input element rather than a sentinel, and leaves later-finite selection intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible source for the exhaustion value, both x0 and xconv paths, retention of the finite-filtering branch, and any new behavior imposed on other _safe_first_finite callers.
metadata.oracle_test: For nonempty [nan], exhaustion must retain or return that NaN; for [nan, 1, 2], finite search must still select 1; both _convert_dx searches must avoid leaking StopIteration without changing empty-input or unsupported-generator behavior.
metadata.stage: Select the compatibility boundary and fallback; Implement and inspect the focused source change

scale.1: An applied cutoff-visible implementation is semantically contradictory: it returns None, fabricates finite data, removes finite-first selection, drops the bar, or otherwise loses the actual all-nonfinite element.
scale.2: The cause or intended fix is discussed, but no applicable resolution is visible, the final source is ambiguous, or local handling covers only one of the two conversion-reference searches.
scale.3: An applicable change addresses both target searches and can prevent the reported StopIteration, but it changes the shared helper to raise a new exception for nonempty all-nonfinite input or leaves similarly material compatibility risk unresolved.
scale.4: By final source inspection, a narrow applicable fallback covers both references, preserves the actual all-nonfinite element, retains later-finite selection, and does not broaden empty-input, iterator, or shared-helper exception behavior.
scale.5: Anchor 4 is satisfied and checkout-backed assertions verify all-nonfinite reference preservation, later-finite selection, both reported NaN-x bar cases, and unchanged iterator or empty-input boundaries.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility-safe exhausted finite-search fallback

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or modifies code to correct autoscaling of the step histogram or the underlying patch path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Fixes limit computation by traversing the complete unsimplified patch path when deriving patch extrema, without changing histogram density values, polygon geometry, rendering simplification, or sticky-edge semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for fixes that append tops.max() to sticky_edges, set ylim directly, alter density normalization, or rewrite step vertices; cap at 3 if simplification is disabled globally for rendering rather than only for limit computation.
metadata.evidence_authority: A source diff in the generic patch-limit calculation overrides prose; a histogram-local sticky-edge or ylim workaround does not establish the correct boundary.
metadata.failure_mode: Applying a histogram-specific workaround that masks clipping for one vertical positive histogram but changes margins, fails horizontal or negative cases, or leaves the generic autoscale defect intact.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible code change that disables path simplification specifically while computing patch data limits, such as passing simplify=False to the relevant path iteration.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or precise implementation plan in the Axes patch-limit helper, especially the path/Bezier iteration used to collect extrema and an explicit disabling of simplification for this calculation.
metadata.oracle_test: Patch extrema used for dataLim must be calculated from every original path segment, while the renderer remains free to simplify the path afterward.

scale.1: No implementation direction, or changes unrelated to the failing limit computation.
scale.2: Implements or proposes a direct ylim, sticky-edge maximum, density, or polygon-shape workaround.
scale.3: Targets patch autoscaling or path processing but lacks a correct visible change, or disables simplification too broadly.
scale.4: Applies a focused unsimplified-path change in the patch-limit calculation with no unrelated behavioral edits.
scale.5: Applies the minimal generic fix at the exact limit-extraction boundary, clearly preserving rendering simplification and existing histogram computation and sticky-edge behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Minimal fix at the patch-limit computation boundary

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, changes, or validates behavior relevant to step-histogram autoscaling
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the strongest repository-grounded milestone visibly completed toward correcting the omission of a step-path extremum from autoscaling, distinguishing successful observation, causal localization, applied work, and validated correction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the asserted mechanism is disproved by visible output, scripts repeatedly fail before producing the claimed comparison, or only an unrelated installed package is exercised. Cap at 3 when an edit is merely proposed, absent from the authoritative diff, malformed, or is a histogram-local ylim, sticky-edge-maximum, density, or vertex workaround.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current checkout contents and git diff/status outrank edit commands and prose claiming an edit. Successful output from code demonstrably importing the checkout outranks output from site-packages. Numeric comparisons of histogram heights, artist vertices, and limits outrank images or visual impressions.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating browsing, failed experiments, summaries, or proposed edits as completed progress; confusing valid density scaling with clipping; or awarding a source-edit milestone when authoritative repository evidence shows no coherent applied change.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires a successful defect-specific observation or an implementation-ready causal localization. Score 4 requires a coherent source edit visibly present in the checkout and a direct behavioral check. Score 5 requires the generic unsimplified-path correction plus a durable focused regression executed against the checkout.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the strongest completed milestone: a successful clipping measurement, localization to patch data-limit extraction, a source change present in the checkout, or a focused regression. Inspect returned heights, polygon vertices, dataLim or view limits, source contents, diff/status, import provenance, and test output.
metadata.oracle_test: Returned bar and step densities for identical data and bins agree and integrate to one; rescaling x legitimately changes density height inversely. The defect is present only when the step artist contains a maximum that the value-axis data or view limits omit because simplified path traversal was used during patch limit extraction.
metadata.stage: early trajectory from reproduction through validation

scale.1: No successful task-specific observation or causal advance; work is unrelated, abandoned, or ends with an unresolved claim directly contradicted by visible evidence.
scale.2: Relevant code and behavior are explored, but no reliable clipping measurement or implementation-ready localization is completed; evidence is inconclusive, from the wrong environment, or still confuses density values with autoscaling.
scale.3: A successful defect-specific comparison establishes that correct histogram or polygon heights can exceed the computed limits, or source tracing yields a precise implementation-ready patch-limit diagnosis, but no coherent corrective source edit is authoritatively present and checked.
scale.4: A coherent source edit is visibly present in the checkout and a checkout-grounded behavioral check shows progress on the omitted-extremum problem, but the edit is incomplete, lacks a durable regression, or has not established the full generic unsimplified-path behavior.
scale.5: The checkout visibly contains the focused generic unsimplified-path limit fix and a durable regression; authoritative test output confirms that the step maximum is included without changing density computation, polygon geometry, rendering simplification, or sticky-edge semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Authoritative progress on the step-histogram clipping mechanism

applies_when: The trajectory creates, runs, or proposes tests for the reported step-histogram autoscaling behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses a deterministic regression that would fail when path simplification drops the step histogram's maximum and pass when the complete path contributes to autoscaling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if tests only prove that density integrates to one; cap at 3 if the test is nondeterministic, runs against site-packages instead of the checkout, or never checks axis/data limits.
metadata.evidence_authority: Assertions and their observed pass/fail output take precedence over saved images, manual inspection, or comparisons run against an unrelated installed Matplotlib version.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking correct numerical density values for proof that the plotted histogram is not clipped, or accepting a generated image without a semantic limit assertion.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an automated assertion tied to the clipped maximum, not merely equality of bar and step returned n arrays or unit density integral.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository test additions and command output asserting that the upper view or data limit contains the maximum returned density/step vertex for a seeded or fixed dataset with density=True, histtype='step', and enough bins to trigger path simplification.
metadata.oracle_test: For deterministic scaled data and a sufficiently detailed step histogram, ax.get_ylim()[1] (or dataLim.y1 before margins) must be at least max(n), and the test must fail on the buggy implementation where that maximum is simplified away.

scale.1: No relevant test or runtime check.
scale.2: Only checks density integrals, returned bar/step equality, or image generation without testing autoscaling.
scale.3: Compares polygon maxima and limits manually or proposes a suitable regression, but lacks a deterministic automated assertion executed against the checkout.
scale.4: Adds or runs a deterministic automated regression asserting the step maximum is contained by the axis/data limits.
scale.5: Demonstrates the regression failing before and passing after the focused fix, using the checkout and explicitly confirming the test exercises a simplifiable step path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Deterministic regression evidence for the clipped density step

applies_when: The task concerns Axes.hist density display or autoscaling for step-style histograms
The visible prefix includes investigation, diagnosis, implementation, or validation relevant to the defect
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how far the visible work advances a causally correct and repository-grounded fix for the step-histogram autoscaling defect, from verified diagnosis through applied implementation and regression validation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claim that work was applied when authoritative source or diff evidence shows otherwise cannot exceed 3. An internally malformed edit, a test that exercises only an unrelated installed package, or output that directly disproves the asserted mechanism caps the score at 2 unless the contradiction is visibly resolved. Treating probability-density height as invariant under rescaling of the x variable is not evidence of this autoscaling bug.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current repository file contents, git diff/status, and test output demonstrably importing that checkout outrank summaries and stated intentions. Direct numeric comparisons of returned bin heights, polygon vertices, data limits, and view limits outrank visual guesses. Results from a separately installed Matplotlib version may characterize semantics but do not prove the checkout or a proposed fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting prolonged code browsing, faulty extraction scripts, density-normalization misconceptions, tests against the wrong installation, or proposed edits as though they were applied and validated fixes.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a coherent source change visibly applied to the task checkout. Score 5 additionally requires a durable focused regression test and successful relevant test execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect reproduction outputs, the selected execution environment, Axes.hist step-polygon and autoscaling code, current source or diff evidence, and tests that compare rendered artist extents and axis limits. Distinguish histogram density values from whether the axis limits contain the rendered maximum.
metadata.oracle_test: For identical data and bin edges, density=True must produce the same numerical bin heights for bar and step representations, with density area equal to one. Rescaling x legitimately changes density height inversely with the x scale. The defect-specific check is that the step artist's rendered maximum is included in the autoscaled value-axis limits, for vertical and horizontal orientations and without regressing related step or stepfilled behavior.
metadata.stage: early trajectory: diagnosis through focused validation

scale.1: No reliable task-causal progress: the work remains generic, abandons the investigation, or rests on claims contradicted by visible outputs.
scale.2: Relevant code or behavior is explored and a plausible area is identified, but the reproduction is non-authoritative or inconclusive, the density and autoscaling mechanisms are confused, or unresolved contradictions prevent a dependable diagnosis.
scale.3: The visible evidence correctly distinguishes density computation from axis autoscaling and establishes a credible cause with an implementation-ready change and test plan, but no coherent source fix is visibly applied to the checkout.
scale.4: A coherent task-causal source fix is visibly applied and directly checked against the reported behavior in the checkout, but a durable regression test, broader relevant validation, or an important orientation or variant remains missing.
scale.5: A coherent source fix and focused regression test are visibly applied; authoritative tests demonstrate that step-histogram axis limits contain the rendered density maximum while preserving density semantics and relevant orientation or histogram variants.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-backed progress toward correcting step-histogram autoscaling

applies_when: The visible trajectory proposes, attempts, or applies a source-code change intended to correct step-histogram or generic patch autoscaling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how far the implementation advances from a concrete source-level candidate to a coherent applied repair at the generic patch-limit boundary, while distinguishing wrong-boundary histogram workarounds from the intended unsimplified-path fix.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A histogram-local maximum sticky edge, direct axis limit, extra autoscale request, density modification, or step-vertex rewrite cannot exceed 2 even if applied. A claimed edit that is absent from final source, syntactically malformed, or non-importable cannot exceed 2. Disabling simplification for rendering or globally rather than only during limit extraction cannot exceed 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final repository contents, parse or import results, and git diff or status outrank edit commands, temporary patch files, summaries, and claims of success. When no final diff is available, exact source snippets and commands may establish a proposal or attempted edit but not an applied implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating an explicit workaround with mere browsing, or conversely treating an edit command, temporary patch, malformed source, or successful unrelated script as a coherent applied generic fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an implementation-ready change at the generic patch data-limit calculation that requests complete unsimplified path traversal. Scores above 3 require that generic change to be visibly present and coherent in repository source. Score 5 additionally requires direct validation that rendering simplification and histogram semantics remain unchanged.
metadata.judge_focus: Classify the strongest implementation state visible at the end of the trajectory: no concrete edit, explicit proposal, attempted but absent or malformed edit, coherent applied workaround, implementation-ready generic patch-limit plan, or coherent applied generic fix. Inspect both the edited boundary and whether the final repository actually contains the change.
metadata.oracle_test: The generic code deriving patch extrema for data limits must inspect every original path segment, for example by disabling simplification only in the relevant path or Bezier iteration, while leaving renderer simplification, histogram density values, polygon vertices, and sticky-edge behavior unchanged.

scale.1: No concrete source-level implementation candidate is reached; work remains exploratory, repeatedly fails before forming an edit, or proposes a mechanism unrelated to patch autoscaling.
scale.2: A specific source edit is proposed, attempted, or coherently applied at the wrong boundary, including histogram-local sticky edges, direct limits, density changes, polygon rewrites, or extra autoscaling; also includes a relevant edit that is absent, malformed, or contradicted by final repository evidence.
scale.3: The trajectory gives an implementation-ready generic patch-limit change that explicitly uses the unsimplified path for limit extraction, but it is not visibly applied, or an applied generic change is incomplete or affects simplification too broadly.
scale.4: A coherent repository change applies unsimplified traversal specifically at generic patch-limit extraction, with no visible modification to histogram computation, polygon geometry, sticky edges, or rendering simplification.
scale.5: The focused generic patch-limit change is visibly applied and directly validated, demonstrating complete extrema collection while preserving rendering simplification and existing histogram behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implementation maturity of the patch-autoscaling repair

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a density step histogram can be visibly clipped despite returning normalized bin heights.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that histogram density computation and step-polygon heights are correct, while autoscale data limits can omit a true path extremum because the patch path is simplified during limit calculation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims numpy.histogram density normalization or the step y-coordinate assignment is corrupt despite visible evidence that bar and step return equal heights and integrate to one; cap at 3 if it attributes the root cause only to missing sticky-edge maxima.
metadata.evidence_authority: A deterministic local reproduction comparing max(n) or polygon vertices against Axes.dataLim/view limits takes precedence over visual impressions; source evidence from the patch-limit path traversal takes precedence over speculation about density normalization or sticky edges.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing the expected inverse scaling of a probability-density height under x rescaling with a normalization bug, or treating sticky edges as the source of the missing upper data limit.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence that the density values or polygon vertices contain the missing maximum while the computed axis/data limit does not.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or runtime evidence separating returned histogram heights and polygon vertices from the resulting data/view limits, followed by identification of path simplification in patch-limit calculation.
metadata.oracle_test: For the reported 100-bin density step histogram, max(n) must equal the maximum plotted step vertex, and the y view limit must contain that maximum. The failure is in autoscale limit extraction from a simplifiable path, not in density semantics.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by observed histogram values and limits.
scale.2: Recognizes an autoscaling symptom but continues to blame density normalization, step construction, or an unsupported mechanism.
scale.3: Shows that density values are normalized and/or that bar and step return the same heights, and localizes the discrepancy to autoscaling, but does not identify path simplification during patch-limit extraction.
scale.4: Connects the missing step maximum to simplified path data used while updating patch limits, with relevant source inspection or a convincing runtime comparison.
scale.5: Provides a deterministic reproduction proving returned heights and polygon vertices are correct while data/view limits omit the maximum, and precisely traces this to simplification in the patch path traversal used by Axes limit calculation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of autoscaling failure and path simplification

applies_when: The visible prefix establishes an unchanged production state, applies a production-source edit, or displays production code that determines alignment execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how far the applied production state advances the causal shared-helper correction, distinguishing unchanged behavior, local compensation, incomplete shared-helper work, and a complete descent-preserving implementation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later visible production state retaining the original reversed mapping, omitting the production edit, or containing malformed executable code caps the score at 1. A caller-only name translation, `extent - descent` input transformation, or wrong-layer compensation caps it at 2. A shared-helper edit with missing membership, overlapping predicates, or altered descent terms caps it at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later displayed source excerpt or Git diff overrides earlier commands and claims; an explicit restore overrides prior edits. Otherwise, a successful command that writes the tracked production file establishes an applied attempt when no later source evidence contradicts it. Prose, generated images, and edits only to scratch scripts are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating intent as applied code, rewarding a visibly unchanged final helper, equating a caller workaround with the shared correction, or granting complete credit before both complementary predicates and formulas are visible
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible production code showing both disjoint directional predicates with `left`/`bottom` using `[d for h, d in hd_list]` and `right`/`top` using `[height - h + d for h, d in hd_list]`. Score 5 additionally requires visible preservation of raw `(h, yd)` and `(w, xd)` caller tuples and unaffected branches.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest visibly applied production semantics in `_get_aligned_offsets` and its two packer call sites, not proposed edits, rendering prose, or test expectations
metadata.oracle_test: The minimum physical edge is `offset - d` and the maximum physical edge is `offset - d + h`; therefore minimum-edge aliases are `left` and `bottom`, while maximum-edge aliases are `right` and `top`, with callers supplying raw descents.

scale.1: No applied production change is established, or the latest visible production state preserves the reversal, is malformed, or otherwise does not advance executable behavior.
scale.2: An applied production edit targets the symptom through a caller-only translation, transformed descent, unrelated packing layer, or another local compensation rather than correcting the shared directional dispatch.
scale.3: An applied edit targets the shared helper’s directional branches, but its exact resulting state is not shown or at least one membership, disjointness property, or descent-aware formula remains incorrect or incomplete.
scale.4: The visible shared helper has both correct disjoint memberships and both correct descent-aware formulas, but preservation of caller inputs or the complete surrounding state is not fully visible.
scale.5: The visible production state unambiguously contains the complete shared-helper correction, preserves raw caller descents and unaffected branches, and contains no competing local workaround.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied executable alignment semantics

applies_when: A production edit is visible and the prefix attempts behavioral, mathematical, or syntax validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures affirmative evidence from discriminative checks, while keeping absence of validation separate from contradictory evidence.

metadata.failure_mode: Only images, copied logic, syntax checks, external-installation output, or commands that fail before assertions
metadata.judge_focus: Assertions reached against the edited implementation
metadata.oracle_test: Use unequal dimensions and verify both directional edges from the checkout or directly extracted edited source

scale.1: No usable post-edit behavioral evidence is reached.
scale.2: Evidence is weak or indirect, such as copied arithmetic, images, one direction, or unclear source provenance.
scale.3: Discriminative unequal-size checks support both directions from the edited source, but compatibility coverage is limited.
scale.4: Repository-grounded checks cover both directions and meaningful shared or unaffected behavior.
scale.5: Focused checks pass for both packer orientations, nonzero descents, and unaffected modes with verified source provenance.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository-grounded validation strength

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains task-relevant work at the Prepare the evaluator-facing artifact stage.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether a terminal continuation provides a valid, evaluator-usable patch artifact whose tracked production source contains the complete scoped correction, with no malformed hunks, conflict markers, generated build products, or unrelated edits. Nonterminal continuations are not penalized for lacking a final artifact.

metadata.failure_mode: Empty, prose-only, malformed, truncated, test-only, externally sourced, or contaminated final submission
metadata.judge_focus: Terminal patch parseability, production-source inclusion, and evaluator usability
metadata.oracle_test: For terminal continuations, inspect the final unified diff and repository state for `lib/matplotlib/offsetbox.py` containing both disjoint membership changes; treat `terminal_at_cutoff=false` as not applicable

scale.1: At a terminal cutoff, no usable production patch is present, or the artifact is malformed, empty, or unrelated; a nonterminal cutoff is not scored at this anchor.
scale.2: A terminal artifact contains some relevant material but is incomplete, ambiguous, or difficult to apply, such as a partial hunk or missing production source.
scale.3: The terminal artifact is generally parseable and includes a production change, but scope, completeness, or repository cleanliness remains uncertain.
scale.4: The terminal artifact is a valid, scoped patch modifying the production source with both intended directional changes and no visible material contamination.
scale.5: The terminal artifact is a clean, complete, parseable patch generated from the final repository state, includes the shared-helper correction in `lib/matplotlib/offsetbox.py`, preserves unaffected code, and contains no unrelated or generated changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Valid final patch artifact

applies_when: The prefix reasons about helper inputs, offsets, descents, child edges, packer orientation, or the location of the fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible reasoning connects the observed behavior to the shared cross-axis helper and remains internally consistent with physical-edge arithmetic.

metadata.failure_mode: Unresolved coordinate speculation, treating reference offsets as physical edges, or editing based on an interpretation contradicted by the shown arithmetic
metadata.judge_focus: Resolved causal reasoning rather than confident wording
metadata.oracle_test: For visible `(extent, descent)` values, compare `offset - descent` and `offset - descent + extent` across children

scale.1: Reasoning is absent or persistently points to an unrelated mechanism.
scale.2: Relevant code is found, but the coordinate interpretation remains materially confused or self-contradictory.
scale.3: The shared helper and directional reversal are identified, but descent-aware arithmetic or caller compatibility is incomplete.
scale.4: The helper, both callers, and edge semantics are correctly connected with only a minor evidentiary gap.
scale.5: The reasoning explicitly derives both physical edges, preserves raw descents, rejects unsupported caller transformations, and predicts discriminative unequal-size behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal and coordinate coherence

applies_when: The prefix runs validation, reports behavioral output, interprets arithmetic, or claims that a correction works.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures concrete reasons to distrust the trajectory's conclusion, emphasizing relevant executed contradictions and unsupported success claims rather than missing evidence.

metadata.failure_mode: Claimed success after a relevant failed assertion, contradictory unequal-size geometry, wrong implementation provenance, or malformed source
metadata.judge_focus: Whether visible output supports the stated conclusion
metadata.oracle_test: Check command completion, assertion outcomes, measured edges, implementation provenance, and whether later evidence resolves earlier failures

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliability of observable behavior evidence

applies_when: Visible production code changes lookup-index conversion or sentinel assignment in `Colormap.__call__`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the applied production control flow makes every supported `xa` path capable of storing the distinct under, over, and bad LUT indices before any such index is assigned.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if sentinel values are cast or wrapped to `xa.dtype`; score 1 if any sentinel write visibly precedes widening, the reported `uint8` path remains narrow, broad warning suppression is used, or a supported path aliases a special row because its destination is non-representable.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible production source or complete diff outranks comments, claimed passes, source-string checks, simulations, and runs against copied or installed code; direct edited-source execution corroborates but cannot override contradictory source.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking Python `int(...)` or `np.array(sentinel).astype(xa.dtype)` for destination widening, overlooking unsigned or masked paths, or trusting runtime evidence from code that is not the latest visible production source.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require that all supported input paths reaching sentinel assignment produce a destination capable of representing `N`, `N + 1`, and `N + 2`, after float preprocessing and before the first write.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the dtype and control-flow path of `xa` immediately before all three sentinel writes, including narrow unsigned, signed, masked, scalar, and other accepted array inputs.
metadata.oracle_test: For `N == 256`, inspect or execute the edited method and establish that `xa` can hold 256, 257, and 258 before assignment while `cmap(np.uint8(0))` retains the same lookup index as `cmap(0)`.

scale.1: No effective destination fix is present: a relevant path remains non-representable, conversion occurs after a sentinel write, warning suppression substitutes for widening, or special indices visibly alias ordinary rows.
scale.2: The immediate warning is avoided by explicitly overflowing, clipping, or narrowing sentinel values, so distinct representable sentinel indices are not preserved.
scale.3: A production promotion handles the reported numeric path, but visible dtype-kind exclusions, placement ambiguity, or another concrete path leaves complete pre-assignment representability unresolved.
scale.4: All visible supported paths are widened before sentinel assignment and preserve distinct indices, but placement relative to float classification or another concrete compatibility detail remains uncertain.
scale.5: After unchanged float preprocessing, every supported path reaches a representable integer `xa` before all three ordered sentinel assignments, with coherent source and no contradictory visible execution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal consistency of the latest production state

applies_when: Visible repository production source, a production diff, or a submitted production patch establishes or changes PSD normalization inside `lib/matplotlib/mlab.py::_spectral_helper`.
Visible production evidence changes nearby magnitude, complex, angle, or phase handling in the same normalization block.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate the latest effective production implementation of `_spectral_helper`. Density PSD scaling must divide by `Fs` and window energy `(window**2).sum()` or its real-window equivalent. Non-density PSD scaling must divide by the square of the signed coherent sum `window.sum()**2`. If nearby output modes are changed, magnitude must retain `np.abs(result)`, magnitude and complex may use the signed window sum, and angle and phase must remain unnormalized.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest production density branch using `window.sum()**2`, lacking `Fs`, using a malformed energy expression, or otherwise not using window energy is capped at 1 regardless of a correct non-density branch or successful demonstrations. If density is correct but non-density uses coefficient magnitudes, window energy, or another non-coherent denominator, cap at 2. Correct PSD formulas with visibly damaged magnitude, angle, or phase semantics cap at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest inspected repository source or complete production diff wins over reasoning, comments, scalar demonstrations, test banners, and summaries. A later complete hunk wins over older source views. Added and removed diff lines establish the effective edit; unchanged lines omitted from a focused diff retain their most recent visible production state. Proposed formulas and independently reconstructed calculations are not implementation evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating blanket removal of `np.abs` as correctness, overlooking a density branch changed to coherent gain, collapsing both PSD branches to window energy, or assigning the same severity to a correct-density residual defect and a density-semantics regression.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require production evidence establishing both effective PSD formulas: density division by `Fs` and window energy, and non-density division by signed coherent gain squared. Score 5 additionally requires every visibly touched magnitude, complex, angle, or phase operation to remain semantically valid.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect both PSD branches in the latest effective production hunk, including the preceding `Fs` division; do not infer density correctness merely because the non-density signed-sum line is correct. Inspect required output-mode operations only when those lines are touched.
metadata.oracle_test: Effective density denominator is `Fs * (window**2).sum()`; effective non-density denominator is `window.sum()**2`. For a negative-valued real window, implementation output should satisfy `spec * win.sum()**2 == spec_a * Fs * (win**2).sum()` within tolerance, while magnitude output still applies `np.abs(result)`.
metadata.stage: Apply and immediately verify the focused edit

scale.1: Production evidence confirms an incorrect density branch, regardless of the non-density branch: the `Fs` factor is lost or misplaced, coherent gain is used instead of window energy, both branches use coherent gain, or the density energy expression is malformed.
scale.2: Density scaling is correctly divided by `Fs` and window energy, but non-density scaling is confirmed to use the sum of coefficient magnitudes, window energy, or another expression instead of the square of the signed window sum.
scale.3: Both PSD branches are correct, but production evidence confirms a separate required semantic regression in touched nearby code, such as removing `np.abs(result)` from magnitude output or normalizing angle or phase output.
scale.4: Both PSD formulas are established as correct, but concrete conflicting or truncated production evidence leaves the effective state of a visibly touched magnitude, complex, angle, or phase operation unresolved.
scale.5: The latest effective production state divides density PSD by `Fs` and window energy and divides non-density PSD by signed coherent gain squared. Any touched magnitude, complex, angle, and phase operations remain valid. Focused non-density fixes, two-site PSD fixes, complete consistency fixes, equivalent real-window energy spelling, working-tree source, and applicable patches receive equal credit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Per-instance Text property reasoning

applies_when: The visible cutoff contains repository-state evidence and investigation, editing, or validation relevant to the SubFigure spacing defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Classify current causal repair viability using the scale as a strict first-match decision table. The latest repository summary and complete diff determine what is persistent, while the visible trajectory may still establish causal precision, an inspectable attempted implementation, or an exact repair direction. Distinguish speculative propagation theories from the concrete boundary where GridSpec retains spacing but actual SubFigure bounds discard it. Do not reward activity volume, environment setup, rendered output, or stored spacing alone.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest clean repository cannot receive persistent-edit credit, but may receive up to 4 for an exact, source-grounded repair plan. A wrong-layer edit affecting parent subplot parameters, inner Axes, ordinary subplots, constrained-layout padding, or child layout configuration is capped at 3. An actual-bbox edit that imports ordinary subplot margins, changes omitted or explicit-zero behavior, inverts extents, mishandles spans, or competes with an active layout engine is capped at 4. An incoherent or destructive current artifact scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Use the latest repository summary, changed-file list, untracked-file list, and complete diff to determine persistence. Use visible source inspection and command output to assess causal understanding and attempted implementation even when the final diff is clean. Repository runtime source and individual SubFigure bbox observations outrank GridSpec attributes, overall tight boxes, rendered images, prose claims, and mixed-version installed-package results.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents clean but materially different investigations from collapsing into one score, while still withholding persistent implementation credit when the authoritative diff is empty. It also separates exact canonical repair directions from speculative spacing propagation and wrong-layer configuration changes.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires an inspectable persistent repository runtime edit that reaches actual SubFigure bounds. Score 4 requires either such a bbox edit with incomplete compatibility evidence or an exact source-grounded plan that identifies canonical spacing geometry and the necessary compatibility guards. Scores 1 through 3 do not require a persistent edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine persistence first, then classify the strongest currently demonstrated causal leverage: incoherent direction, speculative investigation, concrete spacing-loss boundary, exact canonical repair or actual-bbox edit, or complete persistent repair.
metadata.oracle_test: The decisive observable is individual SubFigure bbox_relative or pixel-space bbox geometry. A sound repair uses full-parent spacing-aware GridSpec positions, keeps explicit zero adjacent and unmanaged omitted spacing unchanged, preserves top-row orientation and ordered extents, and leaves layout-engine-provided bboxes authoritative.

scale.1: The current artifact is destructive, malformed, or incoherent, or the investigation commits to a causally contradicted direction without a concrete recovery—for example treating inner Axes placement or child layout configuration as the SubFigure-bbox repair.
scale.2: No persistent repair exists, and the visible work remains generic, speculative, indirect, or dominated by environment and mixed-installation activity. It may confirm that spacing values are stored or images differ, but it does not isolate how actual SubFigure bounds lose the spacing.
scale.3: The work establishes a concrete task-specific causal boundary—such as GridSpec retaining spacing while the ratio-only SubFigure transform omits it—but does not present an exact compatible repair. This also includes a localized, inspectable wrong-layer edit whose effect is clear but does not update actual SubFigure bounds.
scale.4: Either an exact source-grounded repair direction is demonstrated without a persistent final edit, including canonical full-parent GridSpec positions, actual bbox updates, explicit-versus-omitted handling, and layout-engine authority; or an inspectable runtime edit reaches actual SubFigure geometry but has incomplete validation or a remaining compatibility risk.
scale.5: The latest persistent repository runtime edit applies canonical spacing-aware geometry to actual SubFigure bounds and visibly preserves full-parent edges, explicit-zero and omitted-spacing semantics, ordered row-major extents, relevant ratio or nesting behavior, and authoritative layout-engine bbox overrides.

applies_when: The trajectory encounters a successful POSIX reproduction, conflicting path-match results, or evidence that the current code already respects the configured path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses contradictory evidence to refine the experiment toward the reported Windows and argument-spelling conditions instead of abandoning the defect or forcing an unrelated fix.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the trajectory declares the bug already fixed or submits no change solely because a Linux reproduction passes. Cap at 2 if it reacts by changing regex semantics without reconciling the path evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: A controlled experiment varying one condition at a time outranks repeated end-to-end commands with changing working directories, configurations, dependencies, or targets.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding repeated contradictory reproductions, environment churn, or unsupported conclusions that the issue is configuration misuse.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit recognition that a POSIX pass does not refute this Windows-specific report and a corrected experiment aimed at separator normalization.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible response to Linux success, absolute-versus-relative confusion, malformed fixture/configuration, or inconsistent path outputs; productive recovery includes inspecting exact path strings, using `ntpath` or Windows CI semantics, and isolating the trailing-slash recursive argument.
metadata.oracle_test: The decisive comparison keeps the same config and file tree while varying only path normalization/platform semantics; the affected spelling fails to match before normalization and matches afterward.

scale.1: Ignores or misreads contradictory evidence and reaches an unsupported conclusion.
scale.2: Notices the contradiction but responds with unrelated experiments or an unjustified broad fix.
scale.3: Narrows the contradiction to platform, working-directory, or path-spelling differences but does not complete a decisive comparison.
scale.4: Correctly reconciles the evidence and performs or specifies a controlled Windows/path-normalization experiment.
scale.5: Provides the anchor-4 recovery and explicitly rules out the major competing hypotheses with stable, minimal, reproducible evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovers correctly from misleading cross-platform evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why recursive discovery fails to honor a configured path regex on Windows or with a trailing-separator directory argument.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses source inspection and path-match evidence to determine whether recursive traversal constructs a mixed-separator path that matches neither compiled path-regex alternative.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 for a causal conclusion contradicted by visible source or match results, including claims that configuration is not loaded, `ignore-paths` universally fails, absolute paths are inherently the reported defect, or the defect is solely missing per-file filtering. Cap at 3 when separator or trailing-slash sensitivity is recognized but the mixed Windows descendant path is not established.
metadata.evidence_authority: Printed path values and direct regex results under Windows or controlled `ntpath` semantics outrank verbal inference. Relevant source flow outranks unrelated configuration experiments. A controlled comparison varying only trailing-separator or normalization state outranks repeated commands with different targets, working directories, or rcfiles.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents source browsing, generic path speculation, and successful POSIX runs from being scored as diagnosis, while ensuring an unresolved investigation outranks a confidently disproven cause.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require an explicit source-to-value chain showing how an input equivalent to `src/` can produce a mixed path such as `src/gen\about.py` on Windows and why neither the all-POSIX nor all-Windows compiled alternative matches it.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect concrete values flowing from the recursive input through `os.walk` and `os.path.join` into `_is_ignored_file`, together with the alternatives produced by `regexp_paths_csv`. Separate observations from hypotheses and note whether claimed causes survive focused comparisons.
metadata.oracle_test: For `^src/gen/.*$`, the compiled alternatives accept consistently POSIX or consistently Windows spellings. Starting recursive traversal from the unnormalized `src/` spelling on Windows can retain `/` in the prefix while joined descendants use `\`, yielding a spelling accepted by neither alternative.

scale.1: Commits to a task-causal explanation that visible source or controlled path-match evidence disproves.
scale.2: Does not establish a supported task-specific diagnosis and leaves the relevant hypotheses unresolved.
scale.3: Provides sound evidence for separator, path-representation, or trailing-argument sensitivity but does not complete the Windows mixed-separator causal chain.
scale.4: Establishes the complete recursive-input-to-mixed-descendant-to-regex-miss chain with concrete source and path-match evidence.
scale.5: Provides the anchor-4 diagnosis and uses controlled comparisons to rule out configuration loading, generic absolute-path matching, directory-only matching, and missing per-file filtering as competing causes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Establishes the mixed-separator causal chain without false diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory creates, proposes, or runs tests for recursive discovery with an `ignore-paths` regex.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Demonstrates the reported behavior with a fixture containing both an ignored generated Python file and a non-ignored Python file, using the recursive directory argument spelling and path semantics that expose the Windows separator bug.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the fixture files cannot emit distinguishable diagnostics, the configuration is malformed or not loaded, or the command includes extra targets that invalidate interpretation. Cap at 3 if only a POSIX run is shown and it already passed before the proposed change.
metadata.evidence_authority: A targeted automated test under Windows or controlled Windows path semantics outranks an ad hoc Linux run; output that identifies exactly which modules were analyzed outranks a score-only result.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating empty output, a 10/10 rating, a Linux-only already-passing reproduction, or direct linting of an ignored file as decisive evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require both negative and positive assertions: the ignored module is absent while the neighboring control module is still analyzed.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test code or runtime output using `--recursive=y`, an argument equivalent to `src/`, `ignore-paths` equivalent to `^src/gen/.*$`, a diagnostic-producing file under `src/gen`, and a diagnostic-producing control file outside it.
metadata.oracle_test: The regression should fail before normalization on Windows by reporting the generated file, then pass by omitting that file while continuing to report the non-ignored file.

scale.1: No relevant test or runtime evidence is present.
scale.2: Attempts a reproduction, but setup errors, ambiguous files, wrong working directory/configuration, or unrelated output make it non-diagnostic.
scale.3: Has a relevant recursive fixture or focused helper-level path-match test, but lacks platform sensitivity, a control file, or clear assertions.
scale.4: Provides a decisive regression setup with ignored and non-ignored files and verifies the expected recursive selection under the affected path semantics.
scale.5: Provides the anchor-4 test as a maintainable repository test and also shows before/after failure discrimination or an equivalent direct assertion of normalized discovery paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces a decisive recursive ignore-path regression test

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a configured ignore-path regex fails during recursive discovery, especially for a directory argument ending in a slash or on Windows.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the task-causal mismatch between the path strings produced during recursive discovery and the POSIX-or-Windows alternatives compiled for `ignore-paths`, rather than treating configuration loading or recursive ignoring in general as broken.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory concludes that configuration is absent, that `ignore-paths` universally fails, or that absolute paths are inherently the defect despite visible evidence that the requested relative-path case works on POSIX. Cap at 3 if it identifies only the directory-without-trailing-separator symptom without explaining why matching the subsequently discovered file also fails on Windows.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete printed path values and direct regex-match results under Windows path semantics outrank speculation; relevant source inspection outranks unrelated configuration experiments.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards plausible but incorrect diagnoses such as stale configuration, an uncompiled regex, absolute-path matching, or merely failing to test each individual file.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an explicit causal chain from the recursive input/path construction to a representation that the compiled all-POSIX and all-Windows regex alternatives do not match.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or experiments connecting `PyLinter._discover_files`, `os.walk`/`os.path.join`, the `regexp_paths_csv` transformation, and a path such as `src/gen\about.py` or another mixed-separator result caused by starting from `src/` on Windows.
metadata.oracle_test: With `ignore-paths = ["^src/gen/.*$"]` and the recursive argument `src/`, the semantic reference is that Windows recursive discovery must present a consistently normalized path such as `src\gen\about.py` or `src/gen/about.py` to the dual-format regex, not a mixed-separator spelling.

scale.1: No task-specific diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the inspected code and observed behavior.
scale.2: Finds the recursive discovery and ignore helpers but gives only a vague or materially incorrect explanation of the failure.
scale.3: Recognizes a path-format, separator, or trailing-slash sensitivity and supplies some relevant source or regex evidence, but does not establish the complete Windows recursive causal chain.
scale.4: Correctly explains that recursive discovery from the supplied spelling can produce a path representation incompatible with both compiled path-regex alternatives, with concrete source and path-match evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in anchor 4 and decisively distinguishes it from configuration loading, generic absolute-path, directory-only, and file-level-filtering hypotheses using focused comparative evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnoses the Windows recursive-path representation failure

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or edits production code to make recursive `ignore-paths` matching use stable path separators.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Confines the implementation to normalizing recursive filesystem arguments or equivalent discovered-path inputs before traversal and ignore matching, preserving the established `ignore-paths` regex semantics and shared ignore helper.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for globally changing regex matching from `match` to `search`, rewriting user regexes, appending separators merely to force a directory match, or substituting `_ignore_paths` for `config.ignore_paths` without evidence of a stale-value defect. Cap at 3 for adding duplicate per-file filtering without addressing the mixed-path source.
metadata.evidence_authority: A coherent diff in the recursive discovery path outranks prose. A narrowly equivalent normalization backed by path evidence can receive full credit; broad changes to regex matching or configuration parsing cannot.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for overbroad semantic changes that may make the reported example pass while changing anchored-regex behavior or unrelated ignore options.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a concrete localized implementation or exact patch plan that normalizes the path used by recursive discovery while retaining `_is_ignored_file` and existing option values.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or concrete patch plan in `pylint/lint/pylinter.py`, especially `_discover_files`, that applies `os.path.normpath` at the recursive input/traversal boundary before `os.path.isdir`, `os.walk`, and yielded-path construction.
metadata.oracle_test: Normalizing an input such as `src/` with the host path rules before `os.walk` makes all descendants use one separator convention, allowing the existing transformed `^src/gen/.*$` pattern to match on Windows.

scale.1: No implementation boundary is identified, or the proposed edit is unrelated to recursive path discovery.
scale.2: Proposes a broad or incorrect production change that alters regex semantics, configuration parsing, or unrelated lint behavior.
scale.3: Works near `_discover_files` and could suppress the reported files, but duplicates filtering, handles only a symptom, or leaves the path representation inconsistent.
scale.4: Presents a localized normalization change at the recursive discovery boundary that preserves existing ignore semantics and plausibly fixes the Windows case.
scale.5: Presents the anchor-4 implementation with clear ordering and scope, explains why normalization occurs before traversal/path construction, and shows that package, non-package, and explicit non-directory inputs retain their established control flow.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Targets normalization at the recursive discovery boundary

applies_when: The trajectory contains commands or test code exercising modify_sys_path or runpy.run_module behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces trustworthy runtime evidence that arbitrary leading paths are preserved and intended current-directory representations are still removed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible failed assertion, misleading expected result, dependency failure before the relevant function executes, or a test harness that does not isolate the entry being tested caps credit at 3 unless later corrected by decisive evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing output from the actual modified function or runpy reproduction outranks simulations and assertions without observed results; later corrected tests outrank earlier flawed harnesses.
metadata.failure_mode: Awards strong validation credit to tautological simulations, broken test setup, or output that never reached pylint's path-modification code.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires observed passing results for both preservation of an arbitrary entry and removal of at least two intended cwd representations.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed commands and their output for the reported "something" case, plus cases for "", ".", and os.getcwd(); distinguish actual function execution from merely restating the condition.
metadata.oracle_test: A matrix over sys.path[0] values "something", "", ".", and os.getcwd() yields preserve, remove, remove, and remove respectively.

scale.1: No executable behavioral evidence, or only evidence showing incorrect behavior.
scale.2: Attempts a reproduction or test, but it fails before exercising the relevant behavior or has an invalid harness.
scale.3: Shows one trustworthy passing side of the behavior, typically preservation of an arbitrary path, without adequate complementary removal evidence.
scale.4: Shows trustworthy passing output for arbitrary-path preservation and for at least two of the three intended removable forms.
scale.5: Shows the complete four-case oracle matrix passing and also demonstrates the reported runpy scenario or an equivalent end-to-end invocation of the actual modified function.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive behavioral evidence for preservation and removal

applies_when: The trajectory contains a proposed or applied change to modify_sys_path or its immediate callers.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible implementation preserves an arbitrary sys.path[0] while continuing to remove "", ".", or the current working directory and retaining coherent existing PYTHONPATH cleanup behavior without unrelated control-flow changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An inverted condition, unconditional arbitrary-path removal, malformed function, or early return that visibly suppresses required unrelated cleanup caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible file content or unified diff outranks earlier proposed snippets and verbal summaries; runtime evidence cannot rescue visibly inverted or malformed code.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes a patch that removes arbitrary entries, returns at the wrong time, or accidentally rewrites multiple pop sites for the requested guard.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible coherent implementation whose condition removes the three intended working-directory forms and preserves other first entries.
metadata.judge_focus: The exact condition around the initial removal, placement and reuse of cwd, safe access to sys.path, and the unchanged or equivalently correct behavior of subsequent PYTHONPATH branches.
metadata.oracle_test: For first entries "", ".", and os.getcwd(), the entry is removed; for "something" or another non-cwd path, it remains. Existing leading/trailing-colon PYTHONPATH processing remains reachable and coherent.

scale.1: No implementation, syntactically corrupted implementation, or behavior opposite to the requested fix.
scale.2: Shows the intended idea but the visible code is incomplete, inverted, unsafe, or introduces a clear control-flow regression.
scale.3: Implements the central guard correctly but leaves a visible robustness or compatibility concern, such as unsafe empty-list access or questionable alteration of adjacent cleanup logic.
scale.4: Provides a coherent focused implementation that preserves arbitrary first entries, removes all three cwd representations, and keeps the surrounding PYTHONPATH behavior intact.
scale.5: Provides a precise, robust, and minimal implementation with safe indexing where relevant, consistent cwd handling, and no unnecessary behavioral or formatting changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantic correctness and boundary of the implementation

applies_when: The trajectory contains analysis, source inspection, or runtime evidence concerning pylint.modify_sys_path and runpy execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that modify_sys_path unconditionally removes sys.path[0], although runpy or an embedding application may place an arbitrary library path there, and distinguishes that entry from current-working-directory representations that pylint intentionally removes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the trajectory concludes that arbitrary first entries should be removed, or reverses which entries are protected, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and successful direct runtime observations outrank unsupported narrative; a genuine runpy reproduction outranks a hand-written simulation of pop behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards superficial recognition of a sys.path issue despite misunderstanding which entries are safe to remove.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly distinguishing arbitrary injected paths from "", ".", and os.getcwd().
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of pylint/__init__.py, pylint/__main__.py, sys.path before/after output, and reasoning connecting the unconditional first pop to the reported embedding failure.
metadata.oracle_test: With sys.path beginning with "something", calling the relevant pylint path-modification behavior must not remove "something"; the original unconditional sys.path.pop(0) does remove it.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis incompatible with the reported behavior.
scale.2: Mentions sys.path or runpy but does not localize the unconditional first-entry removal or misstates its effect.
scale.3: Localizes the unconditional sys.path.pop(0) and explains that it can remove an injected path, but does not fully distinguish the intended removable entries.
scale.4: Correctly explains the arbitrary-path failure and the intended treatment of "", ".", and os.getcwd(), with source-based reasoning.
scale.5: Provides the complete source-supported causal model and decisive observed before/after evidence, while also distinguishing the initial removal from the later PYTHONPATH-specific cleanup.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of the sys.path mutation

applies_when: The task concerns modify_sys_path behavior when pylint is invoked through runpy or module execution
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The applied implementation must preserve an arbitrary caller-injected first sys.path entry while still removing only "", ".", or the current working directory where the existing initial and PYTHONPATH-related cleanup requires it.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible applied code uses the reverse polarity, still unconditionally removes an arbitrary first entry, or returns early in a way that prevents required cleanup of later cwd-equivalent entries. Score 1 if the function is visibly malformed, syntactically invalid, or has duplicated or misplaced statements that make its behavior incoherent.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository source or a final unified diff outranks assistant explanations, proposed snippets, and test claims. Direct observed before/after sys.path values outrank narrative assertions. If tests conflict with the applied code, score the code semantics and apply the contradiction cap.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for matching the issue wording while implementing the opposite condition, for treating successful-looking ad hoc output as stronger than corrupted source, or for preserving the injected path by broadly abandoning the function's remaining cleanup responsibilities.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visibly applied, syntactically coherent change to modify_sys_path; merely describing the intended condition or testing an unattached helper cannot receive those scores.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible applied source or diff for the initial-pop condition, its polarity, placement of cwd computation, and the resulting indices and control flow of the existing PYTHONPATH branches. Use focused executions only to corroborate the applied code.
metadata.oracle_test: Starting with an arbitrary injected value at sys.path[0], calling modify_sys_path must leave that value present at index 0. With sys.path[0] equal to "", ".", or os.getcwd(), that entry must be removed. PYTHONPATH leading- or trailing-colon handling may remove only the cwd-equivalent entry at the position intended by the existing algorithm, never an unrelated injected path.

scale.1: The visible applied function is malformed or its behavior clearly still removes arbitrary leading entries without a valid selective guard.
scale.2: An applied change exists, but the condition has wrong polarity, unsafe indexing, or broad control flow that preserves the repro value only by breaking required cwd or PYTHONPATH cleanup; alternatively, the correct fix is only proposed and not applied.
scale.3: The applied code preserves the arbitrary first entry in the main repro, but visible branch logic leaves a material unresolved semantic defect in removing cwd-equivalent entries or handling the existing PYTHONPATH positions.
scale.4: The applied code coherently preserves arbitrary first entries and removes the ordinary "", ".", and cwd cases, with no visible contradiction, but some relevant branch behavior is not fully inspectable or remains weakly justified.
scale.5: The applied code is coherent and correctly selective across the initial entry and existing PYTHONPATH branches: arbitrary injected paths are retained, only cwd-equivalent entries are removed at the intended positions, and focused visible evidence corroborates these semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly preserve injected sys.path entries while removing only working-directory entries

applies_when: The trajectory contains a proposed or applied change to modify_sys_path or its immediate path-cleanup logic.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The applied change guards the original initial sys.path removal so that "", ".", and the current working directory are removed while arbitrary caller-injected first entries are preserved, without introducing a concrete defect into the surrounding PYTHONPATH cleanup.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 if the applied patch uses reversed polarity, still unconditionally removes the initial arbitrary entry, or introduces an early return that bypasses required existing cleanup. Score at most 3 if the central guard is correct but the patch newly adds a concrete adjacent defect such as accessing sys.path[1] without establishing that index 1 exists, changing a required pop target, or duplicating cleanup. Score 1 if the latest function is malformed or incoherent. Do not penalize unchanged legacy positional cleanup solely because it was not redesigned.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest applied repository source or unified diff outranks proposed snippets, simulations, summaries, and test claims. Executions of the actual modified function or focused repository tests corroborate source semantics but cannot override a visibly malformed, inverted, or regression-inducing patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating a focused correct fix as defective merely because it leaves legacy PYTHONPATH logic unchanged, while still withholding high credit from patches that obtain the simple repro behavior by introducing unsafe adjacent edits or bypassing existing cleanup.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a visibly applied, syntactically coherent guard at the original initial-removal site that preserves arbitrary first entries and removes all three requested working-directory representations. Merely proposing the guard or testing an unattached helper cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final applied diff or file state for the condition replacing the original unconditional initial pop, its polarity and placement, and any newly edited adjacent pop indices, bounds checks, or returns. Treat untouched pre-existing PYTHONPATH branches as neutral rather than requiring this task to redesign them.
metadata.oracle_test: At the original initial-removal point, first entries "", ".", and os.getcwd() are removed, while "something" or another unrelated injected path is retained. Any surrounding PYTHONPATH code changed by the patch remains reachable, uses valid indices, and removes the intended entry; unchanged surrounding branches are outside the demanded fix.

scale.1: The latest applied function is malformed or incoherent, or the initial removal plainly retains the original opposite behavior.
scale.2: No valid applied selective guard exists, or the applied approach has reversed polarity, still removes arbitrary first entries, or uses broad control flow such as an early return that visibly suppresses required cleanup.
scale.3: The applied initial guard has the correct polarity and requested value set, but the patch newly introduces a concrete adjacent defect such as unsafe new indexing, a wrong pop target, duplicated cleanup, or another material regression.
scale.4: A coherent applied guard correctly preserves arbitrary first entries and removes "", ".", and cwd; adjacent cleanup is unchanged or equivalently coherent, with no visible introduced regression, but focused runtime corroboration is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: Meets the score-4 implementation standard and is corroborated by trustworthy execution of the actual modified function or a focused repository test covering arbitrary-entry preservation and removal of "", ".", and cwd.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct selective initial removal without new adjacent regressions
